From CG MISLE rpeort: On 12 August 2009, at Approximately 1430, the recreational boat, MI 4956BK, was 32 Miles offshore fishing with seven people on board when a storm set in and capsized the boat.  The storm had not been forecasted when the vessel left the dock at 0600.  The boat was attached to a rig via a rig hook, and when it capsized it threw 6 of the seven passengers overboard.  The seventh passenger was trapped in the cabin and was unable to escape.  2 of the passengers climbed up on the rig while the remaining 4 climbed on top of the capsized boat.  The capsized boat broke free from the rig and began to drift off for 4 miles.  The boat was found by a passing commercial fishing boat, The Fighting Chicken, and were rescued.  The Fighting Chicken reported the casualty to the CG.  The remaining 2 passengers were rescued by a Coast Guard Helicopter.  All passengers taken back to Biloxi for medical treatment.  No further incident.

From MISLE report: D8 RECEIVED 406 EPIRB ALERT FROM PLATFORM MATAGORDA 519. D8 CONTACTED PLATFORM AND ESTABLISHED THAT THE EPIRB WAS ACTIVATED DUE TO A P.I.W. A SMALL P/C CAPSIZED UNDER THE PLATFORM WITH 3 POB. THE PLATFORM RECOVERED 02 P.I.W. SAFELY HOWEVER A 3RD WAS SEEN DRIFTING AWAY FROM THE PLATFORM. THE PLATFORM THREW A LIFE RING AND IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE P.I.W. WAS ABLE TO RECOVER IT.

According to the operator and one passenger, Passenger 1, the boaters were traveling upstream.  Passenger 2 was sitting in the front of the boat, Passenger 1 was walking to the front of the boat, Operator was operating and pulled back on the throttle ejecting Passenger 2 and Passenger 1.  Passenger 1 was able to get back into the boat after receiving injuries to his left hip and lower right leg.  Passenger 2 surfaced face down and quickly sunk.  Operator was charged with BWI.  Passenger 1 was transported by helicopter to Mercy Hospital.  Passenger 2 was found, deceased, on 06/29/2009.  There were inaccessible PFDs in the boat, no throwable device, and no fire extinguisher.

Passenger 1 told Conservation Officers (CO) CO 1 and CO 2 that she and her husband, Operator, went down the river to find a spot to watch fireworks during a 4th of July celebration. Passenger 1 said they left the Birdland Marina at approximately 1500hrs and first went upriver towards Prospect Park. They then turned around and went down river toward the dam. When they got close to the Center Street Dam, Operator turned off the boat and put out anchor. The boat would not hold in the current, and Operator told Passenger 1 they needed a bigger anchor. Operator pulled up the anchor and tried to put it out again. Passenger 1 told CO's CO 1 and CO 2 that the boat began to spin as it went downstream. Operator told Passenger 1 to put her life jacket on. Passenger 1 said that Operator put on a jacket, but did not fasten it. Passenger 1 told CO's CO 1 and CO 2 that she thought Operator was trying to start the boat as it went over the dam. Passenger 1 said that Operator was thrown from the boat as it went over, and his jacket was torn off by the current. Passenger 1 was able to stay in the boat until it flooded and capsized. Passenger 1 said next remembered the rescue attempt and subsequent rescue.

When the boat was recovered, the throttle of the boat was in the neutral position and the key was turned off. The warning cable that went across the river upstream of the dam was missing.

Victim 1and his girlfriend Operator 2 had borrowed two jet skis from their next door neighbor and were using them going up and down the river from the boat ramp area at Winnebago Park to the roller dam and back.  Operator 2 admitted that she and  Victim 1 had a couple of beers at the park prior to going out on the water and also had a couple beers prior to leaving for the park.  She stated that initially she was riding the jet ski that  Victim 1was on, however he was concerned that she would get in trouble with it because it was the faster machine, so they switched.  Witnesses advised that Victim 1and Operator 2 were riding up and down the river and often coming very close to the roller dam on several occasions. They stated that Victim 1drove into the roller dam at a high speed until the water pouring off the dam struck the jet ski turning it over and tossing Victim 1into the water. Victim 1struggled for about five minutes trying to get out of the boil before it appeared he went unconscious.  Victim 1was wearing a lifejacket and the autopsy report verifies that he drowned.

Vessel #1 was a 14 foot raft with 4 persons on board.  The operator broke an oar at the entrance of the "let's make a deal" rapids.  The vessel got caught between a rock pillar and the rapid and the operator could not get the vessel free from danger.  After being pinned against the pillar for about 5 minutes and being washed out of the vessel once, the occupants were forced to leave the vessel and try to swim to another vessel.  Three occupants were able to swim to another vessel and get to an island.  The victim was not strong enough to swim out of the eddy and rapids.  He was washed back to the stranded vessel where he hung onto the side and kept getting pulled under by the vessel.  He was eventually pulled under for a time of about 3 to 5 minutes and drowned.  The victim resurfaced and floated to the island where the others had swam.  CPR was performed on the victim.

An empty boat was found nosed into the bank with the motor running, a cowboy hat was found floating in the water approximately 100 yards away.  Reportedly, the victim had launched at approximatley 1400 hours.  The County Sheriff used sonar and dive teams to retrieve the body of the 76 year old victim.

THREE ADULT MALES IN A 6 PERSON RAFT HEADING UP THE CDA RIVER GOT CAUGHT IN AN AREA WITH SEVERAL FALLEN TREES IN THE WATER.  THEIR RAFT OVERTURNED LANDING ALL 3 MEN IN THE WATER, NONE WERE WEARING PFD'S.  1 24-YEAR-OLD MALE SWAM TO SHORE WHERE HE WENT FOR HELP, ONE MALES BODY WAS RECOVERED STUCK TO A LOG, THE OTHER MALES BODY WAS RECOVERED ABOUT 12 MILES FROM THE ACCIDENT.

Operator 1 and passenger were operating a personal watercraft (Vessel 1).  Operator 2 and passenger were operating a personal watercraft (vessel 2).  Operator 2 had been operating the PWC approximatly 5 minutes prior to the accident and had limited experience.  Vessel 1 was ahead of vessel 2 and they were doing crossing patterns and vessel 2 was jumping vessel 1 wake.  Vessel 2 was operating too close to vessel 1 and vessel 1 made a turn to the left.  At the same time vessel 2 made a hard turn to the right, possibly to avoid a collision.  When vessel 2 made the hard turn the PWC caught a wake and turned violently, causing operator 2 and passenger to be ejected.  Operator 2 then struck vessel 1 with her body and sustained sever internal injuries, and later died.  Vessel 2 passenger also struck vessel 1 and sustained some minor injuries to his right arm.  Operator 1 and passenger were not ejected from their watercraft and did not sustain any injuries.

VICTIM WAS A PASSENGER IN A VESSEL WHEN HE DECIDED TO JUMP OVERBOARD FOR AN UNKNOWN REASON.  THE OPERATOR AND OTHER SUBJECTS ATTEMPTED TO HELP THE VICTIM BY THROWING HIM LIFE JACKETS AND DIVING INTO THE WATER, BUT VICTIM REFUSED HELP AND PUSHED THEM AWAY.  VICTIM ENDED UP GOING UNDER WATER AND IS MISSING AND PRESUMED DROWNED.
Update:  The body of the victim was recovered a couple of weeks later with the use of side scan sonar.
Kayaker (victim) was found by one of his party, hung up on shoulder strap of floatation vest, on a sweeper.  The victim is believed to have drowned.

VESSEL 1ATTEMPTED TO JUMP A WAKE CAUSED BY VESSEL 2.  AS VESSEL 1 APPROACHED AT APPROXIMATELY 60 MILES PER HOUR (50 - 100 FEET AWAY) HE WAS SPRAYED IN THE FACE BY THE WATER JET FROM VESSEL 2.  VESSEL 2'S DECISION TO MAKE A SHARP LEFT TURN, COMBINED WITH THE JET NOZZLE AIMED TO INTENTIONALLY SPRAY VESSEL 1 CREATED A SITUATION WHERE VESSEL 1 OPERATOR COULD NOT SEE VESSEL 2.  VESSEL 1 THOUGHT VESSEL 2 WAS GOING TO CONTINUE TOWARDS THE FAMILY CABIN.  VESSEL 2 COMPLETED HIS LEFT TURN DIRECTLY INTO THE PATH OF VESSEL 1.  VESSEL 1 JUMPED THE WAKE AND UPON RIDING THROUGHT THE SPRAY SAW VESSEL 2 DIRECTLY IN FRONT OF HIM.  VESSEL 1 WAS UNABLE TO AVOID THE COLLISION.  VESSEL 1 STRUCK THE OPERATOR OF VESSEL 2 WITH THE BOW AREA OF HIS PWC ON HIS LEFT SIDE EJECTING HIM FROM THE PWC.  THE UNDERSIDE OF VESSEL 1 THEN CONTACTED THE OPERATOR OF VESSEL 2 CAUSING MASSIVE INTERNAL INJURIES. NOTE:  THE OPERATORS OF BOTH VESSELS WERE WEARING LIFE JACKETS THAT WERE NOT APPROVED BY THE US COAST GUARD.

Vessel 1 was traveling south by southwest, just coming on plane.  The boat was traveling to the north of two lighted hazard buoys.  The operator states he went between the hazard markers and then was on the north of them.  At this point, the boat struck a partially submerged rock causing a violent crash.  According to statements, 11 of the 12 passengers were thrown clear of the vessel.  The boat vaulted off of the rock and landed on its port side taking on water.  As the boat filled up with water from the damage holes and from landing on its port side, the boat started to sink and capsize.  Seven people swam and made it to Channel Island.  Three people remained with the boat, and two people were missing, the two were later located and were deseased.

A large raft was put into the Payette River approximately 3.5 miles above Banks, Idaho.  The raft had 10 people on board; none of these people had been involved in rafting class 5 rapids and the rapids they were going to encounter for the next 3 miles were all class 4 and 5+.  All people in the raft were wearing life jackets but helmets or other safety equipment were not aboard the raft.  Approx. 10 minutes in, the raft hit a rapid sideways and three people were ejected.  Two of the people were pulled back in but the third was not able to get back in before the raft went around an island.  The raft went on one side of the island and the person in the water went on the other side.  A few hundred yards down river, the rafters pulled over to the side and ran back to look for the victim (47 yoa).  The victim was located alongside the island underneath a log.  Rescue personnel could not revive the victim.

A Pocatello man is missing after his bass boat turned up empty in some willows along the shore of the American Falls Reservoir on the Snake River.  The man had been scheduled to return from the fishing excursion on Saturday evening, but never turned up.  There was no appartent damage to the boat when it was found on Monday.  Several searches have been conducted, to date (10/22/09) no body has been recovered.

Vessel 1, 1961 Larson with an outboard motor was operating upriver (east) on the Spokane River from Johnson Park at Mill River with a passenger sitting in the passenger seat.  At the same time, operator of vessel 2 was sitting in the operator's seat of his 1998 Blue Water on the south side of the river across from the Mill River condos and his passenger was in the bow of the boat fishing facing the south shoreline.  Vessel 1 hit a large wake which caused him to lurch forward pushing the throttle lever down even more causing the vessel to accelerate more.  Vessel 1 turned suddenly to the right possible due to the wake, or steering control issues and within approx 2 seconds vessel 1 struck vessel 2 in the bow area approx 4' back from the tip of the bow on the port side.  Vessel 1 struck vessel 2 between 240 degree and 250 degree angle.  When the two boats collided, vessel 1 pushed down on vessel 2 and started to rotate vessel 2 in a clockwise direction.  Vessel 1 continued to ride up on vessel 2 and the outboard engine, skag and propeller struck the gunwhale of vessel 2.  The boats then separated and vessel 1 continued in the water and struck the shoreline approx 10-15 feet away.  Vessel 2 rotated approx 180 degrees as a result of the accident.  The passenger in vessel 2 who was in the bow was struck by vessel 1 in the back of the head and thrown into the water.  The victim sustained massive head injuries and a fractured skull as a result of the accident, causing his death.  The operator of vessel 1 was arrested for operating a vessel under the influence of alchol.

Vessel was drifting down the river, as they had the day before bass fishing just above Copper Creek, they struck a partially submerged rock close to the bank.  The bow of the boat was facing the shore drifting back at an angle almost 45 degrees.  It grounded the boat on the rock, causing the boat to lurch and throw the occupants on the bow overboard.  The operator and passenger were on the bow of the boat.  The passenger stated that they went about ten to fifteen feet in the air before hitting the water.  The passenger indicated that the current was so fast that even though he was about fifteen feet from shore, there was no way he could swim to it.  The passenger said that the operator came up, and then disappeared below the water.  Neither party had a life jacket on.  The passenger was able to be retrieved by the other passengers that were also on the boat.  Passenger 4 took control of the boat to get it freed from the rock and was able to pilot it over to passenger 1 and throw a life jacket to him.  They were unable to do the same for the operator.  The body of the boat operator was discovered 2 weeks later.

A 1981 Weldcraft was north bound on the Snake River near the Interstate Bridge.  The operator either by inattention or contributing medical conditions, struck the third suspension pier of the bridge from the Idaho side.  A passenger in the vessel was thrown forward in the vessel where he struck the infrastructure and was momentarily stunned.  The passenger said he tied the boat to a piece of metal framework on the bridge and went back in the boat to help the operator who had been unconcious.  The passenger said the operator was now awake, but pinned in the vessel and he was unable to get him out.  The passenger said that the boat sank and he swam to the surface.

Three men were in a canoe that flipped throwing them all into the water.  One individual was able to swim to shore and retrieve another boat.  He was able to go back and get the second victim into the boat with help from a neighbor.  The other victim had disappeared in the water.  The three subjects set out in the afternoon to do some fishing and drink some beer.  About ten minutes into their trip, the owner of the canoe started to fish while the other two subjects paddled, as they took turns paddling and fishing the subject in the front was attempting to get a cigarette out and dropped them from his pocket.  As he dropped them he attempted to catch them causing the canoe to become unstable and capsize.  All three subjects were ejected into the 33 degree water, an attempt was made to get back into the canoe which resulted in it flooding.  The subjects decided they needed to swim to shore in order to survive.  The owner made it to shore, went to his garage and retrieved a small jon boat and went back out on the river to save the other two subjects.  The owner made it to one of the subjects and was able to get him to shore where the fire departments and EMS were waiting.  The third subject was last seen in the middle of the river near the swamped canoe and was seen going under the water just before the Sheriff's Department got to the area of the canoe attempting to save him.  The subject in the middle of the canoe was seated on a plastic lawn chair placed in the canoe and there were only two life jackets on board.  Neither of the life jackets were used or attempted to be used and were located in or near the swamped canoe when the Sheriff's Deputy got to the canoe.  It is the opinion of the investigating officer that due to improper seating and high center of gravity in the canoe contributed to the instability of the canoe and the quick movement by the subject caused the capsize.  A search for the missing subject continues, but high water and flooding conditions have made it difficult.  The search continues for the missing subject.  The owner/operator was cited for  insufficient number of pfd's, failure to display valid registration, and fishing without a valid license in possession.
For unknown reasons the vessel got lodged on a large rock submerged in the water.  The operator fell into the water and drowned.  The body of the victom was recoverd 50 yards down river.

While fishing, the victim's line became tangled on a tree limb.  After freeing the line, he stood up and lost his balance.  He fell backwards into the water, causing the operator to fall overboard as well.  The operator was able to re-enter the boat.  The third individual on the boat threw the bow line towards the victim unsuccessfully, and tried to dog paddle the boat to the victim.  The victim surfaced twice before disappearing.   His body was recovered approximately and hour later.   Autopsy reports indicate the victim died from drowning.

Research and estimates on the maximum boat weight capacity compared to the estimated passenger and equipment weight at the time of the accident revealed the boat was likely over maximum weight capacity by 173 pounds.  Measurements of the boat show the sides and transom were 15 inches tall and the width (beam) was 50 inches.  The weight in the boat at the time of the accident would have left little room for weight shift from either side of the centerline. The additional weight would have reduced the amount of freeboard or distance from the waterline to the top of the sides or gunnels.  Movement by passengers left or right of the boat’s centerline would have also reduced the freeboard dangerously close to the point water entered over the gunnels.  Occupant and officer observation indicate there was at least 6 inches of water in the bottom of the boat.  It is likely that the water entered at the same time when weight in the boat shifted off center due to a passenger standing unexpectedly.  The operator and passengers may not have realized they were over the weight limit because the boat was manufactured prior to capacity plate requirements.  However, the reduced freeboard would have been an obvious indicator the boat was overloaded.   *(Note-Official weight capacity test were not conducted as outlined in the Federal Code of Regulations 33 CFR Part 183.  It is believed research conducted provided enough information to determine the vessel was overloaded at the time of accident.)

The semi-V hull configuration, length and width of the vessel also contributed to the overall stability of the boat in the water.  The basic rule of “Wider is better” applies in this situation.  The more hull touching the water, the more stable a platform.  The hull narrows as it reaches the bow and forms the semi-V configuration.  Persons moving in this area would cause a greater disturbance in the boats stability.  

In addition to the hull configuration, the center of gravity also plays a large part in stability.  Aftermarket seats on pedestals were added at the bow and stern raising the center of gravity 8 to 12 inches.  In addition, the passenger standing in the vessel also raised the center of gravity.  Raising the center of gravity makes the boat susceptible to capsizing.

Finally, the deceased was wearing a serviceable USCG rated “Type 3” personal floatation device (PFD).  However, both witnesses/occupants claim the PFD was not properly buckled.  When the deceased impacted the water, he most likely raised his arms in an attempt to swim or reach for the boat.  The PFD easily slipped off during the struggle to stay afloat.

Per significant incident report--witnesses observed a boat with one individual aboard traving south on the lake.  A few moments later, they observed the boat traveling north and turning in circles with no on aboard.  They notified EMS.  Search and rescue operations were immediately started and a ground search was also initiated.  The victim's body was recovered on 4/16/09 near lake lot 300.  Vessel assessment indicated that victim tied the steering wheel off with a line, placed the motor in forward gear (full throttle), and left the helm to remove the stern drain plug in an attempt to remove water from the hull.  He would have been standing or leaning over when moving to the stern to remove the drain plug and would not have had the lanyard cutoff switch attached to his person.  This a careless practice, but it is not believed to have caused his fall overboard.  Preliminary coroner's report indicates that the victim had 80 % blockage in 3 major arteries that may have caused a severe angina attack causing him to fall overboard.

It has been concluded that the operator of this vessel fell overboard while conducting repairs on his 25 horse power Johnson motor.  It is probable that while adjusting the carburetor, the operator was standing up and attempted to start the motor while in gear.  The motor started at full throttle and caused him to fall overboard.  The victim was not wearing a personal flotation device.  Starting the vessel in gear, disabled neutral safety switch, which allowed motor to be started in gear and at full throttle.  There was no lanyard cut off switch to disable the motor.  The victim's body was recovered 2 days later .66 mile South of where his boat was intially found.

Two females and one male were operating a raft on the Vermilion River in LaSalle County.  They failed to navigate the bypass at the Buzzi Cement low head dam and went over it.  They were caught in the boil.  Two of the victims escaped but the third drowned.  They were all transported to IVCH.  The two survivors were treated for hypothermia and released.

The two men were on board a Hobie Wave sailboat that capsized and both men were thrown into the water.  Due to a cardia arrhythmia, one died and fell overboard.  With the weight not being on board, it may have been enough for the wind to capsize the boat, causing the operator to fall off; or,  the boat may have capsized, causing both men to fall overboard.  While in the water the passenger may have had cardiac arrhythmia and died.

The victim was on board a 17ft bass boat with one unknown male subject.   It was reported that the operator and passenger both fell out of the boat, going underwater and disappearing.   The operator's body was found floating down river by divers.  The other unknown subject has yet to be found.  What caused the men to fall out of the boat is undetermined.  Cause of death of operator was determined to be drowning.

The passenger of the vessel stated that she left the vessel to swim and the operator followed her.  While they were swimming, the vessel drifted away.  The passenger was able to swim to the boat and climb aboard.  She could not see the operator in the water.  The passenger had a bac of .18 and stated the operator had as much to drink, maybe more.  The operator's body was recovered southeast of where the vessel had been located in about two feet of water.

There were 3 passengers and the operator on the boat along with miscellaneous equipment.  One passenger was seated in the front of the boat holding a portable generator.  There was also a trolling monitor (including foot remote), marine battery, fishing poles and anchor secured inside the bow.  They were en route back to a marina and attempting to beat an approaching storm when the water became rough.  As they exited a cove into the main body of the lake, they encountered rough waves generated by wind.  The waves entered over the bow of the boat adding additional weight to the front of the boat (weight of water 8.34 lbs/gal).  The additional weight caused the bow to become submerged and the forward momentum of the boat continued to drive the bow beneath the water.  The passengers and operator were immediately pushed back by the oncoming water.  Weight transfer within the boat from unsecured items, passenger movement and oncoming water caused the boat to capsize to the starboard side.  The passengers and occupants entered the water as the boat capsized and partially sunk.  The bottom of the outboard motor and only a small portion of the transom were exposed above the waterline.  Two of the passengers swam to shore, one passenger wearing a life jacket was pushed away from the scene by wind, and the operator subsequently became unresponsive and slipped beneath the waterline.  The operator and passenger were recovered from the water and attempts to revive the operator were unsuccessful.

The victim stated to a friend that he was going fishing on the pond.  He left his truck at the friend's residence.  Later that night, the friend noticed the victim had not returned and notified the authorities.  Attempts to locate the victim were unsuccessful that night and the search resumed the next day.  The victim's fishing equipment was found floating and the canoe was found capsized.  A short time later, the body was recovered fully clothed and wearing a pair of hip wading boots.  Autopsy reports indicate the victim drowned.  The only other injury was a slight laceration to his head.

It was concluded that the canoe the victim was fishing from was a very unstable platform.  Any movement left or right of the center would have caused the canoe to become susceptible to capsizing.  The victim is believed to have fallen overboard after the canoe he was fishing from capsized.  The hip wading boots he was wearing likely restricted his ability to swim and prevented him from making it to shore.  The victim was not wearing a lifejacket.
location: Cook County Forest Preserve Po, IL

description: The occupant stated that she and her father (victim) motored over to a spot to fish and dropped anchor approximately 30 feet from shore.  She felt the boat start to rock and she grabbed onto the sides of the boat.  She looked back and all she saw was the bottom of her dad's shoes before they hit the water.  She nor her father were wearing a life jacket at the time of the accident.  She yelled for help and two nearby boats came to assist.  One boat pulled the victim's boat to shore.  The other boat operator dove into the water attempting to find the victim.  The body was recovered at 9:00 p.m. by Wayne City dive team.  The victim had a history of seizures.  The cause of death was determined to be drowning.
location: Sam Dale State Park Lake, IL

description:
The men were fishing in a tournament scheduled from 5:15 p.m. to 8:15 p.m. .  At around 7:40 p.m, the operator was continuing to fish but was unresponsive to questions from the occupant.  Approximately 5 minutes later, the operator put down his fishing pole without securing it, put up the trolling motor, took a step back and fell of the port side of the boat with his head down, face first into the water.  The occupant stated that the victims arms and feet did not raise and he went straight down into the water.  The occupant wen to the port side of the boat and jumped in after the victim.  He felt the victim's shirt but before he could grab it the CO2 inflated in the personal flotation device he was wearing and took him to the surface.  The occupant looked for the victim a few more times, then called 911 from his water-proof cell phone.  He also called other fisherman to help look for the victim.  The victim was not wearing a pfd.  It was on the passenger's seat of the vessel.  The body was recoved a few hours after the accident face down in 8 feet of water with both arms "locked" near his chest.

Coroner's report received with cause of death listed as "pending investigation" on 10/16/09.

The operator of the boat stated that he was trying to set the anchor in the current behind a dike.  The passenger had already thrown out his fishing poles and was seated on the port side off the port quarter of the boat next to the driver seat.  The operator stepped up to the bow of the boat on the decking to try and adjust the anchor which appeared to be stuck in some brush.  He pulled twice on the anchor which was secured to the aft-starboard side of the boat to a cleat.  The boat rocked towards the port side of the boat causing the operator to fall down on the bow of the boat facing aft.  When he looked up, the operator saw the passenger in the water hanging onto the port side of the boat with his left arm only and his head slumped on the left shoulder.  The operator tried to pull the passenger back into the boat but on the third attempt, the operator fell into the water head first over the passenger off the port side of the boat.  The operator surfaced after falling in and was approximately 20 feet downstream of the passenger.  The passenger was wearing a life jacket and thrashing around in the water.  The operator swam back to the boat and retrieved a life jacket for himself.  He swam back to the passenger who was unconscious and face down in the water.  The operator rolled the passenger over and began swimming with him to shore.   The operator yelled for help for approximately 30 minutes before someone heard him to send help.  The deceased victim had Parkinson's Disease and had recently had a pacemaker installed that he was having trouble with.

The victim and a friend were fishing from a semi-v jon boat on a private lake.  The victim was attempting to pull up the anchor from the stern of the boat.  He "jerked" the line up and the boat capsized.  No pfd's were on board the boat.  The passenger was able to hold on to a floating log, but the operator drowned before his friend could reach him.  The dive team recoved the body in 12-15 feet of water approximately 10 feet west of where the vessel capsized.

August 2, 2009 at 1635 hrs. I received report via Dispatch of a child in the water- unable to find- at Roush Reservoir, beach side of the Dam.
8-2-2009, North Region notified, additional ICO unit requested.
8-2-2009, 1646 hrs.- I and Reserve Deputy arrived at beach area- The incident was not at that location. 
8-2-2009, 1647 hrs. -Was advised  that location was at South boat ramp- began to drive to that location along with other responders, including EMS. 
8-2-2009, 1704 hrs - Sheriff's dispatch advised location to be Kilsoquah boat ramp (North ramp). All responders then went to that location.
8-2-2009, 1710 hrs- Arrived at Kilsoquah ramp with all units. Child was on ground near boat mooring area. CPR was underway by family members. First Responders from Huntington County Rescue, then EMS (Medic 82, # 0046) from Huntington Parkview took over. CPR continued throughout.
I noted that the victim displayed a red appearance that is not indicitive of drowning incidents. This caused me to look further into what might have occurred.
 Parkview Samaritan helicopter EMS arrived and later transported victim to Parkview Hospital main unit, Fort Wayne.
8-2-2009, 1715 hrs- At location- assisted in gathering information.
8-2-2009, 1800 hrs.- Boat IN7959DA removed from the water and inspected by me, ICO 1, and EMS from Parkview Huntington.
8-2-2009, 1815 hrs- Preliminary information given to Lt.
8-2-2009, 1830 hrs- Scene cleared.
8-2-2009, 1830 hrs- Preliminary report given to North Region and ICO 2.
8-2-2009, 2000 hrs.- Parkview Hospital advised Victim 1 was condition "very, very critical"
8-3-2009, 0930 hrs- Condition unchanged, child in Pediatric ICU, Room 1227, bed 1.
8-3-2009, 1230 hrs- ICO 2 reported being advised by Coroner office, -  that Victim 1 is deceased. Autopsy to be 8-4-2009.
Investigation-
     Operator1 reported that she was operating Owner 1 boat eastbound from about the beach area to about the County Road 200 E  bridge. She reported that she was operating at "trolling"  speed. During this time Victim 1 was on a wooden swim platform off of the stern of the boat along with four other children. At about the location of the bridge crossing  Operator 1 was told that Victim 1 had "slipped off the back of the boat". A water search was immediately begun and "911" called. Operator 1 reported that the child was recovered from the water within about a minute, whereupon CPR was initiated and they started toward the boat ramp in the boat while continuing CPR and continuing to call "911" with the location. Operator1 further reported that Victim 1 had been sleeping while on the swim platform and had suffered a headache and upset stomach. I explained to Operator1 that is was very dangerous and not legal to allow passengers to ride on the swim platform or anywhere outside of the passenger area.
     Owner 1 (boat owner, and witness) reported that "the kids ride on the back all the time". "We've never had any trouble". He supported the report of Operator 1 as to the circumstances of the incident.  I told Owner 1 that allowing persons to be on the platform was illegal and extremely dangerous.
     Witness 1 (Victim's father and witness) had the same account of the circumstances, except that he told me Victim 1 had been feeling ill before getting on the boat. He reported that Victim 1 was "asleep" while on the swim platform.
     Other children had been on the swim platform . One of the children appeared to be more red in color than normal. All of the adults were told by me to get the children checked for possible carbon monoxide exposure. Huntington City Police Sgt. Foster also called the family on a cell phone while they were enroute to the hospital and advised them to have the children checked.
     The boat involved is inboard, prop. propulsion, ski boat, dual through stern hull.

On 8/29/09 I was dispatched by north region enforcement to respond to a possible drowning at the Mississinewa reservoir red bridge ramp area.  I arrived at approximately 5:34pm and was soon joined by units from the county sheriffs dept, red cross, city south fire dept. Ambulance, and numerous other ICO units from surrounding counties.  I spoke with deputies Deputy 1 and Deputy 2 who were the first units on scene and they advised me that the victim had apparently fell overboard while positioning himself near the back of the boat in preparation to go tubing according to the witnesses.  The four remaining occupants of the boat  were seated next to their boat.  I was advised by Deputy 2 that the witnesses had attempted to locate the victim for several minutes before going back to the red bridge ramp to summon help.  Deputy 2 advised me the witnesses stated they had thrown the victim the tube first and Victim 1 was unable to grab it.  Two of the occupants (Occupant 1 and Occupant 2) then swam after Victim 1 however the ensuing struggle caused Victim 1 to begin pushing them under so they had to return to the boat.  They then threw life jackets at him but Victim 1 had drifted too far away to reach them.  Victim 1 then slipped under the surface and was not seen again.  
ICO’s and I took two of the witnesses separately out with us to pinpoint a location of the drowning.  Both subjects (Occupant 2 and Occupant 1) pinpointed an area approximately 250 yards east of the Mississinewa road bridge near the south shore.  
    I advised the three ICO units that had responded to run the side scan sonar boat of the location which we had subsequently marked with buoy.  Lt.  headed up the sonar boat.  ICO divers bollman and neargardner were in my boat with rescue diver ICO reed.  As we were conducting recovery operations, detective randy Detective 1 of the co. Sheriffs dept. Took the four witnesses back to his dept. And interviewed each one separately.  
     Officer Deputy 2 also administered portable breath tests to all the occupants just prior to detective 1 taking them to the jail for interviews and he advised me that the only one that tested positive was  .07%.  I was advised by Lt. that they had a good mark with the sonar and they had marked it with a buoy.  ICOs then made the recovery of the victim at 8:06pm.  The exact GPS coordinates of the body were as follows: 40* 40' 801n by 85*52'991w.  ICO advised the victim was in 34' of water and the temperature at the bottom was 70'.  The victim was then remanded into the care of the coroner and one of her deputies and the victim was transported to the hospital by the city fire dept. Ambulance.  
     All ICO units then had a post incident briefing and the scene was cleared.  I then went to the sheriffs dept. To speak with detective 1.  While enroute I was advised by ICO  that notification had been made to the victims' wife by the marion city pd chaplain  who we had summoned for help in finding her as none of the witnesses knew where to find her.  Detective 1 stated that he did not feel foul play was involved and all the witnesses seemed genuinely upset at the death of Victim 1.  Detective 1 had conducted personal interviews at length with each of the remaining boat occupants and I will supplement this case with detective 1s report as soon as I come into possession of it.  
     Detective 1 and I then went to the hospital to talk with the coroner and view the body once again.  Preliminary blood tests had been conducted and I was advised by the deputy coroner that no drugs were found in Victim 1's system and there was a minimal indication of alcoholic beverage in his system.  Victim 1's wife came to the hospital and identified the body and she stated that he could swim.  A complete autopsy was performed on 8/30/09 at 2:30pm

On 10/25/09, I Conservation Officer was contacted by Dispatch and informed of a personal watercraft accident that had occurred on the Maumee River in Allen County.  I was able to depart for the accident scene at approximately 1730, and arrived on scene at approximately 1800.  Already at the scene were Indiana Conservation Officer District 2 Lieutenant, Indiana Conservation Officer  1, Indiana Conservation Officer Investigation Section Sgt. 1, the Fort Wayne City Police Department, Fort Wayne Fire and Rescue, and the Allen County Coroner.  When I arrived on scene, I was informed that the victim, Victim 1 and his friend, Operator 2 were riding their jet skis down the Maumee River.  Victim 1 was riding about 40 yards ahead of Operator 2, and attempted to pass under the Tecumseh Street bridge.  As Victim 1passed under the bridge traveling 30 to 40 miles per hour, he hit a steel cable that the Pioneer Associates construction crew had left strung between the pillars of the bridge 34.5 inches above the surface of the water.  He was flipped off of the jet ski and fell into the water.  He died instantly from the trauma of the cable hitting his neck. 
      I then got into a boat with the Ft. Wayne Fire Department and the Allen County Coroner’s Office and went to the center bay of the three bay bridge where the accident happened.  We could see nothing in the water, on the cable, or on the front of the bridge that marked the area as a construction zone, or the cable as being a hazard.  We were able to identify exactly where Victim 1hit the cable by a piece of blue cloth from his life jacket that was stuck on the cable.  We measured from the surface of the water to the cable, and got a reading of 34.5 inches.  Deputy Coroner took several pictures of the bridge, and the cable.  There were also cables strung across the bay to the north, that had a barge tied to it, and a second cable in the middle bay, that was mostly under water, and out of the way of the jet skis.  The only bay that did not have a cable was the South Bay, but that bay was partially blocked by a floating log, and would appear to be unpassable to boaters. We marked the cable with several pieces of white cloth to prevent any further accidents that night, and returned to shore.  The fire department then towed the jet ski that Victim 1was riding back to the Johnny Appleseed Park Boat Ramp, where his truck was parked.  The jet ski was loaded onto the trailer, and hooked to Lt. 1's truck, and then taken to the District 2 post and locked inside.   Operator 2 was interviewed at the scene by Detective Sgt. 1, then escorted by Officer 1 back to Albion to make the notification of death to Victim 1's wife.  
     Sgt. 1 and I went to the residence of Witness 1 and Witness 2, who were on a putting green next to the river, and witnessed the accident.  They said that they had looked at the construction on the bridge and discussed it before the jet skis came down the river, and never saw the cables strung across the water.  They said that the cables were not marked in any way.   They said that they were putting and heard the two men coming down the river.  They turned to see what was coming, and watched Victim 1drive into the cable.  Witness 2 said that she heard the sound of something getting tight, like a twang, and saw Victim 1flip backward off of the jet ski and land face down in the water.  She said that Operator 2 then stopped and pulled up beside Victim 1and pulled him to shore.  She then ran to a STS Security car that was parked on top of the bridge and used his phone to call 911.  She said that emergency personnel arrived within 5 minutes of her making the call.  Witness 1 said that he ran down to the bank where Operator 2 and Victim 1were, and held on to Operator 2 as he tried to pull Victim 1onto the steep bank.  Victim 1was already deceased

On February 3, 2009, I received a call at my home from Officer 1 who reported to me that he was goose hunting on Turtle Creek Reservoir.  He further stated that he was in need of my assistance with my patrol boat because there was an overturned boat on the lake and that there were several people in the water.  While I was responding to the scene to assist Officer 1, he and Officer 2 were able to rescue one of the occupants of the overturned boat.  This victim was one Victim 1.  This person was treated at the scene for mild hypothermia, and transported to a local hospital.  

		When I arrived at the reservoir and was preparing my boat for launch, a second victim was recovered by Officer 1 and other volunteers.  This victim was Victim 2.  When Officer 1 arrived at the boat ramp with the second victim, the victim was unconscious and unresponsive.  He was immediately placed in the care of EMS personnel on scene and was transported to a nearby hospital.  We were advised a short time later that he had been pronounced dead.  An investigation was initiated into the apparent drowning death of one Victim 2.  

Details of Investigation:
		On February 3, 3009, at approximately 0651 hours, I received a phone call from  Officer 1 on my mobile phone.  I was at my residence when I received the phone call.  Officer 1 advised me that he was at Turtle Creek Reservoir.  There was an obvious stress in his voice, and I had a hard time hearing him due to winds in the background.  Officer 1 told me that he was on Turtle Creek Reservoir and was attempting to locate an overturned boat that he believed was occupied by several goose hunters.  He requested that I respond to the reservoir with my patrol boat.  He further stated that he and Officer 2 were going to attempt to located the downed hunters.

		I immediately got dressed and retrieved my patrol boat from my garage.  The weather outside at this time was very foul with heavy snowfall and sharp north winds.  The blowing snow caused drifting in front of my garage where I store my patrol boat and forced me to dig the snow out around the garage door, before I could remove my boat.  Once the snow was removed, I retrieved my boat and headed toward Turtle Creek Reservoir.  I advised the SCSD via mobile radio that I was en route to the reservoir.  The time was approximately 0715 hours.

		At approximately 0738 hours, while en route to the reservoir, I attempted to contact Officer 2 and Officer 1 by telephone to get an update on the situation.  Roadways at this time were extremely dangerous, with high winds and blowing snow that reduced visibility to near zero.  With my boat in tow, I could only drive about 35-40 mph safely.  A short time later, I spoke to Officer 2 on the phone again.  This time, he advised me that he and Officer 1 had recovered one of the victims in the boat and that he was being treated by EMS, who were on the scene.  Officer 2 advised me that conditions were not favorable for any type of dive detail to recover the second victim if necessary.  I contacted South Region Headquarters by radio and asked them to send additional units to assist us.

		I arrived at the main boat ramp at Turtle Creek Reservoir at approximately 0740 hours.  I immediately met with Officer 2 who was standing by near the check station.  Officer 2 told me that Officer 1 was still on the water in another boat attempting to locate the second victim, with the assistance of several other goose hunters that were there to hunt that morning.  Officer 2 told me that the overturned boat had 2 people on board.  Officer 2 then assisted me in preparing my boat for launch at the Turtle Creek ramp.  I also prepared my side-scan sonar unit for use in the recovery.  Weather conditions were still very poor as the blowing snow was causing a 'white out', and it was beginning to show daylight.

Operator and Occupant 1 had borrowed a canoe from Owner 1 and put in at 106th ST. It was approximately 2:00 PM. They canoed down river to the area of Owner 1's home and were going to take out there. As they approached, there was a tree limb extending out, over and into the water from the side of the bank. They tried to go between the river bank and the limb, but the bow went into the limb and was forced down. The boat then pivoted so that it was perpendicular to the current. The water started to come in over the up river side and the canoe capsized. Both subjects went into the water. The subjects had been sitting on their PFDs and not wearing them. They both were able to grab hold of the canoe, but hypothermia was quickly affecting them. Occupant 1 told Operator “We have to make it to shore” As she started for shore she heard him call for help and she told him to “push through” Operator again called for help as she  got to shore. Occupant 1 could see he was free of the boat, possibly with the bow rope in his hand.
	Occupant 1 got onto the bank and started to disrobe. She was wearing silk undershirt, wool sweater & jacket, long johns and sweat pants. She was having trouble with buttons, but finally got her jacket off. She called for help, called for victim and then ran up the hill to Owner 1's home. This is where they had planned to take out.
	Owner 1 heard what he thought was a dog barking and looked out his window to see the canoe and an object go floating down river. He then realized it was someone calling for help. He ran outside, found out what happened, called 911 and slid his PWC into the river. Owner 1 went down river to the canoe but did not find Operator. Owner 1 made four to five trips between his home and the canoe without finding the victim. He returned to his home to get some heavier clothing. He made three to four more trips to the canoe and back without find Operator. Owner 1 did pull the canoe out onto the shore.
	Operator was wearing a black fleece cap, rain coat, red plaid pants, and leather hiking boots. According to his father he was not a strong swimmer. Occupant 1 stated they did not have any drugs or alcohol. They had been snacking on trail mix, fruit & cheese. 
	The Indianapolis Fire Department arrived and conducted a boat search of the area, but was unable to locate the victim. IMPD flew over the river with a spotlight & FLIR but they too were unable to locate the victim. The search was discontinued until 09:00 on 2/15/09
	On 2/15/09 I along with Officers 2, 3 and 4 put in at Lake Indy boat ramp and searched from the 16th St Bridge up river to the accident location. IFD put in their hovercraft at Lake Indy and went north. They also put two Jon boats in up by the accident site and worked south. The victim was not located by boat, so IFD put a sonar unit in the water, but did not locate anything. 
	2/16/09 Officer 5 brought his side-scan sonar and boat over from Dist. 5. He and Officer 4 worked the area of the accident. IFD had cadaver dogs come in and ride in their boats and walk the bank. They also had their urban search team walk both sides of the river down to the Michigan Rd Bridge.  Officer 2 and I did a boat search from the 16th St. Bridge to the accident site. Nothing was located by the dogs or search team, but Officer 5 did see something on sonar. A drag bar was deployed and hooked a couple of things, but not the victim.
2/17/09 I checked from the 16th St. Bridge to the site and back without success. 
Officer 2 and I checked the river on 2/25/09 and IFD checked it on 2/24/09. Officer 6 and 2 ran it on 3/9/09. All were without success.

On 5/9/2009 at 12:55 P.M. Monroe County Dispatch contacted South Region of a possible drowning at the Paynetown Ramp. I and Sgt. 1 responded to the scene. Capt. 1 was in the area and he also responded. 
It appears that the victim, Victim 1 and his wife Occupant 1 had just launched their boat. Occupant 1 backed the boat to the courtesy dock to pick up Victim 1. He stepped on the back platform and told her to go. She accelerated a little fast and Victim 1 fell off the back into the water. Occupant 1 tried to get back to him but could not get Victim 1 back in the boat. 
Good Samaritan 1 was fishing from his boat by the bank across from the courtesy dock and heard the motor rev and a splash. He then heard someone yelling for help. He saw the victim in the water and dove in and swam over to him. Good Samaritan 1 was able to get the victim back to the shore by his boat. He was trying to get him out of the water when Good Samaritan 2 and Good Samaritan 3, who were camping just above the scene, arrived to help. They too had heard the calls for help. Good Samaritan 2 helped Good Samaritan 1 get the victim out of the water. Good Samaritan 3, who is a nurse, another camped by the name of Good Samaritan 4, an off duty Johnson County Deputy and another subject started CPR on Victim 1.  Capt. 1 arrived at the ramp and saw they were doing CPR. He went around to the campground and assisted. Bloomington Ambulance arrived and transported Victim 1 to Bloomington Hospital where he was pronounced dead.

On 4-03-09 an autopsy was performed on Victim 1. 

Present for the autopsy were ICO 1, Posey County Chief Deputy Coroner 1, Posey County Deputy Coroner 2 and I. Assisting with the autopsy were autopsy surgeon 1 and autopsy surgeon2. 

Victim 1 was wearing a pair of leather loafers, Levis blue jeans (size 34x32), brown belt, green tee shirt and a tan zip up jacket. The green tee shirt was ripped on the left side, which was explained by Coroner 2 as having been done by the medics. Victim 1 was not wearing any underwear. 

The zipper (fly) for the blue jeans was down and during the autopsy we were informed that the victim's bladder was full. 

In the front left pocket of his blue jeans were two Bic lighters and in the left front pocket of his jacket was an open pack of Marlboro cigarettes. 

After examining the victim, autopsy surgeon 1 advised that there wasn't any evidence of external trauma. autopsy surgeon 1 did locate a small ½ cut on the victim's left thumb and a mild bruise on the inside of the victim's left knee. After the autopsy,  autopsy surgeon 1 advised that he didn't observe anything that would indicate anything other that a drowning. 

Autopsy surgeon 1 advised after the autopsy that everything was consistent with an accidental drowning. 

Blood was collected by the autopsy surgeons for the toxicology testing. 

Photographs were taken before and during the autopsy.

On 10-5-09 at approximately 20:15, I was contacted by South Region regarding a missing fisherman at Glendale Fish and Wildlife Area.  I then made contact with Daviess Co. dispatch who advised that the victim was an 84 year male with some medical problems who had gone fishing at Glendale and had not returned.
	I arrived on scene and met with Daviess Co. Deputies who had talked with family members.  According to family, they had attempted to call the victim, Victim 1, several times throughout the afternoon and evening but had got no response.  They stated that Victim 1 had been having some health problems for the last week and was very weak from flu symptoms.  They checked Victim 1's house at around 17:30 and noticed that both his truck and boat were gone.  Still not hearing from Victim 1, they then drove to Glendale and located his vehicle and trailer still parked in the parking lot.  At 20:08, they made a 911 call.
	At 21:00, ICO 1 and I launched a boat and headed toward the east end of the lake, where witnesses stated that Victim 1 fished a lot.  Other rescue units also launched and began searching the lake.  
	At approximately 21:50, we were notified by dispatch that searchers had located Victim 1's  boat in the boat shack area east of the campground cove.  The boat was anchored in 16 feet of water, but the victim was not there.  As we got to the area, we located  the victim's body floating face down approximately 50 yards from the anchored boat  (N38' 32.941/W087' 01.945).  The time of recovery was 22:04.  The temperature of the water was 64 degrees.
	At this time, we secured the victim's body in our boat and headed toward the shore.  The victim's boat was taken to shore by rescue personnel.  The victim and his boat were photographed at this time.  There were no visible external injuries to the victim and there was no sign of struggle in the boat. The victims personal items (wallet, keys, and cell phone) were given to family members.
	At approximately 23:00, Daviess County Coroner Steven Cullen arrived at the scene and examined the victim.  He declared the death as an accidental drowning.  He further stated that due to the victim's age and known health issues, he did not plan to do an autopsy.  The victim's body was taken away by ambulance.  The boat was taken to a location requested by family members.
	Rescue units on the scene included:  Daviess Co Sheriff's Dept, Indiana Conservation Officers, Harrison Twp Fire Dept., Daviess Co EMS, and several fishermen.

On 5/28/2009 this unit received a telephone call from a volunteer fire fighter with Battleground, who said that Sheffield Township and Lafayette Fire Departments where getting toned out for a possible drowning at the Fairfield Ponds.  This unit was enroute to Fairfield ponds located  in Tippecanoe County.  The Tippecanoe County dispatchers said that one person was last seen in the water trying to swim to shore when he went underwater and never resurfaced.  This unit went to the east-side of the east pond and observed 3 subjects in the water trying to locate the victim.  This unit assisted Tippecanoe County Deputy 1 with his dive gear and explained to him where the initial search was at.  This unit then helped Tippecanoe County Deputy 1 with his gear and at the time there were 4 divers in the water.  The Tippecanoe County Water Rescue Boat had arrived and Tippecanoe County Detective 2 needed another person in the boat to tend the line for the divers.  Lafayette fireman 1 made a recovery of some fishing poles that were located in the area close to where the victim was last seen and marked the spot with a marker buoy.  Tippecanoe County Deputy 3 brought his personal boat with a sonar fish finding unit on it and fellow members of the Sheffield VFD informed this unit that he had marked a black mass on the bottom of the pond with his sonar and marked it with a marker buoy.  This unit and Detective Deputy 2 got all the divers that were ready and set up the “V” pattern.  The first pass from the South to the North was unsuccessful and on the second pass from the North to the South, the divers signaled this unit that a recovery was made and we picked up the victim and transported him to shore where an ambulance was waiting.  According to the Tippecanoe County diver and Lafayette Diver the depth was around 25 feet of water where the body was recovered. On 10-18-09 at approximately 1830 hrs I, an Indiana Conservation Officer, received a telephone call from the Whitley County Sheriff's Department Dispatch advising me of a hunting accident which had just occurred on Goose Lake. Upon receiving all available information I immediately proceeded to that location. Upon my arrival the three subjects involved in the accident had just arrived back at the Public Access Site in their Canoe. One subject was unconscious and being administered CPR by emergency personnel on scene and the other two subjects were rushed inside one of the ambulances on scene in order to warm them up because they were completely wet from head to toe.
After looking over the canoe and gathering some information I interviewed both subjects inside ambulance on scene. On the following day 10-19-09 I interviewed both Operator 1 and Passenger 1 at their residences to obtain further details of the incident. While speaking with both Operator 1 and Passenger 1, they stated they had been duck and goose hunting near the southeast end of the lake in their canoe with their friend Victim 1. 
They had all met at Operator 1's house at approximately 4:00 pm on 10-18-09 and headed over to Goose Lake. After finally making it out on the water and getting their decoys set up they sat for approximately a half hour or so when Operator 1 noticed a goose swimming near shore just across the lake from them. They believed the goose was injured so decided to paddle over across the embayment and attempt to shoot the goose.
As they approached the goose it began to swim away from shore out into the lake. With the goose swimming across the water Victim 1, sitting in the front of the canoe, took a shot at the goose. Immediately after this Passenger 1, sitting in the middle seat of the canoe, also began to shoot at the goose. During the process of both men shooting at the goose multiple times, something happened causing the canoe to flip backwards resulting in all three men ending up in the water. Operator 1 stated that as both men were firing their guns he caught movement out of the corner of his eye just as the boat flipped over. He was not sure if Victim 1 had attempted to stand up or was just moving around to reposition himself to take another shot.
Once in the water all three men eventually began swimming towards shore some 30-40 yards to the south of them. Passenger 1 dropped his shotgun in the lake when he entered the water.  Because of this he was able to make it too shore first. Once on shore began talking to Victim 1 attempting to get him to calm down and swim towards shore. As Operator 1 was swimming to shore, with his shotgun still in his arms, he stopped with Victim 1 and gave him a blue boat cushion he was holding onto because Victim 1 was struggling so badly. After leaving Victim 1 he continued swimming towards shore and began struggling himself. He was able to grab a hold of his dog swimming in the water next to him and make it too within a few feet from shore. In a last ditch effort to make it into shore he was able to hold out his firearm still in his possession and allow Passenger 1 to grab onto the other end and pull him the last couple of feet into shore.
Once on shore Passenger 1 and Operator 1 began removing some of their heavy hunting clothes while at the same time talking to Victim 1 trying to calm him down and get him to shore. Once out of some of their clothes Passenger 1 swam back out into the lake and to retrieve the canoe. Operator 1 walked out onto the end of a downed tree along the shoreline of the lake and began trying to help Victim 1 make it the rest of the way into shore. Victim 1 was still holding onto the boat cushion as well as his firearm as he was attempting to make it too shore. At some point he did drop his firearm into the lake but remained holding onto the boat cushion. 
As Victim 1 made it closer to shore he continued struggling. Once almost into shore Operator 1 was finally able to make his way far enough out onto the downed tree in the water that he was able to reach out and grab Victim 1.

On December 10, 2009 I, Indiana Conservation Officer was called by Officer 1 to assist with a missing person on Winona Lake. The missing person was reported initially to Warsaw Police Department early in the morning. 

I met Officer 1 at the Kosciusko county fairgrounds boat ramp. The winds were high out of the west-southwest. The temperature was ~ 7 degrees Fahrenheit with slight cloud cover. Fog was lifting from the lake water making visibility somewhat difficult. At 0755 we launched the 16' Jon boat to begin the search for the boat and missing individual. At approximately 0820 I received information from Warsaw city officer on the contact information of the caller of the missing person.

At 0832 Officer 1 called me to advise he discovered a capsized aluminum V-bottom style boat ~50 yards from the shore on the north east portion of Winona lake.

At 0837 I called a Reporter 1 to get descriptors of her husband and the boat. I asked her if her missing husband, Victim 1, had any possible friends that he may have went to visit. She said, "there was no one that she could think of he would visit at that time of night". She said that Victim 1 "liked to take lake cruises at night and it was not unusual for him to go out". She said she thought he would be wearing tennis shoes, carhart style outer clothing and a face mask. She said that they were getting along fine and that she knew of no problems, personal or financial, that would cause for suspicious behavior. She said he was employed with the Times Union. She described his boat as a "silver jon boat with a small tiller motor". She was not sure of the make of the boat. She said she thought he left around midnight because she woke at 2AM and the boat was gone but his truck was still in the drive. She woke again at 4AM and he was still not home and she called into the Kosciusko dispatch to report him missing. 

Officer 1 came back to shore and around 0850. At ~0900, a fairgrounds maintenance employee discovered a face down human body along the north shore of the lake just south of the county fairgrounds. The individual was wearing camo rubber knee boots and brown hooded heavy-style coveralls. Photos of the body were taken and I contacted dispatch to advise the county coroner. Times Union photographer  was present and took photos as well. Times Union supervisor, was present also and both were not positive but almost definite that the face down body was Victim 1. I contacted Warsaw PD detective 1, who was with Reporter 1 and ICO detective 2, whom at that time were conducting an interview with Reporter 1. I advised Detective 1 that we had found a body along the shore.  We checked the body for a wallet but were unable to find one on the subject through the ice on the clothing. Officer 1 had to break formed ice around the legs of the body in order to move him. Officer 1 and I were able to roll the body over to try and get a positive ID from the times union photographer. He was able to determine that it was Victim 1. Warsaw PD chief also was able to ID the body as Victim 1. 

ICO's 1 and 2 were able to retrieve the capsized aluminum boat and return it to shore. I ran a license check through North Region Law Enforcement of its registration numbers. They read 360 SW. The return came back as a 1977 aluminum make unknown boat and the registered owner being a Victim 1. The boat was loaded by Crouse wrecker service and delivered to Warsaw PD for temporary storage for Reporter 1.

On 5/24/09, Victim 1 had called Landowner 1, the landowner of the pond, and asked if he could drive into the property and go fishing.  The pond  is enrolled into the Fishing Impoundments and Stream Habitats program within The Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks.  Victim 1, the victim, Passenger 1, witness, Passenger 2, witness and Passenger 3, witness, were using a 12 ft. flatbottom boat with a trolling motor attached to the stern to check a trout line in the pond at approximately 2:30 a.m.  The boat began to fill with water and then the boat capsized and all four individuals went into the water.  Victim 1climbed on the capsized boat and Passenger 1 began to pull the boat toward shore.  Victim 1slipped off the boat back into the water.  Passenger 2 tried to help Victim 1back into the boat but was unable to because Victim 1grabbed her and started to pull her under water.  Passenger 2 fought off Victim 1from pulling her under the water and made it to shore.  When Passenger 1, Passenger 2 and Passenger 3 made it to shore with the boat they thought that Victim 1had been holding onto the boat. At approximately 2230 hours I was contacted by NRO in Brown County.  NRO advised me that he believed there had been a drowning in Nemaha County earlier in the evening.  NRO  advised that Brown County dispatch had contacted him reference the event.  I ended my conversation with NRO and contacted Nemaha County Sheriff’s Office.  Dispatch put me in contact with one of the deputies at the scene.  The deputy advised that a person had possibly drowned in a farm pond approximately ½ miles south the intersection of 116th road and V rd.  I advised Nemaha County I would be enroute to the location to assist in anyway that I could.  

At approximately 1145 hours I arrived on scene and made contact with Sheriff.  Sheriff advised me that he believed that Victim 1 had possibly drowned in the farm pond.  Sheriff advised me Victim 1’s boat was capsized and that no one had seen Victim 1 since earlier in the afternoon.  While speaking with Sheriff, Brown County Rescue Squad towed the small flat bottom boat to shore.  Sheriff asked if I would be willing to help drag for the body.  I advised that I would assist in the dragging for the victim.  

At approximately midnight we started dragging for the body.  I advised the operator of the boat that I wanted to concentrate on a small area where the boat had been located before the rescue squad had removed it.  Approximately 0035 hours I caught a small portable fish finder from the bottom of the pond.  I advised the operator of the boat to continue going back and forth in the area where we had located the fish finder.  At approximately 0045 hours I was able to catch Victim 1 and bring his body to the surface of the pond.  Once his body was on the surface of the pond I held onto the body by holding onto the victims’ sweatshirt.  I advised the operator of the boat to back slowly toward the shore where we would remove the hook and then remove the body from the water.  

Once we made it to the shore emergency personnel removed the body from the water and placed the body in a body bag.  During this time it was noted that the hook had snagged on the right thigh of the victim.  A knife was used to cut loose the hook from the victim’s denim jeans.  

After the body was removed from the scene Sheriff and I looked the boat over for damage.  The boat was a 14 foot flat bottom jon boat, the boat had a tiller style 7.5 horse power Mercury motor attached to the transom.  The throttle had been broken off and was lying in the boat.  When the boat was retrieved it was drug completely onto shore with the motor dragging on the bottom. During this time the transom and motor would have been dragging on the bottom which was consistent with the tiller handle being broken off of the boat.  Upon further inspection it was found that the gear shift was in a forward position, which is not consistent with a boat being pulled to shore.  One possible explanation is that the victim could have been operating the boat motor, tried to turn too sharp and possibly overturned the boat.  This would be consistent with someone that had just purchased the boat and was unfamiliar with how the boat would handle when the boat was under power.  It was noted that the victim had purchased the boat the day before and had spent the morning of the incident working on the boat.  No life jackets were located at the scene.

On July 18, 2009 Operator 1(DOB 4/11/40) and Passenger 1 (DOB 2/28/25) drove to Passenger 1's property in Greenwood County to go fishing at a farm pond. Passenger 1 is a paraplegic and in a wheelchair. Operator 1said that this was the fourth time he had brought Passenger 1 out to fish at the pond.
Operator 1 loaded Passenger 1 onto a 12' x 4' Hilltop Pontoon boat by using a cement slab and a metal ramp. Operator 1and Passenger 1 started fishing at approximately 5:30 pm. Operator 1said that he had only operated this boat four time and no other boat. Operator 1was wearing his PFD because he did not know how to swim. Passenger 1 would not wear a PFD. Operator 1said that there was no alcohol involved because neither of them drank.
They were anchored in the pond and decided to move to another location to continue fishing. Operator 1 looked at his watch and it showed 7:30 pm. As Operator 1leaned over to pull up the anchor he saw water coming into the boat and saw that Passenger 1 was also leaning over. The boat capsized dumping both men into the water. Operator 1said that Passenger 1 was approximately twenty feet away from the overturned boat trying to swim. Operator 1yelled at Passenger 1 to try and get a hold of the boat. Operator 1grabbed the anchor line to hold onto and tried to swim to shore using one arm.
Operator 1 saw that the wheelchair was lodged under the boat and kicked at it several times to dislodge it because he knew that it would be a drag on the boat. Operator 1said that he could not kick the wheelchair lose. Operator 1then looked for Passenger 1 and saw that he was face down in the water. Operator 1was wore out and stopped to rest, holding onto the line. Operator 1would swim, pulling the boat, stop and rest. Operator 1repeated this several times before he was able to touch the bottom of the pond with his feet. Operator 1then let go of the anchor rope and made it onto the north shore of the pond. Operator 1said that it took him almost a hour to get out of the water.
Operator 1walked across the dam to where the vehicle was parked. Operator 1's cell phone would not work because of being under water so long. Operator 1proceeded to drive the approximately ten (10) miles back to Johnson's General Store in Eureka where a clerk at 8:44 pm called E911 to report the accident. An ambulance transported Operator 1to the Greenwood County Hospital to be checked out. Operator 1said that Johnson's General Store was the only place he knew about.
The first rescue squad reached the pond at 8:59 pm . Passenger 1 was pulled from the pond at 9:22 pm. EMS personnel detected a pulse and CPR was started. Passenger 1 was transported to the Greenwood County Hospital where he was pronounced deceased at 10:07 pm.
