Two occupants were transported to the Pointe Coupee General Hospital, one was released with moderate injuries and the other was in critical condition with severe head injuries.  Vessel 2 had 4 occupants on board.  Three of the four were fatally ejected from the vessel.  One passenger was not ejected and had no injuries.  After impact the occupants of vessel 1 donned PFD's and the survivor of vessel 2 grabbed two PFD's and a whistle as the vessel he was in began to sink.  Alcohol beverage containers were found on both vessels.  Wildlife Agents met the operator of vessel 1 at the hospital and advised him of his rights concerning a chemical test.  operatorA refused to submit to the blood test, however due to the fatalities and injuries agents were able to obtain a blood sample.  The sample was sent to the Louisiana State Police Crime Lab.

Vessel #1 LA 5294 AM was traveling north in Grand River when according to a witness who saw them pass earlier, stated heard a noise then saw the vessel had sunk and water splashing.  The area where the incident occurred has a lot of downed trees in the water.  Two men that were in the vessel were later identified.  Both men were not wearing PFD's and their body's were recovered from the water.  There were no impacts marks on the vessel or motor to show if anything was hit.

Operator was traveling north in Lake Misere.  Operator had one (1)  passenger onboard.  While Operator was traveling, on step, he ran his vessel through a large tree top.  This submerged tree had several large branches protruding 10' to 15' above the waterline.  This collision caused Operator to be thrown from the vessel.  The vessel then traveled west, and stopped.  Operator swam back to the vessel and did not see Victim.  He began looking for him and returned to the camp for help.  When he got back to the camp, he realized Victim was in the vessel, unresponsive.  They began CPR on victim, and another subject drove the vessel to Gary's Landing.  Victim was pronounced dead, at the landing.  Victim was wearing his PFD, but Operator was not.  The ignition safety switch was not used.  Operator was given a intoxilyzer test, for the presence of alcohol, and had a result of .087g% BAC.

     Charges have been filed w/the Cameron Parish D.A. office - Wreckless operation of a water craft, DWI, and  Vehicular Homocide.   Citation # D504672.

this incident was a single vessel collision.  The evidence indicated that a 16 foot aluminum hull Weldcraft flat boat powered by a 50 hp Mercury outboard at or near full power crashed straight into the downstrream-midstream concrete bridge pillar at the La. Hwy. 494 crossing on Cane River Lake.  Evidence indicates that Victim (not wearing a PFD) was a passenger in the boat and was thrown from the boat at initial impact.  Victim sustained severe injuries and drowned.  the operator of the boat sustained severe injuries.  Investigators believe the initial impact stopped the boat immediately throwing Operator into the steering console which prevented his ejection from the boat, and severly injured his pelvic area.  The bridge exhibits evidence of a second less violent collision at the downstream west bank pillar.  The boat exhibits evidence of a second less violent collision on its port side near the stern.  Operator was found out of the boat sitting in the water under the bridge near the west bank.  Operator was in close proximity to the boat at this location.  Neither PFD's nor kill switch lanyard were utilized.  There was no evidence of equipment failure.  Investigators believe both Victim and Operator were impaired by alcohol.  The accident occurred at night.  The bridge was not marked with lights or reflectors.

On May 21, 2009, Wildlife Agents were notified of an accident that happened sometime between approximately 9:00 pm and 9:00 am on Falgoust Canal near Dularge.  Agents arrived on scene and found a single vessel, LA1036FK, had collided with two barges that were tied togetther on the north side of the canal.  It appeared that the vessel was heading west in Falgoust Canal toward Dularge when they collided with the northern most barge. The vessel was occupied by 5 subjects.  All 5 subjects were discovered at approximately 9:00 am by two of the workers for the barge company.All 5 subjects were found deceased. Four of the subjects were trapped in the vessel that was partially submerged under the barge.  The fifth  subject was located on the top of the barge. Judging by the blood stains on the side of the barge, it appeared that the subject was able to climb onto the barge after colliding with it. Agents noticed that there were several full beer cans and several open beer cans throughout the vessel and near the scene of the accident. None of the subjects were wearing personal floatation devices.  The accident is under investigation until results are returned from the coroner's office concerning chemical tests.

The two subjects were on the water at anchor and fishing.  There was a storm coming and they were attempting to pull anchor and go into the landing.  Lightning struck the vessel.  The survivor, Operator 1, was knocked to the floor of the vessel and Occupant 1, the decreased, was still sitting in the pedestal chair on the bow of the vessel.  A moment later Operator 1 observed Occupant 1 collapse from the pedestal seat into the water.  Occupant 1 was wearing his P.F.D. and was floating near the boat.  Operator 1 was not wearing his P.F.D. and went into the water to assist Occupant 1.  Another vessel came to their aid and brought them back to the landing.  Occupant 1 was airlifted back to Lake Charles and was pronounced dead on arrival.
location: Old Black Bayou near ICW, LA

description: ON AUGUST 24, 2009 AT APPROX. 6:20P.M., OPERATOR 1 WAS STANDING ON THE FRONT DECK OF VESSEL LA-2145-EY AS IT FREELY DRIFTED IN THE AMITE DIVERSION CANAL IN ACSCENSION PARISH. OPERATOR 1 WAS THROWING A 6 FOOT CAST NET ATTEMPTING TO CATCH BAIT FISH WHEN HE FELL OVERBOARD INTO THE WATER. OPERATOR 1 NEVER RESURFACED, NEVER ATTEMPTED TO RE-ENTER THE VESSEL AND SUBSEQUENTLY DROWNED.

On August 15, 2009 at approximately 8:15 PM vessel LA-0421-YY, departed from the main Indian Creek Reservoir boat launch.  The vessel had six occupants on board including himself.  The boat began to take on water over the bow as he manuevered a turn causing the vessel to capsize.  All six people entered the water as it over turned.  Two local boaters quickly assisted with retrieving five of the six people over board onto their vessel but operator was last seen in the water after the vessel capsized.  The vessel was equipped with three personal floatation devices.  Operator’s two year old son was the only person in the boat wearing a pfd.

THE VESSEL OPERATOR 1 WAS LAST SEEN IN WAS FOUND ADRIFT IN THE VARATARIA WATERWAY NEAR CHANNEL MARKER #8.  THE VESSEL WAS UNOCCUPIED WITH THE ENGINE OFF AND IN THE UP POSITION. THE ALUMINUM CONSULE WAS IN THE WATER AND WAS ATTACHED TO THE VESSEL ONLY BY THE STEERING CABLE.  OPERATOR 1 WAS LAST SEEN IN THE VESSEL AT APPROXIMATELY 12 NOON.  THE VESSEL WAS FOUND UNOCCUPIED AT APPROXIMATELY 12:30 P.M.  THE INVESTIGATION IS ONGOING. THE SEARCH FOR OPERATOR 1 WILL CONTINUE ON 09/28/09.

Operator 1 was operating his vessel on the Houston River.  Operator 1 was not wearing a personal flotation device, nor was he wearing the safety cutoff lanyard.  Operator 1 fell overboard and drowned.  During the autopsy, the coroner observed a strong odor of an alcoholic beverage coming from the body.  Final results of this investigative summary are pending based on the results of the toxicology report.  Toxicology results along with the Coroner's report were received on October 22, 2009.   The results indicated that Operator 1 had a blood alcohol concentration of .20 grams percent.

 Sheriff's Office was on the scene and had moved both vessel and body prior to our arrival.  Some information concerning the vessel was uncertain and therefore not recorded on report form.

THE OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 WAS DROPPED OFF AT THE WESTWEGO BOAT LAUNCH BY HIS BROTHER . HE LAUNCHED HIS VESSEL AND TRAVELED SOUTH IN BAYOU SEGNETTE.  AT APPROXIMATELY 12:00 NOON, HE WAS LAST SEEN BY A WITNESS, WITNESS 1.  THE OPERATOR STOPPED BY THE WITNESSES CAMP TO RETRIEVE BRICKS TO WEIGH DOWN THE FRONT OF HIS VESSEL DUE TO CAVITATION.  THE WITNESS STATED THAT THE OPERATOR THEN LEFT THE CAMP WITH THE INTENTIONS ON TRAVELING BY WATER TO THE TOWN OF LAFITTE IN ORDER TO FISH. THE OPERATOR WAS REPORTED MISSING BY FAMILY MEMBERS THE FOLLOWING MORNING AND AGENTS FROM THE LDWF BEGAN SEARCH AND RESCUE OPERATIONS IN THE AREA. VESSEL 1 WAS FOUND ADRIFT IN BAYOU SEGNETTE AND THE OPERATOR HAS NOT YET BEEN LOCATED.  ACCORDING TO THE WITNESS, THE OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 WAS WEARING A TYPE II PFD WHILE ON THE WATER, HOWEVER THE BOTTOM STRAP WAS NOT BUCKLED.  THE PFD HAS NOT BEEN RECOVERED AND WAS NOT IN THE VESSEL. IN ADDITION THE WITNESS STATED THAT THE OPERATOR APPEARED TO BE HEAVILY IMPAIRED AND HAS A HISTORY OF ALCOHOL AND DRUG USE.  FAMILY AND FRIEND OF THE OPERATOR MADE STATEMENTS THAT HE HAD GONE MISSING ON TWO PREVIOUS OCCASIONS AND THAT THEY HAD FOUND HIM IN THE MARSH SLEEPING SEVERAL DAYS LATER.  IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE OPERATOR HAD FALLEN OVERBOARD, HOWEVER, HIS PIROR HISTORY MAY SUGGEST THAT HE IS IN THE MARSH AREA AROUND BAYOU SEGNETTE. SEARCH AND RESCUE OPERATIONS ARE ONGOING.

Operator 1 was operating a motorboat on Cypress Lake.  According to Passenger1, Operator 1 apparently lost control of the motorboat for some unknown reason.  Motorboat travelled erratically, tossing both people into the lake.  Passenger 1 managed to get Operator 1 to shore with help from another person.  Operator 1 did not survive.  Neither person wore PFD's.

On November 15, 2009, at approximately 6:30 a.m., Operator 1 launched LA vessel at Red River South Marina on the Red River in Bossier Parish.  When Operator 1 failed to return, his family reported him missing.  Operator 1's vessel was located approximately one mile south of Red River South Marina on November 16, 2009.  The vessel was found unoccupied stuck on a mud point of an island with the throttle in the maximum forward position and the key on (the engine was not running at the time located.)  The motor was trimmed all the way down.  Several items that Operator 1 was known to carry in his vessel were found floating in the river approximately eight miles down the river from where Operator 1's vessel was found.  After an extensive search by land, air, and water no further evidence as to what happened to Operator 1 was found.

Operator 1 and his 5 year old, Passenger 1 were in a small aluminum vessel paddling back to Barrot's Boat Dock after duck hunting.  Passenger 1 was wearing PFD. Operator 1 was not.  Passenger 1 stated that his father dropped a flashlight and leaned over to retrieve it.  As a result of leaning, the boat began to take on water and swamped causing both occupants to enter the water.  Witnesses, Witness 1 and Witness 2 launched a vessel on their own and went to swamped vessel. They state that when they arrive on scene, Passenger 1 was holding onto the side of that boat crying and Operator 1 was face down in the water near the rear of the boat.  They placed Passenger 1 in their boat.  At that point, Witness 2 reports that he grabbed Operator 1 and got his face out of the water and they began paddling the boat to shore dragging Operator 1 with them.  Witness 1 reports that his mother administered CPR to Operator 1 after they got him on dry ground. Operator 1 was transported to St Francis North Hospital via ambulance, where he was later pronounced dead.  Passenger 1 was transported in a personal car and sustained no injuries.

On 12/29/2009, I, learned of a boat incident which had occurred the night before in the Oxy Field, st. Martin Parish.  After contacting the St. Martin Parish S/O and the family of the victim, Victim 1, it was learned that Victim 1 had gone to tend some fish lines when the person camping  with him, Good Samaritan 1, heard him yelling for help.  When good Samaritan 1 walked out of the tent, he saw the vessel going in circles and Victim 1 in the water attempting to swim. Good Samaritan 1 attempted to help Victim 1, but was unsuccessful.  The St. Martin S/OP and the  Assumption S/O was on the scene shortly after the incident took place. Capt.  recovered Victim 1's body shortly after.  No PFD's were used and it is unknown if there were any drugs or alcohol involved due to the fact that the incident was learned of a day later and no autopsy or toxicology was performed on Victim 1.

subject was running crab pots in the marsh.  Subject spoke to the vessel owner at approximately 3:10 P.M. and stated that he was having engine trouble.  Evidence suggests that the subject had some type of engine failure, causing him to have to push pole, and enter the water to push the vessel.  It was raining, foggy and windy on this night.  Due to some type of miscommunication, no one repoted the subject over due until approximately 4:00 P.M. on 12/8/2009.  Subjects vessel was located, capsized.  agents found the subjects body on 12/9/2009.  The vessel was equipped with adequate PFD's.  Alcohol or drugs were not a factor.

Still on-going investigation as of 7/10/09.  Victim was found unresponsive in the lake by person who observed a canoe afloat.   He waded out to discover victim floating face down.  He carried victim to shore.  Victim was wearing what appeared to be a type III pfd.  Transported to hospital, later declared deceased and transferred to ME's office awaiting autopsy and tox results.  Alcohol is a possible factor is this accident.  Will update when more info becomes available.

Vessel collided with jetty rocks, on starboard side at the mouth of the river during in-coming tide, under heavy fog conditions with storm surge and a 10 foot tide.  Vessel was traveling in a northerly direction, upriver.  Vessel sank was submerged and drifted out of the mouth of the river in a southerly direction.  A mayday call was made to Salisbury PD by a cell phone.  3 out of 4 parties were rescued by USCG.  Operator is still reported missing at this time 7/10/09.  All were reported not wearing pfds.  Vessel was found the next morning by divers fully submerged on the ocean floor, on it's side and heavily damaged with a 6 ffot hole, wheel hourse/stern and flybridge destroyed.  According to state police several parties on board consumed alcohol prior to collision.  A passenger was taken to hospital.  Another passenger was taken into protective custody for alcohol intoxication.  On-going investigation as of 7/10/09.

Two motorboats collided.  Victim was a passenger in vessel #1 stiting in the rear of the boat when it was struck.  Victim was ejected and landed in water.  Vessel #2 fled the scene of the accident.  Search and rescue teams recovered body on day 4 on of the search.  Still on-going investigation.  Prelim info only as of 7/16/09.  Charges are being taken out by DA's office.  Will update when more info becomes available.

Victim was found floating face down near a nearby unocuupied jet ski by a pssing boater.  He was taken to shore and then to the hospital were he died later that evening.  His fiancee told the investigating officer that the victim was an alcoholic.  Victim was found wearing a bicycle helmet and lifejacket.  ME's officer determined death.  The incident was ruled an accident.  It is believed this accident could have been prevented had victim been more experienced with the operations and maintenance of the vessel and its maneuvering characteristics as well as its capabilities for the sea state he was operating in.  There is a strong possibility that victim was under the influence of alcoholic beverages as well as marijuana prior to and/or during the operation of the vessel, which may have been a contributing factor to this accident (final toxicology screen pending).  Right now possible factors are alcohol and operator inexperience.

Mother of deceased stated she whistled and called out to her son around 7:30pm wanting him to come in from the pond due to darkness setting in.  She stated she observed her son fall backwards out of the canoe.

Owner of both vessels involved stated that he was operating vessel #1 (open boat) at the time of the collision.  2 of his friends were taking turns operating the PWC.  All three operators comsumed alcoholic beverages and several containers both open and unopened were in the open boat.  Victim was operating the PWC at the time of the collision.  According to operator and the other friend they saw victim suddenly traveling straight at the bow of the boat with the PWC, strke the boat and knocked both operator and friend on the open boat off into the water.  The PWC shut down while the boat continued to travel around them while they were afloat in the water awaiting assistance.  An off duty firefighter brought victim and friend in and called 911.  A subsequent search of the vessel revealed more alcoholic beverages and what appeared to be 3 small burnt marijuana cigaretts in a small compartment in the dash area.  As of 11/3/09 I have not received the completed report for cause of accident.

Father and son were out sailing without any pfd's being available or worn.  Father was a very experienced sailor in good health was steering the sunfish.  Son said they were running when his father lost control of the sailboat and it capsized.  Both occupants were thrown from the boat.  Son swam towards the sunfish to right it.  It was drfting very fast and had filled with water making it difficult to right.  He struggled to right it and had lost sight of his father.  He got close enough to shore to ground the boat and run for help.  He called to his brother to call 911.  The victim was recovered by the harbormaster who preformed cpr.  Cause of death is pending as of 11/3/09.

Three people were on a borrowed canoe with the plan to go fishing.  When the vessel started taking on water they decided to head back to shore.  The victim seated in the iddle attempted to grab a nap sack, the weight shifted and the canoe tipped/capsized.  None of the parties were wearing pfd's nor was any found on board.  Two of the three onboard swam to shore safely and flagged down a motorist for help.  They reported that one male party had gone underwater.  The canoe had also sunk to the bottom of the river.  Victim was found two days later down river.  Investigator concluded that unequal weight distribution/and or sudden sift of one of the parties onboard caused the canoe to capsize.  The canoe had two built-in seats only.  An examination of the canoe at the scene disclosed fiberglass repairs had been made on the inside surface, mid center near the interior frame support sections.  The victim sitting mid-center may have put excessive weight/stree on the fiberglass repair cracks that caused the canoe to take on water.  Victim may have survived if he wore a pfd.

Owner/operator had just purchased  new boat and had just had it serviced and tested for repairs.  The three friends went out for a day of boating and swimming.  Several times during the day the operator would stop the vessel and the friends would jump off the boat and swim.  The victim was not a strong swimmer.  The vessel was not equipped with an anchor or line.  The operator was cited for same.  The victim got into trouble swimming.  The operator drove closer to the victim and was attempting to throw a line to them which was not working.  There were lifejactkets on board but not used.  Operator inexperience due to the fact that he just purchased this vessel would seem to be a cause of accident as well as passenger behaviour as the victim was not a strong swimmer he should have been wearing a pfd while swimming.

According to roomates of the victim he decided to take a friend's inflatable boat with an electric motor out onto the lake with the intend to go swimming.  He did this on many afternoons after work.  A passing officer saw a boat adrft and appeared to be unoccupied.  Occupants of a local taven flagged down the officer and stated they saw the victim jump/fall (conflicting witnesses) into the water.  This lake was full of vegetation, very murky and had a layer of sediment on the bottom.  One of the rescue swimmers himself became entangled in the vegetation and had to be assited to shore.  He was found 4 days later.  His roomates said he was a very strong swimmer.  The vessel was not anchored.  It is felt by the officer that the victim became entangled in vegetation.

On 04/04/09 at approximately 2130 hrs., this writer was contacted by Lt in reference to a boat accident / missing person's investigation in the Nanticoke River ( Wicomico County). This writer made contact with Sgt to find out any additional information; and also to provide him with any assistance in the incident. He indicated that he spoke with the witnesses about the incident. In addition, he stated that he was checking several local boat ramp areas for a possible vehicle & boat trailer to confirm the identity of the missing individuals from identification items located in a camouflage backpack that was found floating in the river by rescue personnel.

On 4/5/09, this writer met with Sgt. at the witness's shorefront residence on the Nanticoke River to retrieve the backpack and its' contents; and to obtain any additional information on this incident. In addition, this writer processed, photographed, and completed an inventory form of the items on the vessel (DL 5504 AA) before it was removed from the location and transported to a secured area for storage at the Johnson Regional Office during this investigation. Next, this writer spoke with the witnesses about the incident. They stated at approximately 1900 hrs. on 4/4/09 that they were sitting in their recreation room looking out their window towards the Vienna Bridge. They can see quite a distance down the river. they both saw what appears to be spray coming from a boat heading up river (towards Sharptown). as the boat began to come better into view, it turned sharply to the side and they could tell it was a small fishing boat. It suddenly hit a wave and partiallytilted over such that they could see the boat's bottom and ejecting what appeared to be one person and maybe a dog. It happened so quickly; and was at a distance, so they could only see a quick profile. Thus not being sure whether it was a dog or second person being thrown overboard. witness immediately tried to pull their kayak in the water to see if he could paddle out to the victims while his wife  called 911. He saw no individuals swimming or any sign of person in distress. He also summoned one additional kayaker and another passing boat to look for any survivors, with negative results.

On 5/01/09 at approximately 1400 hours, the writer was assigned the complaint of a possible missing person by Sgt. Sgt stated that he had spoken to the complainant, and was advised by Complainant that he and a friend were fishing on the Susquehanna Flats at about  1100 hours on 4/30/09. Complainant repoprted that he fell asleep on their boat at about 1930 hours and slept until about 2130 hours, at which time he found that subject was no longer in the vessel. Complainant ran out  of fuel searching for his friend and did not arrive home until approximately 1300 hours on 5/01/09. Complainant stated to Sgt that he thought that it was possible that his friend had boarded another boat and was not concerned about his friend's welfare until he arrived back home and was that subject truck was still parked in a vacant lot behind the house. Sgt stated that Complainant had a felony criminal record and that the license plate displayed on subject’s truck came back.

Complainant stated that the two headed out to the Susquehanna Flats and estimated that it took approximately 30 - 40 minutes to arrive at their destination near the Aberdeen proving Ground. Neither man was wearing a PFD. Cpl asked Complainant if there were any other vessels nearby and he stated that he remembered a U.S. Coast Guard vessel was tied to a buoy with sight of them. Complainant stated that they remained at that location for approximately 2 hours, during which time the only fish that they caught were catfish and eels. The two saw several boats on the North East Flats near Turkey Point and decided to try their luck over in that area. Complainant stated that they anchored the boat in that area and stayed there for the remainder of the time. Complainant said that he laid down in the boat to get some sleep sometime between 1900 and 1930 hours. He awoke at approximately 2130 hours and Subject was no longer on the boat. Complainant had thought that Subject may have gotten on another boat while he was asleep because Subject knew a lot of people and had recognized and acknowledged people on five or six different vessels who called him by his nickname.

On 5/05/09  at approximately 1400 hours, this writer was contacted by Tawes Communication Center in reference to a body recovery in the Northeast River out in front of the Sandy Cove ministries Retreat Camp - North East, MD. Upon arrival. this writer met with additional NRP Personnel at the scene. This writer made contact with the two young men who discovered the body in the water. The writer obtained a voluntary written statement from them. The body was observed in a face down position in approximately 4' feet of water and about 70 yards offsjore. No life jacket was observed on the body.  Subject's sister responded to the location and made a positive ID that this was her brother. The decedent's body was transported to the medical Examiner's Office in Baltimore City for an autopsy.
location: Turkey Point Area - Upper Ches, MD

description: 06/01/09 at approximately 0945 hrs., a concerned citizen called the Talbot County 911 Center to report an unmanned vessel running in circles in Harris Creek behind her residence. At approximately 1000 hours, the vessel stopped circling as it appeared to have run out of fuel. Uniformed Natural Resources Police Officers responded, secured the vessel, and began searching the area. The vessel was determined to belong to the victim. The last confirmed sighting of Victim had been at approximately 0430 hrs. by his wife as he left the house to go crabbing in his boat. No one saw Victim operating the vessel. St. Michaels Fire Department, Oxford Fire Department, Maryland State Police, the U.S. Coast Guard, and the Preston Mid-Shore Dive team all assisted with the search for the victim. At approximately 1645 hrs., the body of the victim was recovered within 25 yards of where the concerned citizen had first seen the boat spinning in circles. Victim's body was transported to the office of the Chief Medical Examiner in Baltimore for autopsy. Results of the autopsy will not be available for some time; however, it appears that the nature of Victim's demise was related to a long history of serious heart disease. No one witnessed Victim operating the vessel before the accident. No one witnessed the accident. This case remains open pending autopsy results.

On February 16, 2009 at approximately 0925 hours, a witness saw a boat with a subject in it going in circles at the north west end  of Clopper Lake at Seneca Creek State Park, in a cove near Kingfisher Overlook. A short time later a second witness noticed a boat going in circles in the same area with nobody on the boat. That witness called 911. The Montgomery County E.M.S. and Montgomery County Police responded to the scene and located and recovered the body. The Montgomery County Police identified the victim by his driver license. The victim was transported to M.E. Office in Baltimore City. Notification was made to the victim's wife by Sgt. and Sgt. Cpl. spoke with the victim's wife who stated that her husband had previously had a heart attack in his thirties and that his father had died at a young age as a result of a heart attack. All property was released to the wife. Cpl. will attend the autopsy on 2/17/09.
location: Seneeca Creek State Park, Clop, MD

description: On June 08, 2009 at approximately 2218, Ofc responded to a report of a vessel that had run aground in the Thousand Acres area of Deep Creek Lake. Complainant found the motor of the boat to be running and found no occupants on board. The vessel in question was a 24 foot Harris pontoon boat bearing Maryland registration 8568 BC. Responding Officers located a local address for the registered owner and checked his residence but were unable to make contact with anyone. involved personnel then made contact with the Hardy County Dispatch in West Virginia in an attempt to have the vessel's owner residence contacted. A surface search was then conducted in the area with no sucess and that search was called off at 0230 hours. At 0800, approximately five and one half later, on June 9, 2009, Sgt responded to the scene by vehicle and again checked the missing residence with no sucess. At that time Sgt entered the unlocked residence and found no one inside. Sgt then locateda Dodge pick-up truck registered to the owner of the vessel parked at the community dock parking lot. At that time, Sgt contacted the Hardy County, West Virginia Dispatch Center and requested a law enforcement officer to respond to the Hardy County residence of the missing boater. This request was fruitful and the Hardy County Sheriff's Department relayed the information that Victim was now living by himself at his Deep Creek Lake residence. At the same time Officers began conducting a surface search. Maryland State Police helicopter, Trooper 5, was requested and responded from Cumberland Airport. At 0920 hours Trooper 5 located the victim floating near the shoreline adjacent to a residence. this investigator arrived on scene approximately 1005 hours and observed the victim floating face down in the water. Officer and this Investigator then pulled the victim to the water's edge and this Investigator retrieved a wallet from his left front shorts pocket. Driver's license photo identification confirmed the victim, the registered owner of the vessel found aground the night before. The vessel registered to Victim was then examined by the Investigator. The vessel was located tied to a tree along the shoreline approximately 1/4 mile from where the victim was located. There were several empty beer cans on the deck and a partially consumed beer can in the cup holder at the operator's console. Located on the deck were some clothing items including a pair of jeans indicating the victim may have put his shorts on while on the boat. Although not running, the vessel was in gear with throttle at about a 2/3 forward position. There were no other remarkable contents found on the vessel.
location: Thousand Aces area of Deep Cre, MD

description: VICTUM JUMPED OUT OF CANOE AND DROWNED. ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES WERE CONSUMED BY THE VICTUM PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT.  TOXICOLOGY REPORT OF DECEASED SHOWED BAC OF .27.
location: SEVERN RIVER AREA OF HERALD HA, MD

description: ON 11/03/2009 THERE WAS A REPORT OF A YELLOW KAYAK FLOATING IN THE BAY IN THE AREA OF ARUNDEL ON THE BAY. subject 1 SAID HE WAS SAILING SOUTH IN BAY. HE ADVISED THERE WAS A KAYAK WITH A WHITE MALE 25 TO 30 YEARS OLD IN IT. HE SAID THE MAN WAS WEARING BRIGHT SHORTS AND A DARK SHIRT.subject 1 SAID HE WENT NEAR THE MAN AND SAID "ARE WE HAVING FUN YET?" THE MANS ANSWER TO THAT WAS "SUMMER ISNT OVER UNTIL I SAY IT IS."subject 1 TOLD ME THAT WHEN HE TURNED AND CAME BACK BY THE AREA WHERE THE KAYAK WAS,HE SAW THE KAYAK WITH NOBODY IN IT,AND A PADDLE AND A LIFEJACKET FLOATING. THE LIFEJACKET IS A YOUTH SIZE AND WOULD NOT HAVE FIT THIS PERSON. subject 1 SAID HE CALLED USCG IMMEDIATELY.THERE ARE KAYAKS THAT ARE KEPT ALONG THE SHORE IN THE AREA OF BAY RIDGE AND ARUNDEL ON THE BAY. RESIDENTS IN THE DEVELOPMENTS WERE NOTIFIED OF THE SITUATION AND WERE ADVISED TO CONTACT THE DEPARTMENT IF ANYTHING DEVELOPED THAT MAY BE OF INTEREST HELPING TO LOCATE THE WHEREABOUTS OF THE PERSON IN THE KAYAK.
location: CHESAPEAKE BAY, OFF OF OYSTER , MD

description: VESSEL # 1 WAS OCCUPIED BY VICTiM. iT WAS TRAVELLING 25-30 MILES PER HOUR OUT OF MARLEY CREEK TOWARDS CURTIS CREEK. VSSEL #2 WAS OCCUPIED TWO TIMES. THE OPERATOR AND HIS 13 YEAR OLD DAUGHTER WAS THE PASSENGER.  VESSEL #2 HAD COME FROM FURNACE CREEK INTO MARLEY CREEK AROUND POINT PLEASANT AND WAS ALSO TRAVELLING 25-30 MILES AN HOUR. AT THIS TIME BOTH VESSELS WERE HEADED TOWARD EACH OTH.OPERATOR OF VESSEL 2 STATED HE ATTEMPTED  EVASIVE MANEUVERS, BUT EVERY TIME HE TURNED, VESSEL #1 TURNED TOWARDS HIM.  tHE STARBOARD BOW OF VESSEL #2 STRUCK THE STARBOARD BOW OF VESSEL # 1.  tHE COLLISION CAUSED VESSEL # 2 TO ROLL OVER ONE TIME AND EJECTED BOTH OCCUPENTS. NEITHER WERE SERIOUSLY INJURED. VESSEL #1 WENT INTO A SPINWITH THE VICTiM BEING THROWN TO THE BACK OF THE BOAT.  SOMETHING STRUCK THE THE VICTiM DURING THE COLLISION THAT SLICED OPEN HIS HEAD AND CAUSED TRAMATIC EVACUATION OF HIS BRAIN.
location: MARLEY CREEK OFF POINT PLEASAN, MD

description:
FIVE SUBJECTS LEFT PIER SEVEN MARINA ON THE SOUTH RIVER IN EDGEWATER,AACO ON BOARD VESSEL ONE. THEY TRAVELLED TOWARDS THE MOUTH OF THE SOUTHER RIVER. AT THE TIME,SEAS WERE APPROX. 2-3FT AND THE WIND WAS OUT OF THE SOUTHEREAST AT APPROX. 15MPH. ONCE THERE,THE BOAT WAS TURNED OFF AND DRIFTED AND THE OPERATOR AND subject 1 JUMPED OFF OF THE REAR SWIM PLATFORM TO GO SWIMMING. subject 1 BECAME FATIGUED AND STARTED TO CALL FOR HELP. operator MADE AN EFFORT TO SWIM TO HIM AND PULL HIM OUT, BUT HE WAS UNSUCCESSFUL. THE OTHER INDIVIDUALS ON BOARD ATTEMPTED TO THROW PERSONAL FLOTATION DEVICES AND LINES TO subject 1 TO RESCUE HIM,BUT WALLACE WAS UNABLE TO GRASP ANY OF THEM. A GROUP OF INDIVIDUALS ON A SECOND BOAT(ABOVE LISTED WITNESSES) ATTEMPTED TO RESCUE subject 1 AS WELL.WITNESS  ATTEMPTED TO SWIM TO subject 1 TO SAVE HIM, BUT BY THE TIME SHE REACHED THE AREA THAT HE WAS IN,HE HAD GONE UNDERWATER AND WAS NOT SEEN AGAIN. A SEARCH ENSUED INVOLVED USCG,AACO FD, AND NRP.

ON TUESDAY 28subject 1'S BODY WAS RECOVERED IN THE VICINITY OF WHERE THE SEARCH FOR HIM ORGINALLY BEGUN. HIS BODY WAS LOCATED IN 15-17 FEET OF WATER. THE SURFACE WATER TEMPERATURE WAS 81.9 DEGREES. HIS BODY WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE OFFICE OF THE MEDICAL EXAMINER IN BALTIMORE FOR AUTOPSY.

ON 07/24/09 NRP RESPONDED TO THE SASSAFRAS RIVER IN REF TO POSSIBLE FATAL BOAT ACCIDENT. UPON ARRIVAL IT WAS LEARNED THATsubject 1 WAS OPERATING A 24FT MASTERCRAFT TRAVELING UP THE SASSAFRAS RIVER AT APPROX. 35MPH.  HE ENCOUNTERED A WAKE FROM A PASSING VESSEL CAUSING HIS 11 YEAR OLD DAUGHTER WHO WAS SITTING IN THE BOW TO BOUNCE VIOLENTLY OUT OF HER SEAT.  UPON OBSERVING THIS, subject 1 PULLED BACK ON THE THROTTLE.  AS HE DID THIS, HIS DAUGHTER  BOUNCED OFF THE BOW OF THE VESSEL.  subject 1 IMMEDIATELY PLACED THE VESSEL IN NEUTRAL HOWEVER THE MOMENTUM OF THE BOAT CAUSED THE BOAT TO CONTINUE OVER HIS DAUGHTER. subject 1 JUMPED OVERBOARD IN ATTEMPTS TO LOCATE HER BUT WAS UNABLE TO DO SO.  SHE WAS NOT WEARING A PFD AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT.

ON THE RETURN TRIP FROM ROCKHOLD CREEK,subject 1 WAS OPERATING. ONCE THEY ENTERED HERRING BAY AND CLEARED THE CRAB POT LINE, subject 1 TURNED THE HELM OVER TO subject 2 AND STEPPED OUTSIDE OF THE CABIN ON TO THE BACK DECK OF THE BOAT. APPROX. ONE MINUTE LATER,subject 1 SAID THE BOAT HAD A VIOLENT IMPACT AND RAISED UP IN THE AIR. THE VESSEL HAD COME TO REST ON TOP OF THE STONE JETTY JUST  TO THE RIGHT OF RED DAY MARKER #2 AT THE MOUTH OF ROCKHOLD CREEK. subject 1 ESTIMATES THAT AT THE TIME OF IMPACT,THE VESSEL WAS TRAVELLING AT APPROX. 20KNOTS.subject 2 SUFFERED BLUNT FORCE TRAUMA INJURIES.subject 1 UNINJURED.PARAMEDICS RESPONDED TO THE SCENE AND REMOVED BOTH MEN FROM THE VESSEL. subject 2 DIED AS A RESULT OF INJURIES SUSTAINED IN THE IMPACT. subject 1 WAS INTERVIEWED AND GAVE A WRITTEN STATEMENT CONCERNING THE ACCIDENT. THE VESSEL WAS RETRIEVED FROM THE JETTY BY TOW BOAT U.S,AND PUT ON A TRAILER AT A RAMP IN ROCKHOLD CREEK. IT WAS TRANSPORTED BY NRP PERSONNEL FOR STORAGE AT MATAPEAKE FACILITY.
location: HERRING BAY AT THE ENTRANCE TO, MD

description: ON 12/01/09AT 1422HRS, VESSEL 1 WAS OPERATING NORTHBOUND IN THE CHESAPEAKE BAY OFF PT.LOOKOUT.  2 PEOPLE ON BOARD.  OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 STATED THAT VESSEL 1 WAS BETWEEN BUOY'S 70 AND 72 AT A SPEED OF APPROX. 3 KNOTS.  OCCUPANTS WAS PREPARING TO FISH AND VICTIM WAS PREPARING PLANER BOARDS TO GO OVERBOARD.  OPERATOR HEARD A SPLASH, TURNED AROUNG AND OBSERVED THAT THE VICTIM HAD GONE OVERBOARD.  OPERATOR THREW A BOAT FENDER TO VICTIM WHO WAS UNABLE TO HOLD ONTO SAME.  OPERATOR TURNED VESSEL 1 AROUND BUT WAS UNABLE TO GET VICTIM BACK ON BOARD.  OPERATOR SECURED VICTIM TO VESSEL 1.  VICTIM WAS FLOATING FACE DOWN WHEN VESSEL 1 RETURNED TO VICTIMS LOCATION.

ON 08/02/09 AT APPROX 1700HRS, VESSEL 1 WAS OPERATING IN BACK RIVER OFF PORTER POINT.  VESSEL 1 HAD A TOTAL OF 7 OCCUPANTS ON BOARD, 2 OF WHICH WERE BEING TOWED ON AN INFLATABLE TUBE BEHIND VESSEL 1.  1 OCCUPANT HAD FALLEN OFF THE TUBE.  VESSEL 1 TURNED AROUND TO PICK UP THE OCCUPANT/VICTIM WHO HAD FALLEN OFF.  AS VESSEL 1 GOT CLOSE TO THE VICTIM, OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 LOST SIGHT OF SAME.  VICTIM WAS STRUCK BY THE BOAT AND PROPELLER RESULTING IN FATAL INJURY.

ON 08/11/09 AT APPROX. 0930 HRS.  VESSEL 1 WAS FISHING ALONG GREEN GLADE COVE WITH 3 POB.  OPERATOR/VICTIM WAS SEATED IN THE BOW WHEN A FISHING ROD'S LINE BECAME SNAGGED. ROD WAS PULLED OVERBOARD.  OPERATOR/VICTIM IMMEDIATELY JUMPED OVERBOARD TO RETRIEVE THE ROD.  UPON ATTEMPTING TO SWIM BACK TO VESSEL 1, HE WAS UNABLE TO DO SO AND CALLED FOR HELP.  WIND HAD PUSHED VESSEL 1 FURTHER AWAY FROM VICTIM.  AN OCCUPANT OF VESSEL 1 JUMPED IN TO ATTEMPT A RESCUE.  HE WAS UNABLE TO KEEP THE VICTIM AFLOAT AND EVENTUALLY HAD TO LET GO OF THE VICTIM TO SAVE HIS OWN LIFE.  NEITHER THE VICTIM NOR THE OCCUPANT WHO ATTEMPTED RESCUE WAS WEARING A PFD.
location: DEEP CREEK LAKE - GREEN GLADE , MD

description: ON 10/07/09 AT APPROX. 1737 HRS, VESSEL 1-A SMALL SAILBOAT WAS OPERATING IN CRAB ALLEY BAY.  SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY WAS IN EFFECT WITH 30 TO 40 MPH WINDS.  ROUGH WATER CONDITIONS PRESENT.  VESSEL 1 OVERTURNED PUTTING THE OPERATOR/OCCUPANT IN THE WATER.  OPERATOR HAD A PFD HOLDING IT BY A STRAP BUT WAS NOT WEARING IT.  A SECOND VESSEL ATTEMPTED TO ASSIST THE OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 BUT WAS UNABLE TO GET OPERATOR INTO THE SECOND VESSEL.  OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 DROWNED UPON EXAMINATION BY MEDICAL EXAMINER.

individual reported as overdue from trip.  Subject departed residence on the River between 1300 and 1330 to go crabbing  and was due to return before sunset.  Cell phone was going straight to voice mail.  Witnesses had spotted victim aroudn 1900 with a fouled prop. deceased subject was located .25nm from his boat.

Unknown.  Vessel was found at anchor, motor running, no one on board.  Victim was last seen om 05/24/09 at about 1500.  He was leaving Stonington, enroute to Goose Island, off Flye Point in Brooklin.  He was going to spend the night and pick his family up at about 1030 on 05/25/09.  He did not show up.

Victim recovered on 6/25/09, found deceased on the shore of Tinker Island, Tremont.  Medical Examiner positively identified subject , cause of death was drowning.

OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 WAS USING HAND-POWERED PROPULSION WHILE PASSENGER IN VESSEL 1 WAS LOOKING BACK AT HIS FISHING POLE. VESSEL 1 STARTED TO TIP TO IT'S SIDE AND PROCEEDED TO CAPSIZE. OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 INFORMED PASSENGER THAT HE COULD NOT SWIM AND WENT UNDER WATER AND DROWN. THERE WERE NO WEARABLE PFDS IN THE BOAT AND OPERATOR AND PASSENGER OF VESSEL 1 WERE NOT WEARING PFDS. THE OPERATOR AND PASSENGER OF VESSEL 1 HAD BOTH BEEN CONSUMING ALCOHOL PRIOR TO CAPSIZING THE CANOE (VESSEL 1)

Subjects renting cottage on lake that includes the use of canoe. Two subjects took canoe out on lake for a short fishing trip. A short time later the subject in the rear of the canoe stood up to cast fishing pole. This caused the canoe to capsize and both subjects were thrown into the water. One subject was able to swim back to shore. The second subject was last seen struggling to swim in the area of the canoe. No PFD's were used or taken in the canoe by the subjects.

Drowning victim's body was recovered a day after the accident.

Operator was traveling down a river with another kayak.  The operator's kayak overturned in some whitewater.  The operator traveled downstream for a period of time and drowned.  The operator was not wearing a life jacket and did not have a life jacket in the kayak.

Vessel A departed a marina after delivering a larger sailing vessel for seasonal haulout. Vessel A is described as a small aluminum watercraft with a 4hp motor. The transit was to be a several mile voyage to return its mooring. The weather conditions were such that a choppy sea with heavy current had formed. The vessel was reported overdue and a search ensued. Vessel A was found during the night submerged and overturned with it's operator missing. Vessel A's sole occupant victim #1 was found a few days later deceased, washed up on an adjoining shoreline wearing his flotation device.

Owner and operater of the only vessel involved was found dead on the shore south of Kings point Southwest Harbor on 11/25/09 at approx. 1130.  The Old Town Otter kayak was found a few hundred yards to the north 2 days prior.

Victim #1, and the passenger were paddling a canoe approximately 40-50 feet off the shore. The canoe capsized and both individuals came to the surface and began swimming towards shore, without wearing their PFD's. The Victim then went under the surface of the water. Witness #1 observed the capsizing of the canoe and swam out to assist. He located the vicitim in 10 feet of water on the bottem of the lake. Witness #1 then swam down, retrieved the victim and brought him to shore. The passenger then began CPR. The victim was taken to the hospital, by ambulance, where he died in their care. 

Two PFD's were located in the overturned canoe.

I observed several full and empty beer cans as well as a half empty bottle of Coffee brandy, at the scene of the capsizing. I also located a baggie floating, which appeared to contain Marijuana. I had the passenger submit to a Blood alcohol test, which resulted in a .02 BAC. The victim's BAC was .174. As a result of the evidence at the scene and the victim's Blood Alcholol Test it is evident that alcohol played a factor in this incident.

Victim was a 60 year old male from Jonesport.  Victim routinely went to the shore each day and rowed out to his sailboat to check it.  On 05/21/2009 Victim did not return home after going to check on his boat.  Victim's wife called to report him overdue.  A search and rescue operation began approximately at 1945 hours.  Victim was located along the shoreline near his overturned skiff.  He was deceased.  It is assumed that he was trying to get out to his sailboat and fell overboard from his skiff and drowned.

Three teens were trolling in a small boat when it began taking on water due to waves coming over front of boat. Boat capsized and all 3 occupants were thrown into the water. The victim and one of the survivors attempted to swim to shore.  The other survivor, who could not swim, stayed with the capsized boat. Both of the survivors eventually made it to safety. By that time, the victim had disappeared. There were three life jackets in the boat, but none were worn when the boat capsized.

Both boats were cruising on plane as they approached the tip of Indian Point on the lake. The operator of boat #2 (traveling East approx. 100 feet from the shore) observed boat #1 approaching from the West and made a minor course change toward the shore to ensure adequate distance between his boat and the approaching vessel. Operator of boat #2 was distracted and turned his attention toward the interior of the boat, when he looked up again boat #1 was directly in front of him and the two boats then collided head on. Neither boat swerved prior to the collision. The operator of boat #1 was thrown from his boat into the water. The passenger of boat #2 jumped into the water to assist the injured party. A nearby boat came over to assist and they were able to get the injured operator into the boat and transport him to shore. However, the operator of boat #1 was pronounced dead by EMS personnel after they were unable to revive him.

Victim was out in canoe alone, had been drinking. Victim capsized the canoe and was hanging onto the side of it. By the time anybody could get to the area where the canoe was to help victim he had fallen underneath the water and was not located for approximately 20 minutes. No pfd.

Victim was fishing with father. Victim had been consuming alcohol. While urinating out of rear of boat victim fell overboard. Father attempted to assist victim into boat and boat capsized. Father could not swim and held onto boat until help arrived. Victims body was found 30 feet from shore in 5 feet of water. Two throwables were located. Neither party had lifejackets on or in the boat.

Victims boat was found floating. Engine was not running, but had 1/4 tank of gas, was in forward gear, throttle was 1/2 way open and tether kill switch was removed and on the floor of the boat.  Victim was found floating face down. There were PFD's in boat, but victim wasn't wearing a PFD. No alcohol involved.

Four individuals were fishing on lake. As the waves grew larger they headed back. While en-route to shore they had engine problems. Waves began going over rear of boat. Bilge pump was not working. Attempted to start kicker motor but it died. When boat went underwater occupants jumped from boat and attempted to swim to shore. A resort pontoon boat observed this and attempted to rescue boaters.  Two successfully rescued, two disappeared below surface. Waves were 4-5 feet at time of incident. PFD's were in boat but not used.

Boat was drifting while the motor was being worked on. The motor caught fire and all four occupants jumped overboard and into the lake. Although PFD's were on the boat, no one took one when they jumped overboard. A recreational tube was also in the boat and attached with a rope. The boat was recently purchased and the owner was not able to swim and subsequently drowned.

Victim apparently drowned after falling out of her non-motorized Jon boat. She was fishing on a pond. It is unknown when she actually entered the water; it may have been up to two hours before help was summoned by a neighbor's son around 4 pm. He had noticed her boat, floating with no one on board. He then went out with his mother's boat to investigate. He found the victim floating face down in the water and called for help.

Boat motor and prop had become entangled in a navigational maker. The victim exited his watercraft and untangled the motor. After freeing the watercraft, the victim attempted to re-enter the boat without success. After several attempts, the boat began floating away from the victim. As the victim was walking out towards the boat, he stepped off an underwater ledge, where the water goes from 2 feet to approximately 20 feet in depth. The victim initially went underwater and re-surfaced. The victim then attempted to swim to safety but went beneath the water and re-surfaced 2 more times, before disappearing beneath the water's surface. Members aboard the boat attempted to throw the victim ropes and wearable life jackets, but their attempts were unsuccessful in saving the victim. An observant boater, noticed the victim's failed attempts to re-enter his boat and went to offer assistance. As the boater was approaching she observed the victim disappear beneath the water and dove in within 30 seconds and recovered the victim. The victim was pulled into the boat and CPR was performed.

Operator was pulling tube Northbound on lake and turned to the East, swinging tube to West. Operator was too close to shore, and using a newly purchased, longer tow rope (60'). Tube struck docked pontoon facing South at end of dock. Victim transported to Douglas County Hospital ER and was later pronounced dead.

Victim had been drinking alcohol before getting into canoe. Victim went out on pond in canoe to calm down after argument with family. Victim yelled to family on shore he dropped "I Pod" into water. Shortly after family heard a splash and victim yelling for help, then nothing. Victim had no PFD on or in canoe.

Victim apparently entered the water somehow from his canoe. He shouted for help upon entering the water and two men in boat,  along with a resident on shore, responded. The lake resident on shore paddled out in his canoe to the accident site, preceded by the two men in the rowboat. One of the rowboat occupants saw the victim's face about a foot below the surface. He jumped in and between the two rescuers they were able to get him aboard the rowboat. The rescuer from shore then climbed aboard and rowed the boat to shore. One of the trio called 911 from a cell phone. The operator assisted with CPR instructions while they were getting back to shore. A deputy arrived in his car and commandeered a canoe to help get the rowboat to shore faster. Once on shore, deputies continued resuscitative efforts, and made use of an automatic external defibrillator. EMS personnel then arrived and continued resuscitative efforts, but to no avail.
Canoe capsized. Neither party wearing PFD's. One party able to swim to shore. Other party drowned while trying to swim to shore.

Victim drowned after apparently falling overboard from boat.  The victim had been in the area hunting for some days and left his van at the boat access.  A Citizen called police just before 9 am on the 17th to report that the vehicle had been parked there since Saturday morning.  The boat was found overturned on the morning of the 17th and his body was located in 5-6 feet of water at 2:30 pm that afternoon.

3 men fishing from raft on Bitterroot River from Angler's Roost to Hamilton. The operator was rowing, Passenger 1 in front of raft, Deceased in rear seat. At the confluence of Bitterroot and Skalkaho Creek, there was a small log mostly submerged sticking out from the bank. The strong current pushed them into the log. The raft swung around and was pinned against a smaller log that was completely submerged. The raft instantly flipped and threw the men out upstream of the log.  None of the three men were wearing PFDs. The operator grabbed the log and held on. Passenger 1 was under water and pushed downstream about 20 yards as his wadders filled with water.  He crawled to the bank. The operator felt the deceased grab his legs underwater, but he let go when the current pulled him away. deceased never came to the surface.  The operator said he saw their life jackets floating in the river.  The deceased was found 3/4 mile downstream pinned under a log about 2 to 2 1/2 hours after the incident.  Rescuers tried CPR and other life saving measures, but were unsucessful.  The operator and passenger 1 were found by a rescue helicopter on an island in the river and flown to the site where the deceased body was recovered.

Vessel # 1 was traveling east at 28 MPH (according to the GPS unit on board) when it struck the port side of vessel #2 that was traveling northwest.  Vessel #2 navigational lights were not functioning and the rear anchor light was functioning according to witnesses.  Vessel #1 navigational lights and rear anchor light were functioning according to witnesses.  Vessel #1 had 10 people on board and recommended capacity is 8.  Operator of Vessel #1 had a BAC .02. Operator BAC on Vessel #2 was 0.0.  There were the required number of PFD's on both vessels and nobody was wearing PFD's except the 2 kids under the age of 12.

On July 14, 2009 at about 0808 hours Park Dispatch notified me at my residence that a possible drowning had occurred in the Swiftcurrent Lake near the Many Glacier Hotel, that rangers were on scene conducting a search and that I was being dispatched to the scene to conduct an investigation.  I drove to the scene arriving at approximately 1011 hours and met with the Incident Commander District ranger who game me a brief summary of what he believed happened.  ranger told me that ranger2 had started the investigation by talking to the Grizzly Security contract security guards who were among the first to respond when the call came in around 0330 hours.

I found ranger2 near the Swiftcurrent Dam and adjoining jammer residence on the Many Glacier Hotel access road.  Ranger2 told me he had just been talking with the primary boat operator (PBO), who was in the jammer dorm.  Ranger2 also told me that according to what he had been able to learn so far PBO and the deceased were among a large group of GPI employees attending a party in the Many Glacier Hotel employee recreation hall.  While attending the party both the PBO and the deceased had been consuming alcoholic beverages.  At about 0300 to 0330 the PBO asked the deceased if he wanted to go for a canoe ride on Swiftcurrent Lake in the PBO’s canoe.  The deceased said yes and they went from the party to the PBO’s residence where the deceased took his wallet and cell phone out of his pockets and left them in the PBO’s room.  The PBO and the deceased then took the PBO’s 14 foot canoe, paddles and two life preservers to Swiftcurrent Lake where they went onto the water without putting on the life preservers on.  Shortly into the paddle they capsized, the PBO made it to shore, and the deceased did not and the two security officers arrived shortly after hearing a commotion on or near the water.

Ranger2 said he and ranger3 had already taken statements from the two security officers and the PBO.  He gave me those statements and they are attached to this report.  Ranger2 and I then went to talk to the PBO at his room in the nearby jammer dorm.  I asked the PBO if he was up to talking and he said yes so I drove him over to the Many Glacier ranger station complex where at 1105 hours I interviewed him in the community room.  Ranger2 was sent to ask GPI management to canvass any dorm rooms where the deceased might be staying if he got out of the water and wasn’t seen.

The PBO related the following description of the incident to me:  About a week before he had gone to Kalispell and bought a canoe.  He has considerable canoeing experience and because of all the lakes in the area wanted one in Montana.  He went to the employee party at the hotel after work and decided after it quit raining that he would like to go on a canoe paddle on Swiftcurrent Lake so he went in search of someone to go with him.  A couple of people said no but he asked the deceased if he wanted to go and he said yes.

The PBO and the deceased went to the PBO’s room where he told him to take anything out of his pockets that he didn’t want to get wet and they took the canoe to the lake.  The PBO said about 5 minutes into their paddle he told the deceased to quit paddling as he wasn’t doing it right.  PBO explained to me that the deceased was constantly paddling too hard on one side or the other and pulling them off course.  PBO said they were about 50 yards from shore when suddenly the boat capsized and he and the deceased were in the water.  The deceased was trying to right the boat but the PBO told him that wasn’t going to happen and that they should swim to shore.  He said they kept calling out to each other by first name and that when he was almost to shore he hit bottom, stood up called for the deceased but he didn’t answer.  He was still calling to the deceased when the security officers arrived to help.  I asked the PBO if he had been drinking and he said yes, he had drunk four beers a

The Boat owner and the deceased were fishing on Dailey Lake starting at 1630 hours.  Because of storms moving in and out of the area, they had to go to shore several times to seek shelter.  At around 1930 hours the wind started to blow from the North.  The waves were about two to three feet high.  While trying to turn the canoe into the wind a large wave went over the side of the canoe causing it to capsize and sink immediately.  The boat owner had a life vest on and the deceased did not.  While in the water the boat owner last saw the deceased trying to make a life vest out of his wind breaker jacket.  The boat owner floated to the south end of the lake where he was able to get out of the water.  The deceased, a fishing boat captain of a 75-foot craft, was found on the 30th of July within 20 yards of the canoe.

Victim's kayak overturned upon entering Tumbleweed Rapid in the Alberton Gorge section of the Clark Fork River.  A PFD and helmet were worn and the victim successfully swam out of the kayak. Victim struck his head when kayak flipped, and was hanging on to side of rescue boat momentarily but slipped under water before the boat reached shore. Victim was recovered but was unconscious and CPR was unsuccessful.  Deceased was recovering from brain cancer and may of been a contributing factor to the fatality.

3 men were floating the Yellowstone River in a drift boat.  The boat struck an object in the river (rock?) and the boat began taking on water.  All three men were thrown from the boat.  One man held onto the boat and floated with it to an island and another man swam to the shore.  victim was unable to overcome the current that pulled him under the surface.   He was found at about 9:30 that evening in about 10 feet of water.

ON FEBRUARY 17, 2009, ABOUT 12:00PM, OPERATOR AND OCCUPANT LEFT RHODHISS ACCESS AREA FOR A DAY OF FISHING.  OPERATOR WAS OPERATING A 17 FT FIBERGLASS BASS BOAT POWERED WITH A 150 HORSEPOWER ENGINE.  AFTER LEAVING THE ACCESS AREA, OCCUPANT STATED THAT HE AND OPERATOR FISHED MOST OF THE AFTERNOON WHILE DRINKING A FIFTH OF CANADIAN MIST.  THEY TRAVELED TO CASTLE BRIDGE AND BACK STOPPING ALONG THE WAY TO FISH AND DRINK.  ON THE TRIP, OCCUPANT STATED THAT THERE WAS A LITTLE WATER COMING IN THE BOAT AND THEY WOULD HAVE TO BILGE IT OUT BY HOLDING THE WIRES FROM THE BILGE PUNP TO THE BATTERY.  WHEN OPERATOR AND OCCUPANT CAME BACK DOWN THE LAKE NEAR RHODHISS ACCESS AREA, OPERATOR STARTED TO OPERATE IN A CARELESS AND NEGLIGENT MANNER.  OCCUPANT STATED THAT OPERATOR WAS DOING DOUGHNUT TYPE MANEUVERS AND AT ONE TIME HIT THE SHORE AT A HIGH RATE OF SPEED.  AT THIS TIME, THE BOAT HAD TAKEN ON SOME WATER SO THE MEN DECIDED TO LEAVE.  OPERATOR DROPPED OCCUPANT OFF AT THE ACCESS AREA ABOUT 5:00PM.  OCCUPANT THEN BACKED THE TRAILER INTO THE WATER.  OCCUPANT STATED THAT OPERATOR HIT THE SIDE OF THE TRAILER, TRYING TO DRIVE THE BOAT ONTO THE TRAILER.  OPERATOR THEN BACKED UP IN A HIGH RATE OF SPEED, LOWERING THE STERN UNDER THE WATER LEVEL FLOODING THE BOAT.  OPERATOR THEN PUT THE ENGINE IN FORWARD GEAR AND BEGAN TURNING AROUND TO GET LINED UP ONTO THE TRAILER AGAIN.  AS HE WAS TURNING AROUND, THE ENGINE STOPPED RUNNING AND WOULD NOT START AGAIN.  AT THIS TIME THERE WAS ABOUT 8 TO 10 INCHES OF WATER IN THE BOTTOM OF THE BOAT.  OPERATOR THEN TRIED PADDLING TO SHORE WITH A RISHING ROD.  NOT BEING ABLE TO PADDLE THE BOAT, OPERATOR JUMPED IN TO SWIM TO SHORE.  THE BOAT WAS APPROXIMATELY 35 YARDS FROM SHORE.  OCCUPANT STATED THAT OPERATOR SWAM ABOUT 40 FEET AND SCREAMED "I'M NOT GOING TO MAKE IT".  OCCUPANT JUMPED IN AND SWAM ABOUT 10 FEET TOWARD OPERATOR.  REALIZING THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO MAKE IT TO OPERATOR, OCCUPANT SWAM BACK TO THE SHORE, TOOK HIS JACKET OFF AND LOOKED FOR OPERATOR.  OCCUPANT COULD NOT SEE OPERATOR.  OCCUPANT THEN JUMPED BACK INTO THE WATER BUT COULD NOT RESCUE OPERATOR.  THE RESCUE SQUAD FOUND THE BOAT ADRIFT ABOUT 600 YARDS AWAY ONE HOUR LATER.  THE BOAT HAD ABOUT 8 TO 10 INCHES OF WATER IN THE BOTTOM.
  ON FEBRUARY 19, 2009, ABOUT 12:00PM, OPERATOR'S BOPDY WAS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 40 FEET FROM SHORE AT RHODHISS ACCESS AREA.  

  THE TOXICOLOGY REPORT OF OPERATOR'S BAC HAS NOT COME BACK AT THIS TIME.

ACCIDENT ON LAKE TILLERY IN STANLY COUNTY ON MARCH 21, 2009.  CALL CAME IN ABOUT 22:00 THAT A BOAT HAD BEEN GOING IN A CIRCLE FOR OVER 30 MINUTES.  WHEN I GOT TO THE LAKE, THE BOAT WAS STILL GOING IN CIRCLES.  THE RESCUE SQUAD GOT THE BOAT STOPPED AND PULLED IT BACK TO A DOCK.  WE STARTED SEARCHING FOR THE VICTIM IN THE AREA THAT THE BOAT WAS FOUND.  A WOMAN CAME TO THE DOCK AND STATED THAT HER HUSBAND HAD WENT OUT ON A BOAT ANS WAS NOT BACK YET.  THE DESCRIPTION OF THE BOAT MATCHED AND IT WAS REGISTERED TO THE VICTIM'S UNCLE.  THE BOAT WAS FOUND 300-400 YARDS AWAY FROM THEIR DOCK.  I PUT A MEDIC AND A RESCUE PERSON IN MY BOAT AND BEGAN TO SEARCH ALONG WITH TWO OTHER RESCUE BOATS.  ON MY SECOND PASS THROUGH THE AREA WE SPOTTED THE VICTIM FACE DOWN IN THE WATER.  WE TOOK THE VICTIM TO THE DOCK AND HE WAS TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL IN THE AMBULANCE.  THERE WAS NO TREATMENT GIVEN DUE TO THE TIME IN THE WATER AND THE CONDITION OF THE BODY.

BROUGHT THE BOAT BACK TO THEIR DOCK AND SECURED IT AND CHECKED BOAT FOR ANY INDICATION OF AN ACCIDENT, BUT NONE FOUND.  THERE WAS THREE PFDS ON THE FLOOR OF THE BOAT BESIDE THE DRIVER'S SEAT.  THE VICTIM DID NOT USE ONE.  THE WIFE STATED THAT HE HAD 5-6 BEERS AND HAD TWO MIXED DRINKS THAT EVENING.  AFTER LEAVING THE AREA, I WENT BY THE HOSPITAL TO SEE IF THEY HAD FOUND ANY CUTS OR BRUISES THAT I DID NOT SEE, BUT THEY STATED THAT THEY DID NOT FIND ANY.  THE MEDICAL EXAMINER STATED THAT THE BAC RESULTS WOULD NOT BE BACK FOR ABOUT A MONTH.

THE RESULTS OF WHAT CAUSED THE VICTIM TO FALL OVERBOARD IS NOT KNOWN.  THE BOAT WAS UNSTABLE WHEN YOU STOOP UP OR WALKED ON IT.

ON JUNE 10, 2009, AT APPROXIMATELY 7:00PM, OPERATORWAS OPERATING A PWC WITH 2 CHILDREN ON BOARD.  THE VICTIM'S HALF BROTHER (7 YEARS OLD) WAS SEATED BEHIND THE OPERATOR.  THE VICTIM (DECEASED) , AGE 11, WAS SEATED BEHIND HER HALF BROTHER.  ALL WERE WEARING PFDS. The following is a description of a boating accident that occurred on June 14, 2009, at approximately 1900 hours.

The operator of Vessel 1 was driving in a northerly direction parallel to shore in order to drain some water that had accumulated in the stern of the vessel.  Once he had completed this, he made a turn toward the left and was hit by a wave.  The wave knocked the seated passenger over the starboard side of the vessel and into the water.  The operator took his hand off the tiller to attempt to grab the passenger and was also thrown overboard.  The passenger became frantic in the water and insisted upon removing his sweatshirt before he could begin to swim toward shore.   The operator attempted to assist the passenger, but the passenger began hyperventilating and pulled the operator under water several times.

A man fishing on a nearby jetty noticed Vessel 1 circling around with no passengers, and saw the two occupants of the boat in the water.  The witness called 911 and flagged down a passing boat.  The boat drove toward the men in the water and the occupants began throwing PFDs, lines, and life preservers to the men.  They observed that the passenger of Vessel 1 was under water and the operator was struggling to pull him up while keeping his head above water.  He was unable to reach any of the flotation devices that were thrown to him and began to sink underwater, so the operator of the passing boat drove up to him and the passenger of the passing boat used a boat hook to pull the operator of vessel one up by the hood of his sweatshirt.  The pulled the man into their vessel until the Hampton Fire Department arrived and transferred the operator of Vessel 1 onto the rescue boat.  The body of the passenger was found approximately one hour later by a witness on shore, who swam out to retrieve the body from the waves.

NH Marine Patrol was contacted at 0932 hours on May 2, 2009, regarding an overturned boat on Lake Winnipesaukee.  Two Marine Patrol officers responded to the scene.  A Dunkin Donuts receipt bearing a time stamp from that morning indicated that there had been at least one occupant of the boat.  NH Marine Patrol and Fish and Game conducted a search of the area in which the boat was found, which yielded some personal effects, including a tackle box.  Eventually two bodies were located in the vicinity, in about 25 feet of water.  The cause of death for each fatality was determined to be drowning.  While one PFD was found in the boat, neither of the deceased parties were wearing PFDs.

The following accident took place on July 15, 2009, at approximately 1710 hours.

The operator of vessel 1 was kayaking with a companion.  Each person was in their own vessel, in which PFDs were located, although neither person was wearing one.  The operator of Vessel 1 saw a baseball hat floating in the water and attempted to use his oar to retrieve it.  He apparently leaned over too far, which caused the kayak to capsize.  When his companion heard the operator of Vessel 1 yell, she jumped into the water to assist him, as she realized he was unable to swim and was becoming frantic.  She attempted to stabilize his kayak so he could hold onto it, but in his panic he was unable to do this and the kayak drifted away.  His companion then tried to get him to float on his back so she could swim him to shore.  She believes that he fainted at this time, and she attempted to pull him to shore; however, he was too heavy and she was being pulled under by his weight.  She let go and swam to shore to get help.  Several witnesses searched for the man until the local fire department arrived on scene to continue the search along with NH Marine Patrol.  The body was recovered the next day through the cooperative efforts of NH Marine Patrol (using side-scan sonar) and the NH Fish and Game dive team.

The following accident occurred on August 18, 2009, at approximately 1341 hours.

The occupants of Vessel 1 were all onboard when the operator stopped the vessel near the middle of the lake.  The operator decided to go for a swim off the stern of the unanchored vessel.  While he was swimming, the wind caused the vessel to drift away from him.  The operator began to tire and signaled for one of the occupants to bring the boat closer to him.  The occupant instead entered the water without a PFD to assist the operator.  Before long, both swimmers began to struggle.  Another occupant entered the water wearing a PFD and carrying an additional PFD.  One of the occupants who remained on the vessel started the boat and attempted to maneuver toward the three people in the water; however, the third swimmer yelled to stop the boat because the woman driving did not know how to operate the boat and the third swimmer feared that they would be run over.  The original operator (first swimmer) was able to return to the boat with the extra PFD along with the third swimmer.  The first swimmer drove the boat closer to the struggling victim, grabbed a line from the boat, and jumped back into the water to help the second swimmer, but he sank below the water before the first swimmer could reach him. 

A recovery effort was launched by NH Marine Patrol and NH Fish and Game, and the body was recovered two days after the accident in about 135 feet of water.

The following accident occurred on April 18, 2009, at approximately 1500 hours.

The three occupants of Vessel 1 began fishing on the morning of April 18 around 1030 or 1100 hours from the operator's canoe.  Around 1500 hours, the cell phone of one of the occupants rang.  Apparently due to the sound, the person seated in the middle of the canoe stood up, causing the canoe to capsize.  The occupant who stood up ended up underneath the capsized vessel, while the two other occupants were outside the canoe and began swimming it toward shore.  After about 30 minutes, someone driving by noticed the two men in the water and launched his boat to assist them.  He brought the two men to shore but the third occupant (under the canoe) was not seen.  The two injured parties were taken to the hospital and treated for hypothermia.  The third occupant was later found in the water and was deceased, as determined by the autopsy, due to drowning as a result of hypothermia.

Based on preliminary investigation, it appears that the Victim had set his anchor while rigging his fishing gear.  After laying the rods and reels out on deck, along with three personal flotation devices, he engaged the motor to move forward and retrieve the anchor.  Due to wind, or possibly slack in the line, the anchor line became caught on the lower unit of the outboard motor and was then caught by the propeller.  The engine then siezed and quit working.  The Victim appears to have then taken a pair of needle-nose pliers to the swim ladder location and attempted to release the line from the prop.  It is suspected that at some point he fell overboard.  Because the propeller had raised the anchor off the lake bottom, the wind caught Vessel 1 and it drifted away from the Victim.  The family of the Victim stated that he is a strong swimmer, however, it is suspected that he couold not catch Vessel 1 and was not wearing a personal flotation device in very cool water (approximately 50 degrees).

Vessel 1 left Bass Haven Marina to travel to Channel Grove Marina for fuel.  While in route to Channel Grove Marina, fuel odor was detected and Vessel 1 was stopped to check conditions.  Upon inspection, nothing was found and Vessel 1 proceeded to Channel Grove Marina.  After adding $50 in fuel to Vessel 1 and leaving the fueling area, Vessel 1 was observed to have black smoke coming from the exhaust.  Occupants aboard Vessel 1 discovered the fire and tried unsuccessfully to extinguish the fire with one fire extinguisher; a subsequent explosion blew the engine cover off of Vessel 1.  As a result of the explosion, all four Occupants of Vessel 1 ended up in the water.  Two of the Occupants were able to swim to shore under their own power; the Operator grabbed the inflatable PFD of the other Occupant and both went over the side of Vessel 1 where the Operator tried to support the Occupant in the water while trying to buckle the belt of the inflatable PFD.  The inflatable PFD failed to fire (auto inflation design).  The Operator and the Occupant were taken aboard a Good Samaritan vessel in the area and returned to shore where EMS arrived on scene.  The two Occupants on shore were transported to MacGruder Hospital while the Occupant with the failed inflatable PFD was air flighted to St. Vincent Hospital in Toledo; the Operator refused treatment for his injuries in order to ride along with the air flighted Victim to Toledo.  No alcohol involvement was suspected and there were no PFDs worn by any of the Occupants prior to the explosion.

BASED ON INFORMATION TO DATE:  On 10/4/2009 at approximately 10:50 am, P1 was operating vessel one on Cherokee lake near the Hwy 25E Bridge.  He was traveling upstream toward point 20.  Witnesses at Linda’s Lakeside Marina and Boat Dealership (P2) saw the vessel traveling past their business with the bow of the vessel pointing high in the air, thought the vessel’s plug may have not been installed, and then lost sight of the vessel as it continued up the lake. After leaving the sight of the dealership, the vessel capsized and the operator/victim entered the water.  A witness on a nearby personal dock (P3) stated he saw the vessel overturned with the “bottom showing” and saw a man in the water yelling for help.  P3 ran for help but during the elapsed time, the victim had drowned.  P4 and P5 from Linda’s Marina found the victim face down in the water and held him on the surface until rescue squad personnel could remove him.  The victim was transported to Lakeway Hospital where Grainger County Coroner pronounced death and routine blood draws were performed.  Later that afternoon, TWRA officers scanned the bottom of the lake with a side scan sonar unit and located the vessel located in approximately 50-60 feet of water approximately 190 feet inside the Grainger County line as based upon the river channel.  The vessel was removed from the lake bottom on the evening of 11/06/2009 and was examined for investigative purposes.  Blood results were obtained from the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation Crime Lab and all toxicology was found to be negative for drugs and alcohol.  An additional witness, P6, was contacted and advised he had spoke with the victim a bit before the accident while both were boating.  P6 stated he had encountered the victim and saw that P1's vessel was traveling with the bow high in the air and the stern just above the waterline.  Based on the investigation, it is believed the vessel was improperly loaded with no weight in the front of the vessel and the rear just above the waterline.  The vessel's plug was found installed when it was recovered from the lake.  It is believed that water spilled over the rear of the vessel while it was being operated, and the vessel quickly filled with water.  The vessel (being manufactured before flotation requirements) sunk rapidly with no internal flotation to keep it above water.  Testing was performed on the vessel and it was found to be loaded below total capacity, but the weight the vessel was carrying was at the rear of the vessel and not evenly distributed throughout the boat.

Four occupants average weight 200lbs each were near the bow of a 15 foot fiberglass boat with a 55hp Evinrude engine.  The 37 year old craft was in swift waters.  Witnesses describe the waters as "white capping."  Statements from witnesses and occupants indicate that the deceased was operating the vessel when it took on water, reportedly fragmenting the bow and capsizing.  Witnesses reported seeing vessel nose dive exposing the outboard motor to air, with the engine wide open, expelling the occupants.  The vessel then quickly sank.  Two men swam to shore, the owner and vehicle operator both drowned.  A green leafy substance and rolling papers were found on the body of the decesased, the vehicle owner.  Alcohol use was reported the night prior, but unknown at the time of accident.  BAC results still pending.  No occupants were wearing PFD's.

WAVE HEIGHTS WERE ESTIMATED TO BE 8-9 FOOT IN HEIGHT.  THE BOAT WENT UP A LARGE SWELL, DOWN INTO THE TROUGH OF THE WAVE AND WHEN THE BOW ROSE INTO THE NEXT WAVE, IT PENETRATED THE WAVE AND WATER FILLED THE TOP DECK.  THE WEIGHT OF THE WATER KEPT THE BOW SUBMEREGED AND THE BOAT LISTED TO THE STARBOARD SIDE.  ONE OF THE OCCUPANTS WAS WASHED OVER THE BOW AND ANOTHER OCCUPANT EITHER JUMPED OR FELL OVERBOARD.  THE BOAT EVENTUALLY RIGHTED ITSELF AND MOST OF THE WATER LEFT THE DECK.  ONE OF THE OCCUPANTS ON BOARD RETRIEVED HIS CELL PHONE AND CALLED 911 FOR HELP.  THE EFFECTS OF THE WIND ON THE BOAT CAUSED IT TO TRAVEL SOUTH AT A SPEED THAT PUT DISTANCE BETWEEN IT AND THE TWO PEOPLE IN THE WATER AT AN EVER INCREASING RATE.  THEY WERE ABLE TO KEEP TRACK OF THE PEOPLE IN THE WATER FOR A WHILE, BUT EVENTUALLY LOST SIGHT OF THEM.  APPROXIMATELY ONE HOUR LATER, THE BOAT FROM THE MARINA LOCATED THE PONTOON BOAT AND THE OCCUPANTS.  THE MARINA BOAT SEARCHED FOR THE TWO PEOPLE IN THE WATER FOR AN HOUR, LOCATING ONE PERSON, AND RETRIEVED HIM FROM THE WATER.  THEY EVENTUALLY FOUND THE OTHER PERSON.  HE HAD DROWNED.

On 01/16/10 at 7:00am, received a call about a boat accident on Maddox Bay Run-Out involving 8 duck hunters and that 2 of them became trapped inside the vessel when it sank.  Several officers responded to the scene.  All survivors were interviewed and the operator was given a BAC test.

After interviews were conducted it was determined that as they left the boat ramp at St. Charles V1 immediately had steering problems.  The operator worked on the steering cable for a short time and then advised that he had the problem fixed.  They continued to travel up the run-out for a short time when the occupants began noticing water accumulating in the bottom of V1.  As the water was being noticed, the operator began throttling down.  As V1 slowed water began entering at a high rate from the port side of the stern.  Operator advised everyone to grab a life jacket and exit the boat.  The survivors made their way to brush and hung on screaming for help.  Several boats nearby came to assist and took the survivors to a floating blind.  

On 01/17/10 several wildlife officers and law enforcement personnel from other agencies met to lift and recover V1.  V1 was taken to AGFC's Andrew Hulsey Fish Hatchery so that a reconstruction investigation could be conducted.  During the investigation it was determined that V1 is 17ft in length and has a 73 inch beam width.  The cab was not an original piece of equipment on V1 and it did not contain any internal flotation.  We obtained a brochure on Monark boats that were produced in 1970 and none meet the exact specifications of V1.  The closest are as follows:  Monark Commercial Fishing Boats Model 1652 -  which is 16ft and has a 73 inch beam rated for a 35hp motor and 6 passengers with a total weight capacity of 1,465lbs, Model 1852 -  which is 18ft and has a 73 inch beam rated for a 45hp motor and 7 passengers with a total weight capacity of 1,645lbs, and the Monark Belle (cab boat) which is 18ft with a 76 inch beam rated for a 50hp motor and 6 passengers with a total weight capacity of 1,445lbs.  V1 was occupied by 8 passengers and powered by an Evinrude 115hp E-Tech motor.  The weight of the passengers was approximately 1,660 pounds (weights taken from DLs) and the weight of the motor was 375lbs for a total of 2,035lbs.  This weight does not include the occupant's gear (guns, waders, blind bags, ammunition, decoys) or the dog due to most of it being lost during the accident or returned to the owners prior to being weighed.  We used certified scales and filled 5 gallon buckets and other containers with bricks to simulate the weights of the occupants onboard.  The weights were placed according to each occupant's seating position with 935lbs on the port side, 650lbs on the starboard side and 75lbs on the bow.  V1 was then put into the water and measurements were taken of the port side freeboard at the stern, which was 3 1/2 inches.

Therefore it was determined that V1 was grossly overloaded in both occupant weight and person capacity.  Thus making it extremely dangerous for any weight shift changes while under power or when powering down.  It was also noted V1 had no damage to the bottom of the hull which would have allowed water to enter through the hull.  During the reconstruction V1 was in the water for approximately an hour, at which time no water was observed coming into the boat.

USCG is investigating and charges are pending at this time.
