On 06/04/10 at approx. 17:30 the body of victim 2 was located by PCSO approximately 360 yards south of Camel Island next to the NLR shore.  While retrieving his body, other rescue units located the body of victim 1 near the shore of Camel Island in shallow water.

Both bodies were turned over to the PC County Coroner's office.  An autopsy was completed on 06/10/10 and it was determined that both subjects had drowned and the manner of death was accidental.  NOte: State recorded case as one accident invovling two boats.  It is unknown if one kayak caused the other to become involved in the accident.

Received a call from the Sheriff's Department of a possible boating accident at the Bank of Brinkley access to the Cache River Refuge on Bayou Deview.  Upon arrival, deputies advised they had located the victim in the water about 6 feet from V1.  The victim's truck was running and was backed into the water as if he was in the process of loading or unloading V1.  V1 was on the opposite side of the bayou, approx. 60 - 70 feet away and the victim was floating face down beside V1 between V1 and the location of the truck.  The only part of the victim on the surface of the water was the top of his head.  We are not sure if he was in the boat and fell out or if he forgot to disconnect the rear tie downs from the trailer and was doing so and stepped off the steep drop-off behind the trailer.  There is little to no current in this section of the bayou.

After further investigation, victim had left his house around 15:00 to go fishing.  His vehicle was discovered around 20:15 by three teenagers .  They reported the accident and were gone before I arrived.  The county coroner determined the cause of death as drowning.

According to statements, victim and his granddaughter (juvenile occupant) went fishing on one of his private ponds on his property.  Sometime later the occupant reported to subject that the victim had fallen into the pond and not returned.

On 08/19/10 a subject called 911 and advised that a sailboat (V1) had capsized on the other side of the lake and she could hear screaming.  Operator and occupants of V1 had launched at approximately 19:15.  V1 did not have a weighted keel or rudder underneath it.  According to witness statements they had only been on the water for approximately 20 minutes when a strong wind came from the South and capsized V1.  Weather conditions at the time of the accident reported that the wind was blowing out of the south at 10mph with gusts up to 16mph.  

Operator made it back to V1 and tried to upright it.  He stated he turned V1 over 5 times but it kept rolling back over.  He eventually made it to a small cove and was able to get the motor started and took it back to the dock of departure.  An observer from another dock had gone and picked the female occupants off the bank.  The operator stated he had motioned for subject2 to help get the other occupants while he was trying to get V1 upright and the motor started.

During this time, the other passengers were treading water trying to keep the victim above the water.  Both passengers said they were in the water 8 - 10 minutes and that the victim kept trying to pull them under while they kept him afloat.  Both passengers finally had to let go of the victim and swim to shore to save themselves.  

The victim's body was recovered on 08/21/10 approximately 300 feet from the shore line in 76 feet of water.

Operator (victim) and passenger were fishing on the Current River on 09/28/10.  They had motored up river and at approx. 2:25 they were motoring back down when they struck a submerged log.  Operator was ejected and V1 began circling out of control and struck the operator.  The passenger was finally able to make his way to the back of V1 and gain control.  By this time V1 had run into some floating logs and it took the passenger a few minutes to get free.  Once free, the passenger proceeded to go to the operator who had been treading water.  As he approached he noticed the operator had severe trauma to his facial area.  The operator started to go under and the passenger grabbed him by the back of his shirt and pulled him to the side of V1.  Operator put his right arm over the side of V1 and then went limp.  Passenger was unable to pull him into V1; he called 911 at 2:28 and held onto him until help arrived.  First responders pulled the boat across to a sand bar and when EMS arrived they confirmed the operator was deceased.

The incident began on 09/23/10 at approx. 10:30pm when the victim motored north from the Woodstock Landing to jug fish on the Old Mississippi River.  The next morning 09/24/10 at approx. 04:30am he was not back from fishing and his camping party began a search for the victim and found his capsized boat south of Ashbrook Landing.  This discovery led to an intense search and recovery effort which included the use of a cadaver dog.  On 09/25/10 at approx. 2:30pm the victim's body was recovered less than 100 yards from the overturned boat.

Upon inspection of V1 no visible damage was found.  The 25hp Yamaha motor was in forward gear with the tillar handle at idle speed, the cut-off switch was also attached to the motor.

USCG requested clarification on the cause of the accident.  The State responded, "Not a clue, no witnesses, no damage, nothing. Obviously he somehow fell out of the boat, whether he struck something, tripped in the boat, reached to grab something in the water and fell overboard, etc. we'll never know."

On 10/29/10 statement was taken from subject:  He and operator/victim had been putting a depth finder on V1.  Around 1400hrs Subject launched victim at the Hwy 165 boat ramp on Lake Enterprise and returned to victim's camp to wait on his arrival.  Around 1415hrs Subject became worried and went looking for victim with a party barge.  Subject found V1 heavily damaged at the bow but was unable to locate victim and returned to camp.  At approximately 1445hrs subject2 was motoring his vessel on Lake Enterprise when he came across the victim's body floating in the water.  He secured the body to a tree at 1453hrs and contacted 911.

Upon my arrival on scene, the victim had already been removed by the coroner.  The coroner was contacted and blood samples were requested for BAC testing.  The samples have been sent to the Crime Lab, results are expected in 4 to 6 weeks.  Also during examination water was found in the victim's lungs indicating he died as a result of drowning.

Inspection of V1 revealed the key was in the "on" position with the throttle 2/3rds of the way engaged.  The kill switch was found attached and laying beside the driver's seat giving the appearance that it had not been worn.  The motor was turned toward the starboard side.  V1 sustained heavy damage along the bow indicating a heavy impact with a fixed object.  A cypress tree was located east of the vessel with a large gash in the center of the tree mirroring the bow of V1.  The drivers console was damaged indicating the operator was ejected over the steering wheel.  Scuff marks and a damaged fish finder were also found on the console.  Victim was not wearing a life jacket.  A search of V1 revealed 3 PFDs.

USCG addition: USCG asked the State if a cause was assigned.  The State replied, "No witnesses, so we don't know what caused the collision. Medical examiner didn't find anything to indicate a medical condition cause. On the 2/3rds throttle, that was our assumption - that it indicated the speed he was traveling - again no witnesses and rescuers/retrievers did not touch or move anything in the boat, just towed it in."

Subjects were fishing on a private pond off Mt. Holly road near El Dorado.  Operator was operating V1 by paddle in the front of the boat.  He advised that the victim was adjusting his position in the boat and got off balance.  Victim then fell into the water.  When he did, this caused V1 to capsize.  Operator was able to make it to the bank where he called out to the victim but got no response.  He then went to a nearby house and told them to call 911.

On 3-22-11 this officer was notified by the Franklin County Sheriff's Office of two fishermen that had not returned from a weekend fishing trip.  I was advised their truck and boat trailer was located at White Oak Park on White Oak Creek, a tributary to the Arkansas River in the Ozark Pool.  A search for the bodies and vessel was conducted by responding agencies.  The body of V1's occupant was discovered on the south side of an island just north of the river channel adjacent to Citadel Bluff Park (GPS - N 35 28 16.9 W 93 56 24.1).  The search continued during daylight hours when the conditions were not too bad on the river with no success until the following Sunday morning (3-27-11).  During our search that morning, approximately 1 hour after a barge went by the operator's body was located in the water (GPS - N 35 28 08.0 W 93 59 05.4).  The Arkansas Game and Fish Dive Team located V1 with their sonar and were able to recover the vessel without incident (GPS - n 35 27 55.3 W 93 59 29.6).

V1 was a 20ft fiberglass hull with a 25hp tiller handle motor.  The bow light is permanently mounted to the bow but the stern light was inserted, there was also a spotlight mounted to the bow and all light controls were in the "on" position; the spot light was blackened where it had blown when it was submerged.  The spot light was also facing straight up, I believe due to the force of the water.  There was no flotation in the vessel and some of the supports had been removed.  The motor was in forward gear and the throttle was at 100%.  Victim 1 (operator) had a cell phone in his vehicle last used on Saturday 3-19-11 at 05:11PM  for 7 minutes.  The person called was interviewed and he advised that he had planned on meeting Op/Victim 1 to go fishing, but they never met and The person called never heard from him again.  The person called went to Op/Victim 1's residence on Sunday 3-20-11 and tried to call him without success.  The person called also advised it was not uncommon for Op/Victim 1 to be out on the river after dark.  This officer believes Op/Victim1 was traveling east, downstream, when water came over V1's bow swamping it Saturday evening after dark.  Op/Victim 1 never let off the throttle thrusting V1 downward until submerged.  The front seat Occupant/Victim 2 was washed from V1 and was unable to swim; Op/Victim 1 was submerged with V1.  V1 never turned over and was retrieved on the bottom of the river upright with the lower unit imbedded in the sand on the floor of the river.  The contents of the vessel were still inside, including a fishing pole, a shad throw net, a large rock, a trolling motor in a homemade forward compartment, loose sinkers and a tackle box just to name a few items that would have been washed out if V1 would have turned over at any time.  Two life jackets were found floating on the north bank in the area of the recovered vessel.  There was no bilge pump and the kill switch lanyard was still hanging from the motor.  

This accident was not reported to us until Tuesday (3-22-11) due to the fact the reporting parties stated it was not uncommon for these subjects to spend all weekend fishing.  Therefore, we cannot know for certain the time the accident occurred (but evidence does point to the fact it occurred after dark).

V1 was designed for trout waters and was not adequate for the Arkansas River.  The river flow was at 24,800 CFS on Saturday night (3-19-11).

On 4-7-11 this officer was advised of a boat (V1) reported to be floating without any occupants at White Oak Creek.  Once I arrived on scene, V1 could be seen on the east bank on a bluff line on the opposite side of an island from the boat ramp.  The entire White Oak Creek area is a shallow area which is a tributary to the Arkansas River.  When I approached V1, I could see the trolling motor was down and the front pedestal seat was in place.  Just to the south of V1 I could see the tip of a fishing pole sticking up out of the water.  When I approached the fishing pole, I could see the back of the victim just under the water.  The water was shallow (about 2 to 2.5 feet deep).  I brought his body into the boat; the victim's sunglasses were still on his face and there were no obvious abrasions on his head or hands and the shore line is rocky.  

The trolling motor was set on position 4 and his aerators were on after checking I found a few crappies in his live well.  There was no damage on his trolling motor and nothing out of place or suspicious in V1.  The victim's body was taken by the Franklin County Coroner and it will be taken to the State Medical Examiner to determine cause of death.  A BAC was also requested as required.  Inventory of V1 revealed a .410 bolt action shotgun in a rod box and a bottle of Vodka found under the driver's seat.

The Arkansas River flow was less than 300 CFS most of the day so there was no water affected back in White Oak Creek.

ME Report Pending.

At approx. 03:00 hours, the three teenage boys (occupants) were walking along the banks of Beaver Lake and found a 2-man Kayak (V1) tied up to the bank.  They decided to take V1 for a ride in the cove.  They made it about 15 feet from the bank and capsized.  Two of the boys made it back to the bank and could hear the victim calling for help.  Occupant 1 returned to the water to help his friend, but the victim could not be found.  The Benton County Dive Team was called to the scene an the body was recovered at 10:06 hours on 03/31/11.  

Upon interviewing the occupants, there was a very strong odor of intoxicants coming from them; however they denied any drinking.  Toxicology results from the victim revealed a .112 alcohol level. 

We were unable to locate the owner of V1 - no one claimed ownership in the area.

Passenger 2 called 911 and advised she was fishing with 2 friends below the I-430 bridge and that the operator had fallen overboard and not resurfaced.  V1 and occupants were located on a sand bar and were taken back to the boat ramp and occupants were checked out by EMS.  Statements were taken from both.  They both stated at approximately 18:00 they launched and went west (upstream) in Maumelle Creek.  At some point they motored east (downstream) into the Arkansas River and pulled into the South bank just above the Murray Dam approximately 200 yards above the Murray Lock wall.  Around 21:00 passenger 1 was near the bow of V1, passenger 2 was in the port passenger seat attempting to get a line untangled and operator/victim was sitting in the rear pedestal seat fishing.  They said they heard a splash on the starboard side and looked up and noticed operator/victim had fallen out of his seat into the water.  They suspected he had fallen asleep.  They advised that operator/victim had an orange PFD around his neck but it was not strapped around his waist.  They advised when he went into the water, the PFD came off and was floating in the water next to him.  Passenger 1 repeatedly threw a rope in the direction of operator/victim and yelled for him to grab the rope and/or PFD.  They advised he came up 3 times gasping for air then never resurfaced.

Both occupants were administered a breath test and they each blew a .00.  From 5/7 to 5/11 searches for the victim were conducted and his body was located on 5/11 exactly were the witnesses had stated he fell in.  

At the time of this report, no autopsy results were available.

Victim was floating on the Mulberry River with a group of people in an open-top kayak.  Victim became separated from the group for a brief period.  The group pulled up on the bank near Redding Camp Grounds.  Witnesses stated the victim had his PFD on before they got separated.  While waiting for him to catch up, the group saw the vicitm overturn and heard him yelling for help.  A witness headed to his location and according to his statement, the victim was holding onto his paddle, trying to keep his head above the water.  When he reached the victim, the victim let go of the paddle and went under water.  The witness tried diving into the water where the victim was last seen but could not locate him.  The rest of the group was able to recover the kayak and the victim's PFD down stream.  

Victim was recovered by the Arkansas Game and Fish Dive Team at a depth of about 9ft on 05/08/11 at 19:15 hours.

The group stated the victim had been drinking alcohol all day and could have been intoxicated at the time of the accident.  A blood sample was taken from the body once recovered and sent to the State Crime Lab.  To date, results are still pending.

Operator stated they had launched V1 at about 05:30 off the levee due to high water conditions.  They were going to do some fishing and camping.  They had not been in the water but about 10 minutes when water started coming over the front of V1 and it quickly capsized.  Operator and passenger 3 were wearing PFD's and were able to make it to the bank.  Passenger 2 and the victim remained with V1 and continued to float down river.  Passenger 2 stated the victim said he was going to try and get V1 to the bank and for her to hold on.  At one point Passenger 2 lost her grip on V1 due to the current pulling her away, but she was able to make it to the west bank.  She stated she didn't know how much further her husband (victim) was able to float downstream with V1.  

V1 was located the following day approximately 15 miles down river.  Upon inspection a small hole was detected in the floor of V1 toward the bow.  Operator stated that a screw driver had been punched through the bottom of V1 to drain water out; he said he had forgotten about the hole being there until they got it in the water and Passenger 2 said something about it.

Victim's body was recovered on 06/01/2011 about 12 miles down river from the accident site.  It is this officer's opinion the primary cause of the accident was due to overloading the vessel, coupled with the hazardous water conditions and failure to wear PFDs.

On 5/28/11 this officer received information from the White Co. Sheriff's Office about a possible boating accident.  Upon arrival at the scene a deputy informed us that both victims had borrowed V1 from V1's owner on Friday 5/27/11 at about 7:30pm to go put out some trot lines and yo-yo's.  They were supposed to return around midnight but never did.  Victim 2's father advised he noticed they hadn't returned from their fishing trip the next morning and he headed to the lake to look for them.  He said when he arrived, he had some fishermen take him out in their boat to look for his son and that he found V1 northeast of Reeds Access around the bend in the lake and it was turned over on a stump.  

He searched the entire lake for the victims but never found them.  We then launched our patrol boat and when we found V1 it was turned upright and was floating down the lake on the opposite side from where the father originally located it and turned it over.  V1 was full of water but no contents.  We towed V1 back to the landing where the owner identified it as the boat they borrowed.  I then asked the owner what they used to power V1 with and he advised paddles.  We launched a search to try and find the victims.  Upon searching we found a wooden box with yo-yo's inside, two black shoes, a can of Off and a pack of stink bait floating at the edge of the bank on the west side from where V1 was found.  Directly across from these items on the east side we located a white Styrofoam cooler.  Later that evening we found a white Puma shoe on the east side of the bank about 75 yards north from where V1 was found.  We also found a bucket with a rain jacket inside floating next to the bank where it appeared that someone had gotten out of a boat and consumed 5 beers and left the bottles lying on the bank.  Later it was discovered that the 5 beer bottles were the same kind missing from the victim's vehicle.  All items found were identified by the families of the victims as theirs. 

*When the White Co. deputy assisted the family with unlocking the victim's truck, he found a case of beer with around 13 beer missing from the box. 

The search continued with dive teams, sonar equipment, cadaver dogs, drag hooks and multiple agencies for the next 13 days.  On 06/09/11 at 7:00am the body of victim 2 was located floating next to the bank about 100 yards from where V1 was found; later that same evening at 6:54pm the body of victim 1 was located floating in the middle of the lake approx. 100 yards from where V1 was found.  Both bodies were sent to the Crime Lab for an autopsy and toxicology test.  Cause of death for both victims is listed as drowning but the toxicology is still pending on both at the time of this report.

At this point there has not been any witnesses located and it is impossible to really know what happened or to determine seat position they were in at the time of the accident.  We also don't know what time it occurred because there was no witnesses, the best we can say is that it happened between 7:30pm on 5/27/11 and 7:00am on 5/28/11.

I was notified of a 2 vessel accident in the area of Stokes Creek on Lake Hamilton; dispatch advised both operators were out of the water and located at 200 Edgewater Circle.  When I arrived on scene, operator of V2 was unconscious and being attended to by EMS.  Operator of V1 stated he had no injuries.  V2 had damage to the port side and the steering control system was disabled.  V1 had damage to the starboard side and bow.  V1 operator stated he was following V2 jumping the wake of the craft.  He stated he was following too closely when V2 turned sharply left.  V1 tried  to avoid the collision by turning hard to the starboard but was unable to and collided with V2.  V1 passed completely over V2 ejecting both operators.  V2 operator was transported to St. Joe ER where she later died from her injuries.

V1 was pulling a tube in the Ventris area of Beaver Lake.  While tubing the occupant fell off and the operator stopped the V1 to allow the occupant to maneuver back on the tube.  At that time the victim was sitting across from the operator, he stood up while V1 was stopped and dove/jumped from V1 into the water.  Victim did not resurface and after several minutes the occupants of V1 called 911.  

Witness statements all say the victim did not stike his head or struggle in the water, he simply dove in and never resurfaced.  They said the vicitm had been drinking earlier that day and was acting intoxicated and refused to eat, but they didn't believe he was really intoxicated and they thought he was just pretending to be drunk.

Victim was recovered by AGFC Dive Team 3 days later on 07/19/11.  There were no obvious signs of trauma to his body.  Toxicology results are still pending at this time.

On 05/27/11 a call came into the Ashley Co. Sheriff's Dept. stating a vehicle was backed up to the water's edge at the AGFC boat ramp at Stillion.  The keys were in the ignition and turned off.  The boat trailer was connected to the vehicle but was submerged under water and the trailer was empty.  V1 was floating upright lodged in the trees approx. 50 yards west of the boat ramp.  V1's gear shift was in reverse and the ignition key turned on.  The motor cowling was lying upside down on the back of V1.  The motor was not running.  Victim's body was located about an hour later 25 yards west of the boat ramp, about 25 yards from the bank in approx. 15 to 20 feet of water.

Operator and passenger/victim were fishing from V1.  At approx. 8:30pm they started to troll back to the boat ramp and operator stated he saw the victim drop his head like he had passed out.  Operator said he had just started to ask victim if he was alright when he slumped over and fell out of V1 on the port side.  The water in this pit is very clear and operator stated that as V1 went by the victim, he noticed he was floating just under the water with his back up and never attempted to swim and never appeared to be conscious.  Operator immediately jumped into the water and grabbed the victim before he could sink.  He stated he had left the trolling motor on and had to swim to V1 and was having trouble hanging onto the victim's body because of his physical size.  When he was able to reach V1, he was unable to lift the victim into V1 so he tied his body to V1 and used the trolling motor to return to the boat ramp.  Operator stated it took almost an hour to troll back to the ramp.  Once at the ramp, he called 911 for an ambulance.  Medical personnel attempted to revive the victim without success.  

Upon interview the operator stated he had witnessed the victim pass out several times in the past but wasn't aware of any medical problems or any medication he may have been on.  The victim's mother also confirmed that the victim had been passing out a lot the past few weeks.  

I delayed entering this report due to the fact we were waiting for the ME's report because all indications pointed to a medical condition.  The autopsy report still is not available, our Crime Lab can take as long as 6 months to finalize and release reports.  However, a request was sent to the ME asking simply for cause of death and he reported his determination to be drowing as the cause of death.  *We won't know if victim was on any drugs or medication until the autopsy report is released.

Upon arrival at the accident scene, I noted open containers of alcohol in V1 along with a red ice chest with beer in it.  The victim was also located inside V1 laying on the floor face up.  The victim was pronouced dead at the scene by the Garland County Coroner.  The victim had obvious signs of trauma to his upper right thigh conducive with a propeller strike.  Witnesses/occupants on V1 stated they were in the middle of the channel between the Hwy 270 river bridge and Blakely Dam when the incident occurred.  The victim was seated in the front of V1 and attempted to get up; he fell backwards off the bow of V1 and the operator was unable to put the engine in neutral in time.  The victim traveled between the port and center pontoon of V1, coming into contact with the lower unit.  The victim's right leg came in contact with the gear case and prop causing two large lacerations.  The occupants stated they could hear the victim screaming and attempted to throw him a PFD.  Two of the occupants jumped in the water and retrieved the victim.  Once the victim was onboard, they attempted to administer CPR until they arrived at Marine Land Marina.  The operator had a strong odor of intoxicants, slurred speech and bloodshot eyes.  He consented to a blood test and results are still pending.

On 09/27/11 at approx. 12:13pm we received a 911 call in reference to a possible drowing near the flood gates on Big Bayou Meto.  Upon officer arrival a witness stated he was fishing upstream from the flood gates when he observed the victim pass by going towards the flood gates at approx. 11:30am.  Witness stated the victim slowed down as he passed and then continued on towards the flood gate at a high rate of speed.  A short time later the witness decided to go back to the boat ramp and as he was approaching the flood gates he observed V1 floating empty next to the west bank approximately 250 yards upstream from the flood gates.  After a quick search the witness located the victim's hat floating in the bayou approx. 100 yards downstream from V1.  Upon my arrival at the scene, V1 was inspected and found the kill switch was missing, the motor was in forward gear and the throttle was turned wide open (tillar handle).  V1's contents were in disarray and up against the right side of V1.  A camo PFD was laying in the floor next to the operator's seat.  

Officers began dragging the area where the victim's hat was located and at 4:35pm the victim was recovered.  The kill switch lanyard was still attached to the left leg of the victim.  

No damage to V1 and it was also noted that the capacity plate had been removed.

Occupants and V1 were traveling south (downstream) on Glaze Creek. Operator stated there were 2 trees that had fallen down blocking part of the creek channel, the first one on the left side and the second was on the right side with about 20 yards in between them.  Operator stated when he went around the first tree, victim 2 fell over on him and pinned the throttle down and sent them into the trees where they struck small trees along the bank.  Operator stated he was going too fast even before victim 2 fell on him and that V1 wasn't turning very good.  Operator stated when they finally stopped, they were in the trees and victim 1 was hanging off the front of V1 with his head in the water and he was lying on his back; victim 2 was lying on top of some brush in the water on the port side with his head in the water and his back facing up.  Operator then got both victims back into V1 and performed CPR on both of them, got them breathing and called 911.  

Operator refused treated but was transported to the hospital by a deputy and voluntarily submitted to a blood/toxicology test.  The local hospital transfered victim 2 to UAMS Trauma center in Little Rock due to his condition.  On April 28, the Pulaski County Deputy Coroner advised us that victim 2 had passed away at 08:45am that morning.  An autopsy has been requested.

On 04-21-12 the Operator was given Miranda and interviewed.  He advised that they all had smoked marijuana about an hour before the accident and that victim 2 was the one who brought it and "rolled" it.  He also advised he had consumed 4 beers prior to the accident and that he also takes some prescription medication.  On 04-23-12 victim 1 was interviewed.  He stated he was kneeling down on the front deck looking toward the back of V1 and they had just gotten on plane and were leveled out; he then heard someone yell "Brush" and that was the last thing he remembered before waking up in the hospital.  He also stated he did not smoke marijuana with them while they were on the water, but that he and the operator had smoked some that morning around 08:00am.  He said he personally handed the operator 2 beers from the cooler and that he saw the operator get one of victim 2's mixed drinks from him; he said the cooler was close to the operator so it is possible he could have gotten more beer out of it without victim 1 knowing it.

Upon inspection of V1 it had a large hole ripped out of the port side of the bow and the trolling motor that was mounted on the bow was ripped off and missing.  V1's steering wheel was also broken off and missing.

Occupants attempted to "sail" across a section of Crown Lake in V1 which they had modified by sawing away part of the interior and adding a make shift mast and sail system.  Approx. 3/4 of the way across the cove, wind caught the sail system and caused the vessel to capsize.  Victim tried to swim out to grab one of the paddles but had trouble and swam back to the now sunken V1.  The passenger then swam out to get the paddles and when he turned around, the victim was gone.  Victim's body was recovered on 04/16/12 at approx. 07:30.

Operator of V2 began pulling four passengers on 2 tubes in a northeasterly direction.  Immediately upon bringing his vessel on plane, passenger/victim who was riding on one of the tubes fell into the water.  Operator of V1 was stopped roughly 100 feet behind V2 and upon seeing V2 leave, he took off to begin following them as the "pick-up vessel"; while attempting to get on plane he did not see the victim fall off the tube, thus striking her in the water.

Neither operator realized what had happened until they heard yelling/screaming from people aboard a nearby partybarge that witnessed the accident.  Both V1 and V2 immediately stopped and began rendering aid to the victim unsuccessfully.

Both operators were taken to have blood drawn for testing.  The samples were taken to the Arkansas State Crime Lab. Results from the toxicology tests are still pending; therefore the investigation is still open.

07-02-12 Toxicology results from the Crime Lab received.  Operator 1 had a BAC of .03 and Operator 2 had a BAC of .02; both under the legal limit.

According to witnesses, the following is the sequence of events:

A neighbor noticed the victim "bobbing" up and down in the water after he fell out of V1.  She told the victim's girlfriend to call 911.  At the same time, the victim's mother was entering the water to try and help the victim back towards the direction of V1 (they were approximately 150 feet from the shore).  The victim was noted as being a strong swimmer.  As his mother got close he was trying to swim away from her with a paddle in his hand.  She was able to reach and grab V1 and tried to put it between her and the victim asking him to grab hold of V1.  The victim continued to "bob" up and down in the water.  The victim's mother stated she remembers him gasping for air before going under.  She yelled to other family members to help her find him but by this point it was dark.  She swam back to shore with V1.

AGFC Dive Team was notified and responded the following morning.  Victim's body was recovered at 11:55am on 06/06/12.  The body has been sent to the Crime Lab for an autopsy and toxicology screens.  Results are pending; therefore there has been no determination or verification of the cause of the accident (alcohol/drugs are highly suspected).

09/17/12 - Autopsy and Toxicology results confirm Drowning as cause of death, BAC of .24 and positive results for Benzodiazepines and Cannabinoids.

V1 was cruising downstream turning starboard into a right hand curve of the channel.  V2 was cruising upstream turning portside into a left hand curve of the channel.  Both vessels were in a head on situation in a sharp curve.  V1 turned starboard to avoid the collision while V2 turned to port, thus resulting in the collision.  The collision occurred near the Union Co. shore of the channel.  The bow of V2 collided with the portside bow of V1 creating tearing breaks and deep gouges in V1.  V2 rotated on impact causing the starboard stern to rise and collide again with the port stern of V1.  After the collision V1 traveled a short distance to the Union Co. shoreline with the bow first stopping at GPS Coordinate N 33 11 22.1 W 092 10 26.2.   

V1 Operator was unconscious with injury; V1 Passenger 2 was alert with possible injury; V1 Passenger 3 was unresponsive; V1 Passenger 4 was unconscious with injury and V1 Passenger 5 was alert with injury.  None of V1 occupants were ejected. 

V2 rotated 180 degrees during the collision and traveled downstream to GPS Coordinate N33 11 22.0 W 092 10 23.3 on the Union Co. shoreline before stopping.  V2 Operator was not injured and V2 Passenger 2 had a possible injury.  Again, none of the occupants were ejected. 

Autopsy on the victim and all Toxicology test requests were sent to the Arkansas State Crime Lab.  Due to the backlog of cases at the Crime Lab it could take several months to get the results and therefore determine cause and close the investigation. 

Autopsy received 07/25/12; still waiting on Toxicology screens from operators.
 
01/12/13 - all Toxicology screens received.  Criminal charges have been filed but no court date set as of today.  Regardless, I am submitting this report for review as the deadline is this week.  The facts to be known are included in this report.

Both operators traveled to the Hogscald area from the Garfield area to find party cove.  They stopped near an old boat ramp to visit with some people.  As they took off again, V1 was in front of V2.  V1 stopped for reasons unknown; as he stopped V2's bow was high as he was attempting to get on plane.  V2 Operator then noticed V1 stopped just as he broke over on plane.  V2 was traveling at full speed when it struck V1.  V2 traveled from the starboard side to the port side causing multiple injuries to V1's operator and ejecting him into the water.  Operator of V2 jumped off and swam to the victim who was floating face down in the water.  He grabbed him and swam him to shore, where 911 was called by subjects on the shore.

10/05/12 - Autopsy and all Toxicology results received from the Crime Lab.  Autopsy confirmed death as accidental due to blunt force trauma and drowning.  ME noted injuries sustained would have been rapidly fatal in and of themselves; however since victim was probably still alive when he entered the water, drowning was stylized into the cause of death.

Toxicology results for deceased victim came back negative for alcohol and/or drugs.

Toxicology results for Operator of V2 also came back negative for alcohol and/or drugs.

Grossly Negligent Operation charges being filed again operator of V2.

On 9-4-12 at approx. 1:22pm, passenger called 911 to report her brother-in-law (victim) was missing in the water and gave their location.  She advised they had unloaded V1 at Bo's Landing boat ramp and traveled approx. 1 mile past the 412 bridge where they stopped and everyone got in the water to swim.  Other passenger/witnesses on V1 stated the victim complained of leg cramps once everyone was in the water.  Passenger advised he stayed with the victim until the cramping stopped.  He then advised that V1 had drifted away and once the victim stated he would be okay, he swam to retrieve V1.  Passenger was picked up by a passing boat and transported to V1.  Passenger then drove V1 back to where everyone was swimming and at that time he and the other passengers/witnesses/swimmers were unable to find the victim and that's when the 911 call was made.

Responding Emergency personnel established a perimeter in the location and the WCSO Dive Team was called.  The Dive team located the victim's body in approx. 16 feet of water.  The body was sent to the Crime Lab for an autopsy.  No visible injuries were located on the body and cause of death was listed as drowning.  Upon inspection of V1 there was no evidence of alcohol on the vessel and no reason to believe alcohol was involved.

According to the surviving passenger, he and the operator/victim had launched from South Shore Landing earlier that day to go fishing.  The passenger advised he thought his friend (the victim) operated V1 too fast and it scared him as they headed straight to the closed area of the lake where the water intake structure is located inside a restricted zone of water that is marked by buoys.  He stated he asked the operator to slow down but he refused to comply.  He said they fished inside the closed area about 10 minutes and when the operator cranked up the motor to leave, he decided to put on his PFD and he asked the operator to wear his also.  The operator refused and began to motor away heading east.  Passenger then advised V1 was going very fast and then for an unknown reason turned hard to the south then immediately turned hard back to the north and at that point V1 took on water and sank.  The passenger floated because of his PFD and he instructed the operator to calm down because he panicked.  He said he got him to calm down for a little while and was able to assist him in floating; while trying to swim to shore.  He said all at once the operator just started to sink down and he couldn't keep him afloat or save him.  He continued to swim toward the closest bank and once he reached the shore he took off his PFD to mark the spot where he came out; then proceeded to walk through the woods to the nearest residence and call for help.  
 
Searchers worked until 21:30 that night trying to locate V1 and the victim without success; the efforts had to be called off due to foggy weather conditions.  We began the search again the following morning at 09:30 using sonar equipment. Late that afternoon both the victim and V1 were located.  
 
The Coroner drew blood from the victim which has been sent to the AR Crime Lab and we are still waiting on the results.  Once V1 was raised, this investigator observed the motor was in gear and the throttle was in the wide open position.

On June 25, 2010 at approximately 0730, the operator fell overboard his 2010 Polarkraft fishing boat and drown.  The victim began fishing Pana Lake at approximately 0500.  His wife spoke with him at approximately 0700 prior to leaving for town.  At approximately 0800, his wife tried to contact the victim several times but was not successful.  the wife began a ground search at approximately 0900 and continued to try and make contact with the vicitm via cell phone.  At approximately 0915, subject contacted Pana PD to report an unoccupied boat he observed earlier in the morning.  subject indicated he observed the boat at approximately 0730, drifting in a cove off of 1100N road.  At approximately 1015, the wife made contact with subject2 to see if the victim had made contact with him.  subject2 indicated he had not spoke with the victim and began searching for the victim via boat.  At approximately 1100, subject2 located the boat unoccupied with the engine off.  subject2 tied the boat to the nearest dock and called 911 to report a missing person.  The boat was recovered in the cove west of 650E and north of 1100N, Shelby county.  Conservation Police Officer (CPO) arrived on scene at approximately 1242.  Pana PD was already on scene securing the area.  At approximately 1250, Shelby County Dive Team arrived on scene and began searching for the victim via side scan sonar.  I, CPO, arrived at approximately 1300.  I was briefed on the situation and I began interviewing the wife and her son. The son indicated his father fished the cove, where the boat was recovered, often, next to a large, underwater tree.  the son indicated that the vicitm would only stay out fishing for 2-3 hours at a time and was not a good swimmer. the wife indicated that the victim did not normally wear a life jacket.  

After completing the interviews, I photographed the vessel and found the trolling motor mount broke in half.  There was no damage to the prop or shaft of the trolling motor, indicating something heavy fell on top of the trolling motor.  Shelby County Dive Team along with Effingham County Search and Rescue and Illinois Department of Natural Resources, searched for the subject throughout the day and into the evening.  The searched resumed at 0700, June 26, 2010.  Effingham County Dive Team and Moultrie County Dive Team joined the search.  At approximately 1100, the victim was confirmed to be in the water approximately 30 yards off the shoreline near the location of the boat.  At approximately 1120, the subject was recovered and the Shelby County Coroner took possession of the victim at approximately 1143.  An autopsy will be conducted to show cause of death.  At approximately 1300, there was a multi-agency debriefing and agencies were free to disperse. 

Agencies involved:  Illinois Department of Natural Resources; Shelby, Moultrie, and Effingham County Dive Teams;  Effingham County Search and Rescue;  Pana Police;  Pana Fire;  Pana Ambulance;  Shelby County Police;  American Red Cross.

Supplementary reports will be filed at a later date.

On 07/05/2010 at approximately 10:15 p.m., I overheard a conversation via radio through Clinton County Sheriff's Department regarding a possible missing boater on Carlyle Lake.  I called Army Corps of Engineers Ranger via telephone regarding the situation.  Ranger informed me that the subject had rented a pontoon boat from Dam West Marina around 9:00 a.m. on 07/05/2010.  Ranger told me that the owner of the boat rentals, called Clinton County Sheriff, to report his boat was never returned to the marina.  The Army Corps of Engineers Rangers went out to look for the boat and discovered it adrift just North of Allen Branch boat ramp between points 5 and 6.  The Rangers returned to the dock to pick up Clinton County Deputy,  to go with them to inspect the boat.  They did not find the renter of the boat anywhere on board or around the boat.  The radio was playing loudly, the door was open, and the ladder was down in the water.  The subjects keys, two open containers of beer, nine full bottles of beer, his clothes, and his wallet were on board the boat. The boat, IL registration IL8219 RB, was towed back to Dam West Marina, where it was pulled into one of the slips to be inspected.  Ranger told me he would call back if he heard any word of locating the victim.  I called my boss, Sgt., and informed him of the situation and possible missing boater.  I informed him I would meet with the Corps in the morning between 6 and 7 a.m. and begin a search for the victim.

On 07/06/2010, I arrived at the Clinton County Sheriff's Office at approximately 6:30 a.m. and met with the father, and his foster mother at one point in his life, a good friend of the family.  Investigator from the Clinton County Sheriff's Department reported that the victim had rented a pontoon boat at Dam West Marina at approximately 9:00 a.m. on 07/05/10, for the day.  According to the boat owner, the victim had returned to the marina at approximately 10:15 a.m. to retrieve something from his vehicle then left the marina again in the boat.  According to his girlfriend, the victim was supposed to meet her and her family back at the marina at 12:00 p.m. to pick them up.  the girlfriend showed up at the marina at approximately 12:00 p.m., but the victim failed to show up to pick them up.  she said she had spoke to victim on the cell phone and he seemed fine and said he would hang around in the area of the marina until noon.  she said she returned to the marina at 2:00 p.m. and again at 4:00 p.m. to wait and gave the Sheriff her number in case the victim returned.  Sheriff arrived at the office and we decided to begin a search of Carlyle Lake and begin where the boat was located the night before.  The family decided they were going to meet and walk the land to help search the area.  I met with Army Corps of Engineers Ranger and we began searching the area near the boat with the side scan sonar unit.  We searched the area until 1:30 p.m and broke for lunch.  Sgt. and CPO resumed the search the rest of the day without finding the vicitm in the water or on land.

I received a phone call from a subject at approximately 6:10 a.m. on 07/07/10 asking if I would come to the Marina Galley to speak to the family on the course of action for the day.  I arrived at approximately 6:30 a.m. and at approximately 6:35 a.m. received an IWIN message on the computer from Clinton County Dispatch that the body had been found floating near where the boat was found abandoned.  I informed the family of the situation.  We retrieved the victim from the water at approximately 8:35 a.m. on 07/07/10 and turned him over to the Clinton County Coroner,  at Allen Branc...

On Sunday July 17, 2011 Natural Resource Officer I (NRO) was on night patrol at approximately 12:30 a.m.at Antelope lake in Graham County, Kansas. NRO had completed a vessel safety inspection with a vessel at the boat ramp. NRO returned to his truck and noticed that there appeared to be a vessel on the water with no lights on. NRO used binoculars to see that there was a silhouette of a vessel out on the water with no visible lights on. NRO walked to the edge of the water approximately 40 feet from where the truck was parked. There NRO found a fishing pole in a rod holder with a metal bell attached and a line in the water. The pole was about 10 feet from a camper that had a boat trailer with no boat on the trailer. At approximately 12:30 a.m. NRO tapped on the pole in order to ring the bell in a simulated manner of a fish striking and taking the baited hook. During an approximate ten minute period NRO tapped on the pole enough to ring the bell three times. No one appeared in order to claim the pole or check on it in any way.
NRO then walked back to his truck and repositioned the truck by turning it from facing east to facing south in order to direct the headlights toward the vessel on the water. NRO then activated the emergency lights in order to get the attention of the vessel occupants. NRO then got out of the vehicle that was now 14 yards from the shore and returned to the edge of the water. After waiting a few minutes with no visible activity or response from the vessel, NRO then used the spotlight on the truck in order to direct more attention to the occupants on the vessel. Then one person was visible on board the vessel and NRO called out to the person and told them to bring the vessel in to shore. The person on the vessel responded that he could not because his boat was stuck. NRO instructed him to get his vessel unstuck and bring it over to the shore. During this time wife came out of the camper. While Operator was working on moving the boat NRO and Wife conversed about how the fishing has been. Wife also indicated that the pole in the rod holder in the shore was hers. She also said that to her best guest that Operator had been stuck for about an hour.
While standing next to the camper with Wife NRO witnessed Operator try to rock the boat and used a long pole to attempt to push the boat off of the stumps that it was stuck on. Operator attempted to get the vessel moving for a few minutes and then he began to remove his clothing and slid off the left side of the vessel into the water. Operator began to swim around for a moment and then stood up in the water a few feet from the vessel. He then asked for the spotlight to be turned off so he could see. NRO turned off the spotlight and emergency lights leaving the headlights on in order to illuminate the water for Operator to work on moving the vessel. NRO then remained in the truck and began to fill out citations for both Operator not having lights on and for Wife having an unattended fishing pole. NRO then heard Wife calling out to Operator and Operator yelling for help. NRO got out of the truck to see what was going on, and saw that Operator had been swimming in to shore and had made it about half of the way. At that point Operator appeared to no longer be swimming toward shore and appeared to be treading in the water to remain afloat. NRO retrieved a rescue throw rope from his vehicle and made several attempts to get the rope out to Operator. However, the rope was not long enough to reach out to where Operator was. Operator went under and drowned.

On Friday July 15, 2011 and approximately 1403 hours the Shawnee County Dispatch received two 911 phone calls reporting a possible missing kayaker on the Kansas River near the weir.  The first caller advised when he arrived at the weir there was a kayak turned upside down in the water below the weir and no one was around and no vehicles were parked in the parking lot.  The second 911 caller was working at the Topeka Water Treatment Plant which is located on the south side of the Kansas River, south of the weir.  Second caller reported that he had seen an individual kayaking down the Kansas River and when Second caller looked back to the river a few minutes later he saw the kayak turned upside down in the water below the weir and that the person in the kayak was nowhere to be seen. Three of Second caller'S co-workers also saw the kayaker when the kayaker was up-stream of the weir but none of the co-workers saw how the kayaker went over the weir. Second caller also reported seeing an individual standing on the weir, talking on a cell phone.  The person Second caller reported seeing standing on the weir was later identified as being the other 911 caller. 

The Topeka Fire Department from Fire Station 11 arrived at the weir at 1414 hours and the first officer with the Topeka Police Department arrived at the weir at 1420 hours.  
  
Shortly after they arrived at the weir the firefighters from fire station 11 recovered the kayak but no one was found in or around the kayak.  At 1437 hours the Topeka Fire Department recovered a body from the Kansas River approximately ½ mile downstream (east) from the weir.  When found the body was face down in the water and only a small portion of the deceased back was visible.  Also when found the deceased was not wearing a personal flotation device (PFD).  The body was then loaded in the boat and taken to the boat ramp by the weir.  At 1555 hrs a Shawnee County Corner arrived at the scene.  

The deceased was later identified.  

On July 30, 2011 Natural Resource Officer (NRO) with Kansas Department of Wildlife, Parks and Tourism contacted Detective with the Topeka Police Department.  Detective was investigating the drowning death of victim.  Detective told NRO that the drowning death of Victim was being considered an accident and no foul play was suspected.  Detective continued to tell NRO about the incident.  

Detective stated on July 15, 2011 he was dispatched to investigate a possible drowning.  When Detective arrived at the scene he was told the deceased was located in the Topeka Fire Department boat at the boat ramp.  The deceased was an adult white male which looked to be in his mid-30s.  The deceased had short brown hair and a receding hairline.  The deceased was shirtless and wearing blue swim trunks and grey gloves on his hands.   Detective also saw a blue and white kayak which is believed to belong to the deceased.  The two hatches on the kayak were closed and in the In compartments were various items which included a small tackle box with fishing gear, glow sticks and a small cooler which contained a can of Dos X beer, a can of Coca-Cola and a bottle of Gatorade in it.  Detective did not see a personal flotation device (PFD) on the body or with the items of the kayak.

Due to no witnesses actually seeing the accident happen it could not be determined how or why Victim and his kayak went over the weir.

See separate narrative report.

V-1 with two occupants on board was underway with a 15 h.p. outboard heading west in a narrow canal on the south side of 30th street in Vero Beach.  This was the first time in a boat for both the operator and passenger.  They were testing the motor, which they had just acquired, and mounted on V-1.  After driving east a short distance on the canal, the operator slowed, and turned V-1 to head back to the west.  Just after the 180 degree turn, while V-1 was still accelerating , V-1 struck a submerged log.  The impact caused V-1 to capsize to starboard, sending both occupants into the water.  Neither occupant could swim. Neither occupant was wearing a PFD.  No safety equipment was recovered during the investigation.  The passenger was able to grab the floating gas tank, and stayed above the surface of the water for a short amount of time.  The operator was able to reach the north bank of the canal, and exit the water.  The passenger lost his grip on the gas tank, slipped below the surface of the water, and drowned.; The operator tried to remove the shoes of the victim to help him swim, but only managed to remove the victim's right shoe.  The victim tried to remain afloat by holding onto the gas can, but lost his grip, and slipped below the surface of the water and drowned.  The preliminary autopsy findings showed the cause of death consistent with drowning.  No other injuries were noted during the autopsy.

On July 26, 2012 at approximately 7:00 pm a single vessel incident occurred on the waters of Salt Run in the City of St. Augustine, Saint Johns County, Florida. The incident involved a 17 foot open style vessel occupied by two males. While changing speeds the two occupants were ejected overboard and into the water. One occupant was rescued from the water and the other was located after a three hour search deceased. 
ACCIDENT ANALYSIS

PRE-ACCIDENT

On the evening of July, 26th 2012 Occupant and Operator decided to go for a boat ride and maybe try and catch some fish. It was warm and sunny with an ocean breeze and an outgoing tide when they left from where Occupant docks his vessel (V1). The two were just going to go on a short trip across Salt Run with Operator operating V1 from the dock. Operator started out at a slow speed in V1 as they left the dock. When Operator was approximately 150-200 yards away from the dock he accelerated V1  to get  on plane. V1 suddenly lurched hard to port taking both Operator and Occupant by surprise.

ACCIDENT

Occupant seated directly in front of the starboard side operators console was ejected over the starboard side of V1 as it turned hard to port.
Operator seated at the operators starboard side console was ejected out near the port stern as V1 turned hard to port.
Both occupants were ejected into the water without injuries.

POST-ACCIDENT

Occupant and Operator were treading water after being ejected from V1. V1's engine shut down about 20 yards from where they landed in the water. V1 was north of both their positions and drifting north with the outgoing tide. Operator panicked and started thrashing about yelling he was going to drown. Occupant tried to calm Operator down telling him to remove some of his clothing and just to tread water. Occupant swam for V1 but couldn't catch up with V1. 
Two people were on Conch Island and heard Occupant yelling for help. Good sam used his jet-ski to rescue Occupant as he was floating north in Salt Run with the out-going tide. Occupant told Good sam about Operator and Good sam had other good sam call 911. Good sam and his brother assisted Occupant with searching for Operator. Rescue personnel arrived on scene and took over the search for Operator.
Operator was found in Salt Run in approximately three feet of water face down deceased after approximately a three hour search using water and air assets.

CONCLUSIONS

Based on evidence, statements and information gathered to date, I have concluded the following; there is insufficient information,evidence to support any conclusions indicating that Occupant and/or Operator may have violated any navigation rules or boating safety Florida Statutes during the operation of V1 at the time of the accident.  Furthermore, my inspection of V1 did not reveal any evidence of damage, equipment/machinery malfunctions, or general deficiencies of the vessel itself.  This concludes my investigation.

On 8/27/12 at approximately 2212 hours, the Escambia County Sheriff's Office (ECSO) received a report (CAD# 12-CAD203530) of a missing person. Operator took his personal watercraft (PWC) out fishing earlier in the day and did not return. The caller reported Operator likes to take his PWC out to the Massachusetts and fish. Operator was driving a green Ford van with Florida and towing a PWC trailer with a Florida license plate of ASHQ62. The PWC was a 1995 Yamaha with a Florida registration number of FL 4737 JN. On 8/27/12 at approximately 0903 hours, Operator' cell phone was "pinged" by Verizon. Verizon placed the cell phone approximately seven miles offshore south of the Pensacola Pass/Perdido area at coordinates of N 30.11.272 and W 87.26.270. At approximately 0933 hours, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) was contacted. FWC pilots could not assist in the search by air due to bad weather. USCG continues to search by air and water. The family of Operator removed the van and the PWC trailer from the Sherman's Cove Marina. At approximately 1500 hours, the USCG calls off the search due to bad weather from the approaching hurricane.

There was no reported search activity on 8/28/12.

On 8/30/12 at approximately 1547 hours, a Good Samaritan walking along the beach outside of Sherman's Cove Marina finds a "kill" switch believed to be for a PWC and turns it in to the USCG. At approximately 1757 hours, subject reported a body that had washed up near Marker 5 just inside of the Sherman's Cove Marina. Officer of the ECSO arrives and begins report and interviews. The Medical Examiner arrives and takes body.

The PWC has not been recovered at this time
.
This incident occurred in Escambia County.

On May 31, 2012, at approx 1400 Hrs, a man (later identified by his fingerprints) was found floating in Lake Okeechobee. The man was found missing his head and part of his left arm. The helicopter found a kayak floating approx 2 miles from where the man was found. After further investigation Operator had bought the vessel a few days prior. According to witnesses he launched his kayak from the Pahokee marina two days earlier in bad weather. His vehicle was also found at the Marina the next day. The missing head and arm was taken off by alligators post mortem, and the cause and manner of death is unknown. 

On May 31,2012, I of the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission was dispatched to the scene of a floating deceased victim. The deceased victim was found floating at Port Mayaca,Marin County, on May 31, 2012 at 1400 Hrs. Martin County Detectives took possession of all evidence found, and were the lead detectives on the case. Tri County Medical Examiners took over Possession of the body.

On June 12, 2012, I filled out a 24 hour death investigation report, but it has not been determined at this time if this is an alligator attack or boating accident. Detective informed me they had exhausted all their leads, and were turning this case over to me. Detective emailed me all of her findings. Murder and Suicide have been ruled out. 

On June 26, 2012, Detective and I met at the Martin County Sheriff's Office so he could turn over all evidence in their possession over to me. Detective also gave me his report, and a disc containing the photos from the scene. 

I logged all found property including the vessel into evidence at the Jupiter compound.  

On July 5, 2012, I talked to the Medical Examiners office reference the death investigation. He informed me he is attempting to retrieve fingerprints of the unidentified man from the Military records Department in St Louis, Missouri. He has also notified the family of the deceased. They are working with him to try and identify the unidentified body.

On July 16, 2012, the Medical Examiner office advised me the unidentified man’s name. The family has been notified. This accident is now being investigated as a boating accident. 

On August 8, 2012, after determining the accident is in fact a boating accident, I submitted another 24 hour report indicating a boating accident had occurred on May 31,2012.

On October 24, 2012, I received the autopsy report reference death. The Manner and Cause of death were both unknown.

On 10/8/12, at approximately 0330, a small vessel with 2POB left Haulover Marina in Miami-Dade County to fish.

The vessel headed south on the ICW and stopped to fish under the Haulover Bridge for approximately 30min.  The vessel then headed offshore via the Haulover inlet. The conditions were small craft advisory and extremely rough with an outgoing tide.  The vessel attempted to travel through the inlet when it began to take on water.  The water entered the vessel from the transom and began to flood the boat and overwhelm the bilge pump. The occupants began to bucket water out of the vessel but they were not successful. The vessel swamped and the two occupants found themselves in the water. 

Both occupants attempted to swim to shore however one was unable to swim and eventually went under the surface and drowned. The other occupant was able to make it to shore and called for local police.

At approximately 1330, the victim was located approximately .5 Miles North from where the vessel began to take on water. The victim was recovered from an sandy bottom in 15ft of water by police divers. He was identified by next of kin and transported to the M.E. Office.

The vessel recovered was a 15' flats boat with a low transom design. Vessel design, rough seas and outgoing tidal conditions all contributed to this accident.;

On 9/2/12, at approximately 2150 hrs, Operator1 was operating PWC (V1) at night on the ICW heading southbound near Sea Isle Marina in Miami, FL when he collided head-on into another vessel (V2) which was heading northbound. V2 was operating at an idle speed through the channel when the collision occurred. The impact caused Operator1 to be ejected forward and hit the anchor bracket on V2, causing a severe chest injury. Operator1 died on scene as a result of his injuries. V2's navigational lights (red and green) were not mounted in a manner that comply with regulations listed in the US Coast Guard Navigational Rules. According to the definitions listed in Rule 21, the "sidelights" (red & green) must be mounted in a manner which allows them to display an "unbroken light over an arc of the horizon of 112 degrees and so fixed as to show the light from straight ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on its respective side." The type of navigational lights mounted on the bow of V-2 were intended to be mounted on a vertical surface. In this case, they were incorrectly mounted on a horizontal surface. V-1 was traveling head-on toward V-2, which still permitted him to see V-2's incorrectly mounted navigational lights. No action will be taken on V-2 for the accident as the incorrectly mounted lights were not a factor in this case. The cause of the accident was that the V-1 operator was intoxicated over the legal limit and was operating a PWC at an excessive speed at night time.  Operation of a PWC after dark is illegal.; Operator1 He was going approximately 30 MPH When he struck V2. He was ejected and collided with the anchor bracket of V2 causing a deep puncture wound to his chest area. He died due to injuries caused by the impact.

I, RFC, member of the CIRT, was contacted by SGT while off duty on May 8, 2010, at 1949 hrs. in reference to a boating incident on Lake Russell involving two bass boats. The incident occurred around 1900 hrs, that day; SGT briefed me on the situation and told me CPL was on the scene. I contacted CPL who briefed me further on the case, he relayed to me the boats would be held as evidence at the US Army Corps of Engineers impound yard at Richard B. Russell Dam. I arrived at the Corps impound yard on May 9, 2010 at 1300 hrs., I met with CPL at the boats, we inspected vessels, witness statements, and safety equipment. We set the impacting vessel as vessel #1, we set the impacted vessel as vessel #2. From there we separated each vessel into quadrants and surveyed all possible damage from the collision. We then took measurements and photographs of the damage and transfer marks of each vessel, from there we accounted all necessary safety equipment was onboard each vessel. I then diagramed the damage on each vessel and we completed a photograph log. From there I went over the scene field notes CPL had obtained and began entering information of vessels and victims onto the Georgia Boating Incident Form. 

In reviewing victim's and witness statements along with the physical evidence, transfer marks, skeg tracks, and propeller damage from the boating incident on Lake Russell occurring the 8th, day of May, 2010 at around 1900 hrs. The evidence clearly indicates the operator in vessel #1 failed to follow "The Rules of the Road". In conjunction with scene diagram figures 1-4, vessel #1 in an overtaking situation, failed to keep out of the way of vessel #2. This indicates that the operator of vessel #1 failed to follow Rule 13, according to Updated Comdtinst M16672.2D, US Dept. of Homeland Security, United States Coast Guard, Navigation Rules, International -Inland. It is also clear from witness statements, vessel #1 failed to use safe speed in the congested area of the Elbert Ramp, a violation of Rule 6, according to Updated Comdtinst M16672.2D, US Dept. of Homeland Security, United States Coast Guard, Navigation Rules, International-Inland. 

Vessel #1 engaged vessel #2 at the port side rub rail just behind the passenger seat. Vessel #1 advanced onto vessel #2 traveling across vessel #2 from the port passenger seating location causing extensive damage to both vessels before exiting the starboard side of vessel #2 forward of the operator console location. During the collision vessel #2 passenger and operator suffered serious injuries' from the direct impact of vessel #1 hull. The passenger of vessel #2 suffered a broken left clavicle, broken facial bones, teeth knocked from the sockets, a bruised back, a laceration to the forehead, borken ribs and collapsed lung. The operator of vessel #2 suffered a broken left clavicle and bruising. The impacting vessel #1 passenger from the impacting vessel #1 was ejected from the vessel #1 clear of the collision. Rule 13, overtaking a vessel was broken by vessel #1 while overtaking vessel #2 causing the two boats to collide. By operating in a manner causing collision of vessel #1 with vessel #2, the operator of vessel #1 failed to adhere to Rule 8 of the Updated Comdtinst M16672.2D, US Dept. of Homeland Security, United States Coast Guard, Navigation Rules, International-Inland. After reviewing all of the evidence and information in this case, the vessel collision could have been completely avoided had the operator of vessel #1 followed the "Rules of the Road". The operator of vessel #1 is at fault causing the boating incident on May 8, 2010 on Lake Russell.

On May 16, 2010 at approx 1900 hrs I was on saltwater patrol in the Isle of Hope area, just across from the Isle of Hope Marina when I noticed a boat adrift near the dock and two people in the water.  At least three other people were in the boat and were motioning me to come over.  As I headed in their direction the two swimmers climbed out of the water onto the dock and also began motioning me to come over.  Once I was close enough I could hear them shouting that someone had just fallen out of their boat and had not resurfaced.  My side scan sonar was already in operation and I immediately got my vessel in place to begin a search.  I advised GSP of the matter and asked that SCMPD be contacted.  Over the next few minutes I was told by the witnesses that the missing person had fallen in from the vessel very near to the dock and was advised of an approximate location that he entered the water.  I continued to scan the area with the sonar equipment starting in the location of the victim's entry and expanding as much as possible around the docks and parked vessels.  The area was very congested with many boats moored to each side of the slips.  With the help of a good samaritan, captain of a yacht moored at the marina, I continued to search visually and with side scan in and around the dock and moored vessels from my vessel.  Over the next few minutes many personnel from SCMPD, local Fire Department, USCG arrived as well as other DNR Rangers.  Corporal, Rangers  got in with me and aided in the continued search.  We identified several targets of interest and relayed their location to the Chatham County Dive Team.  Each location was investigated and nothing found.  We continued to scan the area for several hours with no luck.  After the dive team terminated their search for the night, Chatham County Marine Patrol Officer and I conducted a search of the area with the body drag with no results.  Ranger arrived at approximately 5 am (5/17/10) to relieve me.  The body of the victim (b/m) surfaced and was recovered around 0730 on 5/18/10.

"     On 6/2/12, at approximately 17:30 hours, I, Corporal received a phone call from RFC in regards to a boating incident on Lake Juliette. RFC said that a sailboat had capsized and that an occupant of the boat had been taken to the hospital. RFC explained to me that Victim had been on the sailboat with her husband when the incident occurred. RFC went on to say that EMS personnel were administering CPR on Victim when the ambulance left the boat ramp and that he would advise me later on her condition. A short time later I received another call from RFC advising me that Victim was pronounced dead at the hospital.  RFC told me the details of the incident and I decided that I would wait until the next day to meet with him and begin the investigation. RFC also told me that he would be in possession of the sailboat when we met.
     On 6/3/12, I met with RFC at the Upson County Sheriff's Office. RFC had the 11 foot sailboat with him in the bed of his truck. RFC explained to me again what Operator  said happened. According to Operator, he and Victim arrived at the lake around 14:30 hours and were on the water by 15:00 hours. They sailed a short distance from the dock and decided to return to shore. Operator said that the wind caused the boat to capsize sending both Operator and Victim into the water. Operator went on to say that Victim panicked and said that she couldn't breathe. Victim continued to have difficulty breathing and she was taking on water from the waves. Operator attempted to give Victim her inhaler to help with her breathing, but Victim panicked and wouldn't use it. Operator took the inhaler from Victim and attempted to administer it, but that didn't work either. Two persons in kayaks, a man and a woman, heard the cries for help and approached them. Their attempts to help were hindered because of the wind and more people in kayaks arrived. With the additional help, Victim was placed on one of the kayaks, but she fell off. Someone in a motor boat pulled up to the incident and carried victim to the boat dock where an ambulance was waiting.
     I photographed the Sundancer sailboat to show its size and also to record the information off of its capacity plate. I called Operator and spoke with him briefly about the incident. While speaking with Operator, I made arrangements for him to meet with RFC later in the day to make  a written statement.      On 6/5/12, I made contact with Assistant Coroner and requested a copy of the coroners report for my case file. Coroner told me that because the treating doctor at Macon Medical Center had found water in Victim's lungs, the cause of death would be listed as a drowning. Coroner also told me that the GBI Crime Lab had also denied an autopsy due to the presence of the water in Victim's lungs.

Conclusion of incident:
     It is my opinion that the boating incident which occurred on 6/2/12 and resulted in the death of Victim was the result of the boat capsizing. After they were in the water, it became difficult for them to reboard the vessel and Victim was having difficulty breathing. According to Operator, at some point during the struggle Victim slipped out of her PFD and submerged below the surface of the water. Attempts to resuscitate Victim were unsuccessful and she was later pronounced dead with a cause of drowning.
     This report is based solely on the information made available to me at the time of the investigation and may be changed or modified with the discovery of new information.

After many hours, Officer, with the assistance of other investigating officers, concluded the following:
 
At approximately 1:30AM on May 19th, 2012, vessel1. was heading northbound on plane in O'Connell Slough without any navigational lights when it collided nearly head-on with vessel2, who was heading southbound and not equipped with any required lighting. The boat was found floating near where the victims body was discovered.

Investigator's Report:
49 year old male was fishing alone in a 12-foot aluminum v-hull vessel on May 23rd, 2010.  He disembarked at approximately 1900 hours from the west side of Magic Reservoir.  He reported missing to the Blaine County Sheriff's office on May 26, 2010 at approximately 2000 hours.  He was found deceased on the west shoreline on May 27, 2010 at 0745 hours.  For an unknown reason, victim ended up in the water, probably near the west shoreline.  Victim was partially wearing a type III personal floatation device.  It appeared he either attempted to put PFD on once in the water, or had it on but not secured properly.  The reservoir level had been dropping due to irrigation demand and it is believed that the dropping water levels left his body beached.  The vessel was found on the east side of the reservoir.  It was capsized and appears to have been blown over to the location by the prevailing winds.  The vessel was damaged from being slammed against the rocky shoreline by wind and waves.  It is unknown for certain what had transpired, but it is likely that the victim may have stood up in the vessel and fell overboard or the vessel capsized from weather and he ended up in the water.  It is likely he struggled to get to the west shoreline and succumbed to drowning, hypothermia, or exhaustion.

Their plan was to put in at Corbin Park and paddle to the pleasantview bridge downstream a mile and then go to work at Buck Knives.  Operator told the sheiff's office that they put the canoe in at a point near the up river parking area where there was a calm pool of water.
