One of the passengers was helped out of the river by subjects on the north shore, while the other passenger (the victim) was swept down stream by the current.  The victim was last seen approx 200 yards down stream from the bridge trying to swim up to the north bank.  The operator was later assisted by another boat to the north shore.  The operator stated he and the victim had been drinking while floating and fishing down the river thru out the day.  An alcohol bac test was not performed.

News:
A powerboat operating on Lake Pend Oreille slammed into a rock embankment killing one and injuring three, the Bonner County Sheriff's Department said.
Officials said 44-year-old male died of injuries from the crash on Friday after the boat hit the embankment about 11:20 pm a few hundred yards south of the entrance to a marina at Sourdough Point.
The Bonner County Daily Bee reported that the male lived in the Oden Bay area of the lake near Sandpoint.
Marine patrol said the 18-foot powerboat was traveling at a high rate of speed.
Officers said a man and woman remained hospitalized on Saturday, and another man was treated and released.
Their names have not been released.
Police say it's unclear who was operating the boat.
Report:
Vessel was traveling from the Pend Oreille River to Garfield Bay, Lake Pend Oreille, in company with a second vessel.  The second vessel was leading the transit and made a mistaken turn into Bottle Bay.  The trailing vessel attempted to catch the lead vessel and filed to clear the point leading into Bottle Bay.  Vessel impacted shoreline in a planing mode severely damaging the bow, hull and partially separating the deck and hull sections.
Four people were on board the vessel, three were injured and the fourth was deceased.

4 adult males along with 5 young children were boating on the American Falls Reservoir just north of Mexican Cove.  Male subject #1 was relieving himself off of the bow of the boat, male subject #2 pushes subject #1 overboard, subject #1 cannot swim so subject #2 jumps in the water to save him, subject #1 is struggling and also #2  subject #3 jumps in the water to help #1 & #2, all three subjects are struggling so subject #4 jumps in the water to help all three subjects.  Subject #4 has a life jackt but does not have it on, only in his hand.  All four subject then disappear under the water and do not resurface.  Minor child calls 911 to advise that all four adult subjects went out of the boat and have not came back up yet.  Witnesses are as follows, age 3 female, age 9 female, age 8 female, age 8 male, and age 3 male.

News:  Officials in north-central Idaho say a 35-year old Wisconsin man has drowned while rafting in the Lochsa River.  Idaho County Sheriff says the man from Sun Prairie, Wisc., died Saturday afternoon when the raft he was in hit a rapid and all four people fell into the river.  A new release issued by the Sheriff's office Tuesday says two of the occupants were able to get back into the raft and a third was able to make it to shore.  A kayaker that was accompanying the group threw the victim a rope, but he was unable to reach it and was swept down river by the current.  Two kayakers pulled the victim out of the water down river and began CPR until paramedics arrived.  However, he could not be revived.

Report:  5 people in a raft and 2 people in kayaks were floating down the Locsha River when they hit a big lateral wave on the right side, knocking all 5 occupants out of the boat and into the water.  3 people were able to get back into the raft and 2 (1 male and 1 female) were swept down river.  The 2 people were fairly close together in the water and both were struggling to keep their heads up.  The female saw a rock sticking out form the left bank with an eddie before it and knew if she could get to it she could get out.  She yelled at the male to swim, but he was swept past her and down river.  The female was able to reach the rock and climbed out of the water.  The 2 men in the kayaks come to make sure the female was okay.  One of the kayakers took off down river after the male.  The kayaker saw the male victim and paddled hard and fast to catch up to him.  While chasing the male victim, the kayaker noticed that the victim was unresponsive so he yelled at him multiple times.  The victim went over many rocks and under water after each rock.  When the kayaker got close enough he reached out and grabbed him and get him to shore where he immediately started CPR on the unconscious victim.  After approximately 90 - 120 of CPR they could not revive him.

Call came in of people in the water from a capsized vessel just south of Steck Park by the train trestle on Brownlee Reservoir.  Rescue from four different jurisdictions responded to assist.  Two victims made it ashore, two were still missing.  After approximately two hours of searching the little girl was found approximately 5 miles downriver floating face up, she was wearing a floatation device but it was not Coast Guard approved.  Marine Deputies recovered the victim and transported her to medics on the Oregon side but they were unable to resuscitate her, she was pronounced deceased on scene.  The search was suspended until morning.  I spoke with the operator of the boat and asked what happened, he advised that they had left Steck Park and preceded south they got just past the train trestle when they decided to throw the anchor and fish.  The operator advised that as soon as the anchor caught something it pulled the front of the boat down and under the water forcing all the occupants out of the boat.  This part of the river is very swift as it is a pinch point in the river.  I asked if they had life jackets in the boat and he advised no, he stated the little girl was wearing one but that no one else had one.  I asked how everybody was seated in the boat and he stated that he was the operator in the back the little girl and her dad (still missing) were seated side by side in the middle of the boat, and the other passenger was sitting in the front of the boat.  The boat was a fourteen foot outboard with a ten horse power motor.  I asked if they had left before or after dark, and he advised after dark.  I then asked what kind of lighting did they have and he advised a lantern and a couple of flash lights.  The search for the missing man continued for several days following the accident.  On June 12, 2011, a fisherman called dispatch and advised they could see something floating in the water, dispatched notified Deputies in the area.  Idaho Fish and Game responded and notified that it was possibly the drowning victim.  The Sheriff responded and the victim was recovered and transported back to Steck Park where the County Coroner retrieved the remains.  The Sheriff notified the family.

On 6/16/11 at 14:47 the Custer County Sheriff's Office received a 911 call from a boat passenger using a satellite phone.  The passenger advised the dispatcher that there had been a fatality at the Boundary creek area on the Middle Fork of the Salmon River.  He said a private float trip had launched and a 47-year old male was deceased.
The Custer County Marine Deputy was notified at 14:58, she in turn contacted the Middle Fork River Ranger.  The River Ranger informed the Marine Deputy that a boat had gone through Murph's Hole 7 miles down from the Boundary Creek Boat Launch.  This hole, at 6 foot, has violent hydraulics that is known to wash people out and flip boats.  The river level at this time was 6'6", 9,000 cfs according to the USGS.  The water temperature was approximately 38 degrees ferenheit.  The River Ranger and the Custer County Coroner flew in to retrieve the body of the 47-year old male victim.  Upon the arrival of the plane, the Marine Deputy inpected the body and found the victim had been wearing a full wet suit, including boots and gloves.  He had splash gear over the suit that had been removed, and a type V adult white water PFD on.  The PFD fit properly and was in good working order.
The Marine Deputy interviewed the passenger.  He said that he had been on the boat with the victim, rowing, when the accident occurred at approximately 13:15.  The passenger stated that the current pulled them into the waves above Murph's Hole and they ended up sideways.  They hydraulics were violent and seemed to hold them there for a brief time.  When the boat passed thru the hole, the operator looked back and saw the victim in the water.  He appeared conscious but was not tying to swim.  He said that the victim was in the water for around 5 minutes before he was retrieved down river by others in their party.  The passenger had taken over the oars and was caught in a back eddy for several minutes.  He saw CPR being performed on the victim down river.
The passenger said that the victim (the operator) had changed to a different oar lock system and was nervous about running the Middle Fork.  The victim had experience on multiple rivers and had been white water rafting since he was 15 years old.
After interviewing the river ranger the following day, it was discovered that the victims boat was an W 1550 NRS 15'5" inflatable self bailing white water boat.  The equipment was newer and in good working order.  All the boats in the group were loaded heavy.
On 6/19/11, the marine deputy interviewed a witness that had been in the lead boat (the victims boat was the second one behind them).  The witness indicated that she was watching the victim as he approached the rapid.  The victim was a little right of where he should be, and stopped rowing above the hole.  The victim had the oars in the water several feet above the start of the rapid but was not rowing.  The boat went through the hole and was not quite straight.  The witness said that the victim "just rolled out of the boat into the water".  The witness stated that he was under water, after falling overboard, for no more than 20 seconds.  It was indicated that while he was in the water he did not attempt to swim and was "just looking around".  At one point the witness tried to grab the victim, but missed.  A throw rope was thrown right next to him but on neither occasion the victim did not attempt to grab on.
The witness said that she watched as the victim truned sideways with the river, his head went back with his eyes open.  Boaters yelled at him trying to get him to shore.  A doctor was on the trip, he performed CPR for approximately 45 minutes.
location: Middle Fork of the Salmon Rive, ID

description:
KTVB.com - The Elmore County Sheriff's Office says a Utah woman has died in a rafting accident on the Middle Fork ot the Boise River near Atlanta.  Emergency crews responded to the accident scene Monday night.  The body of the 34-year-old Riverton, Utah woman was not recovered until around 9 am Tuesday.  The victim was attending a family reunion in Atlanta and six of her family went for a rafting trip around 6:30 pm.  Their raft got lodged on a stump.  While trying to dislodge it, the raft got caught on a strainer log and the victim became trapped under the log and drowned.  No one else was seriously injured.  The Middle Fork of the Boise River is flowing at nearly 5400 cubic feet per second, more than twice the average for this time of year.
Report:  While rafting donw the Middle Fork of the Boise River, raft became lodged on a tree stump.  All occupants got out of raft to dislodge it.  The victim was caught in current and carried down stream and became lodged under a fallen tree that was submerged under water and drowned.

News: Tuesday evening before 6 0'clock Bonneville County Sheriff's Offica and Jefferson County Sheriff's Office responded to the reservoir.  They found the two girls in the water.  One was airlifted to Eastern Idaho Regional Medical Center while the other was taken by ambulance.  Bonneville County Sheriff's Office said the two boats were in an area of the reservoir called The Narrows.  He said there are blind corners in the area and that's where the two boats side-swiped each other.  Bonneville County Sheriff's Office said there were at least six people in the two boats.  They were all located and deputies were talking to them to understand exactly what happened.  subject expected to have more information sometime Wednesday morning.
Report:  A 1996 Glastron boat occupied by 7 people pulling a tube had made a right hand turn.  Two 14-year-old girls were on the tube.  The tube swung out over the wake.  Another 1993 boat occupied by 9 persons cmae around a corner near the shoreline.  The tube and the 1993 vessel then collided.  The passengers on the port side of the tube collided directly with the metal trim on the starboard side just under the gunwell at the bow of the boat causing severe head trauma.  The passenger on the starboard side of the tube "glanced" off the portside of the bow of the 1993 vessel.  Both girls were ejected from the tube and were found laying face down in the water. Investigation is still pending due to the number of witnesses in the case.

News:  One man died after an accident on the North Fork of the Payette River Sunday afternoon.  Emergency teams from Valley County and Boise County along with Life Flight responded to the scene at about 12:34 p.m.  The 55-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene.  The Valley County Sheriff's office says the victim was considered an expert kayaker.  The Sheriff's office says the victim was kayaking in class V rapids between Jacob's Ladder and the Jaws rapids when he flipped over.  He was able to right the kayak, but flipped a second time and did not get upright again.  another kayaker pulled the kayak to shore, but efforts to revive him failed.

Report:  Vessel #1 was operating in Class V rapids when the operator was rolled over and forced to right himself over and over again.  A fellow kayaker came to the aid of Operator #1 and towed him to shore.  The good samaritan noted Operator #1 was not conscious when he was towing him.  Once ashore, CPR was performed until Operator #1 was pronounced dead.  During the investigation it was noted Operator #1 suffered blunt force trauma to the head in this incident.

News:  Officials in northern Idaho say a 38-year-old Lewiston man riding a personal watercraft on the Snake River died after coming too close to shore and hitting land.  The Nez Perce County Sheriff's Office tells the Lewiston Tribune that the victim was thrown from the vessel and suffered severe head injuries in the crash that occurred at about 7 p.m. Saturday.  Officials say the victim was traveling north on the Snake River and entering the Captain Lewis rapids when he apparently turned suddenly toward the Idaho shoreline.  The county Sheriff's office says the death remains under investigation.
Report:  Victim was operating a 2001 Polaris Virage waverunner, north on the Snake River at the top portion of Upper Lewis Rapids.  Witnesses reported the operator was traveling at a high rate of speed and was in the shallow area near the Idaho shore.  Witnesses state the operator of the waverunner made a shart right into the shoreline.  Witnesses state the operator was thrown from the waverunner and landed in the rocks at the shoreline.  The wave runner continued across the rocks about 40 feet and came to rest.  The operator received severe head trauma and died at the scene.

News:  The Kootenai County Sheriff's Office announced Thursday that they retrieved the body of a missing boater in Lake Coeur d'Alene.  The 24-year-old was reportedly at the back of the pontoon boat Tuesday night when he fell off into the water.  Officials say he was found between Carlin and Crescent Bay by a side scan sonar in about 130 feet of water around 3 pm.  The body has been turned over to the coroner and an autopsy will be done in Spokane.  Alcohol is believed to be a factor.  Kootenai County authorities said the man fell into the water just before 8:45 PM Tuesday.
Report:  A 24-year-old male was a passenger in a pontoon boat.  The victim needed to go to the bathroom, so the operator stopped the vessel and put it into neutral.  While the victim was on the rear deck of the boat by the engine, he fell in.  The victim was not able to swim back to the boat, and the operator attempted to rescue him, but was having problems keeping himself and the victim above water.  The victim ended up drowning in approx 130' of water.  The victim was recovered by the Kootenai Conty Dive Rescue Team and the Kootenai County Sonar Team on September 1st at approx 1500 hours.  A closer inspection of the victims remains showed no obvious signs of trauma or injuries.

On June 29, 2011 at approxmiately 1440 hours, deputies received a call from dispatch about a rafting accident on the river.  Deputies were also advised that there were 5 occupants in the boat and all were accounted for, one was being given CPR.  The operator of the vessel indicated the raft flipped over in the Lochsa River and everyone was swimming to the shore.  The operator said at one point he could see his friend (the victim) swimming 2 - 5 minutes aftter the raft flipped and then went unresponsive.  The operator said he caught a ride from a passer by on the highway down river to get the victim.  The operator said he jumped back in the river to bring the victim to the shore.  The operator said it was about 5 - 10 minutes after the raft flipped that he finally got the victim to the shore where an EMT that was on shore administered CPR for about 45 minutes to an hour.  EMT was unable to rivive the victim.

At 12:52 hrs dispatch received a 911 call from male who was parked in a small parking lot on the north shore of Mud Lake.  The male had noticed a boat approximately on half mile out from the north shore.  The male began to watch the boat with his binoculars as the water was rough due to the strong winds.  The male advised he saw a male passenger on the boat and described it appeared he was working on something towards the rear of the boat.  The male stated the boat appeared to be sinking as it was listing to the stern.  The male then saw the passenger move to the bow, stand up on the bow and jump into the water feet first.  The passenger began to float further away from the boat.  At this time the male called 911 to report the incident.  The male stated shortly after he called 911 the boat flipped over capsizing, he was unable to relocate the passenger out on the water.  The passenger was located at approximately 14:00 hours face down in the water by a helicopter.  The passenger was pulled from the water approximately 200 yards northeast of the boat location at 14:09 hours.  CPR was immediately started at 14:13 hours, the passenger was transferred from the rescue boat ot the ambulance.  It was noticed that when the passenger was pulled out he had a blue type 3 US Coast Guard approved adult life vest, properly worn.  The passenger was transported to EIRMC hospital and placed on life support.  The passenger died on 4/5/12 when he was taken off life support.  The boat sunk in 7 feet of water with bow up out of the water.  The boat was recovered on 4/9/12 the key was in the on position, throttle was in neutral position.  The bilge pump electrial unhook from the battery, unknown if it came unhooked during the tow and recovery from the water.  All plugs were still in, the boat has three drain plugs one on each side and one in the middle on the lowest part of the boat.  The two side plugs are used to drain water out of the fuel tank and battery compartments.  Due to high winds the waves were hitting the stern and filling the boat with water.  The male witness advised the boat was facing in a north east position.  The wind was blowing from the southwest, causing the waves to directly hit the stern coming over the lowest portion of the boat.  The wind speed was sustained at 25 mph with gusts to 40 mph.

On April 21, 2012 at approximately 10:14 PM Custer County deputies received a call of a missing rafter.  It was stated that 2 men were rafting down the Salmon River, when they hit a tree causing their raft to flip.  One of the men got out of the river but they could not find the other man.  The man that got out of the river, made it to the Mormon Bend campground where campers called for help.  Deputies arrived at the campground an asked the man what had happened.  The male indicated that the last time he saw the victim was when their raft flipped after being hung up on strainers in the river, he yelled at the victim to swim to shore.  After the man arrived on shore, he could not find the victim.  So he went to the campground to have someone call for help.  Authorities searched the river for several days.  On April 25, 2012 at approximately 12:43 pm, the body of the victim was discovered, and then later retrieved from the river.  Both men were under the influence of alcohol, and neither man was wearing a PFD.

News:  Custer County sheriff's deputeis are attempting to recover the body of a missing rafter in the Middle Fork of the Salmon River.  Ther sheriff's office said the unidentified person fell from an inflatable river raft at Velvet Falls, about 5 miles downstream from the Boundary Creek boat launch site at approximately 8:30 pm Sunday. The sheriff's office said 14 people were rafting.  They used four inflatable river rafts and seven inflatable pontoon boats.  They reported the Middle Fork River is running at an average 8 miles per hour and a height of 6.5 feet.  It is continuing to rise daily.

Report:  Two people in a 16' Airline Cataraft on the Middle Fork of the Salmon River entered left in Velvet Falls with the victim at the helm.  As the victim was rowing through Velvet Falls he fell out of the boat.  A second boat in the party picked up the victim down river.  The victim was unconsious, one of the passengers (a parametic) on the second boat performed CPR for 55 minues.  The passenger on the boat was unharmed.

News:  A Meridian woman has lost her life after trying to save another in a rafting accident on the Payette River.  Chief Deputy with the Boise County Sheriff's Office says 44-year-old Victim was with three other adults and two children Sunday afternoon when a woman fell out of their boat.  Victim jumped into the river to try to save her.  Victim's boyfriend then jumped in also to try to save both women.  The man and woman that originally fell into the water were able to get safely back in the boat, but the group lost sight of Victim.  The group had launched at the Danskin boat ramp and had just hit rapids seven miles northeast of Crouch.  Deputy says Boise County Deputies and water rescue crews were called about 4:30 p.m. to the area on the Banks Lowman highway.  Garden Valley Fire and Swift Water Rescue began to search for Victim about an hour later.  Deputy says shortly after that Boise County deputies got word that some citizens found a woman, pulled her from the river, and attempted CPR.  The Boise County Coroner pronounced her dead at the scene near the Alder Creek Bridge, about five miles downstream from where she had fallen out of the boat. One of the children in the raft was Victim's six-year-old son.

Vessel #1 was traveling north bound on plane at night.  For unknown reasons, vessel #1 made a left turn and struck the west side of Salmon Reservoir (rock wall) head on causing severe damage and injuries.  The operator of the vessel was killed in the crash.  There was no alcohol or drugs involved.  Witnesses on the vessel saw the operator with the steering wheel in his right hand and a flash light in his left hand just prior to the crash.

A victim running Chipmunk rapids on the Priest River in an inadequate raft.  The raft overturned.  Victim went into the water and was not seen for 2 days.  The victim was recovered by the Bonner County dive team.  The victim was not wearing a personal floatation device.

Canoe traveling down river when it takes on water in rapid.  Operator leaves vessel but stays with it and tries to get to shore with the help of a raft.  The operator has massive heart attack due to exertion and dies.

News:  A 63 year old male died in a boating related fatality while canoeing the North Fork of the Payette River at the rapid "Wet Spot".  The canoe was swamped in the rapid and the male was forced to ride the rapid with his PFD hanging onto his canoe.  As he was trying to get his canoe out of the river current with the assistance of a raft, he collapsed.  By standers removed the victim from the river and started CPR.  The Valley County Sheriff's office patrol and marine division responed along with the Cascade EMS.  Efforts to resuscitate the victim were stopped after more than an hour.  A subsequent autopsy showed the male suffered a major hear attack due to exertion.

Three people were riding in a small 8 foot raft.  As they came around the bend they saw a tree had fallen in the river.  The tree was approximately 70 feet long.  As they rounded the corner, the occupants could see the tree and realized they were going to hit the tree.  They started paddling and struck the tree approximately 10 feet from the top.  One occupant was thrown over the tree, one landed on the tree and the third person grabbed a branch upstream of the tree.  The branch broke and the subject was swept under the tree.  The subject did not resurface.

News:  One woman is dead and a man is in the hospital after their boat capsized on the Snake River. The Bonneville County Sheriff's Office said it happened 6 to 7 miles north of the Byington boat ramp on the South Fork near Table Rock Road.  Sheriff said around 3:15 p.m., the boat hit a log and ejected Deceased victim and her husband, Husband.  Sheriff said Husband was able to swim to shore, but Deceased victim was missing for some time.  Deceased victim became tangled in the ropes that were attached to the boat which took her under, Sheriff said.  An AirIdaho rescue helicopter spotted the boat and Deceased victim, but the sheriff said she showed no signs of life after being pulled from the water.  Husband was taken to the hospital, where he's being treated.  Others who spent the day on the South Fork said the high winds made for some rough waters.  The boat has been recovered and removed from the river.

News:  Rescue crews have pulled the body of a 59-year-old man from Gem Lake, Bonneville County Sheriff said.  A woman and operator1 were riding jet skis around the lake when they both fell off, according to Bonneville County Lieutenant.  Operator was piloting the jet ski, according to police.  A nearby boat circled around to see if the two needed help, but only found the woman, County Lieutenant said.  Operator's body was found in the south portion of Gem Lake, south of 65th and near the hydroelectricity plant.  According to the investigation, the victim was not wearing a life jacket, but instead had it wrapped around the handlebars of his PWC.   The woman was wearing one.  A dive team arrived on scene around 6 pm. Bingham County arrived with its sonar technology at 8 pm.  By 8:30 they had located the victims body and removed it from the water.

Two men were duck hunting in a 10' aluminum jon boat on Medicine Lake. The operator was sitting on a bench seat at the stern. The second male occupant was sitting on the middle bench seat. Both had their shotguns on board and Victim was actively looking to shoot a bird .  While sitting, Victim took a shot over the starboard side of the boat. The recoil of the shotgun knocked Victim off the seat toward the port side, near the stern, at Operator's feet. The boat rocked, but stayed afloat. A short time later, Victim took a second shot over the starboard side. Again, the recoil knocked Victim backwards to the same spot as before. This time the boat rocked more and the port side transom dipped under the water causing water to rush into the boat. The boat sank rapidly and capsized, expelling Operator and Victim into the water.  Neither occupant was wearing a PFD, but quickly found them as they floated to the surface. Operator was able to obtain his PFD and Victim grabbed his PFD along with a seat cushion. Neither put the PFDs on and just held onto them. Approximately 50 yards from shore, Operator told Victim they needed to swim to shore. Victim said he couldn't and would not try. Operator stayed with Victim and helped keep him stay afloat as he became weaker. After approximately 40 minutes in the water, an Idaho Fish and Game air boat arrived and pulled both Operator and Victim out of the water. Victim was flown by helicopter to Kootenai Medical Center where he later died from complications related to hypothermia. 

I checked the capacity of the Lowe jon boat via their website and located a boat with almost identical design and dimensions. The only difference was the boat involved in this incident was 6" narrower at the beam. Based on this, I determined this boat to have a maximum weight capacity of 275 lbs with a person capacity of two people/180 lbs. The operator alone exceeded the maximum capacity of this boat as he weighed 215 lbs. The two occupants combined weighed 345 lbs. I determined the minimum total weight of this boat was 410 lbs., far exceeding the maximum capacity of 275 lbs. Also, this boat was not registered as required, did not have a sound producing device, and did not have an invasive species sticker

Unit 1 was heading west bound at approximately 30 - 40 mph.  As unit 1 turned heading south, unit 1 collided with unit 2.  A good samaritan stopped and assisted the operator of vessel 1.  The crash occurred outside a no wake area, near the shoreline.  Point of impact was at the hull of vessel 2 near the engine compartment and rear engine cover cowling.  This location is at the front of the  operator's position, and near the handle bar steering controls.  The fiberglass at this location was cracked the worst.  It was also fractured inward, showing the direction of force.

Damage to vessel 1 occurred at the bow, on the keel, below the bow eye, near the middle chine.  Minimum planing speed for vessel 1 would be approximately 20-25 mph and this would cause an over-ride situation where vessel 1 would go over vessel 2.  On plane vessel 1 is a high profile vessel causing the bow to ride high in the water and to cause the stern to set lower, due to the weight of the vessel and the engine.  This makes for a good ramping situation, because the bow wants to climb over items in the water and the weight in the rear of the boat to want to depress the item being driven over.

The PWC attitude as it sits in the water is a very low profile, with about 21 inches of height above the water, depending on the weight of the operator.  The weight of the pwc, being light, also plays into the craft being depressed into the water.  This makes for a good ramping situation.  The initial approach and impact angle of vessel 1 in relation to the centerline of the pwc was approximately 225 degrees, + or - 15 degrees.

Upon impact the pwc most likely did not yaw much, due to the point of impact being close to the center of gravity and balance.  The pwc did most likely roll, causing the port side to go down and the starboard side to rise.  At the same time the pwc was depressed downward into the water, causing a ramping or over ride situation.  The pwc went under along the port side of vessel 1 where it slid out from under the boat near the port side lifting strake.  The operator of the pwc most likely went under vessel 1 along the starboard side.  This would account for the injuries to the rear left side of his head and the propeller cuts to his left leg and left hand.  A mark on vessel 1 appears to be a black rubber scuffmark made by a boot worn by the operator.

The body of the operator was taken to the nearest dock for medical assistance.  He was transported to the hospital where he was pronounced dead by medical staff.  The coroner's autopsy reported that the operator sustained blunt force trauma to the head, causing a skull fracture, and traumatic partial amputation to the left leg.  Both injuries were life ending.

This report details a boat accident that occurred at Holiday Shores Lake in Madison County, IL on June 19, 2010 @ 1:30A, resulting in one fatality. the victim drowned while attempting to retrieve articles that had been blown off the pontoon boat he was an occupant on. The boat operator and five individuals went for a boat ride during the early morning hours of June 19, 2010. The boat operator had consumed two beers prior to the accident however the deceased, and his wife, were intoxicated according to statements to Madison County Sheriff, by his wife immediately after the accident. At approximately 1:30A, a severe thunderstorm with lighting, strong winds and heavy rain approached. The boaters were on there way back to their dock when a strong gust of wind blew a container and some chairs off the pontoon boat into the water. The operator cut off the motor and drifted while three people voluntarily jumped in the water to retrieve the items that were blown off the pontoon boat. The operator and occupants remained on the pontoon boat. The swimmers discovered the wind had kicked up the waves which were estimated to be 2-3 feet tall and decided to return to the pontoon boat however the watercraft had drifted away. The operator of the pontoon boat tried to maneuver towards the swimmers to rescue those in the water by using the glow from the lighting strikes. subject1 was able to swim back to the watercraft and subject2 barely made it back to the watercraft. the victim was heard yelling for help but was unable to swim back to the watercraft and drowned. All three individuals in the water were swimmers and although life jackets were on the watercraft none were utilized. 

The operator was given a field sobriety test by Madison County Sheriff, . K. the operator was cooperative and agreed to do so. A horizontal gaze nystagmus test was conducted and the operator's eyes has smooth pursuit, no nystagmus at maximum deviation an to fod no onset prior to 45 degrees. the operator was also given the "walk and turn" test and was able to follow instructions accurately without stumbling. The "one leg stand: test was administered and again the operator passed the test with little effort. Officer indicated that there was no probable cause leading him to believe that the operator was intoxicated. operator declined to submit to a voluntary preliminary breath test. Officer also interviewed occupants shortly after the accident.

searchers of Team Waters Inc. were utilized to assist with the search for the victim. the divers located the body at approximately 2:41A in 20 ft of water and marked the spot with a buoy. GPS coordinates were N38 55.069'  W089 56.218'. the searchers and other search personnel dragged the location and was able to recover the body at 3:46A. the body was transported to Alton Memorial Hospital in Alton, Illinois were he was postively identified.

On August 22, 2010, at 2:31 p.m., the DeWitt County Sheriff's Department received a 911 call in reference to a missing person who had fallen overboard from a boat at Clinton Lake.  the operator and his wife had been boating when the operator opened the port side rail gate and leaned over the side to inspect the boat for algae on the side/hull.  At the same time, several wakes from passing boat traffic caused the operator to loose his balance and fall overboard and disappear beneath the surface. After attempting to gain the attention of passing boaters for approximately 5 minutes, the wife was able to flag down an off duty police officer boating with his family.  The off duty officer called 911 and assisted Delores, operating the boat to the Clinton Lake Marina.  

Prior to operating the boat back to the marina, the off duty officer marked the location with a float tied to a line and anchor.  Illinois Conservation Police sonar operators were able to location the body of the victim and divers subsequently were able to recover his body a few hours later.

(A supplemental report, sonar and body  recovery pictures will be attached to the final report).

On Sunday May 23, 2010 at 7:09 a.m.I, CPO was notified by Sgt. of a lost kayaker on Salt creek in Logan county near Middletown.  Sgt. advised me to respond to Logan Co. road 250 Ave at Salt creek with the side scan sonar.  This location is also known as "Middletown beach".  Upon arrival I spoke to Logan Co. ESDA Coordinator.  He advised me of the following events:  On Saturday May 22, 2010 at 8:48 p.m. a 911 call was placed to the Logan co. Sheriffs office advising them of a subject, who had been kayaking, was missing.  At 9:08 pm Lincoln Fire Dept responded with a boat.  A helicopter was also dispatched to help search due to it being dark outside.  At 11:42 pm the helicopter located a white kayak, upside down, lodged in large log jam approximately four tenths of mile downstream of CR 250th Ave.  Rescue workers were able to retrieve the kayak.  The kayak had a type IV throwable device in it along with a cooler.  The cooler contained 3 unopened cans of Bush Light beer.  The kayaker was no where to be found.  
     I spoke to two subjects who were kayaking with the victim.  They said that all the kayakers were supposed to stop at Middletown beach (CR 250th Ave) to load up after launching from Rocky Ford Bridge.  For some unknown reason the victim continued past the beach area and went around a bend on the creek and that was the last time he was seen.  one subject stated victim was not wearing a PFD and that he had started the kayaking trip with a 12 pack of beer and had only been drinking alcohol for about two hours.  After they loaded up there kayaks they went to the next bridge to wait for the victim to show up.  After he did not show up there they went to the next bridge, which was Hubley bridge, and waited there.  When he didn't show up there they called 911.
   I began to scan the area near the log jam.  The current was fairly swift near the log jam where the kayak was located.  We scanned the area for two days while rescue workers worked on cutting debris away from the log jam.  On Thursday May 27 at 8:50 am, the body was located floating approximately one mile downstream of the log jam.  On Friday May 28th I spoke to the Logan Co. Coroner's Office.  They advised me the autopsy showed cause of death to be drowning with no trauma to the body.  Toxicology test results will not be back for 6 to 8 weeks.

     On August 4, 2010 I obtained a copy of the toxicology report.  The report showed the victim had decomp fluid ethanol reading of 0.265%.

Both Eastbound, Vessel #1 (2 persons on board) struck Vessel #2 (2 persons on board) East of the Ashland Ave bridge on the Cal-Sag channel. The vessels were following each other, at night, after performing maintenance on Vessel #2. Vessel #2 came to a stop in the channel and Vessel #1 struck the stopped Vessel in the stern. the victim, seated in the bow seat, was ejected from Vessel #2 and subsequently died. The operator of Vessel#1 stated he jumped into the water and attempted to rescue the victim, adding he had ahold of victim three times before he was kicked in the stomach and lost his final hold with victim in the rescue attempt. victim body was located and recovered approximately 2.5 hours later by responding rescue personnel.

The operator of Vessel#1 stated he was following in Vessel#2's wake and was having difficulty keep up. The operator of Vessel#1 stated as he crossed
under the Ashland Ave bridge he saw the white stern light of Vessel#2 approaching fast, cut his engine, and attempted to avoid Vessel#2 by turning left. The operator of Vessel#2 stated the victim was holding a spotlight in the bow seat and their vessel was struck approximately "10 seconds" after coming off plane for a log floating in the channel. The operator of Vessel#1 estimated the time as a minute before collision.

The collision caused the passenger of Vessel#1 to strike the winshield of the same vessel causing injury to her head and left shoulder. The operator of
Vessel#1 also recieved injury when he jumped overboard in his rescue attempt of the victim, he stated he struck his shin on his stern light mast, breaking it.

Damage to Vessel#1 was limited to the front starboard quarter with the most notable being a gash in the aluminum hull in excess of 24 inches. Damage to Vessel#2 was limited to the stern at the transom, outboard motor, and stern port quarter. Blue colored transfer was noted from Vessel#2 onto Vessel#1 in the damaged area. The outboard motor of Vessel#2 appeared to have been pushed up and inward distorting both the metal engine mounts and cracking the fiberglass transom. The outboard motor itself appeared to be damaged beyond an operational state and the engine cowling was missing. Diver's reported to have seen the cowling near the location of the body, but did not recover it.

the family was notified by CPO on 06/20/2010 at approximately 8:15 AM.

Cook County Medical Examiner indicates cause of death as "Drowning, Accidental" (case# 321June10).

On Saturday, October 9, 2010 at approximately 10:00am, Conservation Police Officers were called to Lake Mattoon for a boat accident with injuries.  At approximately 10:38am, we arrived.  All of the victims were taken to Sarah Busch Lincoln Hospital prior to our arrival.  Both boats were already at the marina.  The green Lowe (V #1) was at the ramp and the white Lowe (V #2) was tied up to the dock.  CPO took written statements from two witnesses while I began processing the boats.  I took photographs of both boats while still in the water prior to moving the boats.  CPO and I were assisted by the Neoga Ambulance and Fire personal with removal of the boats.  Both boats were pulled onto their trailers using the jack.  I took more photographs and interviewed another witness.  

From witness' statements, ambulance personel injury assessments, and preliminary assessment of the boats, V #2 collided with V #1 near the east shoreline of the lake.  V#2 was traveling at a hight rate of speed, while V#1 was moving very slow, almost at a stand still.  V #2 struck the helm of V #1, pushing V #1 down, causing V #2 to ramp up and slide sideways over V #1.  V #2 struck the operator of V #1 in the head then shoved him over to the passenger location. Initially, the operator of V #1 was to be airlifted to the hospital but was transported by ambulance.  The two other seated in the back of the V#1 were transported to the hospital by ambulance.  The two seated near the front of V#1 were taken to the hospital by a family member.  All passengers of V#1 were treated and released, while the operator was pronounced dead at the hospital.

The operator of V#2 and the passenger near the front of the vessel, were ejected.  The third passenger was thrown to the floor, who then drove the boat closer to the ejected passengers and threw them a lifeline.  Both V#1 and V#2 were assisted by other boat operators.  V#1 was towed to shore and V#2 was driven to shore.  The two ejected from the boat were transported to the hospital by ambulance, treated and released.  Further assesment of the vessels along with interviews of the witnesses and vessel occupants will be documented in a supplemental report.  END OF REPORT.

On 09/05/10 at approximately 8:45 A.M., I CPO was informed of a capsized boat on the West side of Patoka Island on Carlyle Lake by some duck hunters. I rode out to the location of the watercraft to conduct an investigation on it. I observed articles floating along the bank of the island approximately 50 yards from the capsized boat. I approached the aritcles and observed victim lying face down in the water along the shore line. It appeared that he had been there for some time. EMS and the Fayette County Coroner's office were notified. I awaited there arrival and turned victim over to the Coroner's office. I took possession of the boat for conducting an investigation on the accident. Autopsy and complete accident investigation is pending.

This report reflects the fatal boat accident involving a swimmer that occurred on Litchfield Lake Lou Yaeger.  Operator1 was experiencing difficulties with his throttle on his boat when he ran into a anchored boat bouncing off of it and into another vessel and finally running into two females located in front of that boat. One female subject received extensive injuries to her abdominal area causing her death. The other female subject recieved a small cut on her lower back from what I believe to be some part of the starboard part of the boat, possibly the ladder.

On 09/10/10 the operator of unit #1, Operator1 went fishing on the Mississippi River Pool #21.  Operator1's family became concerned after Operator1 did not return home in the afternoon  on 09/10/10.  At about 8:00 PM Operator1's family called the Quincy Police Department  and informed them that Operator1 had not returned home from fishing.  

I was contacted by the Illinois State Police Dispatch at approximately 10:00 PM.  I responded to the scene.  The search for Operator1 was called off until the morning of 09/11/10.  On 09/11/10 the search resumed and Operator1's water craft was located floating on the north side of lock and dam #21, without Operator1.   The boat was towed and seized for inspection.  Search and rescue operations went on through the day of 09/11/10 until called of by the Adams County Emergency Director and Operator1's family.  Aquatech owner and boat mechanic inspected the boat at my request.  At approximately 12:05 PM on 09/11/10 Mechanic called my cellular phone.  

Mechanic stated that when Operator1 brought the boat into his shop on 09/08/10 the motor had approximately (9) nine hours of use on it.  On 09/11/10 Mechanic noticed that the motor had (15) fifteen hours (21) twenty one minutes and (28) twenty eight seconds of use on it.  Mechanic further stated that in the last four hours of the motors use Operator1 attempted to start the motor while in gear (22) twenty two times.  Operator1 also in the (15) fifteen hours of use on the motor attempted to start the motor with the throttle engaged past idle (11) eleven times.  Mechanic also had the information of the last (2) two minutes of run time on the motor which showed the motor ran at 2400-2800-RPM's until it died.  Which showed the motor was turned off or ran out of fuel.  

I told Mechanic that an empty fuel tank was recovered from Operator1's boat.  I asked Mechanic what that information meant.  Mechanic stated that the motor that Operator1 possessed had to be started with the gear in neutral and the throttle closed.  Mechanic further stated that if Operator1 would have started the motor by opening the throttle and pulling the start cord the motor would start, however the motor would only run at idle power / speed.  Mechanic stated Operator1 would have to shut the motor off, close the throttle, pull the start cord to start the motor, put the motor in gear to get full power.  Mechanic stated that Operator1 was attempting to start the motor improperly.  

Mechanic further stated that the error messages are common due to the fact that the old pull start motors had to be started with the throttle open a little to give the motor gas to start.  Mechanic stated middle aged or older individuals that have had pull start motors will still attempt to start their boats in this manner even though its not needed.  Upon speaking with Operator1's wife, I learned that  Operator1 was unexperienced with his new motor and could have contributed to the accident.

On 09/12/10 Operator1 was located deceased floating without a PFD approximately 500 yards  downriver / south of lock and dam #21.  Operator1's body was recovered and transported to Springfield for an autopsy.  On 09/15/10 I spoke with the Adams County Coroner about Operator1's death.  The coroner informed me that Operator1 possessed water in his stomach and sinus cavities which was a finding consistant with drowning.

On Monday, July 19, 2010 at approximately 1:34 AM, the victim and 5 friends  went to Valley Lo Country Club and took 2 canoes and 1 paddle boat for a ride in the adjoining lake.  The 6 were trespassing and using boats that were not theirs, nor did they have permission to take them.  the victim was seated in the paddle boat with one subject, subject2 was in a canoe with subject3, the second canoe was occupied by subjects 4 and 5.  The party of 6 were positioned near the middle of the lake talking and drinking Miller Genuine Draft.  They remained in this area until they were spotted by a local resident walking his dog near the south-eastern portion of the lake.  Four people all paddled towards shore and exited the boats to avoid getting in trouble by local law enforcement for Trespassing.  Three walked to the car and thought the victim was behind them.  two subjects remained in their canoe and paddled toward another portion of the bank.  subject1 reported that the victim boarded a canoe, previously occupied by two of the subjects, and began paddling toward the two remaining in the water, who now were at the bank in their canoe.  one subject turned and saw the victim's canoe capsized and the victim yelling for help.  At first the two thought the victim was kidding around, but then realized that he was not.  one subject jumped into the water and began making her way towards the victim, but had to return to shore due to her now wet clothes dragging her under.  the subject took her pants off and returned to the water, but could not reach the victim before he went under.  the subjec used her legs to try and search for the victim with negative results.  The commotion awoke two of the neighbors, who called 911.  One neighbor dove into the water in an attempt to find the victim herself with negative results.  Glenview Police Department arrived on scene and Glenview Fire Department followed.  Fireman recovered the victim's body in 12 feet of water. the fireman Bear-Hugged the victim and drug him out of the water.  the body was found face down with his head facing south toward the shore.  the body was taken to Glenbrook Hospital where he was pronounced dead at 3:00 AM.  I (CPO) was advised of the accident on Tuesday, July 20, 2010 at approximately 12:40 PM by Capt.   

subject1 reported that this was the victim's first time in a boat and is unsure why he took a canoe out by himself after he had reached the shore.  subject1 added that the victim had never been in a canoe either.  the victim was not wearing a lifejacket at any time during the event, but was a swimmer.  I asked subject1 if the victim appeared to be drunk before he went out in the canoe by himself, subject1 said he did not seem drunk and did not ingest any other drugs in her presence, stating that he had left his son''s birthday party before they had met up to go out on the lake and she only saw him drink 1 or 2 beers in the lake parking lot.   

the Father reported that his son had never been boating to his knowledge and was a good swimmer. 

Dr. of the Cook County Medical Examiner''s office reported finding Adema on the victim's lungs from the ex-rays that were taken.  the victim did not have any signs of blunt trauma, nor did he have any broken bones.  the victim's toxicology report is not yet prepared, results will be submitted with a supplimental report.

See Supplimental Report 2010-2-468-008B #1 for causal factors and listing of Attachements.
location: Valley Lo Country Club Lake, IL

description:
On August 6, 2010, at approximately 0100, four people got underway from DuSable Harbor, Chicago, out to Lake Michigan.  According to two of the subjects, after they had reached a point approximately 1.5 miles from shore they along with the victims dove into the lake to go swimming.  As the boat began drifting away from them, the victims had difficulty staying afloat, while both subjects managed to stay afloat until they were rescued by a fishing boat at approximately 0600 that same morning. The body of one victim was found floating and retrieved from the water, while the second victim's body remained missing.  On August 17, 2010 the body was found and recovered.

One survivor was charged with Possession of Drug Paraphernalia and Illegal Consumption of Alcohol by a Minor.  Another subject was charged with Possession of Drug Paraphernalia.  The court date for both was scheduled for September 29, 2010.  Both subjects appeared in court on their court date, charges were dismissed.
Victim jumped in the water to retrieve a cap and was unable to return to the boat. Two subjects tried to assist the victim but failed.

On March 17, 2011, operator went fishing on Baldwin Lake in a 15 foot Starcraft.  Winds were out of the South around 20 to 25 miles per hour with gusts up to 35 miles per hour.  When operator did not arrive at a predetermined time, a search of the lake was conducted and his unoccupied boat was found on the East shoreline of the lake.  The rear pedestal seat had been broken and was tipping toward the starboard side.  It appears that operator had fallen overboard while on the lake.  Operator's body was recovered by divers on March 18, 2011.  Preliminary cause of death was determined to be drowning.

On 05/04/11 at approximately 8:40 PM, the Adams County Sheriffs Department was notified of a boat, unit #1 floating without an operator.  Unit #1, a 1992 Landau Jon Boat IL registration # IL 4057 HK was located floating on the Mississippi River Pool #21 just south of the Bayview Bridge in Quincy IL.  Canton Marine Towing Co. towed unit #1 into the boat ramp at Front and Hampshire in Quincy.   The Adams County Sheriff’s Department learned through their investigation Operator had last contacted family members on 05/04/11 at approximately 5:30 PM.  Operator was last seen at the Twin Oaks Bar drinking alcohol for several hours.  Operator was known to drink alcohol almost every day.  Operator left the Twin Oaks Bar by boat to return to his river cabin home and has not been heard from again.
          
     Over the period of a week, a search was conducted by the Illinois Conservation Police, Adams County Sheriffs Department and Adams County Volunteer Emergency Corps utilizing side scanning sonar technology and cadaver dogs in an attempt to locate Operator.  
     On 05/14/11 the Adams County Volunteer Emergency Corps recovered Operator''s body on the Mississippi River pool #22 south of Beebe Island.  Operator''s body was turned over to the Adams County Coroner and transported to Springfield IL for autopsy.

The victim was heard yelling for help. Two subjects in another vessel responded and found the victim in the water and unresponsive with his small fishing boat circling nearby. The two subjects were able to hold onto the victim until fire personnel arrived and transported him to shore. The victim was tranported to Aurora Hospital in Kenosha Wisconsin where he was pronounced dead. The Medical Examiner determined cause of death to be heart disease, high blood pressure, and obesity.

CPO and I met up with Springfield Lake Patrol to take a look at the boat involved in the accident. I could not locate any fresh damage on the boat that indicated that it was involved in a collision with another boat or with an object in the water. The boat had extensive damage to it from bouncing up against the rip¬rap. The boat was a small narrow boat with a raised seat that was off set to the starboard side. There was no manufacture flotation located in the structure of the boat. The boat had been assigned a hull number by our department. 
The capacity plate that was located on the boat appeared to be from another vessel and did not belong on the boat involved in the accident.
On 04/04/11 at approximately 8:00 P.M., I CPO was notified of a fatal boat accident that occurred on Lake Springfield involving two victims. I was to report to Lake Springfield on the morning of04/05/11 to assist with sonar and to take over the boat accident investigation. 
On 04/05/11 at approximately 7:00 A.M., I CPO arrived at Lake Springfield and met with Capt who briefed me on the accident. Capt. advised me that the two male subjects, were involved in a fishing tournament the day of the accident. The water temperature was approximately 50 degrees; the wind was blowing around 40 to 50 MPH and producing 3 to 4 foot waves. The male subjects were in a narrow 14 ft. Jon boat with a 20 HP motor on it. 
They located one male subject on 04/04/11 and identified him. He was located by the use of sonar and recovered by dive personnel. 
The other subject was located on 04/05/11 by sonar and retrieved by divers. He was located approximately 100 yards farther north from victim1 and approximately 200 yards from the north shore line where the boat was located bouncing against the rip-rap. 
It was determined that due to the high winds, the high waves, and the boat being extremely narrow that the weather conditions would have been a reason for the boat to capsize. The temperatures of the water were cold enough that a person could die of hypothermia in a short period oftime.

On 5/12/11 at approximately 6:58 PM, the Illinois State Police received a cellular call from Crystal Hillis. She stated she was on the Illinois River below Otter Creek and her boyfriend had fallen out of the boat. Three Rosedale Fire Department personal and a Jersey County responded by boat to her location. She told them her boyfriend was operating the watercraft. He slowed down to idle speed and asked her to take control of the tiller arm, so he could get something out of the cooler. She took control of the tiller arm. After she did, the boat accelerated and went into a sharp right turn. They were both thrown fom the boat. She swam back to the boat. He went under water. A surface search was conducted that evening. 
A surface and sonar search was conducted the next three days.
On 5/15/11, the body was recovered. He was found floating in the Grafton Marina.

Two people were participating in a fishing tournament. They entered a restricted boating area next to the overflow of the spillway on Lake Lou Yaeger. They were using their trolling motor on the watercraft and became over taken by the current created by high water going over the spillway. Their boat was swept over the spillway and down into the creek below Lake Lou Yaeger. occupant was able to grab a life jacket and secure it to himself. The operator was not able to secure a life jacket to himself and did not survive the accident.

On 6/14/2011 at approximately 3:20 P.M., four male subjects were boating in a canoe in Pierce Lake located in Rock Cut State Park. Witnesses from the shoreline said they saw the canoe located approximately 50 yards from the shore tip over, tossing the four subjects into the water. Witnesses stated 3 of the subjects stayed with the overturned canoe while one of the subjects, identified in this report as the boat operator, began to swim toward shore. The boat operator swam approximately half the distance between the overturned canoe and the shoreline when he started yelling for assistance and began showing signs of panic by thrashing in the water.

One of the other passengers from the overturned canoe swam to the operator in an attempt to assist him. The passenger arrived at the operator and attempted to grab him but could not keep a hold of him. The operator went under water and did not resurface.  
Attempts were made to rescue the operator from witnesses on the shore and from swimmers in the water. These rescue attempts were unsuccessful. 

Emergency Medical Services (EMS) arrived on scene approximately 20-25 minutes from the time the operator submerged. They launched their boat and rescue diver. The operator of the canoe was found by the rescue diver beneath the surface of the water on the bottom of the lake. 
The operator of the canoe was placed into the rescue boat and started receiving medical aid while being transported to shore. Once on shore, medical emergency personnel continued administering medical aid to the canoe operator and transported him to Saint Anthony''s Hospital in Rockford Illinois. The operator of the canoe was pronounced dead at the hospital by hospital staff.

The passenger who swam to the operator was thrown a boat fender ( bouy ) by another boater and then swam to shore. The other two passengers from the canoe hung on to it''s side and paddled their way to shore. On their way to shore, one of them was given a wearable Personal Floatation Device from a person in a kayak. This passenger slipped one arm through it and continued to shore. The other passenger was holding a Type IV Personal Floatation Device while holding on to the canoe.

None of the boaters were wearing a Personal Floatation Device when the canoe tipped over.
The passengers in the canoe later stated to me there were no wearable Personal Floatation Devices onboard the canoe and none were recovered after this incident. They did tell me they had three or four seat cushions with them in the canoe. Three Type IV Personal Floatation Devices were recovered after this incident. The three other passengers were treated by EMS on shore. They did not incur any physical injuries from this incident.

On 07/05/2011 at approximately 9:35 p.m., victim and his wife were fishing from their 16 ft Lowe fishing boat on Lake Taylorville.  Wife’s fishing line broke and Victim was putting the equipment back into the storage area and getting ready to head back to shore.  While standing in the boat in front of Wife, who was in the passenger side of the watercraft,  Victim lost his balance and fell backwards over the side of the boat into the water.  Wife stated he did not say anything or make any struggle once in the water and would not respond to her calls to him.  Two people heard the splash when Victim hit the water and Wife calling for Victim.  They immediately responded to the boat and found Victim face down in the water approximatley 6 feet off the stern of the boat.  Good samaritan entered the water and pulled victim back to his boat, jumped into the boat and pulled victim back into the boat.  Good samaritan2 heard the incident and headed to the Victim boat as well.  When the they arrived at the scene, Victim was back on the boat and Goodsam1 was performing CPR.  Goodsam2 boarded the Victim'' boat and took over CPR on Victim.  Goodsam1 drove the Victim'' boat to the marina where the Taylorville EMS was waiting.  Victim was transported to Taylorville hospital in full cardiac arrest.  Victim regained a pulse at the Taylorville Hospital and was ventilated.  Victim was transported to St. Johns Hospital in Springfield where he remained in ICU until he passed away.

On 7/9/11, at 11:41 pm, Copperas Creek Fire Department contacted me on my Dept. cell phone and advised that they had been called to the Hiram Walker Lake on a report of a missing boater.  They did a shore check and were unable to locate the missing boater.  They secured the boat where it was found, and also a hat that was floating in the lake.  We agreed to meet the following morning to continue search and recovery efforts.

    On 7/10/11, Copperas Creek Fire Department members and their dive team,  Mason County Dive Team, Farmington Fire Department, and Conservation Police met at the east end of the lake to launch, and then traveled to the west end of the lake where the boat had been secured the previous evening. Divers entered the water near the boat and did a surface check.  Divers located body in approximately 19 feet of water.

    On 7/12/2011, an autopsy was conducted, and it was determined that victim died from drowning.  The cause the fall from the boat and ultimate drowning remains undetermined.
location: Hiram Walker Lake - Private St, IL

description:
On June 19, 2011 at approximately 4:45am, I was contacted by Sgt. and asked to respond to a fatal boat accident on the Fox River.  At 5:08am, I arrived on scene and was notified by other responding agencies that the victim was found deceased floating in the Fox River in approximately 2 1/2 feet of water, at the accident site.

Preliminary investigation shows that Victim was traveling approximately due south (180 degrees) on the Fox River when he struck a pier which caused his boat to go airborne and land upside down on another pier 25 feet to the south.  The pier was 52'' 4" in length, and faced in a 302 degree angle.  The pier which Victim's boat laid rest on was also 52'' 4" in length.  The boat laid at rest facing 302 degrees.  Victim was found by the Algonquin Fire department floating deceased, face down, approximately 10'' from the impacted pier.  The body was removed and laid on shore, pending removal from the McHenry County Coroner''s office.

The scene was secured by the Illinois Conservation Police.  The Algonquin Police Department and McHenry County Sheriff''s Department made notification to the victim''s family, and assisted in gathering information if any other person was with Victim when the accident occurred.  At the time, it was believed Victim was alone.

The McHenry County Coroner''s office arrived and took custody of the body.

a tow agency was requested to assist in the recovery of the boat.  The boat was removed from the pier, and all evidence was preserved.  The boat was taken to Erickson Marine in Algonquin.  Victim''s boat was secured on his trailer.  CPO took custody of the boat and secured it at Moraine Hills State Park storage facility.

CPO was notified by Sgt. of the accident and was requested to inventory the boat''s contents, photograph, and reconstruct the accident.  His supplemental report is attached to this report.

A more detailed narrative of the report is attached as a supplement.

On 8-27-11, at approximately 11:00 PM, a two vessel collision occurred on Pool 21 of the Mississippi River.  A 28 foot Donzi, traveling south struck a 23 foot Rinker that was drifting at the time of the impact.  The Donzi was carrying three passengers.  The Rinker was carrying two passengers.  Eyewitnesses placed the impact 100-200 yards west of Piggyback (foot of Hogback Island).  Only one passenger was found to be in the Rinker when they arrived.  The owner/operator of the Rinker is still missing and declared dead by law.

On 01-12-11, Macon County Sheriff's Department received a report of a missing lone canoeist on the Sangamon River West of Decatur. The missing subject's canoe had been located capsized and snagged on a log jam. The subject had launched at Wyckle's Bridge at approximately 1300 hours on 01-11-11. The subject was not wearing a personal flotation device. An extensive search was conducted. The subject's body was recovered on 01-16-11, at 9:42am by search personnel. The body was in 4.5 feet of water approximately 50 yards downstream from the canoe. Autopsy results indicated drowning as cause of death.

On July 4, 2011 at approximately 8:00 PM Vessel 1 left Miller Beach in Indiana en route to Navy Pier in Chicago to watch fireworks.  Vessel 1 was cruising 26 knots and upon approaching the Lighthouse Gap breakwater, slowed to approximately 6 knots.  At approximately 10:06 PM three people were walking from the stern along the gunwale up the port side of Vessel 1 to meet with another person on the bow.  Occupant1 was in front, followed by Occupant2, then Victim.  Victim was carrying 2 drinks in his hand and not holding onto the railing.  After Occupant2 reached the bow, she turned and leaned over to see where Victim was since he was not on the bow with the rest of the party.  When Occupant2 did not see Victim, she began yelling for him and alerting the rest of the occupants that Victim was missing.  After the music being played on Vessel 1 was silenced, a search about Vessel 1 inboard and outboard was conducted.  While this was occuring Operator, who was operating Vessel 1, hit the Man Overboard button on his GPS and made a radio call that they had a man overboard.  Operator turned Vessel 1 around to look for Victim.  They were met by a sailboat who said they saw a head on the surface of the water go under, and tried using a lifesaving device with negative results.

All persons aboard Vessel 1 report they did not see Victim go over the side, nor did they know exactly where he was standing before he fell overboard.  Operator and occupant3 were at the operator''s console inside Vessel 1.  Another person was on the stern of Vessel 1.  Two others were below decks in the cuddy cabin.  another was on the bow, and Occupant1 along with Occupant2 were making their way to the bow at the time Victim went overboard.

At approximately 10:11PM US Coast Auxilary (USCGA) boat 067 received the call of man overboard and responded to Vessel 1 in approximately 30 seconds.  USCGA alerted US Coast Guard station Chicago (USCG), Chicago Police Marine Unit (CPD), and Chicago Fire Boat (CFD).  The three agencies arrived on scene at approximately 10:15 PM.  USCG boarded Vessel 1 to collect information and establish a track line for a search grid.  CPD put a diver in the water at approximately 10:16 PM in the location relayed by the assisiting sailboat. On 07/30/11 at approximately 1:30 pm Victim boarded a vessel and  left Belmont Harbor with several of his friends to attend a boat party identified as the "Playpen Party". Victim, according to his friends had consumed a great deal of alcohol throughout the day and was extremely intoxicated. While tied to several anchored vessel in the playpen he fell overboard twice and had to be rescued by his friends. At about 4:30 pm Victim had an altercation with the owner of the boat, the altercation was settled but the they felt it was time to leave the party and return to Belmont Harbor. At about 5:00 pm they left the party heading north, at around North Ave Victim who was seated in the passenger seat on the portside decided to get up and walk toward the stern of the boat where the boat owner was seated. Owner said that Victim grabbed him around the throat and began choking him and then grabbed him in the face. Owner said he grabbed the wrist of Victim to prevent further choking when Victim lost his footing and fell overboard. 

The operator heard the frantic yelling that Victim was overboard so he turned the boat around to rescue him but unfortunatly by the time they arrived at the location Victim was under the water. The operator then used the marine ban radio to notify police and they arrived within minutes. A police diver jumped in and recovered Victim, he was then transported to Northwestern Memorial Hospital where he remains in critical condition. 

All parties aboard the vessel were taken to the Joint Marine Facility to be interviewed by IDNR Law Enforcement, the vessel was also secured and processed at the JMF.

On October 7, 2011 at approximately 06:58, state police communications received a call from a C. and E. railroad engineer regarding an overturned vessel on Lake Shelbyville just north of the railroad bridge.  Conservation Police Officer (CPO) was the first to respond to the area.  CPO confirmed there was an overturned vessel along with a floating body.  When I, CPO2 arrived at the scene, at approximately 08:40, the body had been recovered and shortly thereafter, released to the Moultrie County coroner.  The individual was later identified.  The Shelby County Dive Team (SCDT) transported me to the scene of the accident where photographs were taken.  The boat was still in the water and had drifted to the shoreline just north west of the railroad bridge.  From observing the railroad bridge and the severe damage of the bow of the boat, it was determined the boat struck the far west pillar of the concrete railroad bridge and flipped over, ejecting the operator.  The SCDT along with IDNR officers, scanned the area of the crash for additional bodies and vessels.  None were found.  

At approximately 10:47, the SCDT and Moultrie County Dive Team uprighted the vessel.  More photographs were taken.  At approximately 11:38, the US Army Corps of Engineers transported the vessel to Wilborn Creek boat ramp. The vessel was then removed from the water and placed on a flat bed trailer until Victim''s truck and boat trailer could be located.  At approximately 12:20, Victim''s truck and trailer were located at the Opossum Creek boat ramp parking lot.  At approximately 14:30, towing transported the vessel to Findlay Marina where the boat was lifted from the flat bed.  Sgt. and myself, traveled to Opossum Creek to recover the trailer and inventory Victim''s truck which was later towed.  At approximately 15:30, we transported the trailer to Findlay Marina where the vessel was placed on the trailer and then transported to the Wolf Creek State Park evidence facility.  At approximately 16:30, I began the initial assessment of the damage of the vessel and took more photographs.  

The damage of the vessel indicated Victim was initially shoved forward, causing the console unit to be ripped from the bolts and shoved forward and sideways.  Victim was then launched forward, striking his head on the under decking of the bow of the vessel.  The upper portion of the bow of the vessel had been crushed and laid back, exposing the area underneath.  Initial autopsy reports show the injuries Victim sustained are consistent with being shoved forward onto the console (lacerated liver, multiple severe internal injuries) and striking his head (severe head trauma with multiple frontal skull fractures).  Further damage assessment of the vessel will be conducted.  END OF REPORT.

Five persons went out jug fishing on the Mississippi River. Victim lost his balance and fell off the right side of the bow of the vessel into the water.  Even though there was a slight wind, all other occupants stated that the trees on the islands blocked the wind and it was very calm.  One occupant dove in to save Victim, but could not find him.  They looked for Victim for about 15 minutes before heading to a friend''s house on shore to get a phone to call 911.  Missouri Water Patrol (MWP) looked for Victim that night but could not locate him.  MWP notified the Illinois Conservation Police the following morning and both agencies continued with the search.  Victim was located at approximately 11:32 PM on 10/15/11.  Autopsy has not been completed yet, but all occupants on the vessel say Victim had been drinking and showed signs of impairment.

description: At approximately 7:16 am, a mother stated that her son and another person had gone catfishing for the night at Highland Silver Lake.  The son's wife stated she spoke to him at about 1:00 am and asked him to come home.  Husband said they were getting ready to head home.  At about 5:00 am, mother awoke and realized that her son was not home.  They tried calling him but he would not answer.  The wife and girlfriend of other person, went to the boat ramp at the lake and found his truck and the boat trailer.  They then contacted Highland PD.  A park worker and Highland officer went out on the lake and located the boat floating capsized near duck blind #3 about 3/4 of a mile north of the boat ramp along the East bank of the lake.  The officer secured the area and anchored the boat at the location.  Illinois Conservation Police were contacted and dispatched to the scene.  Conservation Police started a sonar search at 10:11 am.  The first subject was located by sonar at 10:18 am and was recovered at 10:35 am.  The second subject was located by sonar at 12:31 pm and was recovered at 12:41 pm.  The boat is in the custody of the Illinois Conservation Police pending an investigation.  The conclusion of the investigator is that the vessel was small and narrow and the modifcations made to it would have significantly altered the boat's center of gravity.  The deck allowed at least one passenger to be high in the boat making it more unstable.  The added weight of the deck and the pedestal seats would also make the boat unstable.  At some point, the boat capsized throwing the fishermen into the water.  The weather was cold and the victims clothing, when wet, added considerable weight making it difficult to swim.  The cold water temperature would also cause hypothermia to set in quickly.  The weather conditions at the time of the accident were clear and calm so would not have been a factor in the accident.  The bodies were not discovered with pfd's.;
