On 4-2-2012 I, CPO went on duty at 11:00AM.  I was advised by State Police of a boat accident that occurred on 04-01-2012 at approximately 6:43PM.  I responded to the location of the accident.  The location was the  55th St. boat launch in Moline IL, Mississippi River Pool # 15.  I arrived at 11:34AM.  I met with Moline Fire Dept. Battalion Chief on scene.  Chief was in charge of an ongoing body recovery effort at this location.  Chief advised a PWC accident occurred on 4-1-12 @ approximately 6:43 PM, the PWC operator was missing and presumed deceased.  Chief advised operator was not wearing a PFD / life jacket when he fell off his PWC into the water.  Chief advised a juvenile male, Occupant was onboard the PWC at the time and was wearing a PFD.  Chief stated Occupant was able to swim back and reboard the PWC after he fell off with Operator.  Occupant was uninjured.  Chief was asked if he needed anything from IDNR.  Chief stated he had enough boats at that time and would notify me if they recovered Operator.

I called Moline Police Department and requested a copy of the police report completed on 4-1-12.  I was e-mailed a copy of that report.  Multiple eye-witnesses and the PWC involved were on scene.  I located Operator''s girlfriend.  Victim’s girlfriend''s son, was the passenger on the PWC at the time of the accident and was on scene.  Another subject is a friend to the family, was an eye-witness and on scene.  Interviews were conducted with these three persons.  All accounts of the accident were the same and matched what Moline PD had in their report.  Victim’s girlfriend stated Operator recently purchased two PWC''s from Tempo Marine.  I conducted a safety inspection on PWC IL 4485 HU.  I did not observe any signs of damage on the hull, the fire extinguisher was charged and onboard.  Victim’s girlfriend stated Operator was wearing the lanyard kill switch and a whistle was attached to the lanyard.  Witness verbal statements stated Operator was test driving his new PWC''s.  Operator gave short rides to two children prior to the third and final trip.  On the third trip, Operator turned to come back to the boat launch area.  At this time Operator and occupant fell off the PWC and were approximately 20 yards away from where the PWC stopped.  Occupant (wearing a PFD) was able to swim back and reboard the PWC.  Operator (not wearing a PFD) was unable to swim to the PWC and started yelling.  Victim was observed "bobbing" above and below the water line before going under the water and not resurfacing.  Occupant stated he had trouble getting the PWC to start because he did not have the kill switch lanyard.  Occupant was able to get the PWC running intermittingly and returned to the area where Operator was last observed.  Occupant was unable locate Operator.  911 was called at 6:48 PM.  Eye witness assisted with the search.  A search was conducted by Moline, East Moline and Arsenal Fire Departments via boat.  The search was called off at 8:02PM and resumed at 8:00AM on 4-2-12.  I confirmed with Tempo Marine Operator did purchase the PWC''s on Friday March 30th 2012 and picked them up on Saturday March 31st 2012.  Tempo Marine verified the PWC''s were in perfect running order and left with all required safety equipment including three PFD''s and registration paperwork.  I took pictures of the PWC involved and two of the PFD''s on scene.  I filed a significant incident report with our Dept. and briefed Captain via phone.

On 4-2-12 at 7:00PM I was advised by Fire Chief a body recovery was made at 6:55PM.  I met with Rock Island County Deputy Coroner on scene.  A positive identification of the body being Operator was made at 7:20 PM.

On 1 April 2012, Roy C Hildreth fell from his boat while fishing, and drowned.  Ed Hildreth, who is the biological son of Roy, reported his father missing on the moring of 2 April 2012 to Pike County Sheriff Department. Ed indicated his father had been fishing the prior day. Ed became concerned when Roy failed to show up for chores on 2 April. Ed stated he went to Roy''s house and discovered it appeared Roy had not been in the house overnight. Ed went to the pond (located on property) and discovered the ATV Roy used to travel from the house to pond. Ed found the jon boat Roy used to fish from in the middle of pond. Ed could see the fishing pole Roy used still in boat and appeared to have not been casted into the water. There was also a bucket Roy used to sit on turned on its side in the boat. Ed stated at this time he believed his father had fallen into the water and drowned. Ed conducted a brief search of the water himself and after a short while, he contacted the sheriff''s department for assistance.  Pike County Sheriff Paul Petty contacted me at 0915 hours and asked for my assistance in searching the pond for R Hildreth, whom he believed had drowned . I arrived at the scene at 1020 hours. Sheriff Petty and I began searching the pond using my jon boat. After a few passes, I observed a camo hat floating near where Ed stated he first found Roy''s boat floating. After a few passes in the area of the hat, we were able to retrieve R Hildreth from the pond bottom.  Hildreth was removed from pond, placed into a body bag, and was taken by truck to his cabin awaiting for the funeral home personnel to arrive.  An inspection of the boat revealed that the required safety equipments was not present in boat. I also discovered there were no registration numbers were on boat, and I was unable to locate a HIN number. The make and model of the boat was also missing. It appears Hildreth fell from boat and made no attempt to get back into boat after the fall.  I waited till the funeral home transport vehicle arrived and assisted with transfering Hildreth''s body over to funeral home personnel.  I left the scene at 1130 hours.

The Pike County Coronor decided not to have an autopsy performed on the deceased subject.

Conclusion:

Mr Hildreth apparently used a bucket as a seat in the small jon boat.  The position of the bucket (on side) leads me to beleive Hildreth was seated when he fell overboard.  Due to Hildreth''s age, I also beleive it is possible Hildreth had a heart condition which may have contributed to the accident.  Hildreth was not wearing a life jacket and it is probable he drowned as a result of falling overboard.

On May 21, 2012, at 8:45 AM, I arrived at the shoreline of the Rock River, to assist the Winnebago Co. Sheriffs Police with an investigation of a possible fatal boat accident. Once on-scene, I met with Winnebago Co. Detectives who briefed me on the missing boater. According to Winnebago Co. Detectives, Victim had been boating with several friends on the Rock River. At approximately 0330 hours on Sunday, May 20, 2012 Victim was last seen northbound on the Rock River from the Verdi Club, alone on his vessel. 

Friends and family were unable to contact Victim and had become concerned of his whereabouts.

On May 20, 2012, at approximately 1625 hours, Victim''s boat was discovered, unoccupied, and reported to the Winnebago Co. Sheriff''s Police. The vessel was located at the vacant U.S. Coast Guard Auxilliary Station boat launch, however, Victim was missing. 

Evidence suggests the boat had run aground "unmaned" after Victim had gone overboard, most likely shortly after he was last seen.  The boat had sat, abandoned, on the concrete ramp until reported to the police at 1625 hrs.  CPO responded to the scene with the Department''s side scan sonar boat. The IDNR sonar operator discovered what was believed to be Victim''s body in 14'' of water a short distance downstream of the U.S. Coast Guard Auxilliary Boat Launch.  The Rockford Fire Dive Team dove on the site and subsequently recovered Victim''s body.

A joint death investigation/fatal boat incident investigation is being conducted by the Winnebago County Sheriff''s Department and the Illinois Conservation Police.

FINAL SUMMARY- For an unknown reason, Victim left his watercraft or was ejected from his watercraft while it was underway, making way at an unknown speed.  Victim was not wearing a personal flotation device (PFD) at the time of the incident.  There is no evidence of criminal activity.  His Mercury outboard motor has a "kill switch" installed, but it had been overridden.  Victim was not wearing the "engine kill lanyard" (There was none present on the boat).  There were no obvious signs of injury to Victim''s body at the autopsy.  His toxicology report indicates his blood alcohol content at time of death was .152% with the presence of cannabis and cocaine in his system.  There was rumor that he often urinated over the side of his boat while it was underway, making way.  There is obviously no way to confirm that fact in this specific case.  Alcohol/Drug impairment, failure to wear a PFD and failure to have the engine kill switch lanyard properly installed and worn are the primary factors which lead to Victim''s death in this incident. Vessel 1, occupied five times, had launched beneath the Arch in St. Louis.  They drove for a few minutes upstream when the vessel motor quit.  They could re-start  the motor, but when they would try to put it in gear, the motor would die.  Vessel 1 drifted down stream toward some moored barges (Vessel 2), eventually getting wedged under one of the barges rakes.  A commercial tug that was in the area saw the vessel in distress and launch one of it''s rescue vessels, a Zodiac, with two crew members on board.  The Zodiac attempted to rescue the five persons trapped under the moored barges inside vessel 1.  On one of the passes in front of the barges, the Zodiac was caught in some swift current, which caused the front end to swing down stream and hit the front of a flat barge.  This caused it to capsize and eject both occupants into the river.  Both occupants went under the barge, with one being able to pull himself out quickly, while the other could not.  Other commercial tugs in the area responded to a distress call and were able to pick up both occupants of the Zodiac.  One of those persons, the passenger of the Zodiac, was not breathing.  That occupant was later taken to the hospital and pronounced dead.  The driver of the Zodiac, along with workers from the barge that picked him up, tied off to the moored barges, ran to the front, and lowered a line to the five persons still caught under the barge.  As soon as the five persons grabbed onto the line, vessel 1 was forced under the barge by the river current.  One person was lifted onto the moored barges, while the other four were rescued by being thrown lines from a tug positioned on one of the flat barges and being pulled forward.  All persons were transported to nearby hospitals with the one tug worker being pronounced dead.  All other persons involved were checked out, with nothing more than scratches being reported.  Only a small section of vessel 1 was visible the next morning.  A few hours later, the vessel could not be seen.  At the time of this writing (6/15/12), vessel 1 has not been recovered.

On 9/29/12 at approximately 11:00am,  Operator met Subject1 and Subject2 at the 600 N. bridge crossing the Little Wabash River 1/2 mile south of Emma, IL.  Subject1 brought an extra kayak for Operator to use.  Subject1 stated, Subject2, Operator and himself all shared smoking a marijuana joint under the bridge before they left.  All three then got into their own kayak and began heading down river.  At approximately 12:30pm, Subject1 first navigated around a log jam at a bend in the river, followed by Subject2.  Subject2 stated he felt Operator kayak hit the back of his kayak and when Subject2 turned around Operator was not there.  Subject1 stated Operator kayak was pushed by the strong current up against the log jam and caused his kayak to roll.  The strong current then swept Operator under the log jam.  Both Subject1 and Subject2 stated they observed Operator hand come up between the logs but they could not get to him.  Subject1 called 911 at 12:33pm.

I CPO arrived on scene at approximately 1:15pm.  Subject1 and Subject2 were on the bank next to the log jam when they were giving directions to Illinois State Police dispatch.  After searching by land for several minutes Subject2 walked out to the location of our sirens.  Subject2 stated Subject1 could not walk out due to a previous back injury. I brought Subject1 out and we met CPO who had Subject2 with him.  We relocated to a private boat ramp and met with CPO who arrived with a boat and sonar equipment.  Subject2 went with us in the boat to locate where he last saw Operator.  We marked the location and began to search for Operator.  Due to the strong current and amount of debris in the river it was difficult to locate Operator.  At 4:35pm we located Operator kayak 1 mile down river.  Operator family began to arrive and we stationed the family on 600 N. by the bridge.  Every hour we made contact with the family and gave an update.  CPO and Sgt. also arrived to help with the sonar search.

(White County Coroner) was notified and arrived at 10:42am.  Black Township Fire Dept. (Indiana Dive Team) delivered Operator to the boat ramp and coroner took possession of the body. This report documents the investigation conducted by the Lake County Sheriff''s Office, report #2012-08012.

     On 06/18/12,at approximately 9:30 p.m., unit 1 (2008, 18'' Suntracker, IL 7732 KE, HIN BUJ060730808) was drifting on Gages Lake.  The operator and the passenger were reportedly drinking alcohol most of the evening and swimming on Gages Lake.  They had jumped off the boat multiple times over the course of the evening.  According to the Lake County Sheriff''s report, just after 9:30 p.m., both had jumped off the pontoon boat, which was not anchored.  Unit one had drifted away from them, so they both tried to swim to shore.  Subject1 heard Subject2 gasping behind him in the water.  When Subject1 exited the water on shore, he looked back and did not see Subject2.  Subject1 walked home, but did not call 911.

     Unit one drifted ashore at 33740 N. Lake Shore Drive.  A witness at this address observed unit one near his pier, and saw Subject1 walking on the shoreline.  Subject1 hid from police most of the night, and a search for Subject2 was unsuccessful during the dark hours.

     On 06/19/12, at approximately 3:20 p.m., a McHenry Fire Department diver located Subject2 in 44 feet of water.  The GPS location was N42 degree 21.088; W87 degree 59.920.  Grayslake Fire Department assisted in the recovery.  The Lake County Coroner toxicology report indicated Subject2 had a BAC of .324.  

     Subject1 was later arrested and charged with Failure to render aid to Subject2 (Class 2 Felony) and OUI/Alcohol resulting in death (Class 2 Felony). See Lake County Sheriff''s report # 2012-08012 for specific details/interviews.

Prelude:
          In the morning hours of Friday, October 29, 2010 two victims left from their residences to go fishing. Family members of both victims did not know the exact location of where the victims went fishing. The two victims had not returned by Saturday 10/30/10. Concerned family members contacted Gary Police Department to file a missing persons report, Case # 10-85256. On Thursday, 11/4/10 one of the victim's vehicle was located parked on the west side of the south pond inside Pine Station Nature Preserve. Located in the south pond was a floating overturned 10' aluminum jon boat. Divers recovered both victims deceased in the pond.

Details of Investigation/Incident:
          On Thursday, November 4, 2010 at approximately 1043 Hours, I, was contacted by Northwest Enforcement reference two possible drownings at Clark and Pine Nature Preserve, specifically Pine Station Nature Preserve. Police Officer found a van which was reported missing and also observed an overturned boat and possibly a body in the water. I advised DNR Employee that I would be en route to Pine Station Nature Preserve.
          I arrived on scene at 1119 Hours. Other agencies already on scene included: Gary Police Department, Gary Fire Department, Lake County Police Department, Lake County Police Helicopter and Lake County Aquatics. Indiana Conservation Officers arrived on scene a short time later. Inside Pine Station Nature Preserve are two ponds, one north and one south divided by a levee. Parked on the west side of the south pond at the gravel boat ramp, which is located approximately mid way of the pond, was a green Ford Windstar. The Ford Windstar had an Indiana Passenger Plate was parked facing the pond. Gary Police Lt. Detective advised me that the plate came back to one of the missing subjects. I then obtained the missing persons information for the two subjects from Lt. who advised me that according to family members, two subjects went fishing on Friday, October 29, 2010 during the morning hours. The two subjects had not returned on Saturday, October 30, 2010 and family members then contacted Gary Police Department to file a missing persons report. On Sunday, October 31, 2010 Lt. Detective entered the missing subjects into NCIC.  Located in the pond southeast of the Ford Windstar was an overturned aluminum jon boat. Looking back northeast in the pond from the boat was a black object on a sand bar, (This object was later determined to be the body of one victim.). I then photographed the interior and exterior of the Ford Windstar. While examining the interior of the Ford Windstar, inside the glove compartment, I located an Indiana ID Card. Attached to the front bumper and rear hatch area of the Ford Windstar was a yellow polypropylene rope, later determined used to secure the jon boat to the roof of the vehicle. At 1210 Hours the Ford Windstar was removed and impounded from the scene.

On December 1, 2001, Victim went to Sullivan Lake to fish around 1500 hours.  Victim was by himself, after phoning several friends in an attempt to get someone to go fishing with him.  Victim had been at his wife's residence earlier in the afternoon at about 1300 hours to visit with her and his mother.  Victim and his wife, Sue, had been separated since November 21, 2011.  While he was at wife’s residence on December 1, he had consumed a couple of beers.  Victim seemed somewhat impaired but coherent.  His speech was slow and lethargic, but his thought process seemed good.  He had also brought several beers with him in his boat while fishing.  Victim has also been prescribed several medications which he takes regularly.  Xanax and Mehtadone are two examples of what he was currently taking.  Alcohol is not to be consumed while taking either of these medications.

At approximately 1500 hours this same day, Victim arrives at Sullivan Lake and launches his boat at the main boat ramp, located at the Sullivan County Park.  After launching, he parks his truck (White Jeep) and boat trailer on the north side of the parking lot.  He gets in his boat and drives it toward the dam on the south side of the lake.  He makes a loop around the south end of the lake and turns his boat northward.  The boat is not running correctly as the bow of the boat does not seem to want to plane out.  This problem is a result of a large amount of water in the boat's bilge compartment.  The water is a collection of rain water that came from large volumes of rain in the Sullivan area on November 27-29.  

Victim had just purchased this boat about 2 months ago and was storing it at his temporary residence in Sullivan.  This temporary residence did not have a garage or carport in which to store the boat and trailer.  Victim placed a plastic tarp over the boat and motor, but the cover was not without holes, cracks, or leaks.  The boat collected water and Victim did not drain the water from the boat prior to launching it on 12-1-11.

On December 1, 2011, at 1600 hours, there was an abandoned boat on the east side of Sullivan Lake.  Deputy had seen a boat riding around on the lake earlier, but had heard a crashing sound.  The boat's ignition key was turned on, the throttle lever was forward, and the motor was off when the boat was found.  The bilge compartment lid was open and the bilge compartment was nearly full of water.  There were several life jackets in the boat, but none were immediately accessible.  A pair of wet coveralls and a pair of tennis shoes were also found in the boat.  Officer saw another object floating in the water in the middle of Sullivan Lake.  

Victim's boat was removed from the lake and impounded for inspection.  All systems on the boat were functional with one exception.  The bilge pump was wired to a switch labeled as a live well pump, and the live well pump was wired to a switch labeled as a bilge pump.  Both pumps worked properly, but were wired and labeled incorrectly.  The reason that these were wired this way is uncertain.  The bilge compartment was full of water, and it appears that Victim was aware of it and was trying to correct the issue.  The compartment lid was open and wet coveralls and tennis shoes were found in the boat.  These could have gotten wet while Victim was trying to drain the water in the bilge compartment.  Once he realized that they were wet and the possibility of becoming hypothermic was getting stronger, Victim decides to take the wet coveralls off.  In order to take the coveralls off, he removes his tennis shoes.  He returns to the rear of the boat, while the boat was in forward gear (perhaps to help drain the water) and falls overboard without wearing a life jacket.  He is not able to return to the boat immediately because the boat is still moving forward.  He is not able to swim to back to the bank or back to his boat and quickly becomes hypothermic in the thirty-nine degree water.  Victim drowns.

On tuesday, april 19, 2011, at approximately 2230 hours, i was contacted by south region headquarters at home, in reference to a missing kayaker on the big walnut creek.  South region advised that the kayaker reportedly left his residence earlier in the day and never returned home.  South region advised that the kayaker launched his kayak at his residence near the maidens branch creek which flows into the big walnut creek.  

 i made contact with conservation officer to assist me with the search.  At this time, the weather conditions were severe and a large storm cell was moving through the area with a tornado warning in effect with heavy rain and lighting.  The road conditions on highway 231 and highway 40 were at flood stage and in several areas, water covered the entire road.  The area had sustained substantial rainfall which led to severe flooding.  When i arrived on scene at approximately 2330 hours, officer and i were met by the reelsville volunteer fire department (vfd) personnel and an indiana state trooper.  The reelsville vfd advised that the driveway was flooded and that no access was possible.

I was met at the end of the driveway by subject’s brother.  Brother advised me that subject had reportedly left his home at approximately 1800 hours to kayak.  Brother advised that when subject left his home that he told his wife that he would be back shortly thereafter for dinner.  Brother advised that wife had told him that she was cooking dinner and that she expected subject to be back within 15-20 minutes.  Brother then went on to tell me that wife contacted him approximately 2 hours later and showed concern that subject had not returned home yet.  Brother told me that he then got on his atv and drove around the property to look for subject.  Brother then returned home and he and wife contacted the putnam county sheriff's department about the incident.  Brother advised that subject's dog, an australian shepard, had accompanied subject and that the dog never returned home either.  Subject was reportedly wearing a tan button-up shirt, brown hip waders, and dark colored work pants.  Brother advised that the kayak subject was using was a dark green colored kayak and that he could have possibly had a yellow and teal colored life jacket with him.  Brother said that the previous rainfall in the area had flooded the maiden's branch creek enough for subject to float down to the big walnut creek.  Brother advised that it was a common practice for subject to float down to the big walnut creek, and that it was not unusual for subject to be gone for an extended period of time, even with the approaching bad storms, and subsequent bad weather that followed.  Brother told me that subject was a known survivalist and that he suspected that if subject were to get himself in any trouble that he expected to find him huddled up somewhere riding out the storm.    

Brother pointed out the approximate location where subject had entered the water.  A field approximately 50 acres was flooded at the time i arrived on scene.  The field borders woods to the north, big walnut creek to the east and south, and maidens branch creek to the west.  The field was flooded to at least 1 foot of water.  The big walnut creek was flooded at approximately 12 feet at the time i arrived on scene.  The conditions of the search area were flooded and dangerous.  Heavy rain and lighting eliminated the possibility of an extensive foot search on land and eliminated the possibility of a search by boat.  At this time, i advised brother that we would be searching the area by spotlights and on foot where possible. 
 i notified the reelsville fire department personnel that the search for subject would begin at the area of the creek where subject had launched his kayak.

On Monday, May 17th, at approximately 2130 hrs. officers from Butler Co SO received a call from BU CO dispatch about a kayaking accident on the Walnut River south of the city of Augusta.  The incident location is located at the Osage Dam.  The Dam is a low head dam that is located just south of the Santa Fe RR and city of Augusta maintenance shop.  Once on the scene BU CO learned that rescuers had removed one person from the water but one individual was still missing.  The first operator was Operator2, who was pulled from the water and taken to Wesley Hospital where he was treated for hypothermia.  the second operator was Operator1, who was still missing.

BU CO SO, BU CO EMS, BU CO rescue, Augusta Water Rescue and SG CO Fire/Rescue started searching for Operator1.  The search went on until approximately 0130 hrs.  The search was to resume at 0900 hrs.  At 0900 hrs rescuers resumed the search for Operator1.  At approximately 1501 hrs Operator1's body was found downstream from the low head dam lying in a small depression on the river banks edge.  The body of Operator1s was processed by the Butler CO investigation Division and was then released to the forensic center for an autopsy.

On Tuesday, May 18, 2010, at approximately 1300 hrs two subjects met with Operator2 at his residence in Augusta, KS to interview him in regards to the accident on the 17th.  It was discovered that the 2 subjects were not very experienced in kayaking and did not know the layout of the Walnut river.  The 2 subjects had made arrangements for a person to pick them up after they had completed their adventure.  Operator2 and Operator1 arrived at the low head dam and discussed their plan on how to navigate the low head dam.  Operator2 wanted to walk the kayaks around to the dam and put back in, but Operator1 wanted to go over the dam.  Operator2 told Operator1 that if he wanted to go over the dam, that he would have his back if anything happened.  Operator2 recalls Operator1 going over the dam and letting out a loud scream.  Operator2 ran around the dam with his kayak and tried to help Operator1.  Operator2 had Operator1 on his kayak but could not hold on and could not get back to shore.  The water current kept sucking them back in.  Operator2 held onto Operator1 for as long as he could before Operator1 said tell my family I love them and went under not coming back up.  Operator2 stated that the PFD Operator1 had on surfaced but Operator1 was not in it.  Operator1s PFD was still clasped together by the budkles so the PFD was torn from the body of Operator1s underwater.  Operator2 stated that the next thing he remembered was some guy standing above him on the river bank on his cell phone.  Operator2 recalls that rescuers threw him a rope and pulled him out of the water and took him to EMS personnel Operator2 was then transported to the hospital.

Autopsy from the forensic center stated that the cause of death was from accidental drowning.

description: 7 subjects in a twelve foot john boat propelled by trolling motor checking fishing limb lines on Cottonwood River. While checking lines the lone adult male appeared to have a seizure and fell over the side of the vessel into six feet of water. Occupants in vessel said he never resurfaced and they stayed at location until they saw no more bubbles come up to the top of the water. Eight year old operated boat back to launch site and juveniles went for help.

Emergency and law enforcement agencies were dispatched to Cheney Reservoir at 16:05 for a call of a submersion.  Arriving on scene finding a boat accident had occurred.  The nature of accident was that the operator of the boat had inadvertently ran over his niece with boat and propeller.  Victim was triage code black at scene and transported to Sedgwick County Regional Forensic Science Center.
location: Cheney-20 miles W of Wichita, KS

description: On April 30, 2011 the operator of vessel one was attempting to start his motor.  The operator had been having trouble getting the motor to run.  According to statements provided by the other occupants of vessel one the operator did not realize the motor was in gear and when the operator started the motor the motor lurched forwarded ejecting the operator over the side of vessel.  The other occupants of the vessel were unable to render aid to the operator.  Another boater at the Marysville boat ramp heard the cries for help. Upon arriving at the scene the assisting vessel located the operator of vessel one unresponsive and floating.  The assisting vessel was able to load the unresponsive operator into vessel one''s boat and tow the vessel back to Marysville boat ramp.  Miami County Sheriff''s office and EMS responded to the boat ramp where CPR was performed until EMS arrived. The operator was pronounced dead at 0155 hours.  The operator was transported to KU Medical Center.  An autopsy report was completed and showed cause of death as drowning.  Safety inspection of the victims vessel after the incident showed the vessel was deficient two PFD''s and did not have a sound producing device on board.
location: Hillsdale-3 miles NW of Paola, KS

description:
Emergency and Law Enforcement agencies were dispatched to Cheney Reservoir at 17:34 to West Stool Loop at Cheney State Park in Kingman County Kansas.  Agencies were advised that they received a call regarding a subject that was in cardiac arrest involving a Kite Boarding accident.   

Information on accident was provided to dispatch from a off duty firefighter that was on scene and providing CPR. 

Emergency and law enforcement agencies arrived on scene and relieved individuals from CPR and continued until Paramadic advised that CPR had ceased per consultation with Dr..  Time of death as 17:54 per the monitor and cardiac strip printed by EMS. 

Information was passed on to the Kansas Dept. of Wildlife and Parks from Kingman Co. Sheriff''s Office. 

Victim fell from kiteboard due to high winds and was slammed down on the water and pulled and bounced across cove.  PFD was a part of suit and kite harness system victim was wearing.  This was cut off of him and was with board and kite that was picked up and later released to family.
location: Cheney-20 miles W of Wichita, KS

description:
At approximately 1930 hours on 25 August 2012 victim was a passenger in a 1984 15'' Bayliner boat when he jumped from the boat as it was traveling west on Waconda Lake.  The boat operator turned the boat around, took off his boots and pants, threw a type III PFD to Victim, put on a type III PFD and placed a type IV over one shoulder and a youth type III on the other shoulder and jumped in to rescue Victim.  Operator stated he lost sight of Victim due to the height of the waves.  He swam to shore and was found wondering on a county road at 9:24 the next morning.  A second passenger in the boat remained in the boat but was unable to start the engine.  He called 911 and was found by Mitchell County rescue personnel at 2050 on Saturday night.  
Recovery operations began at 2100 hours on Saturday night and concluded when Victim was located on Tuesday morning, August 28th.   Alcohol was present on the boat and is believed to a contributing factor in the death.  No autopsy was performed.  A vessel inspection after the accident found the vessel to be short one adult PFD.  The PFD thrown to Victim was not located and is presumed to be a type III adult jacket.
location: Glen Elder-12 miles W of Beloi, KS

description:
As operator and passenger of vessel one were traveling upstream of lake at full throttle approximately 20mph they encountered vessel two. The initial encounter happened in a sharp left turn moving upstream just above the no ski bouys. 

Operator of vessel one stated that at first encountering vessel two, passenger of vessel one yelled for operator of vessel one to turn right.  Operator of vessel one began to turn right, but then decided to turn left because it appeared the other vessel was heading in the same direction. When encountering a vessel head on, both vessels became the giveway vessels and should always turn right. Once operator of vessel one turned left, passenger of vessel one tried to grab the steering wheel, but it was too late and the collision occurred. 

Vessel two operator was traveling downstream of lake and was throttling down one quarter throttle approximately 25-30 mph approaching the sharp curve. Vessel two operator stated the initial encounter was that operator one of vessel one was approximately 20 ft away in front of him and then vessel one turned left into his direction. Operator two then turned sharply to right to avoid vessel one, but it was too late and the collision occurred. 

Once the collision occurred, operator one and passenger one where ejected from their vessel.  Operator two remained in his vessel. Once operator one and passenger one where ejected, vessel one continued to run full throttle in a left turn counter clockwise motion. The lanyard kill switch was attached to the throttle of vessel one, but was not attached to operator one.  Both operator one and passenger one were not wearing pfd's but were above the surface of the water however they were both in the center of vessel one's counter clockwise motion.  Operator one was holding on to a high rise seat to stay afloat.  Operator one and operator two whre both screaming at passenger one, but there was no response. Vessel one made several counter clockwise circles and began to get closer to passenger one until eventually the bow hull of vessel one hit passenger one in the head.  Passenger one then sunk to bottom of the lake.  Vessel one soon after run around the bank, became lodged in tree stumps. Operator two drove to vessel one to turn the ignition key off, then drove to operator one to help get her onboard vessel two.

OPERATOR AND WITNESS WENT KAYAKING ON THE RIVER AND WERE PLANNING TO CAMP A FEW DAYS ON THE RIVER. THEY PROCEEDED DOWN STREAM WHERE THE AREA WAS EXTREMELY DANGEROUS DUE TO DOWNED TREES, LOG JAMS, AND RAPID CURRENTS DUE TO THE RIVER BEING WELL ABOVE FLOOD STAGE.  BOTH KAYAKERS FOUND THAT THEY COULD NOT FIND A GOOD WAY TO GET DOWN THE RIVER DUE TO THE CONDITIONS AND HAD TO GO BACK UPSTREAM TO FIND A WAY THROUGH. AT THIS POINT THEY WERE BOTH EXTREMELY TIRED BUT THEY FOUDN A WAY TO PROCEED.  WITNESS WENT IN FIRST AND THE CURRRENT PUSHED HIM UP AGAINST A LOG JAM AND HE COULD NOT GET HIS KAYAK OUT OF THE LOG JAM. THEN WITNESS CLIMBED ON TOP OF A LOG JAM AND ATTEMPTED TO HELP VICTIM. VICTIM WAS STRUGGLING TO KEEP HIS KAYAK OUT OF THE LOG JAM WHEN HIS KAYAK FLIPPED AND HE FELL OUT AND DID NOT RESURFACE. VICTIMS KAYAK APPEARED INTACT WITH NO VISIBLE DAMAGE, WARNING LABLES AND CAPACITY PLATE WHERE IN PLACE. ALCOHOL AND DRUGS WeRE FACTORS IN THIS FATALITY. VICTIM WAS WEARING A PFD BUT THE ZIPPER WAS BROKE. IT IS UNCLEAR IF THE ZIPPER WAS BROKEN BEFORE HE ENTERED THE WATER.

OPERATOR AND PASSENGER WERE ATTEMPTING TO CROSS THE CREEK ON A ONE PERSON KAYAK WHEN THE KAYAK STARTED TAKING ON WATER AND PASSENGER GOT OUT OF THE KAYAK INTO THE WATER OVERTURNING BOTH OF THE PERSONS ON BOARD INTO THE WATER. AFTER BOTH PERSONS ON BOARD WENT INTO THE WATER, PASSENGER SWAM TO THE BANK. WITNESS NOT ON BOARD SAID THAT VICTIM WAS SWIMMING BACK TO BANK WHEN WITNESS SAW VICTIM LAST. BOTH PASSENGER ON BOARD AND VICTIM WHERE NOT WEARING PFD'S. ALCOHOL OR DRUGS WHERE NOT SUSPECTED OR INVOLVED IN THIS FATAL ACCIDENT.

Witnesses advised they had been tubing, but had stopped to let two female juveniles get back aboard the vessel. With the vessel stopped, two other passengers on the vessel got into the water. Meanwhile the victim who was sitting adjacent to the drivers seat in the passenger seat got up, walked across the vessel between the front seat and the drivers seat. A passenger stated victim never said anything, he just walked over and dove head first over the protective railing of the vessel into the water. Victim was not wearing a pfd.  One witness stated she saw and heard victim hit his leg on the vessel railing as he dove over into the water. Another witness recalled when victim resurfaced from diving into the water he was reaching for the tube, which was located near the ladder at the rear of the pontoon in the water. Witness advised that victim, with his head out of the water reached for the tube with one hand and once he grabbed the tube it flipped over on his head. Witness then reached over and flipped the tube back over, but victims head was under water at this time, but he still had one hand on the tube. Witness stated victim then let go of the tube and began reaching for the vessel with both hands, but was unable to reach it. Witness recalled it looked like victim was still moving his arms, but had quit swimming and was not moving his legs. Next another passenger jumped back into the water in an attempt to help victim, but witness stated his eyes were closed and he did not try to reach for passengers hand. Two other passengers entered the water but were not able to find victim. No pfd was being worn except for the two juvenile passengers, and victim had been consuming alcohol.

UPON THE OFFICERS ARRIVAL, INDIANA DNR STATED THAT THERE WAS ONE WITNESS TO THE ACCIDENT. ALTHOUGH THE WITNESS DID NOT SEE THE BOATER ENTER THE WATER, HE COMPLETED A WITNESS STATEMENT TO THIS REPORT. HE STATED THAT WHILE STANDING ON THE INDIANA BANKS, WITNESS HEARD A LOUD BOOM COME FROM THE RIVER. SUBSEQUENTLY, WITNESS GRABBED A PAIR OF BINOCULARS AND SURVEYED THE AREA. THE WITNESS SAW A 12' JON BOAT SELF CIRCLING NEAR THE KENTUCKY BANK. AT THAT TIME, HE LAUNCHED HIS PERSONAL VESSEL AND RECOVERED THE VESSEL PLACING IT APPROXIMATELY WHERE HE SAW THE VESSEL SELF CIRCLING. WHILE SEARCHING THE VESSEL, OFFICERS FROM THE COUNY POLICE DEPARTMENT AND INDIANA DNR SEIZED A BACKPACK AND FISHING VEST WHICH CONTAINED ILLEGAL NARCOTICS./ A SWIZURE REPORT AND KYIBRS REPORT ARE ATTACHED DETAILING THE EVIDENCE THAT WAS SEIZED. DAMAGE WAS SUSTAINED TO THE PROP OF THE 7.5 HP JOHNSON MOTOR AND THE TRANSOM OF THE VESSEL. THE THROTTLE WAS LEFT IN A FULLY FORWARD MOTION WITH THE MOTOR TURNED AT AN ANGLE.

Victim was swimming from vessel one on lake. Witness accounts say that he had swam to retrieve a soda can floating in the water approximately 80 yards away. One witness stated she was also in the water and stated that she saw victim swimming back towards the vessel, and she swam around behind the vessel to access a ladder to climb back on board, she stated she reboarded and stood up and asked the other passengers where's the victim. No one had seen him or heard any splashing or yells for help. After looking and yelling for the victim passengers on vessel called 911 for assistance. Officers arrived and witness stated by that time victim had been missing for 20 minutes. Fire and rescue divers arrived and dove till dark with no success due to lots of trees and other hazards one diver became entangled and had to cut himself free with less than two minutes of air.  Diving, side scan sonar and dragging operations were conducted the following days with no result. Daily patrols were conducted with the cooperation of the county fire and rescue and army corps of engineers. Victims body resurfaced11 days later and was located by the army corps of engineers ranger patrol.  It was later learned that the victim was a type one diabetic that had lots of trouble controlling his blood sugar. Before going swimming he had made the comment that his blood sugar must be getting low, witnesses on the vessel said he had consumed 2-3 beers before entering the water. A pfd was not worn and alcohol was a contributing factor.

When officer arrived the subjects involved in the accident had already been transported to the hospital.  The vessel was still in the water approximately 45 yards away from the curtain of the dam. The vessel was upside down. The bow of the vessel was protruding out of the water. The stern of the vessel was on the bottom of the river. Officers pulled the capsized vessel to the lock.  All witnesses saw two white male occupants in the vessel. Witnesses state  occupants of vessel one had their pfd's on when they were approaching the dam. Witnesses stated that when deceased reached the outer lock wall he cut the throttle to slow his speed and coasted toward the dam.  Other person on board vessel one stated that deceased  as running vessel on plane and decelerated to an idle speed before the lock wall. Witnesses estimated speed ranged from 40-55 mph before the vessel slowed to idle. Other person on board stated, that when the vessel reached idle speed he switched places with deceased and other person on board started driving the vessel. Other person on board stated they approached the dam to catch bait with a net. Three witnesses saw other person on board standing on the front of the vessel with a cast net. At this point witnesses stopped observing the vessel.  At this time the vessel was about 10-15 yards away from the dam. Other person on board believes deceased put the throttle in forward on accident and the vessel began to go toward the dam at an angle.  Deceased tried to back the vessel using reverse, but the vessel was sucked closer to the dam by the current.  Other person on board stated the water started sucking the vessel into the dam and water started spilling into the vessel.  The left side of the vessel went under first, then the vessel was upside down. Witnesses heard screams for help. alcohol was not involved. Pfd's were being used but not properly.

Operators of both vessel one and two were heading down river. According to witness accounts, the vessels were traveling at a high rate of speed near the center of the channel. Almost immediately after passing under the purple people bridge the operator of vessel two made a hard port turn. The operator of vessel one was unable to change direction and  ramped over vessel two. The operator of vessel two was struck by vessel one. From the wounds on the leg of operator two, it appears the tow hook on the nose of vessel one impacted the left leg of operator two while ramping over.  The operator of vessel two was thrown approx 20 feet downriver and landed face down in the river and did not move. Operator of vessel one jumped or fell off the starboard side of her vessel after ramping over vessel two.  The operator of vessel one then swam back to the operator of vessel two where she held her head above the water. Operator of vessel one then yelled and blew her whistle for help. Victim never regained conscousness and was pronounced dead at the scene. Alcohol was not involved and pfd's were being worn and used.

THE VESSEL RAN OUT OF FUEL WHILE TRYING TO BEAT A STORM. WHILE TRYING TO SWITCH FUEL TANKS, VICTIM JUMPED FROM VESSEL. A PASSENGER ON BOARD JUMPED IN AFTER VICTIM BUT WAS UNABLE TO GET VICTIM. AFTER GETTING THE VESSEL STARTED PASSENGER WHO JUMPED BOARDED THE VESSEL. AT 16:01 THE VESSEL WAS REFUELED AT LOCAL MARINA. THEN VESSEL THEN CONTINUED TO SEARCH FOR VICTIM UNTIL KDFWR OFFICERS AND COUNTY RESCUE ARRIVED ON THE SCENE. VICTIMS BODY WAS RECOVED THE FOLLOWING DAY ON 8-15-2010. ALCOHOL WAS THE LEAD FACTOR IN THIS ACCIDENT AND NO PFD'S WERE BEING WORN BY THE PASSENGERS. ONE PASSENGER PUT ON A PFD AS A RESULT OF THE ACCIDENT.

Based on statements given by all interviewed and evidence on both vessels: vessel one was traveling upstream, generally in the northeast direction and along the red buoy line. Vessel two was traveling downstream also along the red buoy line and generally in the southwest direction. Operator of vessel two stated that he observed vessel one coming toward them and that he altered his course attempting to avoid the collision. He then stated that he realized that they were still on a collision course and decelerated to the point that the vessel exited plane. Operator two then stated that vessel one kept coming at a high rate of speed and realizing that the vessels were going to hit head on, he turned to the right and accelerated in an attempt to move out of the way. 

Operator of vessel one stated that the two vessels zig-zagged to avoid a collision.  At this point the bow of vessel one struck the port side of vessel two mid ship just below the rub rail. The bow of vessel one penetrated the hull of vessel two at the passenger seat, striking the passengers left abdomen and ejecting him from the vessel. The two vessels then separated and settled in the water. Witnesses from other vessels then assisted retrieving casualty victim from the water, called 911, and began administering cpr as all parties and vessels involved along with witnesses traveled to the boat ramp. Although no violations wre cited, the officer finds that vessel one did not stay to the right of oncoming vessel two and that vessel two did not stay to the right of the mid channel. No alcohol or drugs where a factor in this accident and all persons involved on both vessel where wearing pfd's.

Officer was dispatched to boating accident/drowning at the dam. Call was that a male had been fishing from a jon boat near the flood gates on the tailwater side of the dame and got too close to the gates. Victim was recovered before any le personel could get on the scene and body was taken to coroners office where the coroner identified the body.  Coroner also took statements from three witnesses at the scene who wtinessed the accident. Coroner told officer that victim was using a trolling motor near the base of the dam when witnesses stated he got too close to the water coming through the flood gates. According to the coroner, witnesses stated victims vessel got pulled closer to the spill water and victim tried to move the console to start the outboard but was unable to before water filled vessel full and caused vessel and victim to go under. The vessel never resurfaced and the victim finally floated out of turbulant water where bystanders recovered him. Victim was stripped of all his clothes but his pfd that he was wearing remained on and allowed him to float through the turnulant water that overcame him. At this time the coroner has all the witness statements and copies will be included at a later date after the coroner returns. Posted at the boat launch area below the dam there states a sign that states, no operation of vessel wtihin 500' of dam when flood gates are open. Unknown vessel inpetions and unknown operator education and experience level. Alcohol was not a contributing factor in this accident and a pfd was being worn and uses.

OWNER STATED THAT HE AND CASUALTY VICTIM WENT FOR A BOAT RIDE.  OWNER STATED THAT THEY PUT HIS VESSEL IN THE WATER WITH CASUALTY VICTIM OPERATING IT FROM THE BOAT RAMP AND GOING UP RIVER. OWNER STATED THE VESSEL TRAVELED FOR A SHORT DISTANCE AND CAUSALTY VICTIM PUT THE VESSEL IN NEUTRAL, REMOVED HIS SHOES AND SOCKS, THEN HANDED THE OWNER HIS WATCH, ASKING VESSEL OWNER TO HOLD IT. VESSEL OWNER THEN TOOK THE WATCH INSTRUCTING THE VICTIM NOT TO JUMP IN IWTHOUT A PFD.  OPERATOR STATED THAT THE CASUALTY VICTIM IGNORED HIM JUMPING OVER THE PORT SIDE OF THE VESEEL. THE CASUALTY VICTIM CAME UP ONE TIME, HIS FACE A FEW INCHES OUT OF THE WATER AND THEN WENT UNDER AND NEVER RESURFACED.  OPERATOR PADDLED TOWARD CASUALTY VICTIM THROWING HIM A PFD. OPEATOR THE DROVE THE VESSEL AROUND LOOKING FOR HIM FOR SHORT TIME THEN WENT BACK TO THE BOAT RAMP. OPERATOR CALLED FOR ASSISTANCE. BODY WAS RECOVERED. CORONER DECLARED CAUSE OF DEATH AS DROWNING. AND THE DRUG PCP WAS FOUND IN THE FATAL VICTIMS BLOOD. NO PFD WAS BEING WORN OR USED.

CASUALTY VICTIM DROWN WHILE CHECKING FISHING LINES ON THE RIVER. CASUALTY VICTIM APPARENTLY WAS USING A 12' JON BOAT AND FELL OUT OF IT OR OVERTURNED IT. THE VESSEL WAS FOUND FLOATING UPSIDE DOWN ONLY A FEW FEET FROM WHERE HIS BODY WAS RECOVERED. THE RECOVERY WAS MADE IN APPROXIMATELY EIGHT FEET OF WATER.  CASUALTY VICTIM HAD BEEN DRINKING BEER THAT AFTERNOON ACCORDING TO FAMILY MEMBERS AND PROBABLY GOT IN THE VESSEL AFTER EVERYONE HAD LEFT THE FISHING CAMP. VICTIMS BLOOD ALCOHOL CONCENTRATION OF 0.193 % (w/v). THERE WERE NO PFD'S FOUND ON THE VESSEL OR FLOATING IN THE WATER. ALCOHOL WAS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR IN THIS FATAL ACCIDENT.

OPERATOR OF VESSEL ONE WAS OPERATING HIS 16' FLAT BOTTOM VESSEL UPRIVER WHILE WATERFOWL HUNTING WITH TOW OTHER PASSENGERS/HUNTERS. THE PASSENGERS SHOT AT TWO GEESE NEAR THE MIDDLE OF THE RIVER AND WERE ANGLED APPROX NINETY DEGREES TO PICK UP THE BIRDS. THE WIND WAS BLOWING UPRIVER AND WAVES BEGAN COMING INTO THE VESSEL FROM THE STERN. THE THREE MEN MOVED TO THE BOW OF THE VESSEL WHEN THEY NOTICED THE SWAMPING BUT THE VESSEL QUICKLY SANK. THE SURVIVING PASSENGER GRABBED A TYPE III PFD AND PUT IN ON.  THE OPEARATOR GRABBED A TYPE IV THROWABLE CUSHION. THE CASUALTY VICTIM GRABBED ONTO THE DECOY BAG FULL OF DECOYS. THE DECOY BAG WAS UNTIED AND THE DECOYS SCATTERED.  SURVIVING OPERATOR AND PASSENGER WERE ABLE TO BACKSTROKE TO THE BANK BUT THE CASUALTY VICTIM WAS LAST SEEN BY OPERATOR GOING UNDER WITH ONLY HIS HAND STICKING UP OUT OF THE WATER. ONCE THE SURVIVORS REACHED THE BANK, THEY REMOVED THEIR WADDERS AND RAN TO THE NEAREST HOME WHERE THE HOME OWNER CALLED 911. THE VESSEL WAS OVERLOADED WITH THREE PASSENGERS, GEAR AND A DOG. NO PFD'S WERE BEING WORN OR USED AND ALCOHOL WAS NOT A FACTOR NOR SUSPECTED IN THIS FATAL ACCIDENT.

ON 4/13/2011 DISPATCH RECEIVED A CALL FROM A CELL PHONE AND CALLER ADVISED A CANOE HAD CAPSIZED WITH THREE PASSNGERS IN THE WATER AND TWO HAD MADE IT OUT SAFE. THE CALLER WAS ONE OF THE SURVIVING PASSENGERS. PASSENGER ADVISED HE AND TWO OTHERS PUT IN A CANOE AND WERE GOING TO FLOAT TO THE NEXT TOWN. WHEN VESSEL WENT THROUGH THE NARROWS ABOVE THE CREEK, THE CANOE CAPSIzED AND ONE PASSENGER WAS STILL IN THE WATER. ALL THREE PERSONS ON BOARD STAYED WITH THE CANOE FOR A FEW SECONDS THEN ALL PERSONS ON BOARD SEPERATED. THE TWO SURVIViNG PERSONS ON BOARD MADE IT TO SHORE WHILE THE DECEAsED STATED THAT HE DIDNT HAVE THE STRENGHTH TO SWIM ANYMORE BEFORE HE DISAPEARED AND WAS NOT FOUND UNTIL SEARCH AND RECUE DIVERS RECOVERED THE  DECEAsED  PASSENGER TWELEVE DAYS LATER WITH SONAR EQUIPMENT. PFD'S WERE NOT BEING WORN AND ALCOHOL DID NOT PLAY A ROLL IN THIS FATAL ACCIDENT.

When officer arrived at accident scene, rescue crews were on scene above dam securing a rope to injured who was standing on the concrete ledge below a flood gate. Officers secured a landing zone for helicopter while crews rescued injured passenger.  Officers took statements from witnesses on the scene. According to witness statements a red vessel was fishing in front of a closed gate below dam. The gate to the left was discharging water and started pulling the red vessel closer. Witnesses then stated that one of the three occupants tried to start the outboard but could not get it started in time and the vessel went toward the discharging water. One occupant was said to have jumped out before the vessel capsized under the water. Several fishermen were near and pulled two males out of the water but stated they were not alive. According to statement by surviving injured person, vessel operator tried to start the outboard while the other passenger on board went for the trolling motor.  Surviving injured stated that he knew it was too late and put on a pfd and threw one to the operator after he fell out of the vessel into the water but was unsure if either deceased persons were able to put one on. The vessel was in a restricted area at the time of the accident.  Alcohol and/or drugs were not involved in this fatal accident. A pfd was being worn by the surviving victim, the deceased operator and passenger were not wearing pfd's at the time of the accident.

Due to high water and thick vegetation the boating accident was hard to access. Located on the bank were operator and unconscious casualty victim passenger with the vessel located a considerable distance into the trees. Officer assessed casualty victims  injuries and contacted dispatch to send stat flight.  The causalty victim was placed on a back board with a neck collar and  transported to the waiting state care flight and was taken to the hospital where casualty victim  later died. 

Operator stated he had turned to avoid debris in the water and the steering locked on the vessel.  Operator unable to steer the vessel and crashed into the trees. Operator had tried for approximately one and a half hours  to signal for help, but becuase of the remoteness of the area there was not much boat traffic in the area.  Operator eventually flagged down a rental pontoon boat which called the local marina which contacted dispatch. Officer smelled alcohol at the scene and asked operator how much he had drank that day, operator stated he had not drank any alcohol but deceased victim was drunk when operator picked her up at the gas station that morning. Officer located a two liter of coke that operator said he had been drinking and no alcohol was detected. Operator appeared not to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Operator was field tested with a pbt which showed .000. 

Based on the observations of the damage it appears that when the vessel impacted the third tree, the vessel rolled sharply to the right causing casualty victim to be ejected across the vessel and ending up on the right side of the path traveled. Operator stated that casualty victim was sitting on the port side of the vessel. Based on the facts the vessel would have been traveling 33.1 mph. It is the opinion of the officer that the vessel was being operated in an excessive rate of speed given the environmental conditions as well as the experience level of the vessel operator. Operator failed to take all actions available to operator to avoid the accident or at the very least, reduce the speed of the vessel prior to impact. By operators own words he did not attempt to reverse the thrust of the jet drives. Pfd's where not being worn or used. Alcohol was not a contributing factor for the operator but the deceased victim was under the influence.

ACCORDING TO THOSE PRESENT, THE DECEAsED VICTIM WAS A PASSENGER ON THE VESSEL. THE VESSEL WAS OCCUPIED BY SIX PERSONS INCLUDING THE DECEASED. THe GROUP OF OCCUPANTS WERE CONCLUDING  THEir DAY ON THE LAKE.  OCCUPANTS ARRIVED AT THE BOAT RAMP, WHICH WAS BUSY WITH ONE VESSEL LAUNCHING AND A COUPLE MORE WAITING TO LOAD. THE OCCUPANTS ON BOARD DECIDED TO FLOAT ADRIFT OUT IN THE LAKE AND WAIT FOR THE RAMP TO CLEAR. THE DECEASED, aCCORDING TO THE OTHER PERSONS ON BOARD, WANTED TO GO FOR ONE MORE SWIM BEFORE CALLING IT A DAY. WITH PERMISSION OF OPERATOR THE DECEASED JUMPED IN THE WATER FEET FIRST. THE VESSEL ENGINE WAS NOT RUNNING AND THE VESSEL WAS FLOATING ADRIFT.  AFTER A COUPLE OF MINUTES HAD PASSED, OPERATOR SAW THE DECEASED FLOATING FACE DOWN IN THE WATER. OPERATOR 
CALLED THE DECEASED NAME AND JUMPED INTO THE WATER TO HIM ALSO EVERYBODY ON BOARD ALSO JUMPED IN. THEY SUMMONED HELP FROM A NEARBY BOATER. THE DECEASED WAS PULLED FROM THE WATER, LOADED ON THE VESSEL AND CPR STARTED AND 911 WAS CALLED. THE DECEASED WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE COUNTY HOSPITAL BY EMS. AFTER LIFE SAVING MEASURES WERE EXHAUSTED HE WAS PRONOUNCED DEAD BY THE CORONER. AFTER CONSULTATION WITH THE STATE MEDICAL EXAMINER. NO AUTOPSY WAS PERFORMED. TOXICOLOGY WAS POSITIVE FOR ALCOHOL @ .139% AND ALSO TESTED POSITIVE FOR CANNABINOIDS. PFD'S WHERE NOT BEING WORN BUT WHERE USED DUE TO THE ACCIDENT.

AFTER BEING CONTACTED BY VICTIMS SON OF A MISSING PERSON, OFFICERS LOCATED VICTIMS VESSEL.  SIDE SCAN SONAR WAS USED AND VICTIM WAS LOCATED AND RECOVERED. ACCORDING TO THE CORONER'S REPORT THE VICTIM DIED FROM HYPERTENSIVE ATHEROSCLEROTIC CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE COMPLICATED BY DROWNING.

VICTIM AND PASSENGER WERE ON A TWO MAN VESSEL WHEN THE VICTIM DECIDED TO SWITCH PLACES. THE VICTIM STOOD UP AND STEPPED ON THE SIDE OF THE VESSEL AND THAT WAS WHEN THE VESSEL FLIPPED BOTH PERSONS ONBOARD INTO THE WATER.  WITNESSES RECOVERED THE OTHER PERSON ON BOARD, BUT VICTIM DID NOT MAKE IT. ALCOHOL WAS NOT INVOLVED IN THIS ACCIDENT AND PFD'S WERE NOT BEING WORN OR USED.

VESSEL ONE WAS ANCHORED NEAR A RIVERBEND MUSIC CONCERT AND AFTER THE CONCERT THE PARTY OF FIVE ON BOARD ON VESSEL ONE WENT DOWN RIVER TO A DOCK AND THEN BACK UPRIVER TOWaRDS A BOAT RAMP ON THE OHIO BANK. VESSEL ONE WAS TRAVELING APPROX. 30 MPH. VESSEL TWO LEFT THE HARBOUR HEADING DOWNRIVER TOWARDS CINNCINNATI, CRUISING AT IDLE SPEED WHEN OPERATOR SAW VESSEL ONE CLOSING IN. VESSEL TWO OPERATOR STATED TAHT IT LOOKED AS THOUGH VESSEL ONE WOULD PASS ON HIS PORT SIDE, THEN VESSEL ONE SUDDENLY MADE A SHARP TURN TO VESSEL TWO'S PORT, HITTING THE PORT SIDE OF VESSEL TWO. SOMETIME DURING THE IMPACT, THE FATAL VICTIM WAS EJECTED INTO THE WATER.  THE REST OF THE PASSENGERS ON VESSEL ONE STAYED ON BOARD. WITHIN TWO MINUTES VESSEL ONE SANK AND ALL OCCUMPANTS OF VESSEL TWO THREW THEM PFD'S. THE OCCUPANTS ON VESSEL ONE WERE HELPED ONTO VESSEL TWO BUT ALL SUSTAINED INJURIES OF VARYING DEGREES. NO ONE WAS INJURED FROM VESSEL TWO.  ACCORDING TO OPERATOR OF VESSEl TWO, VESSEL ONE WAS OPERATING WITHOUT NAVIGATIONAL LIGHTS. IT IS UNCLEAR WHO WAS OPERATING VESSEL ONE AT THE TIME OF IMPACT. PFD'S WHERE NOT BEING WORN OR USED. VESSEL TWO HAD NO ALCOHOL INVOLVEMENT, AND VESSEL ONE WAS UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF DRUGS AND ALCOHOL.

VESSEL 1 WAS FOUND WITHOUT AN OPERATOR DOWN STREAM FRoM THE BOAT RAMP. THE OPERATOR FAILED TO RETURN HOME AFTER A DAY OF FISHING. THE SEARCH FOR THE BODY STARTED ON OCT 17TH AND ENDED ON THE 20TH OF OCT. A CONVENIENT STORE HAD VIDEO OF THE VICTIM SHOPPING NEAR 12:30 PM ON THE 17TH. A SEARCH OF THE VICTIM’S TRUCK THAT WAS PARKED ON THE BOAT RAMP CONTAINED HIS WALLET WITH AROUND $500 CASH AND OTHER PERSONAL EFFECTS WITH THE WINDOWS ROLLED DOWN. THIS LED OFFICERS TO BELIEVE THAT HE DID NOT LEAVE HIS TRUCK AT THE DOCK WHILE HE WAS OUT FISHING, BUT RATHER CAME BACK FROM FISHING, RETRIEVED HIS TRUCK AND TRAILER, THEN HAD SOME TYPE OF MISFORTUNE.   THE OPERATOR’S BODY WAS FOUND APPROXIMATELY ¼ MILE DOWNSTREAM FROM THE BOAT RAMP. A DECISION WAS MADE NOT TO DO AN AUTOPSY.

OPERATOR AND CASUALTY VICTIM WERE FISHING FROM A JON BOAT IN THE POND WHEN DECEASED FELL OVERBOARD.  THERE WHERE NO PFD'S ONBOARD THE VESSEL ANDI T WAS MANUALLY PROPELLED BY BOTH PARTIES USING PADDLES. THE MEN HAD BEEN FISHING AND WHEN DECEASED STOOD UP IN THE VESSEL, HE LOST HIS BALANCE AND FEEL OVERBOARD. WHEN DECEASED ATTEMPTED TO REBOARD THE VESSEL FROM THE STERN, HE CAUSED THE VESSEL TO SWAMP.  OPERATOR WAS ABLE TO SWIM TO THE BANK AND WAS ABLE TO SUMMON ASSISTANCE.  DECEASED WAS LAST SEEN SWIMMING TOWARD THE BANK WHERE HE WAS LATER RECOVERED.  DRUGS/ALCOHOL WAS NOT SUSPECTED IN THIS FATAL ACCIDENT.

Vessel one was on the tennessee river below the kentucky dam. There were three gates open on the dam discharging water. According to witnesses at the scene and the surviving passenger from vessel one the following events occurred. Vessel one was near the new bridge piers and drifting south toward the dam due to current. Vessel one had motor problems and the motor would not pull itself. Vessel one drifted too close discharging waters from dam and operator yelled for help.  A witness vessel nearby came to the aid and tried to pull vessel one away from the dam but was unable. Discharged water started landing on vessel one. All three occupants were ejected into the water. One occupant was rescued by a nearby vessel . Two other occupants were not located and are still missing. Small amounts of debris have been located, pieces of seats, fuel tank, life jackets, and a bill of sale. Vessel one has not been recovered..as of 4/1/2013, the bodies of the missing have not been recovered.

OCCUPANTS ON VESSEL ONE WERE FISHING WHEN ONE OF THE OCCUPANTS NOTICED THERE WAS WATER IN THE FLOOR OF THE VESSEL.  THE OPERATOR WENT TO THE DRIVER SEAT TO ATEMPT TO START THE ENGINE WHICH STARTED FOR A SECOND AND DIED. OPERATOR TRIED TO START THE MOTOR 2 -3  MORE TIMES AND IT DID NOT START. AT THIS TIME THE WATER WAS RUSHING INTO THE VESSEL SO HE TOLD THE OTHER PEOPLE ON BOARD TO MOVE TO THE BOW OF THE BOAT. THEY THEN ALL JUMPED INTO THE WATER TRYING TO SWIM TO THE SHORE. ALCOHOL WAS NOT A FACTOR AND PFD'S WERE NOT BEING WORN OR USED.  One person died.

A LOCAL FISHERMAN HAD NOTICED A TRUCK AND BOAT TRAILER AT THE RAMP AND NOTICED A VESSEL ON THE LAKE THAT WAS UNMANNED. THE FISHERMAN NOTIFIED 911 TO REPORT THE INCIDENT. WHEN THE OFFICERS ARRIVED AT THE SCENE, THE BODY OF THE DECEASED HAD BEEN RECOVERED FROM THE LAKE BY SEARCH AND RESCUE. THERE WAS NO VISIBLE DAMAGE TO THE VESSL OR ANY OF ITS CONTENTS. AUTOPSY RESULTS REVEALED SOME HEALTH ISSUES BUT NO SIGNIFICANT TRAUMA. A PFD WAS NOT BEING WORN.

Victim was last seen operating a vessel on the lake before a severe storm hit. Victim was traveling from the mouth of a branch towards the marina. Fiends noticed victims vessel aground on the island near the creek and contacted the marina staff to check and see if victim was at his houseboat. The marina then called 911.
The use of alcohol/drugs is unknown.  The body has not been found.

Vessel one was fishing in very close proximity to dam 53 anchored in the slack water next to the turbulent waters being expelled from the dams wickets. According to the operator of the vessel the passenger attemped to raise the anchor so that they could get closer to the dam. Upon the anchor being raised the vessel was swept into the rushing water from the wickets ejecting both operator and passenger into the water. According to the witness working at the dam the first time the vessel was noticed was approximately 600 yards down stream.  The vessel was floating upright but nearly full of water. A nearby fisherman boated over to the distressed vessel and pulled the operator of vessel one out of the water alive. The fisherman then pulled the passenger out of the water who was deceased. Operator of vessel one stated they had probably been in the water for 30 minutes or so. A vessel from dam 53 launched and they met the fisherman and retrieved the passengers body and attempted cpr and aed but to no avail. The deceased passenger was taken back to dam 53 to await coroner. Alcohol was not suspected. Pfd's where not being worn or used.

Vessel was being propelled by a trolling motor according to statements from the operator of the vessel and surviving passenger all had been consuming alcohol. Due to unknown reasons the passenger in the front of the vessel stood up, lost balance and fell out of the vessel causing it to capsize and ejecting the other two subjects into the water. operator of vessel stated that the deceased victim yelled for operator to get passenger since passenger could not swim.  Operator grabbed passenger  and held onto the vessel which was capsized in the water. Both operator and passenger stated that they never heard from deceased again. Operator stated that the capsized vessel seemed to be sinking and they were calling for help. A nearby fisherman on the bank heard them yelling and called 911. Rescue team members arrived within approximately 10-15 minutes and rescued operator and passenger from the water as they were hanging onto a limb line in a tree. Rescue squad members and wildlife officers searched the lake the remainder of the evening for deceased.  There were empty beer cans floating in the vessel, no life jackets were noticed. Alcohol was a contributing factor, pfd's where not being worn or used.
News media reports indicate that a man's body was found in the water with his boat still running in circles.  Alcohol and drug use was indicated. No knowledge of pfd use.

operator WAS FISHING FROM A PIROGUE WHEN HE LOST HIS BALANCE AND FELL INTO THE WATER. operator's HAND AND ARMS GOT TANGELED IN THE FISHING STRING WHICH PROHIBITED HIM FROM SWIMING AND CAUSING HIM TO DROWN. operator WAS NOT WEARING A PERSONAL FLOTATION DEVICE NOR DID HE HAVE ONE IN HIS PIROUGE.

On 3/8/10 Operator was seen leaving the boat launch on the Atchafalaya River near Butte LaRose.  He was operating vessel LA 6680EZ, a 20 ft. crawfish skiff with a 150 hp tiller handle motor.  A few minutes later witnessess found debris thought to belong to operator floating approximately one half of a mile from the boat launch.  Because witnesses were unsure, authorities were not contacted until approximately 5:00 p.m.  At approximately 11:30 p.m. that same night operator's body was recovered in the same area where the debris was found.  Operator was not wearing a PFD or the kill lanyard for tiller handle motor.  The boat (LA 6680EZ) was recovered.

*Note the River at that time was experiencing a significant tidal change causing a strong current.

Operator was operating his vessel towards a low lying bridge.  One of his occupants was standing as they attempted to pass underneath.  As a result passenger was struck behind the head (and neck) by the bridge causing fatal injuries.  Alcohol was found on board the vessel and blood and urine samples were taken from the driver.  A blood sample was also taken from the victim.  The results from those tests are pending.  PFD's were onboard but did not play a factor in the incident.

SUBJECTS WERE PREPARING TO TIE UP AT THE CAUSEWAY TO FISH WHEN THE VICTIM FELL OFF OF FRONT DECK AND SUFFERED A HEART ATTACK.  IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER OR NOT THE VICTIM HAD THE HEART ATTACK BEFORE HE ENTERED THE WATER OR AFTER HE WENT INTO THE WATER AND PANICKED. INVESTIGATION IS PENDING. PFD'S WERE ON BOARD, BUT WERE NOT USED.  ALCOHOL WAS NOT A FACTOR.

On 5-1-2010 at approximately 1420 two subjects and two large breed dogs were on a 15ft canoe, without any life jackets, in the Mississippi river, near the Carrollton Avenue area, in Orleans Parish. The weather conditions were severe, winds out of the south at 30 mph and a very strong current in the river which created 4ft waves.  The subjects were witnessed by a tug boat Cpt. and his mate having trouble with the current and heading toward a group of rake barges known as the Carrollton Fleet.  As the Cpt. and his mate headed down river they lost sight of the subjects and knew something bad had happened.  They immediately called for help from other tug boats on the river and also notified the Coast Guard and N.O. Harbor Police.  After searching the area a tug boat was able to recover the canoe and a waterproof bag containing one of the missing subject's phones, some dog food, and a twelve pack of Heineken beer.  Search and Rescue crews were unable to locate the two subjects at the time of the incident.  Both were recovered in the river days after the incident.

At approximately 10:18 PM two subjects were running a trot line near the Black River lock and dam.  The boat they were using was a 12' Bateau without any type of motor.  While running their trot line this boat overturned and partially sank.  Neither man was wearing a PFD and, there were no PFD's found in the boat.  According to a witness the men did not take any PFD's with them and they both had been drinking alcohol.  Dragging operation began that night and continued until approximately 3 AM the next morning.  At approximately 7 AM dragging operation began again and their bodies were found at approximately 8:41 AM and 8:46 AM.  Catahoula Parish Coroner Raymond Rouse sent the bodies off for an autopsy.

ON MAY 29, 2010, operator WAS OPERATING A VESSEL (LA-2177-BF) ON LAKE MAUREPAUS WITH 4 PASSENGERS. THE PASSENGERS JUMPED FROM THE VESSEL INTO THE WATER TO GO SWIMMING. operator RETURNED TO THE NOW SWIMMING PASSENGERS TO RETRIEVE THEM FROM THE WATER. AS HE PULLED UP TO THEM, HE THOUGHT HE PUT THE VESSEL IN THE LOCKED NEUTRAL POSITION. IT WAS NOT. operator THEN JUMPED INTO THE WATER, ACCIDENTLY STRIKING THE THROTTLE WHICH CAUSED THE VESSEL TO ACCELERATE. THE VESSEL THEN WENT INTO A COUNTERCLOCKWISE ROTATION (DEATH CIRCLE), STRIKING 4 OUT OF THE 5 PEOPLE. THIS CAUSED 3 FATALITIES AND 1 SERIOUS BODILY INJURY. ALCOHOL IS NOT SUSPECTED TO BE A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR. (BLOOD DRAWN RESULTS PENDING @ LSP CRIME LAB. PFD'S WERE NOT USED AND ONLY 3 WERE SERVICEABLE.

On 7/14/2010 at about 5:25 pm, operator left from the Dulac Store boat launch to go fishing in Lake Boudreaux. He was following his cousinwho was in another vessel. According to family members, operator drives his vessel while sitting on top of the center steering console, in fornt of the steering wheel. As he headed towards Lake Boudreaux, he approached a hard right turn. As he turned to the right, the steering failed and his vessel made an abrupt right turn. Both operator and the steering console were ejected over the port side. The vessel ran up into the marsh and was partially covered with grass. operator was reported missing later that night by his girlfriend at about 10:58 pm. Terrebonne S/O and the USCG searched through the night for him. His vessel was located at 6:45 am on 7/15/2010 and he was recovered from the water by Terrebonne S/O at 5:21 pm that same day. operator was not wearing a PFD, nor was he wearing his killswitch lanyard. The use of drugs or alcohol will be determined by Terrebonne Parish Coroner's Office, pending autopsy report. The steering cable was mounted to the engine improperly and the piece of the steering console that was recovered from the water indicated that the console was rotten. This evidence, as well as the position that operator sits as he drives hi vessel are contributing factors in the cause of the incident.

On may 26th, 2010, the owner / operator of a 1982 sabre, 17 feet in length, which displayed expired florida registration fl-2732-fx, was traveling westbound across lake pontchartrain enroute to the mandeville harbor with Operator’s three (3) year old son and a friend / employee, 35 years of age. According to information provided by Operator, at approx 2355 hrs his vessel went out of control spinning like a "carnival ride" that resulted in him and his son being thrown to the floor and his friend being thrown out of the vessel. Operator advised agents that he did not know what had happened to cause his vessel to go out of control; he stated that he could have possibly hit an object in the water but he wasn't sure. A search was immediately conducted by louisiana wildlife and fisheries, the st. Tammany parish sheriff's office and the united states coast guard, which consisted of numerous patrol vessels and two (2) helicopters, but their search for friend was unsuccessful. Operator voluntarily consented to give blood for any intoxicants at lakeview regional hospital in the presence of senior agent. During the course of the investigation only two (2) pfd's (personal flotation devices) were located, which both Operator and his son were wearing. When asked about the third pfd Operator stated it must have blown out when the boat went out of control. For further information, see the narrative portion of this report as well as all written statements.

operator (34) and his daughter, (17) borrowed vessel "LA 8219 FV" and traveled to Mississippi River Borrow Pits near Delta, Louisiana to go fishing.  Their fishing activities concluded some time after sunset.  As it became dark, they began a return travel to the launch area using a trolling motor.  During the return, operator stated that his daughter asked for a "Gatorade" from the cooler.  He consented and heard the cooler close.  He then stated that he heard a splash.  When he turned around, he could see her in the water.  He claimed to have immediately made a starboard turn to return her to her location.  When he arrived , he claims he never saw her surface again.  At 8:45pm, the owner of the vessel called to check on his property.  At the time, operator stated that his daughter fell out of the boat and he was looking for her.  The owner of the vessel immediately called the Madison Sheriff's Office and reported the incident.  operator 911 *911* call was made and recorded at 8:49pm Emergency responders arrived and began the search for daughter.  Her body was recovered at 2:05am the following morning.
location: MS River Borrow Pit, Delta, I-, LA

description: There were four (4) more passengers onboard the 22' pontoon boat.  The vessel was driven by steering wheel, and contained approximately fourteen (14) type three (3) PFD's, and one (1) type four (4) PFD.  As Operator was idling out of the no wake zone at Indian Bayou, Occupant1 and his girlfriend were concluding an argument in one of the forward seats in the vessel.  The two (2) other passengers were lying out on the back of the vessel.  Girlfriend stated that she told Occupant1 that she needed to use the restroom.  Occupant1 told her to just jump in the water, because they were just idling.  Girlfriend stated that she did not want to while the vessel was moving.  Occupant1 then got up from the seat, and dove directly over the bow of the vessel, between the pontoons.  Operator stated that all he saw was Occupant1' feet going over the front of the vessel.  Operator stated that he looked down to kill the vessel, but could not kill it in time, and he heard the vessel strike Occupant1.  Operator stated that he was unfamiliar with this type of vessel, and had only been sitting at the helm for a minute or two.  Girlfriend stated that occupant2 was operating the vessel, but the other passengers stated that occupant2 had been operating the vessel all day, but had just asked Operator to drive.  After the vessel struck Occupant1, he came up behind the vessel and stated to call an ambulance.  Girlfriend jumped into the water, and they were able to get Occupant1 onto the rear of the vessel.  They then called 911, and pulled to a dock.  Occupant1 sustained major lacerations to his lower body from the prop.  He was transported to the hospital, and passed away later that  night.  Operator was given an HGN on the dock, and showed no signs of nystagmus.  Operator was transported to the Region V office, and given a test onthe intoxilzyer 5000.  The results were 0.000g%.

On Sunday, June 20, 2010 operator, his wife and another subject were traveling in Lake Palourde in LA 2659 EN. At about 1430 the vessel stopped to idle so that subject could urinate. As she leaned over the rear starboard deck, she fell in the water. operator jumped in the water to save her but he never returned. Subject  who wanted to urinate was not wearing any pfd. Operator’s pfd was not buckled so when he jumped in the water, it quickly came off. wife of operator advised that the vessel was idling in neutral. On 6/21/10, operator was recovered from the water by LDWF Sgt. and St. Mary Deputy.

Vessel 1 was traveling south and vessel 2 was traveling north.  According to the operator of vessel 2 (74' tug boat pushing 5 barges), vessel 1 appeared that it was going to pass on his starboard, until just before that time it abruptly turned in the path of the lead barge . The operator of vessel 2 stated he then observed a large splash in that area and stopped his vessel and barges and called authorities. Agents arrived on the scene and could not locate vessel 1 or its operator.  At approximately 5:00pm,8/8/10, the body of the operator of vessel 1 was recovered near the incident scene. PFD's were not used by either party. Vessel 2 was equipped with all necessary safety equipment and navigation lights.  It is unknown  if Vessel 1 was equipped with PFD's or navigation lights.  The operator of vessel 2 showed no signs of intoxication and submitted a proper breath and urine sample at Berwick Police Department. His breath BAC results were .000 and results on his urine are pending tesing by LA State Police Crime Lab.  Two subjects who refused to give written statements advised agents that the operator of vessel 1 had been drinking beer with them at a camp prior to the incident. An ice chest was recovered floating near the incident scene which family members advised belonged to  the operator of vessel 1. Agents observed 13/12oz beer and 8/7oz beers in the ice chest.  A post mortem blood sample was  taken by the St. Martin Parish Coroner with results pending. The deceased had no signs of serious wounds or trauma.

On 6-20-2010 at approximately 9:30 p.m. four subjects were on board a vessel, LA 66410 FS, in Jefferson Parish when they struck the Causeway Bridge while heading West bound.  The driver and two of the occupants were ejected, were wearing their PFD's survivied and one occupant that stayed in the vessel were rescued by the USCG and were transported to University Hospital for injuries.  The operator's body was recovered on 06-22-2010 by LDWF agents and transferred to the Jefferson Parish Coroners Office.  According to the autopsy report the driver was intoxicated with a blood alcohol content of .113 which was the leading factor of the incident.  This boating incident resulted in one fatality and three injuries.

victim's BODY WAS FOUND IN WATER NEAR HIS BOAT BY ANOTHER FISHERMAN.  victim WAS NOT WEARING A PFD, BUT HAD ONE IN THE BOAT.  NO EVIDENCE OF ALCOHOL OR DRUG USE WAS FOUND. THERE WAS ALSO NO EVIDENCE OF ANY TYPE OF COLLISION.  IT APPEARS victim fell ovERBOARD.

Three people were fishing in a 14' aluminum boat on a private pond.  The boat did not have any type motor attached.  Only paddles were used for manuvering.  There were no PFD's used or found near the incident location.  The boat had been anchored by a heavy weight.  As the operator stood up in the boat to pull up the anchor, he lost his balance and caused a weight transfer to one side of the boat.  The boat capsized, and all three occupants went into the water.  one occupant assisted another to the bank and operator tried swimming to the other bank, but went under before he reached it. the two adults had been drinking alcoholic beverages.
location: Private Pond behind Madden Con, LA

description:
On 02/26/2011 at approximately 5:50pm, Senior Agents were on patrol in Ouachita Parish and received a call from Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office regarding a possible drowning in progress on Bayou Desiard.  We arrived on the scene at approximately 6:03pm around the 1000 block of Highway 136, Sterlington, La.  OPSO, Sterlington P.D., and AMR were already on the scene with the recovered body.
