Paramedics on scene stated that victim had been deceased for approximately 35 minutes.  I made contact with the survivor of the incident, and identified myself as a LDWF Enforcement Agent.  Survivor was very upset and unable to answer any questions while at the scene.  I spoke with the victim’s father on the scene and he stated that just before the two brothers started their fishing trip, he advised them not to get in that small boat together.  Senior Agent and I retrieved the overturned vessel at approximately 6:25pm. We observed a small styrofoam ice chest floating next to the overturned vessel and no other items.  We did not observe any personal floatation devices around the scene of the incident.  Photographs of the scene and vessel involved were taken and will be included with the report.

On 02/27/2011 at approximately 1:30pm, Senior Agent and I made contact with the survivor of the incident. Both the victim and survivor reside with their parents at this address which is located on Bayou Desiard approximately ¼ mile from the scene of the incident.  According to his voluntary witness statement, Survivor was at the bow of the boat and his brother was at the stern.  He stated they had no PFD’s in the vessel and each had consumed five beers.  Three possible contributing factors:  passenger behavior, alcohol use, and overloading.  

The vessel measured less than 11 feet in length and likely had no more than a few inches of freeboard.  Survivor stated that he was hanging a yo-yo on a tree when his brother (victim) lost his balance and caused them to overturn.  He stated that Victim was having difficulty keeping his head above water.  He tried helping Victim by pushing the overturned vessel to him and telling him to hang on, but the small boat kept sinking and causing Victim to go under.  Survivor stated that he retrieved their small styrofoam ice chest from nearby and tried getting it under Victim.  Survivor then began swimming to shore go get help.   The distance was approximately 75 feet from the overturned vessel to the shoreline.  Survivor said when he made it to the shore, he turned to look at his brother and he was still floating but not moving. He then ran up the hill to Highway 136 and flagged down a passerby.  Good samaritan stated that Survivor flagged him down.  Good samaritan said he found a small community boat near the scene and was able to make it to Victim’s location by treading the water with his hands.  He stated that Victim was face down in the water and not moving.  He grabbed Victim and was able to get him to shallow water.  OPSO deputies arrived on the scene and retrieved the body out of water.  The Coroner’s office took possession of Victim body at approximately 6:30pm on 02/26/2011.  A preliminary to be autopsy showed victim likely died of drowning.

It appeared that after further investigation, Victim was fishing trot lines, when for some unknown reason he fell overboard.  It appeared that the boat continued to drift off to the North/Northwest until it came to rest on the North bank adjacent to where Victim was located.  The wind was out of the Southeast on this day.  The trolling motor was down in the water and the main engine switch was on the off position.  The throttle was in the neutral position.  We found that the trolling motor switch was off when it was checked, however, it did appear that he was using the trolling motor while setting out his trot lines.  The boat was approximately 229 yards away from Victim’s body.  Victim’s body was found to be approximately 60 yards from the trot line that he placed out.  It appeared that victim died from Hypothermia and heart failure (See attached Coroner’s report and death certificate).

On 02/12/11 at approximately 07:30 a.m. registered vessel AL 1508 LL, a 25 foot Grady White, powered by twin 150 hp Yamaha outboards with remote steering was underway in the Gulf of Mexico occupied by five persons.  According to statement given by passenger and lone survivor, the vessel was traveling at a speed of about 10 mph due to choppy sea conditions (2-3 feet), there were no indications of trouble until one of the vessels two outboards killed. Survivor stated that the operator of the vessel turned off the second engine and was trying to restart the engine that had killed, when it was noticed a large amount of water was entering the inside cockpit area from the rear of the vessel.  Survivor stated that within a short period of time, estimated to be approximately two minutes, the vessel flooded, then overturned sending everyone into the water.  During this time survivor advised they were able to retrieve four life jackets that were contained in the overhead T-Top and send out an emergency call on the VHF radio, but was not sure if it had been received.  None of the subjects were able to don the life jackets before going into the water.  Survivor stated that no one was able to properly get the life jackets on while in the water, but held on to them for support.  Survivor managed to get atop the overturned hull of the vessel and remove himself from the water.  The other four subjects attempted to climb atop the overturned vessel, but were unsuccessful.  Over a period of time all four subjects that remained in the water lost consciousness and succumbed.  Survivor remained atop the overturned vessel until spotted by the offshore supply vessel " SEA ANGEL", at approximately 1:15 p.m., the same day, at which time he was rescued. Agents could not definitively say how the water got into the boat.

Operator1 was traveling in a westerly direction, heading out of Lk. Borne into Unknown Pass, in his vessel a 20 ft. Hydrasport (LA 2166 FS).  Operator2 was heading in an Easterly direction heading into Lk. Borgne, in his 18 ft. Boston Whaler (MT 6078 AZ). Both vessels were operating at a planing speed and met in a head on situation in a blind bend in the pass.  The preliminary investigations shows that Operator 1made a hard turn to port causing a collision with vessel2 which caused both operator2 to be ejected and his vessel to drift a short distance from the collision site.  Both operators received injuries, Operator1’s being fatal.  Operator2 was wearing an inflatable PFD, but it did not inflate.  Operator1 had a PFD on board but was not wearing it at at the time of the accident.  Neither captain was wearing his kill switch at the time of the accident.  Alcohol was not a factor. Note: Unable to determine what specific objects in Vessels 1 or 2 caused the trauma.

We were advised of a sunken boat in Lafourche by LPSO.  The boat was marked with GPS coordinates N29 19 555 and W90 11 842 and rested upright but sunken in approximately 1 1/2 feet of water. The vessel was identified as LA0225ZB a 14 ft Polar Kraft HIN:PLR45669M77A and belonging to Injured victim.  The vessel was equipped with a tiller steer 25 hp Mercury engine SN#0G078410.  Examination of the engine showed the cover to be off, mud on the upper parts of the exposed engine, the engine to be in gear, and the kill switch was in the "run" postion with no lanyard attached.  The vessel appeared to have seen much use and we were unable to discern a fresh collision point, although there was a significant dent mid ship on the  underside of the vessel port side. (A later examination showed an approximately 8" long by 1/8" wide gash in the hull that had been repaired at one time but was now reopened). A body was recovered and later Identified as Operator.  The deceased had a boat plug in his pocket and the vessel did not have a plug in place. I was given an unmarked pill bottle that had been discovered in the debris by LPSO and contained a large quantity of pills (79). I was able to make a possible match for the pills based on their stamp "Watson 540". Pill imprint WATSON 540 has been identified as Acetaminophen and hydrocodone bitartrate 500 mg/10mg. Injured victim was rescued from the water near the accident and brought to Our lady of the Sea Hospital. We met with Injured victim and had the hospital do a blood sample kit (At the time we were unsure of who the operator was and we were in the process of reconstructing the events of the accident. ) After advising the subject of his rights we got a preliminary verbal statement from him. 

He claimed that he and Operator decided to go night fishing the previous night and left off boat launch around 7:30 to 8:00PM.  While trying to find an area to fish they struck an oyster reef and broke the seal on the fiberglass patch on the hull.  He claimed that they pulled the plug of the boat to drain the water while underway and through some misfortune were unable to keep the boat from sinking. Injured victim stated that the vessel sank upright and they abandoned it in favor of walking back to town through the marsh.  I asked Injured victim about possible contributing factors and he stated that the night was clear with a mostly full moon and the water was calm.  he stated that after walking some distance the two of them got separated he decided to try to stay warm until daylight. Given the information from Injured victim, it is at this point that it appears as though Operator returned to the vessel and attempted to try to get in the vessel afloat and operational. this would explain the removed engine cover. It does not provide answers to what events lead to Operator's death.  No PFDs were used nor was a safety lanyard available or used even thought the engine was capable.

On March 19,2011 vessel, LA 2803 AK, was being operated.  Occupant was located in front of console and was seated.  Vessel made a sudden violent turn to starboard ejecting both men from the port side of the vessel.  Vessel's propeller then struck both men.  Operator was removed from the water and was taken to University Hospital where he was pronounced dead. Occupant was seen by eye witness, and family member unconscious in the water, and while removing Operator from the water he lost visual contact with him.  Family member was in his own boat and was NOT PHYSICALLY INVOLVED in the incident. LDWDF in conjunction with the St. Bernard Parish Sheriff's Marine Division and U.S. Coast Guard continued search and rescue missions for Occupant.  Neither of the men were wearing PFD's and the kill switch lanyard was not attached to the boat or operator.  However, the kill switch was in the up position to allow the motor to operate. No alcohol was found in the vessel when investigators arrived on the scene.  The vessel, LA 2803 AK, which is described as an 18 foot Campagna with a 75 hp Mercury outboard motor was seized by LDWF agents for investigative purposes.  The vessel was tagged with evidence tag 67897 and is being stored at the LDWF impound yard located in Chalmette until conclusion of the investigation.  As of March 22, 2011 the body of Occupant was located near the GPS coordinates provided by family member.  He was transported to the Orleans parish Coroner's Office.

On 3/18/11 (operator1), his wife and two grandchildren were in boat (LA-4713-FE) headed down stream on Saline Bayou.  Operator1 states all four were wearing type III PFD's.  Operator2 was by himself in boat (LA-7665-EW) and heading up stream on Saline Bayou.

Operator2 was wearing a type III PFD.  The two boats met near an area commonly called "Hickory Cutoff" in a head-on situation.  Attempts by both operators were unsuccessful in preventing a collision.  Operator2 was ejected from the boat as a result of the collision. OPerator2's body was later recovered and he was pronounced dead by Rapides Parish Coroner's office.  There were no injuries to anyone from the boat1.  Drug and alcohol test are pending on both operators.

On 03/16/2011 Operator was reported missing by wife.  Wife stated that her husband had gone fishing early that Wednesday morning.  When she returned home that evening at 5:00pm she could see his boat but could not see Operator.  Wife notified subject and he came to investigate.  subject found Operator boat "vessel" 1 near the bank, but was not tied.  He found two fishing rods in the water near the boat.  subject stated that there was a 12" aluminium boat "vessel" 2 floating capsized near vessel 1. At the time dragging operations started vessel 2 was approx. 200 yards from vessel 1.  victim was found floating underneath vessel 2.  The events that led to the death of Operator are unknown. Franklin Parish Coroner's Office listed the cause of death was drowing.  It was reported that Operator could not swim and refused to wear a PFD while fishing.  His health was poor and he suffered from the effects of a stroke.  No witness have come forward with information about the accident.

Agents received call in reference to possible boating incident on Calcasieu River.  Upon arrival, agents observed vessel, LA 9289 FW, a 14' Tracker with a semi vee bottom operated by remote steering, floating freely on the west side of the Calcasieu River approximately 50 feet inside of the highline ditch.  Agents observed the throttle was in neutral and the ignition key was off, with the motor trimmed all the way down.  The safety cutoff lanyard was still attached to the safety cutoff switch.  Agents motored south on the Calcasieu River approximately .16 miles downstream to two vessels occupied by the men who called in the incident, and the body of Operator was recovered, agents observed Operator had a fishing bait hooked in the right sleeve of his shirt, in the cuff, near his hand.  Agents also observed Operator had a fishing rod in his left hand, with the tip broken off.  Operator fell overboard from his vessel, and was not wearing a PFD at the time the incident occurred.  The contributing factors are unknown.  Agents did note the trolling motor was down with power setting set on power 2.  The switch has to be pressed to engage the power on the trolling motor.  Toxicology tests are pending.

On 6/3/11 at approximately 5:45 p.m., Operator and Occupant were fishing in the Southwestern Canal located in Leeville. Operator was experiencing motor trouble, so he attempted to tie his vessel, LA3051BH, to a piling in the canal. At this time, Operator fell overboard into the swift current of the Southwestern Canal.  Occupant quickly threw Operator a PFD, which Operator attempted to put on. subject was unable to pursue Operator due to the fact that the engine would not crank and she was unaware of how to use the trolling motor. 

At approximately 6:45 p.m. subject2 and his father noticed a PFD in the water and turned around. They then saw a body attached to the PFD, and quickly called 911.  Officers from the Lafourche Parish SO as well as Harbor Patrol responded quickly and retrieved Operator, who was indeed wearing a PFD.  The PFD was not properly fastened causing the PFD to come off of Operator while the officers were attempting to pull him into their vessel. Sgt. was notified of the accident at approximately 8:00 p.m. and arrived at the scene at approximately 8:45 p.m.  Sgt. inspected the vessel and found no evidence of any alcohol and/or drugs in the vessel. The vessel, LA3051BH, contained 3 type 3 PFDs and the steering on the vessel was in good working order, constructed of a wheel and teleflex steering cable On 6/5/11, Sgt. was contacted by the Laourche DO, and advised that Operator expired from a massive heart attack.  The coroner also Sgt. that here was very little water in Operator's lungs.

On 4/22/2011 at approx 11:30 a.m. Operator was operating a 14' aluminum duracraft flat boat powered by a trolling motor only in a private lake located at 1502 j.h. jenkins lane, denham springs, la. Operator was in the process of putting out a trotline. He was accompanied by two passengers. Operator was sitting in the front of the vessel on the deck in a pedestal type seat. Operator leaned over the port side of the vessel to drop the last trotline weight. When he leaned the vessel also leaned to the port side at which time the hinges that were not secured (see photos) allowed the seat pedestal assembly which was mounted to the cargo storage door to lean as well resulting in Operator and the assembly to fall overboard. 

At this time occupant jumped in the water to assist Operator who could not swim and was panicking. She attempted to help him but was overcome by him and shortly became exhausted and started swallowing water. She then backed off and he went under and never came back up. The vessel had now drifted a good distance away from her due to the wind. When her son saw her struggling he jumped in with a life jacket and helped her back to the vessel. They then called for help. Gps coordinates at the location of the trotline weight was recorded and search for Operator began there. Operators body was recovered by the tangipahoa fire departments drag team at 1:57 p.m. (1357 hrs) in this area. He was pronounced dead via drowning by the st. Helena coroner. Note: the vessel was equipped with three type one pfd's but none were worn. Occupant advised that Operator did advise her he could not swim when getting into the vessel so she offered him a pfd but he advised if it is his time to go then it is just his time to go. No alcohol or drugs suspected.

Operator's vehicle was backed on ramp with the trailer in the water.  Vessel began to sink for unknown reason and operator began to swim to shore but did not make it.  PFD's were on board, but not worn.  Imvolvement of alcohol is unknown at this time.  No alcohol found onboard.

On the afternoon of June 6, 2011, three subjects, three people entered private property west of Hwy 34 in the town of Eros, in Jackson Parish.   They did not have permission to be on this property.  They entered this property to access a pond in which to swim.  All three subjects got into a 12 Brewster aluminum boat (no motor or trolling motor) and paddled into the pond.  At approximately 2 - 4 PM the boat either overturned or began to take on water (conflicting statements from survivors) and all three subjects went into the water.  It was apparent at this time that Victim could not swim, so Subject1 tried to save him.  He grabbed Victim and tried to swim with him, but due to Victim trying to pull him under, he finally got away and swam to the bank.  Victim went underwater approximately 30 feet from the bank.  After Victim went under, both Subject2 and Subject1 walked to Subject2's residence, where Subject2 changed into dry clothes.  Subject2's dad was at home, but neither he nor Subject1 said anything about Victim drowning in the pond.  After changing clothes, Subject2 and Subject1 walked to the Subject1 residence (between 4:15 - 4:30 pm) where Subject1 changed clothes and the two began watching TV.  

At this point, neither had told anybody about the drowning nor had they contacted the Jackson Parish Sheriffs Office (JPSO).  At approximately 6 pm, the mother of Subject1 arrived and told Subject2 that he needed to go home because they were going to a birthday party.  Subject2 left the subject1 residence  between 6 - 6:15.  Mother and son then left for the party at approximately 6:30pm.   Subject1 

still did not say anything about the drowning to his mother.   At approximately 6:54 pm, a 911 call was received at JPSO from Subject2 residence concerning the possible drowning.  JPSO deputies and volunteer firemen arrived at the pond.  Upon arrival, they met with Subject2 and his dad.  Subject2 was in the pond looking for Victim.  

Agents launched a boat and recovered the body of Victim approximately 30 feet from the bank at  8:50pm.  Victim's body was located on the southwest corner of the pond, the overturned boat was located on the northeast corner of the pond.  Victim's body was removed from the pond and he was pronounced dead at approximately 9:00pm,  by Jackson Parish coroner.  The body of Victim was sent to Little Rock, Arkansas for an autopsy.  I seized the boat and transported it to the Region 2 office in Monore.  The boat displayed no registration numbers nor did it have a hull ID number.  The owner of the pond of Chatham stated that the boat did not belong to her or her immediate family, and did not know who owned the boat.  

During the investigation, the primary cause (1) of the accident was overloading of the small 12' boat  (older,  thin aluminum boat with very little free board)  with three people. The secondary cause (2) was all three began rocking the boat from side to side causing it to take on water (conflicting statements among survivors) and eventually capsize. The tertiary (3) cause was improper loading of the boat by having one person sitting on the bow of the boat, causing it to sit low in the water to the point that it began to take on water.

The autopsy report was freshwater drowning.  The autopsy report is also included in this report.

Operator stopped his vessel in lake maurepas so passengers could use the bathroom. As passenger entered the water the boat began to drift away from him due to strong winds. Passenger, not being a good swimmer, began having trouble staying afloat so he asked operator if he could throw him a lifevest. Operator threw the lifevest to passenger, but the lifevest was taken by the wind. Operator entered the water retrieved the lifevest and brought it over to passenger. Passenger returned to the vessel safely with the aid of the lifevest. At this time, operator began having difficulty swimming due to weather conditions. Passenger2 entered the water with a lifevest, swam over to operator, and gave him the lifevest. Passenger2 stated that operator had the lifevest in his possesion but was too weak to hold on to the lifevest and went underwater. Passenger2 made several attempts to locate operator but was unsuccessful. At this time passenger was able to put passenger2 into the vessel where they called 911. Subject was being treated for cancer and may have been under the influence of narcotic pain medicine, autopsy pending.

TWO VESSELS NAVIGATING AROUND A BLIND TURN, AT CRUISING SPEEDS, COLLIDE.  VESSEL 1 WAS OCCUPIED BY TWO SUBJECTS.  THE OPERATOR WAS EJECTED WITH INJURY AND LATER PASSED AWAY.  PASSENGER ON VESSEL 1 WAS SERIOUSLY INJURED AND BROUGHT TO THE HOSPITAL.  VESSEL 2 WAS OCCUPIED BY 7 SUBJECTS.   FOUR OF THE SUBJECTS WERE EJECTED.  ONE SUBJECT SUSTAINED A MINOR LEG INJURY.  AT THIS TIME ALCOHOL AND/OR DRUGS DO NOT SEEM TO BE A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR, THAT WILL BE DETERMINED UPON TOXICOLOGY RESULTS.

On the afternoon of 6/25/11 at approximately 7:45 p.m. witnesses observed an unoccupied vessel going in circles in the middle of Lake Dauterive.  The engine of the vessel soon killed and the witnesses placed the boat on anchor and called 911.  Subject located a cell phone on board the unoccupied vessel and determined the phone belonged to Operator.  Once they ascertained the identity of the missing person, the witnesses began searching the area in an attempt to locate the subject.  They soon located a pair of sandals (Crocs) floating in the near vicinity of the anchored vessel. 

Agents were notified of the situation by Iberia Parish Sheriff's office at approximately 8:50 p.m.  We arrived on scene at approximately 9:20 p.m. and made contact with the witnesses.  Lt. spoke to another gentleman, subject2, who stated that he also observed the unoccupied vessel and hurried to the boat launch to call 911.  The aforementioned witnesses advised us of the recent happenings.  We were able to locate a GPS device aboard Operator's vessel and we followed its tracklog.  At one point along the tracklog, in close proximity to where the vessel was originally located, the vessel appeared to make a 90 degree starboard turn.  We elected to begin dragging body drags at this location and continued to do so until approximately 2:00 a.m. on 6/26/11 at which time we postponed the search until after sunrise.  

On 6/26/11 at approximately 8:00 a.m. we resumed our search efforts with the assistance of the Iberia Parish Sheriff's office and the St. Martin Parish Sheriff's office.  At approximately 12:45 p.m. the body of Operator was located.  We brought the body aboard the vessel and transported the body to the landing where the Iberia Parish Coronor was on scene.  The body was transported to Iberia Medical Center where members of the Coroner's office performed an initial assessment of the body.  Lt. and I arrived at the Coroner's office and were told the body had no visible signs of injury.  We were also told that an autopsy would be performed at which time a full toxicology screening would be conducted.  This report will be available within 8-12 weeks.

Operator1 and father were anchored out along the Mermentau River engaged in fishing.  The boat, vessel #1 (LA 1958 FA) was tied off from both bow and stern  to two separate pipes which were buried in the river bottom.
     Vessel #1 was approached by a commercial crabbing vessel (LA 0312 SK) which was throwing a large wake.  The wake of vessel #2 jerked vessel #1 against its mooring lines, causing both occupants of vessel #1 to be thrown from the vessel.  Both of the occupants of vessel #1 managed to climb back into their vessel and get underway back to the landing.  Vessel #2 did not see that they had caused the incident and proceeded north in the Mermentau River.  It was eventually found out by investigators that the operator of vessel #2 stated that he had never seen the vessel #1 because of a sporadic treeline along the river, blocking his view of vessel #1.  While underway the short distance (approximately one mile) back to the landing occupant, while speaking to operator1, suffered an attack and became incoherent and unresponsive.  Upon reaching the landing operator called 911 and the Cameron Sheriff Office sent medical assistance to Myers Landing to meet Vessel #1.  Ground and air medical ambulances were dispatched to the scene where victim was pronounced dead on the scene.  Alcohol was not suspected to be a factor.  Neither occupant was wearing a PFD.  This was not a factor as both subjects were able to re-board the vessel after the incident.  The Calcasieu Corner's Office performed an autopsy and the results stated that the manner of death was accidential; however, the conclusion stated that the fall into the lake was the precipitating event which led the heart attack and ultimately to his death.

For subjects launched an 18' aluminum hull vessel into Red River Cut in Concordia Parish.  The vessel was being operated east bound towards the U.S. Corps of Engineers Water Control Structure in extremely turbullent waters and strong current.  As a result of operating the vessel into this water, an unknown obstruction struck the engine of this vessel, stopping the engine and pulling this vessel and passengers into even stronger currents and turbullent waters.  Three of the passengers were wearing PFD's and as this vessel capsized, they made it to safety while the operator was not wearing a PFD and eventually drowned.  This vessel was propelled by a Mercury 90 HP outboard motor.  Alcohol or drugs is not suspected as a contributing factor in this accident.

Operator and passenger were traveling south in Grand Lake.  They were in a 14' vessel with a 25 HP Tiller handle outboard.  The seas state on this day was 1'-3' waves.  Operator stated that it started to get rough, and the vessel was taking on some water.  They came down to an idle speed, and attempted to turn around.  When they made the turn, a wave hit the vessel, and began to flood the vessel.  The operator stated that he took off his PFD, and jumped into the water to keep the vessel from sinking.  He stated that the passenger did the same.  The operator then reached over and gave the motor some gas, and began steering it towards shallow water while hanging onto the side.  Operator stated that the passenger was swimming behind him towards the bank.  The operator drove the vessel into the shallows where the outboard was dragging bottom.  He then attempted to bail out the vessel.  The operator stated that he had pulled the plug on the vessel while he was running to drain some of the water out of  it.  Operator stated that he then got back into the vessel to return to get the passenger.  Operator stated that he forgot to put the plug in, so his vessel began taking on water.  The vessel then became flooded with water, and the operator got out of the vessel.  At this point, he could not see the passenger of the vessel.  He called a friend, who was close by, and they began looking for the passenger.  They were not able to locate the passenger.  The operator then called another vessel to come assist, and that vessel contacted LDWF.  Operator stated that both he and the passenger were wearing PFD's and that he was wearing his ignition safety switch while operating the vessel.  SFST was performed on the operator, and found no signs of intoxication.  The size of the vessel the subjects were in was inadequate for the conditions on the lake during their outing, causing the vessel to take on water and become flooded.

We arrived on scene at approximately 2:15 p.m.  I made contact with Caddo Sheriff's Office Marine Patrol. Lt. stated that subject had contacted CPSO Dispatch about a small jon boat adrift on Twelve Mile Bayou at approximately 8:30 a.m. on 6/23/11.  Lt. stated that she arrived on scene at approxmiately 9:15 a.m. and located the jon boat.  The boat was partially submerged and had come to rest in a partially submerged tree top.  Lt. pulled the vessel to the bank and observed a dark colored Dodge truck parked at the top of the bank.  She observed what appeared to be drag marks from the back of the truck to the water.  

Deputies were dispatched to Victim's residence.  At the residence they made contact with Victim's wife who had reported him missing to Shreveport Police Department, Report #: P11136.  Victim’s wife advised that her husband had left home to go fishing between 3:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. on 6/22/11.  She stated that she had not had any contact with him since that time.  Victim’s wife stated that her husband had several medical issues and that it was out of character for him not to make contact with her.  At this time it was also determined that Victim did indeed have a small jon boat.  Sr. Agt. and I photographed the vessel and did not observe any signs of a collision or foul play.  The vessel was a 10' 2" long jon boat with a 30" bottom.  We also did not see any floating debris in the water or any sign of a PFD.  CPSO Dive Team searched the area for several hours until the team was exhausted.  The search was called off at 7:40 p.m.  A plan was coordinated to meet up at the Stoner Boat Launch on Red River the next morning to resume the search.  The next morning, 6/24/11 at approxmately 6:30 a.m. while enroute to the boat launch Lt. crossed over Twelve Mile Bayou on La. Hwy. 538 and observed what appeared to be a body floating in the water.  Sgt. arrived on scene at approximately 7:00 a.m. and located the body.  The victim was then transported to the Common Street Boat Launch and turned over to the Caddo Parish Coroner.  At this time we are waiting on the coroner's report as to the cause of death and any signs of alcohol or drug use by the victim.

On July 24th, 2011, family members reported to the Louisiana wildlife and Fisheries Law Enforcement Division (LDWF/LED) agents that two people had left to go on a fishing trip in the Mississippi River on the evening of July 23, 2011 and failed to return home. A single witness was located and reported that he had observed the two men departing the public boat launch located near the Mississippi River I-10 Bridge in Baton Rouge, La. The two men reportedly launched a fourteen (14) foot, aluminum, flat bottomed vessel equipped with a tiller steered engine. The subjects were both subsequently found deceased and floating in the river, downstream from the Mississippi River Bridge. 

Both subjects are believed to have drowned while the exact circumstances leading to their deaths are unknown, it is reasonable to presume that at some point during their voyage they encountered a sudden catastrophic situation wherein their vessel is likely to have taken on water and sank. The vessel has not been located to date. It was determined that neither man was wearing a PFD at the time this event occurred. Large barge and ship traffic on the Mississippi River regularly create large wakes resulting in hazardous situations for smaller vessels. It is the opinion of the investigating agent that the vessel used was inadequate for conditions commonly experienced in this area of the river. Also noted is the fact that several thunderstorms were reported in the area later that evening. It has not been determined that alcohol was a factor in this event.

Vessel traveling on Red River after midnight on July 19, 2011, when it ran underneath a log protruding from the end of a rock revetment, whereupon operator was hit in the facial area and ejected.  Vessel continued in a wide arc and ran completely aground on the opposite side of the river.  Upon impact, the passenger was thrown to the front of the vessel, rendering her unconscious with severe facial fractures.  Passenger awoke sometime later and found a person on local hiking trail to render assistance.  Passenger was transported to LSU Medical Center in Shreveport, LA with severe head trama.  Body of operator was recovered sometime later that morning.  Both persons were wearing approved PFD's - alcohol is not suspected to be a factor.

Operator was idling through a stumpy area with the wind blowing out of the NNE at 12 mph with occasional gusts of up to 30 mph.  Operator had his stern to the wind while he was idling.  The passenger suddenly noticed that the boat was filling up with water from the waves coming over the stern.  Operator turned on his bilge pumps and cut his engine off.  Both men went to the front of the boat because the back was flooding and the boat capsized.  Both men already had their type 3 PFD's on when the boat capsized.  

Occupant was able to hold onto the boat and stay with it as it drifted away in the wind.  Operator was able to grab a boat seat and held onto it while he was drifting alone in the wind.  Both men were able to communicate with one another for a short time before they drifted too far away from each other.  After approximately two hours in the water, two subjects on land heard Occupant calling for help and went to assist.  They were able to rescue Occupant and then began searching for Operator.  They located Operator approximately 200 yards upwind of his capsized boat.  He was still wearing his PFD but it was not buckled.  His head was underwater and he was unresponsive.  Due to his size, they were not able to get Operator in the boat.  They tied him off to a stump, placed a marker on the stump, and returned to the shore with Occupant.

Sabine Parish Sheriff's Office was notified of the incident via a 911 call at 3:41 PM and they in turn notified LDWF Enforcement.  At approximately 5:00 PM, body was recovered by LDWF Enforcement agents and Sabine Parish S.O. deputies at the same location he had been left.  A subsequent autopsy revealed that Operator had succumbed to a heart attack.

Operator1 was traveling in a northernly direction, heading out to Lake Borgne in Shell Beach Bayou, in vessel LA 3219 FC.  Operator2 was traveling in a Southernly direction heading in from Lake Borgne in Shell Beach Bayou in Vessel LA 3899 FB. Both vessels were operating at planning speed and met in a head on situation in a turn in the bayou.  The preliminary investigations shows that Operator1 made a hard turn to port causing a collision with the vessel2. Operator2 received severe injuries and a passenger on his vessel received fatal injuries.  PFDs were present but not worn and alcohol was not a factor.  Both vessels were seized by LDWF and taken to a secure storage yard in Chalmette, LA.

Agents were notified of a missing person through communications. when agents arrived at Belle River Public boat launch they encountered two friends of the missing subject, whom was identified as Operator. The subjects stated that they had located Operator's vessel  in the 30 " pipeline unmanned. The two men stated that when they located the vessel they observed one of the missing subjects rods laying on the deck of the vessel with a lure in the water and approximately 20' of line on it out. Subjects also stated that the trolling motor was in the down (operation position), and the ignition key was in the off position. The two men stated that they had found the subject's vessel  approximately 20' from the shore, then pushed the subject's vessel to the shore and secured it. Agents went to the location of the vessel. Agents along with St. Martin sheriff Office began searching the area for the subject. Agents inspected the vessel and found one type 3 pfd lying on the seat, and observed several fishing lures on the deck of the vessel (LA2553FT). Agents also noted that the trolling motor was in the down position.  

Agents , with search equipment located the subject's  body approximately 20' behind the vessel, submerged in approximately 7' water. Agents then properly transported the subject back to the Belle River public landing. sheriff office's  vessel towed vessel back to the landing. Agents photographed Operator's vessel, then released the vessel to his brother. Agents turned the body of Operator over to the coroner's office. As agents spoke with family members they stated that Operator has a history of having sudden seizures. The family members, and friends also stated that operator had bronchitis the prior week.  Agents inspected the vessel throughly when it was removed from the water and did not observe any type of damage to the vessel. Agents received two written statements from the subjects who located the vessel. Alcohol is not believed to be a factor. There were two type 3 pfds on the vessel and one type 4.  Pfds were not worn. The vessel was equipped with hydraulic steering.  At this point in the investigation agents believed that the subject fell overboard.  The coroner's  office is performing an autopsy to determine cause of death.

Operator was alone in a canoe checking a trot line.  The vessel swamped and Operator went into the water.  A hook from the trot line was entangled in the canoe's bow line at the bow.  The canoe was still afloat in the upright position and was completely flooded when agents arrived on scene.  The canoe was positioned in the approximately center of the bayou at N 30 06.870 by W 92 33.498 still hooked to the trot line.  The canoe did not appear to have capsized because items (paddle, styrofoam plate containing a trot line, and extra fish hooks) remained inside the hull.  Operator's deceased body was located in approximately ten inches of water at the north bank.  He was not wearing a PFD when his body was located.  Evidence suggested Operator entered the water when the canoe flooded and swam to the bank.  He was not wearing a PFD when his body was located.  Evidence suggested Operator entered the water when the canoe flooded and swam to the bank.  When he reached the bank he collapsed.  The cause of death is pending autopsy report.  Operator's body was located at N 30 06.884 by W 92 33.517.  Blood alcohol and toxicology are pending autopsy report.

On Sunday, October 30, 2011, I, Sr. Agent received a call at approximately 2:10pm concerning a possible drowing in Joe's Bayou North of Waverly, Louisiana.  Agents arrived to find a small vessel anchored in the middle of the bayou, with no occupants, and several beer cans in the vessel.  Agents launched a vessel and started searching for the victim.  After checking the vessel and finding a fishing pole broken with the line snagged, Sr. Agent attempted to move the vessel in order to drag for the victim.  As he moved the vessel he noticed the line pull the vessel back towards our vessel.  Sr. Agent immediately grabbed the line and started pulling.  The first thing that came up was a piece of the fishing pole.  After grabbing the pole and pulling he observed the victims hand coming to the surface.  We pulled the victim from the water and contacted the nearest coroner.  We took several pictures of the contents of the vessel, and the contents of the victims pockets.  The victim was released to the Madison Parish Coroner.

On November 26, 2011 at about 2:43 a.m. three people were traveling in a 16' pointed skiff in Bayou Boeuf.  Operator was the operator, Occupant1 was sitting on the port side and Occupant2 was sitting on the starboard.  The vessel passed the Amelia Belle Casino and turned back south. After crossing its own wake, the vessel made a hard abrupt starboard turn and Occupant1 was ejected out of the port side. the vessel then turned hard to port then stopped. It then took water over the stern and quickly sank. Occupant1 swam to the west bank and was treated at Teche Regional Hospital in Morgan City for minor injuries. However, Operator and Occupant2 were later recovered from the water and turned over to St. Mary Coroner's Office. Operator was recovered by drag at 10:45 a.m. the same day by St. Martin Parich deputies.  Occupant2 surfaced and was recovered by St. Mary Parish deputies on 11/27/11 at 7:43 a.m., about 1/4 mile north of the accident location. The vessel LA6549BV, powered by a 40hp Mercury has not been recovered. LDWF Enf Agents obtained a video tape of the incident from the Amelia Belle. Although the video shows the sharp turn to starboard and to port, it is still unknown why the vessel made these maneuvers.  On 11/26/11 at about 8:00 a.m. a volunteer hooked what was believed to be Operator's vessel. St. Mary S.O. diver, confirmed that it was the vessel and tied a line to it. The line was attached to a float that was used as a search reference.  However, on 11/27/11 when attempted to lift the vessel, the line broke. subject advised that he did feel the throttle control and that it was in forward gear. As of 11/27/11 the vessel has not been recovered.  The use of alcohol or drugs is pending the Stl Mary Coroner's investigation. None of the subjects were wearing their pfd and because the vessel has not yet been recovered, it is unknown if the kill switch was used. However, when Operator was recovered he was not wearing a kill switch lanyard.  It is also unknown if the vessel had any PFDs.

On December 20, 2011 at about 10 - 10:30 a.m. wife left her camp on Beehive Chute in the Atchafalaya Basin. When she left, her husband was still at the camp. She later stated that he wanted to go home to check on the building contractors who were working on their house. She returned to the camp before 2:00 p.m. and Victim wasn't there.  She stated that she wasn't concerned because it wasn't unlike Victim to leave  by catching a ride home from someone else.  Aat about 11:00 a.m. subject was approaching his houseboat, about one mile downstream of the victim's  camp. He saw Victim paddling his pirogue/canoe with the current, headed south.  He stated that Victim was in a small boat with little freeboard and appeared to be having trouble with the current.  He also stated that he asked Victim if he needed assistance and Victim waved his hand in a way that indicated that he was alright.  wife reported her husband missing on Thursday December 22nd when she got to the landing and saw that their truck was still there. LDWF assisted in a search for Victim for several days.  He was recovered from Charenton Lake by St. Mary S.O. on December 28th.  Victim was turned over to St. Mary Coroner's investigator, pending Coroner's investigative report.

The vessel (LA-7804-FN) was found capsized on the Bogue Chitto River below the spillway by a passer-by. The vessel was a 14’ Duracraft flat boat with a transom mounted 15 HP Mercury outboard. The vessel had severe damage to the bow as if it had struck and then rubbed against concrete (spillway). There were two type III PFDs and one throwable found with the vessel. The emergency cut-off lanyard was attached to the motor in operating fashion. It is unclear as to the events which lead to the vessel’s capsizing and the disappearance. On January 12, 2012 victim was found.

victim was reported missing to the Morehouse Parish Sheriff's Office.  I, Sgt. was contacted at approximately 2:00am on 03/11/2012 by Major of the MPSO.  Major requested our assistance in the search for Victim.  He advised that Victim was believed to have gone finishing the afternoon prior and never returned.  He stated that Victim' vessel was tied to the bank behind his residence.  An extensive search of the lake and surrounding areas began at approximately 3:00am on March 11.  The body of Victim surfaced on March 16 and was sent to Little Rock, AR for autopsy.  The examining physician stated the cause of death as "freshwater drowning".  Not a single witness ever came forward that witnessed Victim fall overboard into the water.  I was present when his body surfaced, and I assisted in retrieving him from the water.  His body was initially located roughly eighty yards from where his small aluminum boat was found tied to a tree.  No one ever came forward and admitted to being with subject or moving his vessel after it was found tied to the bank.  One has to assume that he either swam from the bank eighty yards and then drowned or that his vessel capsized in the lake and he drowned.  If the latter happened, then someone was either with him when he entered the water or someone found his vessel afloat and tied it to the bank behind his residence.  Much can be left to supposition.

On March 27, 2012 at approximately 12:40 p.m. operator was fishing in the Ramah Bar Pits located along the west side of the East Guide Levee in Ramah, Louisiana and fell overboard.  Cause of falling overboard is currently under investigation pending autopsy results but current evidence shows that Operator's pedestal fishing seat located on the bow of his 12' Alumaweld had broken and entered the water along with Operator.  After approximately 20 minutes of being out of contact with his fishing party, they discovered his vessel anchored approximately 40 feet from the west side bank; Operator was not aboard his vessel and shortly thereafter, his hat along with (4) fishing poles  and his seat were discovered floating nearby his vessel.  At approximately 1:15 p.m. Senior Agent arrived on scene and began assisting the Iberville Parish Sheriff's Office in recovery.  Operator's body was recovered at approximately 1:40 p.m. I then assessed Operator's 12 foot AlumaWeld flat bottom and gathered evidence of the broken seat which was previously located at the bow of the vessel.  The vessel's contents are as follows: (1) pair of leather footwear slippers (5) fishing poles, (4) of which were recovered from the water, a Styrofoam ice chest with shiners, an empty 6-pack of bottled Budweiser, (1) empty Budweiser bottle located near the bow of the vessel, a Rubbermaid ice chest containing a bag of ice and (3) unopened bottles of Budweiser, (3) boat paddles and (1) Type III PFD in serviceable condition located at the stern of the vessel.  The PFD was not worn and the contribution of alcohol to the incident is currently pending autopsy results.  According to witnesses, Operator had the ability to swim and had no known health defects.

On 3/25/12, LA Wildlife and Fisheries Agents were contacted by dispatch of a boating accident that occurred in the early hours of that day. Agents made contact with Sgt with the Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office who advised that a white male subject was found by passing boaters at approxmately 6:30 A.M. on the north bank of the Intracoastal just east of Bayou Lafourche.  The subject was identified.  Agents arrived on scene and learned that Occupant was at his residence changing into dry clothes. Agents made contact with Occupant who stated that he and his friend Operator decided to go frogging approximately 1:30 A.M. that morning. He said they launched the vessel at approximately 3:00 A.M. and began traveling east in the Intracoastal waterway for approximately 10-15 minutes.  He stated that Operator was operating the vessel owned by Occupant. Occupant stated that he was not familiar with the area so Operator chose to drive the vessel.  He stated that they slowed down and shined the spot light to see where they were and began traveling slowly east.  Occupant stated that as they increased speed they struck an object in the water which caused the bow of the vessel to lift upward and the boat to shift to the Starboard.  

When the boat shifted he fell to the right of the vessel which then caused the starboard strn side of the vessel to take on water.  This caused the vessel to take on water and sink into the intracoastal.Once the vessel sunk Occupant stated he could see the bow of  vessel sticking out the water approximately 2 foot with the running light still on.He stated that Operator told him "we have to swim Champ". Occupant stated that he had a type 3 inflatable PFD on and tried to ppull the cord for it to inflate but it failed.  He stated that he then swam to the north bank and stood up once he hit shallow water.  He stated that he called out for Operator but did not hear him.  He also stated that he could see the boat floating.  Occupant then began to walk west toward Larose where he was picked up by the passing boaters at approximately 6:30 A.M.  Agents arrived on scene at approximately 8:15 A.M. and began searching for Operator and the vessel.  Agentss located the gas can for the vessel, one type 3 inflatable PFD, one Dock Martin Dress Shoe, and 2 Floating Bud Light Cans.  Occupant stated that he had been drinking the previous day and hours leading to the accident.  Agents also spoke to witnesses who stated that Operator had also consumed several alcoholic beverages before the accident occurred.  Occupant  stated that the vessel was equipped with one Type 2 PFD, but Operator did not have it on at the time of the accident.  Occupant stated that the vessel was equipped with one Type 2 PFD, but Operator did not have it on at the time of the accident.  Occupant staated the vessel was 14' with a 23HP Longtail Go-Devil engine.

At approximately 3 p.m. vessel was returning from a fishing trip on Red River with 2 persons onboard.  As vessel made the turn by a rock revetment, the vessel's stern slid into a large rock.  The impact ejected both the operator and passenger, neither of whom were wearing PFD's. Only the operator was able to swim to safety and was air lifted to LSU Medical Center in Shreveport, LA with serious injuries - lacertions to back of scalp and severe contusions to back and leg.  (He later recovered from his injuries.)  Search and rescue/recovery operations for the passenger commenced, lasting until February 24, 2012, when the body of the deceased passenger was located approximately 100 yards from the accident site.  The official cause of death was drowning.  A blood sample was taken form the operator at the hospital, but produced negative results.  The deceased passenger's toxicology report showed his ethanol level at .027g%.  Alcohol was not a contributing factor in this incident.

According to the statements taken by Agent, on the morning of April 4th, 2012, at approximately 7-7:20 a.m., Operator departed his home in Lafitte to go to work, using his pirogue to cross the Barataria Waterway to get from his home to his place of work at Nunez Seafood.  At approximately 8:00 a.m., Subject arrived at Nunez Seafood, expecting to see Operator, but he was not there. Subject stated he did not think anything of it due to the inclement weather.  At approximately 10:45 a.m. Subject called Operator' residence to check on him and see if everything was alright and to see where he was, to which wife replied that her husband already left for work this morning around 7.  At that time a 911 call was placed by Subject to Jefferson Parish SO to report a missing person/possible drowing. At approximately 12:30 p.m. Jefferson Parish SO notified the LDWF Region 8 office, where Sgt. responded to the scene.

Operator death was caused by asphyxia due to drowning.

At 07:44 pm, Sgt was advised of a boating incident on Reserve Canal in St. John Parish.  Sgt. arrived at Reserve Canal boat launch where he was briefed by Sheriff's Deputy Sgt. had the operator in custody.  Sgt. advised the operator of his rights and asked what had happened. According to Operator, at approximately 07:15PM, the subjects were traveling at idle speed while putting out jug lines when the passenger, Passenger, went into convulsions and fell overboard.  Operator attempted to rescue Passenger but advised he was unable to because he was combative and pulling him under water. After several attempts to locate Passenger under the water, Operator found him and was able to pull him on board with the help of another boater.  Passenger was transported from Reserve Canal Boat Launch to River Parishes Hospital where he expired  at 7:48PM.PFD's were on board but not used by the operator or victim.  The kill switch was not used.  There were several empty beer cans in the vessel and a packet of synthetic marijuana which Operator stated was his.  Operator stated he and Passenger had gotten off work at 5:30 PM and drank a few beers before launching the vessel.  He advised he had not used synthetic marijuana in several days.  Operator also stated that Passenger was a" functioning alcoholic".  Operator submitted a blood sample at River Parish Hospital (to be submitted to LSP Crime lab), was cited for illegal possession of a schedule 1 substance, and released.  Agents observed the odor of an alcoholic beverage on Operator's breath and person.  His speech was not slurred and his balance was good.  His vessel and towing vehicle were released, with Operator's permission to Operator's work supervisor.  The medical history of the deceased is not know at this time.

On June 5th, at approximately 0335 hour, a 2006 Proline 21’ dual console fiberglass vessel operated along with the three (3) other passengers departed Oak harbor traveling towards the twin spans at mid throttle when the lake began to get rough. The operator spassengerd he pulled back on the throttle and trimmed the bow up to address the waves but it was progressively getting worse so he decided it was too rough to continue and began making a slow turn to port approximately 100 yards west northwest of the old I-10 bridge around coordinates N 30 12.310’/ W 089 48.078’. While making the port turn, the starboard passenger attempted to stand up and upon doing so the vessel took a side sea which caused him to fall overboard. The occupants of the vessel spassengerd after Passenger fell overboard they saw his head two times before it submerged and all attempts to locate and rescue him failed. The aft port passenger spassengerd that just prior to the incident Passenger told him he was going to try and stand up to see if he could “ride the waves”, and after doing so, Passenger who was holding the starboard stern line fell overboard, after which Passenger2 said he went to the starboard gunwale and witnessed Passenger holding the stern line as he was being pulled by the vessel, before it pulled from his hands. Passenger2  immediately yelled to the vessels operator that subject had fallen overboard and Operator stopped the vessel and turned back around in an attempt to rescue Passenger. The female passenger who was sitting amidships on the port side of the vessel concurred with the above depiction of the incident given by both Operator and passenger2. For further see the attached passenger statements. At approximately 1355 hrs, the body of Passenger was recovered by deputies of the St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s SOD Division near the location where he fell overboard at coordinates N 30 12.379’/W 089 47.998’. The body was remanded to the St. Tammany Parish Coroner’s office for autopsy. No charges have been filed against the vessel’s operator and foul play is not suspected in this incident. The vessel was equipped with all required safety equipment/ PFD’s. After a thorough investigation, neither alcohol nor drugs were found to be a contributing factor in this incident. No further information concerning the above incident is to follow at this time.

Operator and surviving passengers report that on May 5th, 2012, they were aboard a 24’ Baja Islander (LA 7885 FK) as they traveled at a heading of approximately 40’, at a reported speed of “about 15-20 miles per hour, generally from Blind River toward the mouth of the Tickfaw River in Lake Maurepas, in Livingston Parish, La.
Operator, 30, identified himself as the operator of the vessel. Collectively the operator and the two surviving passengers report that at approximately 6:00pm the Operator’s brother, jumped purposefully from the stern of the vessel as another passenger, Occupant2 acted as a “lookout”. Operator’s brother surfaced and he and Occupant2 watched as the third passenger, Occupant3 jumped feet first from the stern of the vessel while holding his nose. According to Occupant2 and Operator’s brother, Occupant3 did not resurface. The men searched diligently for Occupant3 but found no sign of him. Waves were choppy with whitecaps being somewhat common. Winds were blowing at approximately 10-15 miles per hour. These conditions made the search more difficult.
Agents arrived on the scene at approximately 6:42pm and were quickly briefed by the men. A U.S. Coast Guard patrol vessel and patrol vessels from other local law enforcement agencies were also on the scene participating in search and rescue efforts.
Sgt. advised Operator of his legal rights as per Miranda and spoke with him about the day’s events. Operator told Sgt. that they had all consumed a “few drinks”. Sgt. and other agents observed that Operator and his passengers were notably upset with the situation but didn’t note that anyone appeared to be obviously intoxicated. Blood samples from Operator and Occupant3 were later collected and subsequently submitted to the LSP crime lab. Results of those tests indicate that Operator’s blood alcohol concentration (BAC) was 0.0g% at the time of his test. Results indicate that Occupant3’s BAC was 0.15g% at the time of his death.
On May 7th, 2012 at approximately 7:30am a pilot from the Livingston Parish Sheriff’s Office located Occupant3’s remains in Lake Maurepas. LDWF and LPSO personnel retrieved Occupant3 from the waters at, or very near grid coordinates 30’17.968Nx90’32.458W. Occupant3’s remains were released to the Livingston Parish Coroner.
Appropriate PFD’s were on board but not used. Alcohol is believed to have been a factor in this incident.

According to witnesses on 6/23/2012, Victim’s vessel (LA-6228-FX) was anchored in Lake Maurepas with himself and four other passengers when a passing vessel cut his anchor line. Victim reportedly started his vessel and turned over controls of the vessel to a male passenger. Victim then reportedly jumped into the lake in an attempt to retrieve his lost anchor. 

After a few minutes Victim concluded his search and was approaching the vessel from the stern when the vessels active propeller struck him. As a result he sustained fatal deep tissue and vascular lacerations to both his right and left thighs. He subsequently succumbed to his injuries due to severe blood loss and was pronounced deceased at St. Elizabeth Hospital in Gonzales, La.
Alcohol or drugs are not suspected to be a contributing factor in this incident.
The vessel was found to have all of the necessary required safety equipment including PFD’s on board and all were found to be serviceable.

On April 14, 2012 Operator and his son were headed south in LA 7885FX in the Commercial Canal.  Operator was operating the vessel from the port side of the console and Occupant was sitting on the starboard side.  The vessel was a 1999 36' Douglas Marine catamaran hull that was powered by twin 1400 hp Dart engines.  The vessel was a high performance racing type boat.  The subjects left from the Port of Iberia and head out to Vermillion Bay and the ICW.  Two different witnesses advised that they saw vessel pass them in Vermillion Bay at about 11:45 a.m and 12:00 p.m. , see attached.  The witnesses also advised that the vessel headed back towards the Port of Iberia.  This would put the vessel North Bound in the Commercial Canal.  The Port of Iberia Commission has video cameras that scan the waterways.  The video footage captured a large cloud of smoke in the area of the incident.  This footage indicates that the incident happened around 12:15 p.m.  The vessel impacted the west bank of the Commercial Canal at an angle near 75 degrees.  The angle of impact and the direction of the debris field indicate that the vessel was south bound.  

Upon arrival at the scene, LDWF Enf. Sgt. and Sr. Agent found no survivors and the vessel still in flames.  The vessel burned to the waterline and then sank.  On April 15th Leblanc Marine Services of New Iberia recovered the vessel.  LDWF Enf. Sgt took video footage of the recovery of the vessel.  Due to the amount of fire damage much of the physical evidence on the vessel was destroyed.  The hydraulic steering system was burned up to the out-drives.  The only remains of the throttle controls were the actual control levers.  Sgt. obtained photos of the throttle position.  However, the impact may have caused the levers to move.  The vessel was seized and held at LSP Troop I in Lafayette.  According to Iberia Parish Coroner's office, both subjects died on impact due to mult systems trauma.  According to the Coroner's Toxicology report, neither subject was impaired.  Due to the fire, the investigators could not determine if the vessel was equipped with a kill switch lanyard.  Based on the evidence obtained, whatever caused operator to lose control in inconclusive.  However, the vessel should have been operated at a speed that would have allowed operator  to maintain control of the vessel and come to a stop before the collision.
location: Port Of Iberia Commercial Cana, LA

description:
Operator left to go fishing on Kincaid Lake, at approximately 1:20 P.M.  Operator told his mother he was going to fish until dark.  When he did not return she contacted the Rapides Parish Sheriff's Office.  A search for the missing boater was then conducted and Operator's boat was located.  The boat was found with the bow on the bank, in forward gear and at idle speed.  Operator was not located and was presumed to be over board.  Alcohol and or drugs use at this time are unknown.  The boat was equipped with the proper PFDs.  The boat was equipped with remote steering. 
On March 9th at approximately 1215 P.M., Operator's body was recovered from Kincaid Lake.  Operator was not wearing a PFD upon recovery.  Operator's body was turned over to the Rapides Parish Coroner's office, autopsy and toxicology reports are pending.

operator was fishing on Cotile Lake in a 14' Monark aluminum boat equipped with a 25 Mercury with tiller steering.  He was supposed to have fished until around noon.  When he did not return home, his wife attempted to call his cell phone, but got no answer.  Upon searching for him, his boat was discovered in a cove that he frequently fished.  The boat was up against the bank, with the motor's cowling in the bottom of the boat.  We were notified of the incident at approximately 6:29 P.M.  Upon arrival, we went to the boats location and inspected the boat.  The motor's kill switch was in the off position.  There was a type III and type IV PFD on the floor of the boat.  The floor of the boat contained numerous items of gear, making it difficult to maneuver inside the boat.  The Rapides Parish Sheriff's Department used a dog to search the bank for human scent near the boats location.  There were no obvious signs of damage to the boat and it appeared that operator had fallen overboard and was not wearing a PFD at the time.  There was no evidence observed of any alcoholic beverages in the boat or ice chest.  Divers and a side scan sonar were used but we were unable to locate subject at that time.  At approximately 830 P.M. on 7-11-123, Senior Agent contacted me and advised that body had been recovered and transported by the corner with an autopsy requested.

owner/operator of vessel La-7071-FB was operating his vessel in Lake Maurepas. Operator is the only known subject in the vessel at the time of operation. Operator was in Lake Maurepas while it was under rough conditions. He was possibly heading from Tickfaw River to Manchac at the time of incident. He fell overboard (unknown reason) and the vessel was found still in gear turning in a clockwise motion. The vessel was a 200 Carolina Skiff with a steering wheel. Alcohol was found on the vessel “worm bucket” from Prop Stop.  Time of incident is between 1700-1743.

Two men were drifting in a 16' Oauchta fiberglass boat(LA 8767 AT), fishing near Young's Landing on Toedo Lake.  Operator was fishing from the stern of his boat while occupant fished from the front deck.  Operator heard a splash then looked to see what it was, and Occupant was nowhere to be seen.  Occupant’s hat was floating in the water.  Operator recovered it and started scanning for Occupant.  After approximately 10 minutes he went to another boater and asked for help. At approximately 6:45 P.M., Operator's wife called 911 to report that a man fell from  boat and hasn't come back up.  Sabine Parish's deputy and LDWF  arrived at approximately 7:00 P.M.  Operator took agents out to where he thought Occupant fell in.  LDWF Sr. Agent arrived later with one of our vessels to assist with search and recovery operations along with Sabine Parish's Lake Patrol.  While waiting for divers from Natchitoches Parish both vessels and other deputies secured the location and continued the search.  While searching a fishing lure attached to fishing line was found near the entry location.  The divers were deployed at that location and shortly thereafter found the body of Occupant.  Deputy Coroner was on board the vessel that recovered the remains and maintained responsibility for them until transportation arrived to take them to Lake Charles for an autopsy.  Occupant's father arrived on scene shortly after discovery of the remains and was able to positively identify them as his son.  Results of the autopsy are pending and will be attached when available.

The deceased victim was in the act of bass fishing on the afternoon of 09/20/2012, in the Ouachita River, approximately 1/2 mile north of Forsythe Landing.  When he did not return home, a search began and his boat was located at approximately 10:00pm, in the area of Forsythe Boat Dock.  When the boat was located, the key was in the off position, the gear shifter was in neutral and the trolling motor was down, in the use position.  There were several rod and reels on the deck of the boat, one rod in the bottom of the boat with approximately 1/3 of its sticking past over the gunwale, with an artifcal lure attached.  Inside the boat, we located a hat, cell phone, and prescription sun glasses.  There was one small bass in the livewell, which was still alive.  There was no evidence of blood anywhere in the boat.  The boat was located by Ouachita Parish Sheriff's deputies.  A search for subject began and on  the morning of Sunday, 09/23/2012, his body was found floating between the Forsythe Boat Dock and the Louisville Bridge. His body was sent to Little Rock, Arkansas for autopsy.

Party was floating main stem of flathead, hit log jam 4 miles north at Prestine Bar.  Operator / Owner was able to swim through a strainer.  The victim got caught under log and drowned.  Raft sustained $1,000.00 in damages.

The victim became trapped in some rocks as he was descending the rapids in a kayak.  People in the victims party said they were finally able to get him free of the entrapment but attempts to resuscitate the victim were unsuccessful.

description:
On 7/28/2012 at 1713 hrs I was dispatched to the area of the Swan River at the highway 209 bridge concerning the drowning on an adult male.

At 1740 I arrived at 15 Shady Lane in Ferndale and found the deceased on a private deck along the Swan River at this residence.  CPR had been in progress prior to my arrival, however, resuscitation attempts had ceased at the direction of a Dr.

Next, I spoke with Witness 1 and 2 who had been at their parents residence, approximately 1/4 of a mile up the Swan River and had witnessed the victim hanging onto the side of his kayak in the rapids.  The witnesses indicated that the victim was holding onto the side of his kayak, his head was barely above the water and his life jacket had risen above his head.  They yelled at the victim, however, he did not respond.

Witness 1 and 2 then drove away from their parents residence in an attempt to rescue the victim.  Approximately 3 -5 minutes passed before they pulled him from the water near the river side deck.  The Victims head was under water at the time witness 1 pulled him out of the water.  The kayak was not located at this time.

After speaking with witness 1 and 2, I spoke with witness 3, witness 3 along with witness 4 had been kayaking with the victim.  Witness 3 has been a friend of the victim for approximately 15 years and believed that this was the first time the victim had been in a kayak.  Witness 3 advised that he and the victim both entered the rapids and both were thrown out of their kayaks.  Witness 3 said he essentially walked to the shore and then saw the victim holding onto his kayak.  Witness 3 threw his paddle to the victim and told him to stand up.  Despite his efforts to help the victim he saw him continue down the river and around a bend.

I then spoke with witness 4, who is also a friend of the victim.  Witness 4 advised that he had never kayaked with the victim and had been in front of witness 3 and the victim when they were in the rapids.  Witness 4 added that he, Witness 3 and the victim had put into the Swan River at about 1400 hrs at the river access in Lake County (South of Ferndale Drive Bridge).  He also advised that none had been drinking.

After speaking with Witness 4 I examined the victim''s body.  The victims lips were purple and I could see no visible trauma on his body or head.  There was no petechial evidence and rigor or livor had not yet set in.  The victim had been intubated and when I removed the tubes a large amount of clear fluid came from his nostrils and mouth.  The victim han not been wearing a helmet and had been wearing a US Coast Guard Auxillary life jacket of an adult XXX large size.

After examining the victims body I spoke to his wife.  She indicated that her husband had never kayaked before and added that he had a history of heart affibrilation and sleep apnea and was taking atenolol and coumadin.

There was no evidence of foul play and based on the circumstances and evidence at the scene the cause of death will be listed as drowning.  The manner of death is listed as accidental.

On 8/11/2012 at 1436 hrs I was dispatched to a reported unattended death at the Glacier Rim River Access.  Witnesses told dispatch that they had recovered the body of a male that had been floating face down in the river.  CPR was underway.

Blacenship Fire Dept. were first on scene.  Deputy and I arrived on scene shortly after peramedics had declared the victim deceased.  At 1530 hrs the other person that had been floating with the victim arrived at the Glacier Rim Access in his inflatable pontoon raft.

According to Witness 1, he and the victim were floating the river when they came to an area of rough water.  Witness 1 was in the lead and flipped his pontoon raft in the water.  Witness 1 yelled for the victim to go to the left side of the river to avoid the rough water, but the victim also capsized his pontoon in the same area.  The victim was wearing a life vest that had to be inflated.  As the victim surfaced behind the vessel he yelled for help.  Witness 1 yelled for the victim to inflate his life vest.  The victim was swept out of sight.  Witness 1 went to shore and ran downstream 600-800 yards, but couldn''t see the victim.

At Glacier Rim Access Witness 2 was on shore when she spotted the victim floating face down in the river.  While witness 2 called 911witness 3 got in a raft withsome others and pulled the Victims body to shore.  Witness 3 wrote in his statement that the victim "was pulseless blue and cold".  Witness 3 also wrote, " I did CPR for 2-5 minutes with no results. Pupils where fix and dilated. (sic) Paramedic arrived with EKG monitor confirmed asystole."

Note:  The victim''s life vest was not inflated when he was recovered from the river.

Commander was the Coroner; the scene was turned over to him upon his arrival.

On 6/6/2012 Witness 1 and Victim were kayaking in the Gallatin River near Williams Brige. Victims''s kayak overturned and trapped him inside. Witness 1 watched as the kayak and Victim went down river out of sight. At approximately 1730 search and rescue was called and responded. The kayak was located in a log jam approximately 1 mile north of Williams Bridge. Search and Rescue personnel were able to access the kayak by boat. Victim was deceased and still trapped in the kayak under water. At approximately 2030 hours Search and Rescue personnel were able to free Victim from the kayak. Victim''s kayak and life vest were not able to be retrieved because of the water conditions and the way that he was trapped in the log jam. Closed SAR event.

The following summary is the result of the Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks investigation into the boat accident that occurred on September 7th, 2012 in Ski Doo Bay.  Having talked to individuals directly involved, collecting voluntary witness statements, conducting field investigations and documentation of events after the accident, the following summary report is submitted to the Lake County Attorney''s Office.

- The initial call was placed to the Lake County Sheriff''s Office Dispatch center at 1742 hours on September 7th, 2012
-The Sheriff''s Office Dispatch log sheet is attached for references to times, subject''s information and LCSO officers assigned to the case.
- The boat was operating outside of the 200 foot no wake zone in effect for Flathead Lake.
 - The boat operator was aware of the rock obstacle in the water with the warning flag on it.
 - Operator was aware that folks do swim out to the rock.
 - No one was on shore or on the docks located out in front of the rock obstacle in the water with the warning flag on it.
 - victim was swimming alone at the time of the collision.
 - Operators navigated his boat to the shore side of the rock obstacle to avoid hitting it.
 - Operators said he was 30 feet inside the rock obstacle towards shore.
  - The distance from shore the boat was at directly after the accident based on recollection and LCSO boat placed at the spot she directed, was 306 feet.
 -  The rock obstacle distance from the shoreline out in front of the dock was 420 feet.
 - No one was a witness to the actual contact between the boat and swimmer.
- The direction of travel of the boat operated by Operators was in a westerly direction headed into the sun.
 - The weather was clear and slight to no wind on the water.
- Operators said he was traveling between 18 and 20 miles per hour.

Operator ARRIVED AT LAKE WHEELER AT APPROXIMATELY 9:26AM ON THE MORNING OF JUNE 18TH.  Operator WAS SEEN LAUNCHING HIS TRACKER BASS BOAT AT AROUND 9:35 AM BY ANOTHER FISHERMAN.
