On october 5, 2012, around 4:00pm, two people were canoeing down the french broad river.  As they were passing through a small section of lower rapids, the canoe turned over.  occupant was able to get to safety.  The last time occupant saw operator, he was floating/paddling down the river with his feet down stream.  Occupant informed local authorities for help.  Operator was found october 6, 2012 around 11:30am a short distance down river.  Autopsy results are underway.  Two wearable pfds were found in the canoe.  One pfd was lying in the seat.  The other pfd was affixed to the side of the canoe.  Contact has not been made with occupant at this time.  The canoe did have registration numbers affixed to the side.  No records were found through dispatch.

On the 28th of september, 2012, at approximately 9:00pm, operator was operating an 18ft sea hunt triton 186 open motorboat on the pamlico river near the moss landing docks located on the washington, nc waterfront.  Occupant was the only passenger on board the vessel with operator.  The two men were leaving a restaurant on the washington waterfront just before the accident occurred.  While the vessel was drifting, occupant went to the bow to urinate and unexpectedly fell into the river landing face down and was unresponsive.  Operator then attempted to throw a rope to occupant and yelled for him to grab it.  Occupant remained unresponsive floating face down in the water.  At that point, operator jumped in the water and attempted to pull occupant's head up.
 
While the two men were in the water, the boat drifted over to the washington boardwalk near moss landing.  subject was outside of his residence located on water street when he heard operator yelling.  He jumped on his motor bike and drove down to the dock.  He jumped in the boat that operator had been operating and maneuvered over to operator.  Subject then pulled operator out of the water and onto the vessel.  At approximately 9:02pm, a call came and the 911 dispatch was notified.  At approximately 9:29pm the washington fire dept on board fire boat 1 pulled occupant's body into their boat and started cpr.  Occupant was transported to vidant beaufort hospital where he was pronounced dead due to cardiac arrest.
 
North carolina wildlife officers and i arrived at he hospital and interviewed operator.  Operator described the incident and stated that occupant had been consuming alcohol.   We then spoke with the medical examiner who stated that the cause of death was cardiac arrest.
 
We then went down to the moss landing docks and performed a safety inspection on the vessel.  On board the vessel we found 1 type ii pfd, 7 adult type iii pfds, 1 type iv pfd, and 1 type b1 fire extinguisher.  All of the pfds and the fire extinguisher were serviceable and readily available.  The running lights on the vessel were in operable condition also.  On board the vessel we found a small cooler containing two 12 ounce beers and a 20 ounce soda bottle that contained some carbonated liquid with the smell of an alcoholic beverage.  Two empty 12 ounce beers were found in a rear compartment located at the stern of the vessel.

On the above date and time Operator was operating his vessel South in Bayou Fordoche when he struck a stump.  Operator's vessel then capsized ejecting him and his passenger.  Operator advised that when he resurfaced, he swam to the bank and that he did not see Occupant anywhere.  Operator advised that approximately ten minutes later another vessel pulled up onto the scene of the accident and pulled him from the water.  Operator advised that one of the gentleman in the vessel called 911 to report the accident.  Neither Operator or Occupant were wearing their PFD's at the time of the accident.  Occupant was later located and pronounced deceased by the St. Landry Parish coroner.

Operator and Occupant left the I-10 boat launch at approximately 7:30 p.m. to go gar fishing in Lake Charles Lake.  At approximately 10:00 P.M. a thunderstorm with winds in excess of 50 MPH and heavy rain came through the area.  The men were in a 16' ft. Waco semi-vee flat boat powered by a 25 HP Mercury tiller handle motor.  At approximately 4:23 A.M. on July 21, 2012 the vessel was found overturned along the west bank of Lake Charles Lake.  The body of Occupant was found on the west bank of Lake Charles Lake at approximately 4:30 A.M.  The body of Operator was recovered on the west bank of Lake Chalres Lake at approximately  6:30 A.M.  on July 22, 2012.  Occupant was wearing a PFD at the time his body was recovered.  Operator was not wearing a PFD at the time his body was recovered.  Blood alcohol and toxicology results were returned from Operator and Occupant.    Operator report indicated he had a BAC of.070g%.  Occupant report tested positive for Cannabinoids and THC.

Two people were playing in the boat, which was anchored near the bank in the Red River.  subject stated he and his wife were, "rough housing", near the rear of the boat, when they both fell overboard, next to the motor.  He stated that when he surfaced he didn't see his wife.  He stated he went back down several times, but was unable to locate her.  His brother-in-law called 911 and reported the incident to authorities.  Rapides Parish Sheriff's Department stated they received the call at approximately 5:56 PM.  Senior Agent, and I, Sgt., arrived at the scene at approximately 6:50 PM and made contact with the occupants of the vessel.  The Rapides Parish Sheriff's Department personnel arrived, along with divers.  The body was recovered at approximately 8:08 PM.  The body was transported by the Rapides Parish Coroner's Office.

On 3/15/12 Operator was operating his vessel, LA8750 EB in a drainage canal at the end of Cotton Rd. in St. Mary Parish.  The vessel was occupied by operator and two other subjects.  At about 745pm the subjects left the boat landing next to the Cotton Rd. Bridge.  They traveled under the bridge and headed West in the drainage canal to go frog gigging.  At about 11:00 they were headed east and planned to travel past the bridge at the cotton Rd. Launch.  Operator advised that they knew the bridge was ahead of him but he wasn't maintaining a proper lookout. 

He further stated that he advised Occupant1 to pull the drain plug in order to drain the water out of the boat.  Operator was at the helm in front of the vessel while Occupant2 was sitting on an ice chest in the center of the vessel.  Occupant1 was in the rear of the vessel, holding the plug.  Operator was wearing a spotlight on top of his head and continued to look back at Occupant1 so that Occupant1 could see what he was doing.  However, Operator was not watching for the bridge ahead.  The vessel struck the piling supports under the bridge on its port bow.  Upon impact, all three subjects were ejected in the water and the vessel sank.  None of the subjects were wearing a pfd, nor was Operator wearing the kill switch lanyard.  

When Occupant2 surfaced, he used his cell phone as a search light to locate Occupant1 to locate Occupant1 who was unconscious and floating.  Occupant2 and Operator pulled Occupant1 from the water and administered CPR.  They transported Occupant1 to Teche Regional Hospital where he was pronounced dead by St.  Mary Coroner's Investigator. At about 12:00 am LDWF Enforcement Agents responded to Teche Regional Hospital and obtained the attached statements from both Operator and. Occupant2.  Sgt. obtained blood and urine from Operator to determine if alcohol and or drugs were involved.  The blood and urine obtained were sent to LSP  Crime Lab or toxicology and blood alcohol testing. According to the LSP Crime Lab test results, Operator's  BAC was .060g%.  His toxicology report indicated that Hydrocodnne, Tramadol, Amphetamine and Dihydrocodeine were all present.  Sgt. obtained a Subpoena Duces Tecum to obtain Operator's hospital records for the night of the incident.  Upon inspection, the agents found that the vessel HIN was removed but the HIN assigned to the registration was LAZ1294B988.  On October 17, 2012 at about 545 pm  Sgt. issued Operator Citation D586678 and charged with violation of RS 34:851.4, Careless operation of a watercraft and RS 34:851.33A, Possession of a motorboat with the serial numbers altered.

Operator was fishing out of a 10' Jon boat (LA-4189-EP) on Flag Lake on Barksdale AFB in Bossier Parish.  Operator was reported missing after not returning from a fishing trip.  Operator' vessel was located unoccupied on the lake.  A fishing rod and four prong rake were found on top of a mat of hyacinths a short distance from his vessel.  Operator' deceased body was located submerged in the water approximately 15' from the fishing rod and rake.  Operator was not wearing a PFD (personal flotation device).  The body was then turned over to the Bossier Parish Coroner's Office for autopsy.  The autopsy report revealed that Operator likely experienced an acute, fatal cardiac arrhythmia from which he was unable to recover and subsequently fell into the water.  The toxicology report found no traces of drugs or alcohol.  Operator had one Type 3 PFD in the vessel, but he was not wearing it at the time of the incident.  The vessel was powered by an electric Minn Kota trolling motor that was in the off position when found.  The contributing factor in this incident is the medical condition Operator suffered prior to falling in the water.

Agent arrived at the Hwy 20 boat launch   approximately 3:05 p.m. the St. James Sheriff along with sheriff's deputies brought body from the accident scene to the dock and placed him in a black body bag.  Agent spoke with friends and relatives of Victim, and stated that subject had a history of heart related issues and took several different kinds of medication.  The agents launched a boat and investigated the accident scene.  Victim's vessel, a 2000, 15ft aluminum Express, LA1470FB,was grounded on the south bank of Bayou Chevreuil,  approximately 1.65 miles west from the Hwy 20 launch. Victim  was found approximately 5 to  feet behind his vessel, face down in the muddy water, with a type III PFD near him. The steering wheel was turned all the way to the starboard side,with the throttle in the forward position.  Victim was a member of the St. James Hunting Club and according to hunting partners was apparently in route to the hunting camp from making a morning deer hut.  Victim was traveling  in his vessel alone and there were no witnesses to the incident. 
Circumstances surrounding the incident are currently under investigation. The boat was transported back to the launch and released to relatives.

According to a news media report, a 32-year old was missing from a kayaing trip.  The victim launched his kayak from Bridge Side Marina Monday morning and had planned to return later that day.  His truck was still at the marina when the alarm was sounded when the victim didn't show up for work on Tuesday.  The news media reported that the victim had been to Grand Isle to kayak only once before and wasn't that experienced with a kayak.

According to a MISLE report, the victim fell overboard while fishing with two other family members near the HWY 11 bridge.  The two family members tried to save him but the victim couldn't swim, and struggled such that they were afraid for their lives.  The victim's body was recovered.

Preliminary info only as of 3/3/2010: Victim was travelling south on the river with two other kayakers.  The subject was wearing a helmet and a type V pfd that was coast guard approved that stated it was a substitute Type III when worn.  Initial reports describe the victim as an expert and well experienced in the operation of a kayak in all conditions.  He voluntarily left the kayak when he encountered a whirlpool.  He was in the water for about 3 minutes.  Water was extremely cold.  Still under investigation at this time.

According to prelimnary information (3/30/10) victim had been kayaking with his 16 year old daughter and her friend.  According to his daughter, the father went ahead to check for debris when he came to the fork and his kayak turned over.  She saw her father come up and at the 1st tree that was over hanging the river, he disappeared and never resurfaced.  They looked for 10 minutes and run up the hill for help. A massive search was conducted.  The kayak was located by one of the search team.  Victim was found caught in debris about 70 feet down river from his last known position.  The victim was not wearing a pfd or helmet for the water conditions.  This was a fast moving river, steep terrain and branches hanging out into the water that had trapped debris.  More info with be added as becomes available.

Preliminary info indicates that operator's wife and two children were asleep below deck while her husband departed at 9pm to travel from Hyannis to Nantucket (approximately a two hour journey).  At 3:15am the next morning wife awoke from their boat which had run aground.  Her husband was not on the boat.  The husband was not reported missing until 11:54pm that day to the local pd.  The coast guard was not notified until 2:00pm.  At this point a search and rescue mission was conducted but operator was not found as of 4/27/2010.  The DA has decided at this point that there is no evidence of foul play.  There are conflicting reports that the wife gave to different news outlets after her husband went missing as well as the timeline of her reporting her husband missing.  At this time our agency is investigating this accident to determine whether or not it is reportable.  No further info at this time (4/27/10).

Ongoing investigation at this time 5/6/2010.  Two friends were out on a canoe when it tipped over about a quarter mile off the beach.  A person from shore reported seeing the men in trouble and called the police.  An assistant harbormaster and two workers from a nearby boat yard went out to the overturned canoe and pulled the men from the water and brought them to the pier.  Medical technicians attempted to revive deceased at the pier but were unsuccessful.   According to surviving man the canoe was tipped over by a pod of pilot whales.  This has not been confirmed and one of the rescuers reported seeing a pod of dolphins near the over-turned canoe.  Neither deceased or injured were wearing pfd's.

Preliminary info as of 6/11/10 is that 2 friends went out at night on a vessel that was not seaworthy and had prior cracks in the hull.  The vessel started taken on water, swamped and eventually sank.  The vessel sank next to a buoy which the two persons grabbed onto but the deceased lost his grip, floated away and tried to swim to a nearby lighthouse but drowned.  He was holding onto a child's pfd but it was not enough to keep him up.  Will update when more info is available.

Victim had been drinking approximately 3-6 beers on beach before deciding to row out onto the lake.  Victim was asked and encouraged to take a pfd with him but did not.  He stated he didn't need it because he was only going out a short distance and he tossed the pfd on the shore.  According to witnesses victim paddled out about a 100 yards and stood up in the canoe to wave.  The canoe tipped and capsized putting the victim in the water.  The victim yelled for help and began to swim to shore for about 20 yards when he was last seen flailing his arms, going under the water, coming back up, going back under the water and finally not returning to the surface.  The dive team found the victim and was performing the recovery.   Preliminary test results were positive for alcohol and a cocaine based substance.  Cause of accident was not wearing a pfd or having one available, consumpution of alcohol and recklessness.

Preliminary info is operator was trying to tie boat to mooring when he fell overboard.    Waiting for ME's report as of 6/22/10.  The fall overboard was not witnessed.  Witnesses stated that they heard cries for help and saw a boat floating downstream with nobody aboard.   A man was seen in the water struggling to swim against the outgoing tide.  The witnesses jumped into their vessel to the area where the man was and when they were approximately 30 yards away he went under.  At that point a mooring tender boat arrived to the scene and the person aboard that boat reached into the water, pulled the victim up by his arms onto their boat and started cpr.  Victim was transported to hosptial unconscious and unresponsive.  Investigator determined that there was no indication of foul play or alcohol or drugs and that he operator simply slipped and fell overboard.

As of 6/22/2010 very little information has been obtained about this accident.  We were notified by CG in Washington via news article in a local paper.  The local pd has not been forthcoming with information and has redacted their report. PD  Report indicates that they received a call that there was a body floating in the water approximately 100' from the dock area and a capsized canoe aproximately 100' feet from the body.  Not wearing a pfd nor one recovered.  The victim's father said that the last time he saw his son was 8:30pm the evening before and that his son liked to Fish on the lake around sunset.  He said it was not unusal for him to be out late fishing.  A witness called the pd regarding the drowning and said she had a strange person in her yard that evening around 12:30am while she was entertaining friends.  Her backyard abuts the lake.  She described the person as acting strange and just not right.  He told her his name, that he was an out of work mechanic and that he had been out fishing and paddling for about five miles.  She said that he was drinking beer.  She told him her guests were leaving so that he had to leave also.  She said that he got back into the canoe and was paddling with a kayak paddle.  When more information becomes available I will update.

Operator and passengers were out boating celebrating the last day of school.  They had been tubing when a couple of passengers decided to go swimming off the vessel.  The vessel was not achored/secured or running.  The victim was not wearing a pfd.  The victim complained of leg cramps before going into the water and shortly thereafter he began having difficulties staying afloat.  Another passenger made an attempt to aid the victim but was quickly overcome by the panicked victim and nearly brought down by him.  This passenger had to let go of him and went back to the vessel.  Victim was recovered by Dive team in approximately 10 feet of water at or about his last sighted location.  CPR etc where administered at scene but he was declared deceased at the hospital.  As of 6/23 investigation is still ongoing and will be updated as more information becomes available.

Early reports indicate that victim was canoeing with two friends when their canoe capsized.  Victim disappeared into water.  The other two men were found clinging to a cooler.  According to witnesses the men were not wearing pfd's and did not appear to be able to swim.  Victim was located 3:30pm the following day by dive team.  (as of 7/6/10) According to investigator likely factors of accident, no pfds, subjects could not swim, use of alcohol, improper loading, lack of boating/canoeing skills and language barrier.

Pre-liminary info as of 7/13/10 is that the deceased stopped by a store to buy bait at 7:30am.  At about 9:30am his center console boat ran aground on the beach.  The engine was running but no one was onboard.  A search and rescue operation was organized and about 2 hours later his body was spotted from the air by the Coast Guard.  A local fire department happened to be training on an inflatable boat at the time the emergency call was made and were able to bring the body to shore.  Bystanders on the scene advised they was heavy fog and surf that morning.  According to a media release by the local police department it is likely the victim died after falling overboard trying to navigate a treacherous inlet.  He did not have much experience in local waters or much familiarity with the inlet.  Will update when further info becomes available.

Preliminary information is that Operator/owner/deceased had been going through alot of streeses in his life recently such as work related issues and his daughter had been comitted for drug abuse and according to his wife he liked to drink.  On the day of the accident the deceased went out with a friend for lunch and had a few beers with lunch.  They went out in his boat down the river to the "Tipsy Seagull - an establishment that serves alcohol" and had some more beers.  They were waiting to pick-up the victim's son from a camp that was being held nearby.  After they picked up the son the victim's friend piloted the boat to approximately 1 1/2 -2 miles upriver to the house because he said the victim had too much to drink.   They arrived back at around 8pm and the victim decided to go back out because he had some engine troubles that he wanted to work out.  Victim's friend advised him not to go out but he went anyway.  When asked if he knew how many drinks his friend had he said he did not know but that he left with a small coolor on board with beers in it.  Around 11:00pm a witness saw a small boat collide with an adjacent wall.  A call was placed to 911 and various agencies responded.  The boat with significant damage to its bow washed up ashore without the operator onboard.  When the victim's did not return home the victim's wife sent their son to look for him.  The son took out their other boat and found his father's drifting up the shoreline, with all the damage and emergency responders were arriving to the scene.  The body of the victim was recovered on 8/10/10. Alcohol will likely be a factor but tox results have not come back as of yet.  Still ongoing investigation pre-liminary report at this time on 9/17/10.

Three men decided to go out fishing with a cooler full of beer.  Two of the men were friends and the third man was a friend of the surviving friend's son.  He was asked to operate the boat because he did not drink.  The victim and his friend fished and drank beer for a while with no luck when they hooked a bluefish.  The operator backed down and took water in over the transom.  The boat stalled out and could not be restarted.  At that point the victim panicked and said he was going to swim to the island (approximately 500 yards away). He jumped overboard without a lifejacket.   His friend said he was very athletic and thought he would make it to shore.  The VHF was not working so the friend of the victim called his mother who called the Coast Guard for a vessel in distress.  The two remaining men stayed with the vessel as it was sinking, put their life jackets on and were rescued about 20 minutes later by the Coast Guard.  The Coast Guard began a search for the missing victim.  The operator and the victim's friend were given field sobriety tests and portable breathalyzer tests.  The operator admitted to having 1 beer but passed both tests.  The friend admitted being intoxicated and failed both tests.  As the operator was not under the influence there were no charges in this case.  The victim's body was recovered the next day.  Alcohol and drugs were contributing factors in this case.

A father and son were fishing off a 2 person kayak when vessel #1 ran over the kayak causing injury to the father and death to his 10 year old son.  The investigators cited negligent operation in this case.  Still awaiting word for the da if there will be charges in this case.  Vessel #1 was towing a waterskiier at the time.  He admitted to having 2 beers while operating.  He claimed he did not see the vessel due to the glare from the sun.  Info as of 9/29/10.  Will update when more info becomes availalbe.

As of 10/12/10 preliminary information at this time is that three men were on a vessel when the bilge pumps failed and the vessel starting taking on water.  A mayday call was received by the Coast Guard.  Upon arrival from the coast guard the vessel was under with three parties in the water.  Two surviving men were wearing lifejackets and supported the third man who was unconscious and not wearing a lifejacket.    One man was pronounced dead.  Vessel still has not been recovered.  Update 10/15/10 vessel has been recovered by a lobsterman in the area.

Operator and his brother went out to retrieve each of their 10 lobster traps.  They knew the vhf radio was not working and could not check the weather.  The wave conditions were bad - between 4-6 foot but were able to still haul a number of their traps.  Surviving brother stated that he felt the boat was overloaded with the traps, line, buoys and assorted gear.  Wave conditions got worse and his brother told him to put his life jacket on.  Their was only 1 life jacket available and it was tied to the back of the operator's chair.  Survivor could not get it on but clutched it under his arms.  A 15 ft wave hit the side of the boat causing it to overturn.  The deceased and his brother were thrown toward the rocks.  He saw his brother struggling and heard him yell that he was not going to make it.  Three waves later he observed him floating face down.  Survivor was able to get to shore of an island.  The vessel washed up ashore as well and he was able to gather items to stay warm and prepared to light the 5 gal fuel tank on fire as a signal.  He was recovered early the next morning by a Coast Guard helicopterl.  He described his brother as an experienced boat operator but a daredevil.  Cause of accident inattention to weather/sea conditions/overloaded vessel/insufficient/inaccessible life jackets.

At this time 5/19/11.  This is an on-going investigation.  According to witnesses the 2 occupants on board launched the canoe.  It was underway for approximately 15 minutes when it capsized.  One occupant swam to shore safely and the other man died while swimming to shore.   Victim was located about 3 hours later by emergency personnel. 2/17 cause of accident operator inexperience, lack of pfd's and safety equipment.  DA determined not enough evidence to warrant criminal charges

According to victim's wife victim paddled out on his canoe to put a mooring sticker on his sailboat then paddled over to his motorboat.  That was the last time she saw him.  She was notified by neighbors that they saw the victim swimming back to shore and the canoe floating away.  They saw him begin to struggle in the water and went to help him.  They pulled him onto the beach unconscious and began cpr.  He was not wearing a PFD and only had a seat cushion available.  Wife could not confirm whether victim could swim or not.  Investigator believes most likely scenario is victim entered canoe in order to head back to shore was most likely was standing in the canoe when it tipped and he fell into the water.  Cause of accident not wearing pfd or having one available and operator inattention/improper loading.  Toxicology tests came back with no results.

A pontoon boat was underway when a non-swimming passenger jumped overboard from the port side of the vessel without a life jacket.  Three persons entered the water in an attempt to rescue victim when it because apparent that he was having difficulty staying above the surface of the water.  Victim disappeared below the surface.  The body was recovered the next day.  It is believed the victim's judgement was impaired by alcohol he consumed that evening.  Operator of vessel was not drinking.

Vessel was travelling at a high rate of speed and there were also ground swells about 3 ft high according to a witness.  Vessel was bouncing around alot and came out of the water 6-8 feet.  Vessel came down onto a swell and split immediately into a v-shape in the middle of the vessel.  2 occupants were thrown into the water and assisted by and put onto other vessels in the area.  One passenger was unconscious and unresponsive was pronounced dead at the hosptial and the other was also  injured.  The investigator determined that cause of accident was many factors.  Unfortunately due to the severity of the break in the vessel - many parts of the motor and vessel were not recovered.  Factors are overall age of vessel and deterioration of internal portions of structure (hull).  Modifying vessel to convert it from inboard engines to outboard.  Increasing outboard hp to 600hp.  Sea state.  Reckless and negligent operation taking into account time of day, number of vessels in area, and restrictions marked by navigational aids.  Alcohol was .08bac

Operator was enroute to dock vessel.  He and his passengers were drinking.  Steering wheel pulled to left causing the 2 occupants to be thrown overboard.   Vessel was still running and going in circles.  Operator was rescued by a nearby kayaker.  Two weeks later the body of the other occupant was located.  Operator was charged with boating under the influence.  Actual cause of accident was steering because of a loose or missing tiller arm/pivot plate bolt and lock nut.  Sudden loss of steerage and subsequent heeling of the vessel caused it to chine-walk and create a sudden change in direction and velocity ultimately ejecting occupants.  Had the vessel been in better condition and received professional maintenance this incident probably wouldn't have occurred.
Passenger jumped off a moving vessel with no pfd
Fatal accident in which the operator of vessel #1 was found hanging off of the side of his sailboat. He was helped to shore by a local vessel, later pronounced dead at the hospital.

According to the local pd that responded the operator/deceased had recently obtained the vessel on ebay and had gone out on the lake with his girlfriend's two young daughters 10 and 13.  There was no safety equipment on board including lifejackets and no one on board was wearing a pfd.  He experienced a problem with the battery but managed to get the vessel underway when he made a sharp turn.  The young girls were sitting on seats that were even with the gunwale but it was not equipped with sufficient rail to prevent a person from falling overboard.  The 10 yr girl fell off the boat into the water.  The operator/deceased went into the water to retrieve the girl.  The girl was saved by a vessel with some men who had been fishing who brought her to shore and performed CPR on her and saved her life.  A passing kayaker jumped aboard to help the 13 yr old sister who as still on board the vessel which was idling and in gear.  The operator/deceased never re-surfaced.  His body was found by divers later in that evening.  The lack of safety equipment and lack of guardrail are significant factors in this case.  The 10 yr old was required by law to be wearing a pfd and there was none on board.

Operator of vessel #2 had be drinking and struck a moored sailboat.  The crash caused two of the passengers to be thrown into the water.  Both passengers were recovered by Operator.    One woman was pulled into the boat unconscious.  Operator transported victim to the beach where she was taken to the hospital and later died of her injuries.  He submitted to a blood alcohol test at the hospital.  Operator was charged with operation of a vessel under the influence of alcohol causing death.

Owner/deceased had purchased vessel 2 weeks prior.  Owner and 4 friends had a couple of beers at home and decided to go fishing on the reservoir.  They were using a battery operated outboard motor.  Vessel was unregistered, had no lights, no pds's on board and was over capacity.  Motor ran for 40 minutes and the battery died.  They had one oar to paddle with and took turns.  At the time of the capsizing the deceased was paddling and someone else took over because he was becoming tired.  That passenger stepped up to the bow and vessel flipped over sending everybody into the water.  They stayed with the capsized vessel for a while attempting to make it to shore.  They were getting tired and unable to get the vessel to shore decided to swim to shore and go for help.  Emergency personnel arrived, administered first-aid and transported subjects.  One person was deceased.   Cause of accident was alcohol and overloading.

Operator and victim had gone fishing overnight with two other acquaintances.  The operator and victim arrived at the State park to flush the engine and vessel off of salt water.  Both men decided to go for a swim to rinse off salt from their skin and clothes.  Operator does not swim well so he decided to put on a pfd to swim.  The victim jumped off the swim platform and did not seem to be any problem or be in distress.  The operator turned around to enter the water and did not see the victim.  He thought perhaps the victim dove under the water to grab his leg as a joke but realized he did not see him anywhere.  Operator entered the water looking for the victim while yelling for help.  Victim was located on 6/17/12 by a dive team.  Investigator noted alcohol beverages in vessel.  Cause of death was accidental drowning.  Alcohol was found on the vessel and victim tox results came back at .28 BAC and Vitreous humor fluid tested at .37 AC level.  Additionally the victim tested presumptive positive for amphetamine.  Conclusion is that this was a preventable accident had there not been the over consumption of alcoholic beverages.
Victim was a deck hand during a sailboat race, stood up quickly, lost his balance and fell into the water.  He was wearing an inflatable pfd that deployed upon impact with the water.

Investigation still ongoing.  Victim fell off the vessel while standing starboard side of the vessel when a small wave struck the boat.  Victim could not swim and went under.  The two other occupants both jumped overboard to help victim.  They were unable to help victim as he was trying to pull them under.  They swam back to the vessel but it wouldn't start.  They were helped to shore by two people who heard their screams for help.  Pontoon boat drifted to shore.  Victim was very drunk according to his friend.  Operator had a couple of beers but did not seem intoxicated to the investigator.  Violations were operating unregistered motorboat.  Displaying wrong registration number.  Operating after sunset w/o navigation lights.  Bowriding.

According to passenger and witnesses.  Operator was cruising at a high rate of speed, took a sharp turn, went airborne, flipped over and capsized.  A couple of men on a pontoon boat fishing in the area saw the accident and pulled the men out of the water.  Once operator was on the pontoon boat he fell forward on his knees, appeared to pull his arms to his chest, collapsed face down on deck and began vomiting.  CPR was performed on the victim by an observer until the police arrived.  Victim was pronounced dead at arrival to hospital.  Investigator interviewed passenger who was uninjured and noticed a strong odor of alcohol.  The deceased according to passenger only had 1 beer and his wife said he was not a big drinker.  He tested positive for both marijuana and alcohol.

Operator had rented two kayaks for the day one for him to operate and the other for his granddaughter to use.  Suddenly he slumped over and fell out of the kayak into the water.  Victim was face down with the pfd keeping him afloat.  His granddaughter left her kayak and jumped in and turned him over and yelled for help.  Two male parties from the rental office utilized a jet ski to bring victim and his granddaughter to shore.  Victim was unconscious and unresponsive.  Lifeguards on adjacent beaches attempted to assist victim and call for help.  Victim pronounced dead at hospital.    There is no hull number on this report as the rental company had numerous kayaks that were the same size, make and color.  The rental company had put back the kayak and by the time the investigator went to the dealership they were unsure exactly which kayak the victim had rented.

No eye witnesses and summary is a result of location of evidence on vessel and statements from individuals involved in recovery.  It appears that operator (husband) entered water in attempt to retrieve or swim with dog.  Passenger/wife (a non swimmer) entered water in an apparent attempt to assist her husband.  A PWC operator encountered the persons in the water.  Wife was asking for help while husband was lying face down in water.  The vessel from which they embarked was not in the vicinity and it is unclear whether it was underway or making way.   Evidence of drug use was on the vessel when it was found.

Three people aboard a canoe, drinking alcohol for some time while on board.  Canoe capsized.  Two passengers were able to swim to shore.  The deceased was located later on that day submerged in mud.  The men did not know who owned the canoe.  When they arrived at the campsite that day there were 4 canoes on shore and they grabbed one to use.  Accident cause was alcohol use, improper loading, overloading, operator inexperience and the canoe was modified so that the total weight of the canoe was higher.

Operator took his nephew out for a day of fishing.  15 minutes later Operator stood up to hand his nephew a bag.  It rocked once and then flipped over, throwing them both in the water.  Passenger attempted to save his uncle but he started pulling him under so he swam back to the overturned vessel and threw his uncle a Type II pfd because he could not swim.  He attempted to turn the trolling motor over of the boat in an effort to power the boat over to his uncle but the trolling motor propeller got wrapped up in his tee shirt.  He as able to push the boat to where he had left his uncle but he had disappeared.  He swam to shore.  About an hour later divers found the body of the deceased.  Cause of accident overloading, improper loading and unsteadiness of operator while standing, shift of weight in vessel with gear and inadequate # of PFD's.

Operator and passenger were paddling (using a piece of wood as a paddle).  Canoe suddenly capsized as the operator thought perhaps the passenger may have stood up.  Both men ended up in the water.  They righted the canoe and attempted to re board but were unsuccessful.  Survivor shouted to deceased to swim to shore and he could hear him swimming behind him.  Once he got to shore he looked back but was unable to see deceased.  Both men had a few drinks before they went out and no pfd's on board.  Alcohol and improper loading, no pfd's on board were cause of accident.

Deceased borrowed a kayak from a neighbor and decided to go out only wearing red swim shirts and no pfd nor did he take one.  He could swim but not a strong swimmer.  His friends urged him to take a pfd but he refused.  He said he was only going out for a little while.  A significant thunderstorms moved through the area.  About an 1 1/2 later his friend called the pd and reported him missing.  A search process began.  The kayak was found secured under the elastic cargo webbing at the bow of the kayak when it was found washed ashore.  A male body was found by a fisherman wearing red shorts on 10/1/12 and it was identified as the deceased.  Although no conclusive determination can be made to exactly what actions were taken by the deceased the investigator determined through the evidence that and interviews conducted that the deceased most likely landed on a rock outcropping and exited the kayak to explore and look around.  In doing so he took the kayak paddle and secured it under the kayak.  The tide at this time was a flood tide with high tide at 5:40pm.  Severe thunderstorms were on approach to the area and would it causing large waves, extremely strong winds and driving rain.  It is undetermined that he was on the rocks and got swept off by waves, lost his footing and slipped into the strong currents in the area or decided to attempt to swim to shore.  It also can not be concluded that the kayak floated off prior for following the deceased entering the water.  The kayak was located in tact with no indication of an external force or contact applied and with the paddle secured in a manner consistent with exiting by the paddler and drawing up by land.  Unfortunate preventable accident if he had worn a pfd and checked the tide and weather forecast prior to setting out on coastal waters.

Deceased was involved in a sanctioned hydroplane race that has been going on for 33 years.  The accident occurred during the last run.  Victim was extremely experienced.  He was approaching the finish line when the bow of his boat lifted and then went airborne.  The victim and the vessel separated and came back to the surface of the pond with the boat making contact with the victim.  The vessel and motor had been modified by the victim for competitive racing.  The vessel did pass the race inspectors examination prior to the operator setting out for race.  All systems were found to be in operational condition even though there was extensive damage to the vessel.  It is concluded that excess trim had been applied in order to maximize the vessels speed resulting in too great an amount of air to build below the vessel and further resulting in vessel to leave the waters surface and go airborne with the operator being ejected in the process.  Operator error was cause of this accident.

2 friends set out to fish for the day.  They were both experienced kayakers.  Fishing conditions were difficult due to the wind, waves so they decided to paddle back to the a more protected section of the pond.  Victim was complaining that he was cold and he looked yellow.  Normally according to his friend he is a bull and can take anything.  It was tough paddling against the waves until they got to the protected section of the pond.  They had just started fishing when he looked over at his friend and he was overturned.  His friend said that within seconds he got to his friend and got him to shore.  His airway was difficult to open becuase his tongue was large - swelled and got in the way.  Several minutes later he decided he needed help and took his kayak back to shore where they started from and waved a car down to call 911.  Both men had pfd's but were not wearing them.  Emergency personnel arrived and paddled to the victim, performed cpr ut he was unresponsive at scene and pronounced at the hospital.  Tox report and autopsy report have not come back yet but alcohol was found onboard as well as what is believed to be drugs.  It is not known at this point whether the victim took any drugs.  A citation was issued to the other operator for not wearing a pfd during the required time period.

Victim and his friend had gone out in the morning to bait some lobster traps.  They went to lunch and had a few drinks.  They returned to the beach and victim dropped his friend off on shore and went back to his mooring.  He became concerned when he tried to call his friend on his cell phone and got no answer.  He tried to yell at him for shore but did not get a response.  Next thing he saw was his friend in the water.  Another witness stated that he saw victim on his lobster boat standing up leaning against the cabin.  He saw him in the same position for at least a 1/2 hour and thought he might be using a cell phone.  Tide was going out and the boat was attached strangely to the mooring line at the side port side of the boat and not at the bow as it would normally be.  He watched him unhook the dinghy and sit on the gunwale of the lobster boat swinging his legs over the side one at a time.  He saw victim slide feet first into the dinghy which immediately flipped over.  He was hanging on the raised engine off the lobster boat.  He was hanging on the port side as it swung around in the wind.  After a period of time he saw victim face down in water.

It was common practice for this missing person to tie up his dog at the park and row on to his sailboat on the mooring and return to the park and retrieve the dog afterwards.  It appears the sailboat was prepared to dock to the pier on the port of the vessel as indicated by fenders and fender boards being placed on the port side.  This positioning would also indicate an outgoing tide.  The vessel was found dragging its anchor and dinghy secured to stern of the sailboat it is evident missing person made it aboard the sailboat, prepared it for mooring up to the pier, removed the boat from the mooring and subsequently had to anchor the vessel due to the prop becoming fouled with line.  It is presumed that he entered the water after anchoring the vessel and sometime after making an 8:40pm phone call.  The presence of the overturned dingy would indicate he was in it attempting to possibly free the fouled prop or swamped it in attempt to get back into it once he entered the water.  Victim is still missing and has not been recovered.  It is assumed that he accidentally fell overboard.

According to a news media report, a 73-year old fell from a boat.  Even though he was brought to shore and had his head above water, he died.  A firefighter responded to the accident and also died during the rescue attempt. The news article indicates cold water was a factor

DECEASED VICTIM FELL INTO WATER WHILE FISHING. HIS PFD WAS ON, BUT NOT SECURED. WHEN HE HIT THE WATER HE LOST THE PFD. THE SECOND OCCUPANT FELL IN THE WATER AFTER THE BOAT SWUNG AROUND AND CAPSIZED. DUE TO A LANGUAGE BARRIER AND THE SURVIVORS NOT COOPERATING WITH INVESTIVEGATORS, THIS IS ALL THE INFORMATION AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. iT SHOULD BE NOTED THAT THIS CASE IS STILL OPEN.
location: CHESAPEAKE BAY NR ELMS BEACH, MD

description: VICTIM IN VESSEL 1 FELL OUT OF THE BOAT WHEN THE VESSELMADE A SHARP TURN.  THE VICTIM WAS PICKED UP OUT OF THE WATER AND TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL. THE VICTIM DIED OF INJURIES, DROWNING ON 5-20-2010
SUBJECTS IN VESSEL 1 WENT INTO THE WATER AFTER  THE OPERATOR MADE A SHARP TURN CAUSING THE BOAT TO CAPSIZE. THE OPERATOR OF THE VESSEL  NEVER SURFACED AND DROWNED. THE OCCUPANT HAD NO INJURIES.

A HOMEMADE PUSH BARGE OCCUPIED BY TWO MALE INDIVIDUALS, SANK AFTER TAKING WAVES OVER THE BOW AND STARBOARD SIDE. BOTH INDIVIDUAL ATTEMPTED TO SWIM TO SHORE. THE PASSENGER OF THE VESSEL MADE IT TO SHORE. THE OPERATOR DID NOT.
VICTIM WAS OPERATING A PWC DURING A THUNDER STORM . THE OTHER OPERATOR OF ANOTHER PWC THEN FOUND THE VICTIM IN THE WATER AND UNRESPONSIVE. THE VICTIM WAS TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL AND PRONOUNCED DEAD.
location: CHESAPEAKE BAY BRIDGE SOUTH OF, MD

description: VICTIM AND TWO WITNESSES WERE FISHING WHEN THEIR VESSEL BEGAN TO TAKE ON WATER. A GOOD SAMATITAN STOPPED AND STARTED TAKING ALL THREE INDIVIDUALS ONBOARD HIS VESSEL. THE VICTIM'S VESSEL CAPSIZED AND EJECTED THE VICTIM AND ONE WITNESS INTO THE WATER. BOTH MEN SWAM TO THE GOOD SAM VESSEL. ALL THREE INDIVIDUALS WERE NOT INJURED. MORE THAN AN HOUR LATER, AS THE VICTIM WAS BEING TRASPORTED BACK TO SHORE BY POLICE BOAT, HE WENT INTO FULL CARDIAC ARREST.
location: CHESAPEAKE BAY, LOVE POINT TO , MD

description: VICTIM FELL OUT OF VESSEL AND DROWNed. VICTIM HAD MEDICAL CONDITIONS THAT COMPLICATED THE VICTIM FALLING OVERBOARD.

OCCUPANT OF VESSEL 1 ADVISED THAT WHILE UNDERWAY, THE VESSEL STRUCK A BUOY, THROWING THE OPERATOR OVERBOARD. THE OCCUPANT SUSTAINED INJURIES TO THE FACE AND ARMS. THE OPERATOR'S BODY WAS RECOVERED ON 8-16-2010 NEAR THE AREA OF THE ACCIDENT. THE OCCUPANT ADVISED THAT BOTH HE AND THE OPERATOR HAD CONSUMED ALCOHOL PRIOR TO THE ACCIDENT.
VESSEL BROKE DOWN. OCCUPANTS ANCHORED THE VESSEL FROM THE STERN. WAKE CASPSIZED THE VESSEL. TWO OCCUPANTS WERE RESCUED. ONE WAS LATER RECOVERED DECEASED.

A witness observed the operator jump from the vessel and swim alongside it. The victim was not in distress. Later, the vessel was located aground and the victim missing. There is no other information available on what happened. The actual grounding was unwitnessed.

On 4-22-11 at approximately 7:30a.m. 4 men left Breezy Point Marina in a 25' outboard for a fishing trip. The seas were very rough that day. The men began trolling  but after a while realized it was too rough and turned the boat around to go back. As they turned the boat they had following seas and for unknown reasons the motors and electrical systems quit. The vessel began to sink very quickly due to the seas coming over the stern. All the men started to don P.F.D's, only 3 were successful in getting them on before the vessel sank. There was no time to call for help by phone or V.H.F.  2 men swam to shore and were able to summon help. The other 2 men stayed where the boat had sank. A fire dept. boat picked up the unresponsive men. All 4 men were taken to the hospital. 2 men were treated for hypothermia and exposure and the unresponsive men pronounced dead in the emergency room. Autopsies revealed that both men died from "drowning".

OCCUPANT OF VESSEL 1 ATTEMPTED TO FEND OFF OF A PILING WHILE THE VESSEL WAS LEAVING THE SLIP. THE VICTIM INSTEAD WAS LEFT CLINGING TO THE PILING AND THEN SLID DOWN THE PILING AND ENTERED THE WATER. THE VICTIM ATTEMPTED TO SWIM BACK TO VESSEL 1 WHEN THE VICTIM WENT BELOW THE SURFACE AND COULD NOT BE FOUND. DIVERS LOCATED THE VICTIM'S BODY AT 10:08 AND RESCUE PERSONNEL ATTEMPTED CPR WHICH WAS UNSUCCESSFUL.

On 5-26-11, operator was at Leanord's Mill Pond with his two friends. He asked friend if he could take his kayak out on the pond who said yes.  the two friends later heard a shout for help and looked out and saw the overturned Kayak in the pond. They both got in a boat and went out to the kayak but only found the capsized kayak, paddle and shirt. They picked up another witness who heard the shout. They continued to search but never located the victim.  The victim did not know how to swim .

On the evening of 05/27/11, operator and occupant took a 28' Cabin Cruiser from the South River to Annapolis to a Resteraunt/Bar. They left the establishment around  1:45 a.m. and headed back to the South River. operator was operating the boat and he said that occupant went to the stern of the boat.  operator turned around to say something to occupant and noticed that he had disapeared off the vessel. He immediatley called for assistance on the Vhf radio.

On 06/02/11 occupant's body was located in the Bay. An autopsy ruled his death a drowning.
location: Chesapeake Bay, Mouth of Sever, MD

description: On 6/11/11 at approx. 0910 a 16' O.B vessel was anchored in the Ocean City Inlet. On board the vessel were 6 P.O.B.  They decided to pull the anchor and move to calmer waters and continue fishing. As one man was pulling the anchor line, the operator, moved the vessel forward. The vessels prop got tangled up in the anchor line and swung the vessel around stern- to, to the current. The vessel started taking on water and they were unable to cut the anchor line from the prop. As the vessel sank the men grabbed on to coolers , one man swam to shore and the operator, who evidently could not find anything to grab on to keep him afloat, drowned. None of the men were wearing P.F. D 's at the time of the accident and the victim could not swim.
VICTIM WAS OPERATING A PWC. HE WAS LATER NOTICIED FLOATING IN THE WATER.  AUTOPSY STATED HE DIED FROM A HEART ATTACK.
VICTIM WAS A PASSENGER ON A SMALL SAILING VESSEL. SHE WAS WEARING A PFD AND HARNESS. THE WIND CAUSED THE VESSEL TO CAPSIZE. THE VICTIM BECAME ENTANGLED UNDER THE VESSEL AND DROWNED.

VESSEL 1 WAS FOUND UNOCCUPIED IN THE SASSAFRAS RIVER AFTER VICTIM WAS OBSREVED OPERATING THE VESSEL, BUT THE OPERATOR COULD NOT BE LOCATED.  A SEARCH OF THE AREA PRODUCED NEGATIVE RESULTS. ON 7-25-2011 THE VICTIM'S BODY WAS RECOVERED BY NRP IN THE GENERAL AREA WHERE THE VICTIM WAS LAST SEEN OPERATING VESSEL 1. IT IS NOT KNOWN HOW THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED AND THERE ARE NOT ANY WITNESSES OF THE VICTIM FALLING OUT/FROM THE VESSEL.

OCCUPANTS OF VESSEL 1 ADVISED THAT WHILE AT ANCHOR AND FISHING THE VESSEL BEGAN TO TAKE ON WATER. THE VESSEL SANK CAUSING ALL OCCUPANTS TO ENTER THE WATER.THE  VICTIM COULD NOT SWIM AND WENT BELOW THE SURFACE. THE VICTIM WAS LOCATED, CPR PERFORMED AND THEN TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL WHERE HE SUCCUMBED TO HIS INJURIES. CAUSE OF DEATH IS RULED AS ACCIDENTAL DROWNING. NO OTHER INJURIES WERE REPORTED.
THE VESSEL WAS FOUND WASHED ONSHORE ON 8/16/11. ON 8/17/11 THE VICTIM'S BODY WAS LOCATED. VICTIM HAD BEEN CRABBING. NO WITNESSES. INVESTIGATORS AWAITING TOXICOLOGY. SUSPICION THAT DRUGS ARE INVOLVED.
location: COX CREEK OFF WEST RIVER, MD

description: Operator of a personal watercraft, operating at a high rate of speed, was jumping a wave and fell from the vessel. The operator attempted to remount the vessel but was unsuccessful. The operator then started to swim to shore. Waves overtook the individual and he went limp, face down in the water.
location: Chesapeake Bay, Near North Bea, MD

description:
Occupants of Vessel #1 had visited a bar for drinks (alcohol) and food for about 1/2 hour before proceeding in vessel #1 to the marina. (victim) was originally operating the vessel but asked operator if she would like to run the vessel. She took the helm and victim took off his boots, socks and shirt and jumped off the side of the boat. She said he smiled at them when he went into the water but when she circled back to where he went in he did not reappear. She turned the boat off . They flagged down a jet skier to assist them and to call 911. There were 4 people on board the vessel.

N.R.P. Officers were called to the scene and took the above statements from the occupents. 

The victims body was located the following day . His Post Mortem BAC level was .08.

Charges are pending on this case.

On 07/04/11 vessel #1 was underway with 2 P.O.B.  (operator) turned the vessel sharply to the left throwing his passenger out of the vessel on the right side. operator fell out the left side of the vessel. The vessel started circling to the left. occupant was drifting away from the vessel and was yelling for help. She said she could see operator's head above the water and he was yelling for help. A good samaritan picked her up but operator could not be located. 

His body was located on 07/06/11. Alcohol was involved in this accident however the  post mortem B.A.C report is not available.
location: Magoathy River near Dobbins is, MD

description:
Victim was sitting with his girlfriend on the bow of vessel #1 (a pontoon boat) in front of the gate. Their feet were hanging in the water. He was joking with her about what would happen if he fell off" or "what would she do if he fell off". She knew that he would most likely die. He scooted out a little acting like he was going in, to tease her. Unfortunately he must of lost his balance and did fall in off the bow. His girlfriend screamed for the operator (her father)to stop. The vessel was traveling fairly slow. The operator did not hear her at first but finally did and turned the vessel to go look for the victim. The victim did not surface.

All the subjects had been drinking alcohol that day. The operator 's B.A.C was .11. He was charged with O.W.I. 

The vicitims body was recovered the following day on 08/07/11. he had propellor marks on his head, neck ,shoulder and arm. (right)

This report did not have the victims  post mortem B.A.C. level.

VESSEL CAPSIZED DUE TO A GUST OF WIND AND FAILING TO LET SAIL LINES OUT. ALL THREE INDIVIDUALS WERE TOSSED INTO THE WATER. TWO WERE REMOVED FROM THE WATER. A THIRD VICTIM WAS MISSING. THE FEMALE VICTIM SURVIVED. MALE VICTIM WAS DECEASED. SECOND MALE VICTIM WAS MISSING AND LOCATED AT A LATER DATE DECEASED.
location: CHESAPEAKE BAY NR SANDY POINT , MD

description: On 12/15/11, 2 subjects were duck hunting on shore on the Potomac River. At approximatly 4:50p.m. they loaded up there decoys and started to return to the dock where their trailer and vehicle were. The wind and seas were very rough, winds blowing 15-20 mph. and incoming tide. The waves started blowing over the bow of the small vessel ( 15Ft in length)  and they started taking on water. The two subjects decided to head to the closest shore line for safety. The vessel continued to take on more water over the bow and was sinking. The Owner/Operator called 911. The 2 occupants did not have on their life jackets, and at this time they decied to leave the sinking boat and swim to shore.  The Owner /Operator did not make it to shore . The passenger was picked up by a Rescue Vessel. The Victim was located by a dive team the following day. The passenger advised that the victim had drank 2 or 3 beers during their hunt but the autopsy report showed a BAC of 0.00 . The autopsy report shows that the victim died of drowning complicated by hypothermia. The passenger refused medical treatment. The passenger advised he had not consumed any alcohol. The vessel was located and raised.
location: Potomac River, Off Indian head, MD

description:
On 4/25/2012 victim took small sailboat out in the afternoon. He was reported overdue by his wife that night. A search by air and water was conducted that night and the sailboat was recovered, upside down. The victims body was found later that morning floating face down. He did not have on a P.F.D. 

An autopsy report shows the victim did drown complicate by hypothermia and also had a B.A.C. of .13.

The investigator did not give any specifics on weather or sea conditions for this accident.

A vessel occupied four times was traveling north towards the Kent Narrows.  Another operator was chosen since he stated he knew the area well.  The vessel was traveling out of the channel so it could keep its speed up.  The speed zone only applies to the channel.  The vessel's destination was the Jetty Bar.  
There are two jetties -- the jetty closest to the boat (old stone jetty) and a slightly longer concrete jetty.  The operator turned the vessel in an easterly direction towards its destination but not north enough to avoid the other jetty.  The vessel impacted the cement jetty at high speed ejecting one passenger who impacted the jetty and died.   The two bar/restaurants the vessel was heading for do have lights on the dock.  It would only be supposition to deduce the lights might have masked the second jetty.   The major factors in this fatal accident were that the vessel was traveling outside of the marked channel at night at speed and the second jetty was impacted near its northern extremity.

Three of the occupants were injured when they hit the jetty.   The operator complained of pain in the ribs and head.  He had been drinking but was well under the limit.  The injured were taken to shock trauma with non life threatening injuries.

12-foot vessel, occupied five times capsized during a severe thunderstorm. Four of the occupants were recovered from the water and one was not. On Sunday, July 1, 2012 the body of the operator was recovered.

Three adult males were returning from a three day cruise on a 27 foot Catalina sloop.  While mooring near Deale, Maryland, a passenger stood up in the cockpit and slipped.  He grabbed the hatch cover but it slid forward.  The 64 year old 237 pound passenger fell down the companionway into the cabin striking his neck and head.  Despite application of CPR by another passenger, the subject was pronounced dead.  His alcohol level was .16.  The operator had no evidence of alcohol or drug use.
location: Rockhold Ck off Herring Bay, MD

description:
An unoccupied PWC was found drifting. A PFD was found in the area of the unoccupied PWC on July 3, 2012   A search ensued and continued ion to the next day. The body of the operator was located on the evening of July 4th, 2012.  A vehicle with Jet Ski trailer was found nearby close to a boat ramp and was registered to the deceased.  A witness stated he saw the victim swimming  near his jet ski on July 3 and a PFD in the water 100 yards away.  The witness stated the victim did  not appear to be in distress.  The Jet Ski had no apparent damage.  There was an empty beer bottle and two bottle caps in the front compartment.  From the evidence, it appears the victim removed his PFD and entered the water.  The PFD likely drifted away.  The victim may have been attempting to retrieve the PFD.  For  unknown reasons he either became disoriented or exhausted and went under water.  The amount of drugs in the victims system most likelyb contributed to the fatality.
 
The Medical Examiner ruled the cause of death as drowning.  The toxicology results showed the following drugs in the victim's system:  Ethanol (13%), Phencyclidine, Oxyodone.

On 9-3-2012 a 37 foot ODay sloop reported a missing boater in the Chesapeake Bay.  Maryland NRP responded.  The sloop was sailing north in heavy weather when the wind picked up and heeled the boat over.  Two occupants slipped over the leeward side.  The operator picked up one person.  The second male occupant was last seen waving his hands.   The boaters then lost sight of him.  NRP officers boarded the ODay and along with an NRP patrol vessel searched the area for 4.5 hours.  The search continued the next day.  The missing boater was recovered by NRP on 9-6-2012.  The report of the medical examiner revealed a head injury and preliminary cause of death was drowning.  The deceased was not wearing a PFD but was known to have been a good swimmer.  No alcohol was involved and no charges filed.
location: Craighill Channel, Ches Bay N , MD

description: Two individuals were fishing from a small vessel. Both individuals were standing and casting their lines when they lost their balance and the vessel capsized. The occupant was hanging onto the hull of the vessel when he lost consciousness and slid off the vessel. The operator was able to recover the victim and swim him to shore.  Despite CPR by both the operator and EMS, the victim was pronounced deceased on the scene.  No alcohol was involved.  Death was ruled due to a medical incident (cardiac related).

On July 15, 2012 two subjects in a 20 foot bass boat were drifting in the headwaters of Bush River, off the Chesapeake Bay.  They decided to remove their PFDs and swim.  They climbed back in.  The operator, who had been drinking, decided to jump in again.  He immediately seemed to be in distress, and the occupant jumped in after him.  The boat drifted away in the current and the occupant lost sight of his friend.  A good samaritan picked up the occupant and brought him to shore where he was examined by EMS.  Several agencies including MD Natural Resources Police searched for the operator without sucess.  On July 17th a body was recovered and later identified as the operator.  The autopsy reported death by accidental drowning.  The investigation is still open pending recommendations by the States Attorneys office.
location: Bush Rive Headwater, Ches Bay, MD

description: A 200 pound male non swimmer with no PFD available was fishing from a newly purchased small kayak in a private lake.  The kayak was likely over maximum capacity.  He tipped over and according to witnesses disappeared from sight.  He was located drowned in 8 to 10 feet of water by s;ide scan  sonar.

An older model 14 foot outboard with 4 individuals was drifting on August 28, 2012 in the Middle River off the Chesapeake Bay.  Two individuals went swimming.  One individual appeared in distress.  The operator jumped in to assist and drowned as the old vessel drifted away.  No one was wearing a PFD. Natural Resources Police and other agencies searched for the missing operator who was finally found on August 30.  The ME determined death by accidental drowning.  The case remains under investigation.

Two people on a boat were reported overdue.  The subjects had been transiting a recently purchased boat from NJ to FL.  Debris was found (cabin top with rador, and GPS) that is believed to match the boat.  Investigators believe that the vessel took on water because of it's poor condition and perilious route.  It is believed the boat sank and the two are presumed deceased.

Deceased victim was with a group of friends.  While the boat was drifting, all jumped overboard to swim.  The victim was the last to depart and jumped feet first in the water.  About five minutes after he entered the water, his friends noticed that he wasn't around.  They swam back to the boat, anchored it and called for help.  There was a small craft warning, seas were rough and wind moderate.  The victim's father indicated the victim is not a good swimmer.

Victims # 1 and # 2 were reported overdue from a weekend camping trip.  A search of the Island shoreline discovered an overturned and badly damaged 12 foot Carolina Skiff on the Southeastern cove of Bois Bubert Island.  Boat and motor had been separated by wave action rolling boat on shoreline for approx. 4 days before recovery.  The body of victim # 1 was located on the northern shore of the same cove.  Body of victim #2 was located and recovered approximately 1 month later. When located, Victim #2 was entangled in lobster trap buoy line belonging to Victim #1.  It appears that Victimi #1 and #2 were tending lobster traps when the incident occured.  Operator at the time of the incident can not be determined.

Vessel A was located near the boat landing on Onawa Lake.  Vessel 1 was overturned when it was located.  Victim 1 was later located in the water near the shore of the lake.  Victim 1 was not wearing a PFD.  There was a PFD in Vessel 1 when it was located.  Victim 1 was later determined to have died from drowning.  Victim 1 had a BAC of .137% when tested.

Coast Guard received a report of two overdue kayakers who had left Peaks Island for a brief trip around Ram Island.  Victim 1 and victim 2 were found the next day deceased floating facedown in the water.  Cause of death was determined to be hypothermia and drowning.  It is speculated that one of the victims may have tipped over and while trying to assist the other victim tipped into the water.  Water temperature, strong winds and tidal current would have made it difficult for the victims to make it back into the kayaks or back to shore.

Victim was operating vessel 1 with one passenger on board.  They went out on the lake to drain the water out of the boat.  The wind was blowing very hard at the time.  The area of the lake that vessel 1 went out to is a very large bay, allowing the waves to build.  Shortly before the victim went to turn vessel 1 around and head back towards the camp he reached behind to put the plug back in the boat.  A large wave then stuck the vessel at an odd angle, throwing the victim out if the vessel.  The passenger in vessel 1 tried to help the victim back in the vessel with a paddle but was unable to do so.  The passenger then jumped into the lake with a PFD to try and help.  The passenger stayed with the victim and tried to get the victim to put on the PFD but the victim refused.  The wind was blowing very hard and vessel1 was blown away from them very quickly.  They were not able to swim to the vessel.  A short time later the victim went under the water.  The passenger went down and brought the victim back to the surface but could not keep the victim on the surface.  The victim then went under the water again and drowned.  The passenger swam towards shore using the PFD to help float.  Approximately 2 hours after going in the water the passenger was was picked up by local campers that heard his screams for help.   Four days later the victims body floated and was transported to the funeral home.

Victim #1 who was also operator A, departed from Pepperell Cove boat ramp, Kittery Point, Maine, at approximately 9:06 a.m. on 11/06/10, to go duck hunting.  Victim #1 was operating a 15ft. 15hrsp. green, aluminum, open hull motor boat.

At approximately 2:30 p.m. a debris field was located at Lat: 43* 03.00N by Lon: 070* 40.00 off Gerrish Island, Kittery Point, Maine.

At approximately 4:30 p.m. Victim #1 was located on shore at the high tide mark, north of Seward Cove, in an area known by locals as Fresh Pond Cove, on Gerrish Island.   

Victim #1 was fully clothed, but did not have any foot gear on.  Victim #1 did not have a life jacket on, and was unresposive at the time located.

U.S.C.G. Station Portsmouth, who was involved in the search was notified of the location of Victim #1.  A helicopter was sent to the location.  Victim #1 was flown to Pease Air Force Base, New Hampshire, and then transported by ambulance to Portsmouth Regional Hospital in New Hampshire.

According to the news media, a man is still missing after officials found his green kayak and backpack floating near Murray Road.  According to a press release, it is suspected that the victim planned to kayak to Kineo which he did several times last summer.  High winds adn strong waves hindered search efforts.

Operator A was navigating the canoe down the Allagash River when his vessel struck a rock and flipped the vessel.  OperatorA and Operator B were both ejected from vessel.  Operator A saw Operator B float down stream.  When Operator A found Operator B he was unresponsive.  Operator A got Operator B to shore and preformed CPR and tried signaling for help.  Operator B was pronounced dead at the scene.

Operator left rental cottage for short kayak trip wearing a PFD and never returned.  Surface conditions and strong winds cuased operator to capsize.  Victim drowned after capsizing and was recovered wearing his PFD.

Operator A was canoeing alone on York Pond.  Operator A was not wearing a PFD.  Information provided by Operator A's son was that Operator A had a medical issue with blood pressure medicine which made him dizzy and fall when standing up.  The son witnessed Operator A falling in his home previous to the boating incident.  The son said Operator A prefered to stand up when attempting to land a fish.  The son also advised Operator A did not know how to swim.  Operator A did have a PFD onboard but it was  behind the seat of the canoe and was still with the canoe when it was located.  Operator A contacted the son and advised him he was going fishing at York Pond.  When the son failed to hear from Operator A at midnight he became concerned.  The son went to York Pond and saw Operator A's truck parked at the boat landing.  The son went out in another boat with a friend and located Operator A's overturned canoe.  The son then contacted York Police.  York Police contacted York Fire and Rescue and they arrived with another boat. York Fire and Rescue located Operator A floating in the water approximately two hundred yards from the overturned canoe.

Operator A had consumed alcohol and was operating the vessel on plane when he attempted a hard left hand turn.  He was sitting on the port side in the stern and the turn caused the boat to begin to take on water, eventually capsizing the boat.  No PFDs were on board and Operator A could not swim.  The passenger of the vessel could swim and attempted to keep the operator above water, but was unsuccessful.  A local camp owner heard the passenger’s cries for help and rowed a boat out and rescued the passenger.  Operator A had gone under water at this point and not resurfaced.  He was recovered deceased the next morning by divers

Deceased 1, witness 1, witness2, and witness 3 were all kayaking from Hadley Point in Bar Harbor to Lamoine State Park in Lamoine.  Witness 1 and deceased 1 attempted a direct route whereas witness 2 and 3 attemted a longer route along the Lamoine shoreline.  Approximately halfway across Decesed 1 became very panicked due to wind and 2-3 foot chop.  Witness 1 coached Deceased 1 along.  Witness 1 took 3-4 paddle strokes and turned back to observe deceased 1 had capsized.  Deceased 1 was holding onto his paddle and glasses with his left hand and his kayak with his right hand.  Witness 1 told him to let go of the paddle and hold onto the kayak, which he did.  Witness 1 believed deceased 1 was "struggling to stay up" so witness 1 jumped into the water and swam to him.  Witness 1 attempted to hold deceased 1 up and communicate with him, but found him to have very labored breathing.  Deceased 1 then closed his eyes and laid back in the water.  Witness 1 was unable to hold him above the water and he went under.  Witness 1 pulled him back up and began screaming.  Deceased 1 went under again and witness 1 pulled him up again.  Witness 4 and 5 were sailing in the area and immediately rendered assistance.  Deceased 1 and witness 1 were pulled into the sailboat, where CPR was started.  All returned to the dock and paramedics pronounced deceased 1 dead.

Victim 1 was using a friends kayak on beech hill pond in otis maine; victim 1 has very litttle experience in a kayak; the kayak owners wife told victim 1 that he needed to have a life jacket while using the kayak; victim 1 responded that he did not need a life jacket because he was a strong swimmer; victim 1 then paddled further out into the lake; the witness had turned her attention to the wife of victim 1 who was in a separate kayak and was helping her exit the kayak; when the witness looked back to where victim 1 was she observed that he had capsized the kayak and was swimming back toward the dock; victim one had swam approximately 10 meters when he suddenly stopped swimming and disappeared under the surface of the water; the witness immediately paddled to victim 1 location and attempted to pull him from the bottom of the lake to shore, a distance of less than 10 meters; the witness was not strong enough to move victim 1 and yelled for help; the boat owner and a neighbor went out in a boat and located victim 1 on the bottom of the lake; victim 1 was in approximately 7-8 feet of water; the male neighbor dove into the lake and brought victim 1 to shore where life saving cpr was attempted to no avail; victim 1 was pronounced dead at the scene; autopsy on the next day revealed that the victim drowned and had cardio vascualr disease that may have contributed to the drowning. The kayak was recovered approximately 125 feet from the owners dock upside down where it had drifted to shore with the paddle. Chemical and toxicology tests are still pending due to a large amount of prescription drugs being taken by victim 1.

Owner/operater left Scarborough Marsh, took a picture from Bluff Island, was reported overdue.  Hours later kayak found unoccupied and o/o found floating in water.  Cpr administered, CPR stopped on the way to hospital by EMS.  Declared deceased at Maine Medical Center.  No name or model number found on the kayak.

Operator A, aka, Victim 1, and Passenger were trolling for fish on Blake Lake in T16 R6 wels.  At approximately 6:30 pm, the passenger, who was located in the bow of the boat, stood up to urinate off the side.  When the passenger sat back down it rocked the boat to one side.  The gunwale dipped under the water and partially filled the small fishing boat with water.  At that point the boat overturned throwing both passenger and operator A into the water.  The passenger started to swim to shore which was approximately 100 feet away.  Passenger looked back several times in an attempt to find operator A but could not.  At one point, the passenger thought he saw operator A trying to get a hold of the overturned boat but passenger is not positive that was what he actually saw.

Passenger yelled for operator A for approximately 45 minutes but saw no sign of him.  Passenger got into his vehicle and warmed up for approximately 20 mins before driving out of the remote location to get help.  Operator A never re-surfaced.

Passenger stated during an interview that he had consumed quite a bit of alcohol that day.  Passenger stated that operator A had two shots of passenger's mixed whiskey drink and one beer earlier in the day.

Passenger stated that they had two PFD's in the boat but niether passenger nor operator A were wearing a PFD.  Passenger stated that when he returned to the scene after calling for help, he located one of the PFD's floating in the debris field and he picked that up along with the rest of the debris.  The other PFD was located in the boat at the time the boat was recovered.

Maine's Medical Examiner's Office has a blood sample from operator A/victim 1 and will test for chemicals including Alcohol.  Results pending.

Maine Warden Service searched the water the night of the accident until approximatley 12:00 am.  The search resumed the next morning (4-24-2012) with Maine Warden Service divers.  The body was located early in the search and recovered.  The boat was also recovered and remains in Warden Service custody until end of investigation.

The boat operator #1 did not notice the towboat and barges until it was too late to pick-up the victim, now in front of the tow's path. Watercraft #1 had no lights on boat when it collided with watercraft #2.  Operator of boat #1 was ejected from boat and body was later recovered in 20 feet of water. Mild damage to both boats.

A 31-year-old Leonard, MN father took his three young sons out in the early afternoon of April 6th to try out his sailboat. Around 3 pm the boat capsized and all four occupants were plunged into the 43-degree water. The boys and the father were all wearing lifejackets. The father tried hanging on to the boys for a time, but then decided to swim for help. It took him 15-20 minutes to reach shore. He was then finally able to flag down a car and the occupants called for help on their cell phone around 3:24 pm, and then drove him back to the access to await responders. Help arrived around 3:35pm, and they pulled the first boy out at 3:43 pm and the remaining two followed. All three boys, and eventually the father (who was also suffering from hypothermia), were taken to a local hospital. The two youngest boys, 2 and 6, were not able to be resuscitated. The 8-year-old boy, however, was able to be stabilized and then airlifted to a Minneapolis hospital. He was taken off the ventilator and was responding to questions, as of this summary. (PFD’s worn – Yes, by all on board)
