The Three individuals put in the Missouri above Black Eagle damn. They floated above the damn for a while then portaged around the damn then put in at the Black eagle damn island or memorial point. They put the canoe in the water and headed for the rapids.  At this point they did not think that the rapids looked all that bad and a few minutes later they hit the rapids by the first island as you head down river. 

When they got closer to the rapids they tried to turn the canoe toward the shore to avoid the rapids.  The water was very swift and the canoe was turned sideways and dragged them into the rapids which swamped the boat and ejected the occupants.
 
The current was very strong and all three of the men tried to swim to shore.  One subject wasn’t swimming very well and was not able to keep his head above water as well. The subjects were unable to swim to shore line of the river, so they swam to the island that was closer.  They were able to catch their footing just down from the island, and were both completely exhausted. The two looked around for the victim and saw him floating down river. he had missed the shallow water. The survivor explained that the victim did not look like he was fighting very hard at this point to keep his head above water and it was not very long before they could no longer see the victim.
 
The survivors went to the edge of the island to try to get help. After 45 minutes of waiting they were finally able to flag a car down and get them to call for help.  The subjects waited there on the island for approximately 20 to 25 minutes before game warden was able to locate them and pull them from the island.

It was found out later in my investigation that the victim could not swim. The truck that dropped them off at there launch point had three PFDs in the back, but for some reason they did not bring them along with them in the canoe
The SO report number for this case is 6815-10. The CFS on the river at the time of the accident was 19,800

On 09/04/2010 at approximately 1500 hours Warden and I responded to a possible drowning on the Missouri River in the area of 73 Tower Rock Road. Warden2 also responded and assisted with his jet boat. Warden1 and I arrived in the area of 73 Tower Rock Road and parked near the other emergency vehicles already on scene. Warden1 and I walked upriver from 73 Tower Rock Road on the North bank of the Missouri River until we reached the location of the emergency personnel on scene. At that time I observed a Merciflight helicopter on the island where the victim and other occupants of the capsized vessel had landed. I also observed a member of the flight crew performing CPR on victim1.

I made contact with the on-scene Cascade County Deputy. At that time Deputy had no further information to relay to me concerning the boating incident. Approximately 30 minutes after Warden1 and I arrived on scene Warden2 arrived in the area with his jet boat. It was around the same time that emergency personnel stopped CPR on the victim. 

Wardens and I began to shuttle the remaining occupants of the capsized raft from the island to the shore using the jet boat with the assistance of the other emergency responders. Paramedics then began to treat the remaining occupants for shock and hypothermia due to their prolonged exposure to the cool air after becoming soaked. Lastly, Wardens and I transported the victims body from the island to the shore. At some point during the shuttling from the island to the shore Deputy Coroner arrived on scene and began his initial examination of the body shortly thereafter. 

Warden2 and I transported the victim's raft from the island to the shore. After the decedent's raft was transported to the shore Warden1 and I began our examination of the vessel. See attached photos. The vessel involved was approximately 12 feet long and had the following serial number: BZA06736K495. The only other identifying marks on the vessel were the model (Momentum) and a number (A63) probably placed on the raft by the former owner of the vessel. It should be mentioned that the victims wife had mentioned during here interview with Deputy that she and her husband had recently purchased the vessel. No other information was provided as to where or who they purchased the raft from. The raft was transported to the Cascade Volunteer Fire Department and the decedent's wife was notified of the rafts location. 

During her interview the wife also stated that she, the deceased, and two friends had been floating the Missouri River. The four occupants of the raft had worn their PFDs during the majority of the trip but at some point they had stopped on an island to recreate. When the occupants of the raft left the island they did not put their PFDs back on. While they continued their float they were approaching the I-15 bridge near Hardy Creek when there vessel turned sideways and struck one of the bridge supports. Due to the fact the vessel was lodged against the support the buildup of current against the vessel caused the raft to capsize ejecting all four occupants.  Three people were able to grab onto the raft and float along side of it. The victim was unable to grab the raft and succumbed to drowning. It should be mentioned that Warden1 and I only observed two PFDs while on scene.

Warden1 and I cleared the area without further incident. Please see attached Cascade County Sheriff;s Office Coroner's report.

On May 16, 2011 at 7:45 PM, I State Game Warden received a phone call from State Game Warden in regards to a boat wreck on the Smith River.  Warden explained that two people in a boat on the Smith River wrecked and only one individual surfaced.  Warden and I agreed to meet at the Heaven and Earth ranch.  As I was responding I received a call from Captain who stated the following:
•     Accident occurred on the Smith River about 4 miles upstream from the Heaven and Earth Ranch.  
•     Two individuals were in the boat.
•     Meagher County was already responding 
•     Cascade County Search and rescue was on standby
•     Possibility of helicopter in the air.
•     Warden and Warden were to get interviews done on victims and witnesses.

On Thursday, June 23, 2011, at approximately 1115hrs, Operator of vessel 1, 41, of Southbury, Connecticut was operating a 14ft raft on the Big Hole River.  A second adult male was also on board.  The raft hit a submerged object and flipped over causing operator of vessel 1 and the second occupant to be ejected into the river.  The Big Hole River was running high and murky from snow run-off at a flow of approximately 7,300 cfs.  The operator of a second raft ahead of Operator of vessel 1, Witness 1, 39, of Sammamish, Washington and two other occupants in his boat ages 17 and 13, saw Operator of vessel 1 and his fellow occupant in the water. Witness 1 jumped into the river and assisted the second occupant in Vessel 1 to safety.  Witness 1was unable to assist operator of vessel1 also and last saw him floating down a straight section of the river on his back trying to backstroke his way to the west side of the Big Hole River. 

Approximately an hour later the Beaverhead County Sheriff''s Office was called to report the accident and search and rescue personnel, Sheriff''s Office personnel from Beaverhead County and Madison County and Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks officers responded.  

At approximately 1400hrs MFWP officers Wahl and Schmauch and one search and rescue boat launched at the Big Hole River Ranch and floated both the east and west sides of the river to Browne''s Bridge.  We were unable to locate operator of vessel1, but did come across his raft stuck upside down in a logjam.  The raft was flipped over and we observed 4 pfd''s in a bag in the boat and the oars were gone.  Borrowing extra oars, Vessel 1 was floated downstream to Browne''s Bridge.

A short time later a second search effort involved 4 boats from FWP, search and rescue and two other volunteers launching from the Big Hole River Ranch and floating both east and west sides of the river.  A jet boat arrived from Dillon and floated downstream from Melrose.  The search for Operator of vessel 1 was unsuccessful.

A second day of searching for Operator of vessel 1 on Friday, June 24, 2011 involved two search and rescue jet boats, two helicopters and a prop plane as well as searchers walking the shoreline downstream from the accident site. The search for Operator of vessel 1 was again unsuccessful and the river flow increased to over 8,000 cfs complicating efforts.  The search effort was called off  that evening due to poor and hazardous river conditions.

On Thursday, July 7, 2011 Operator of vessel 1 was found and recovered.

On July 5, 2011 I was dispatched to a person who was seen floating by 35701 9-mile prairie road.  The caller told dispatch that the person was wearing a blue life jacket and floating face down.  while en route, I was then told that a second caller was in the party who was floating in a raft when they lost one of the people overboard.
Missoula medical, care flight and the medical QRU unit are all responding.  As I approached the area of 9-mile prairie road I was notified by dispatch that the QRU unit found the deceased floating toward them about MM 5.5 of 9 mile prairie road.  As myself and the ambulance approached the scene, I was then advised they do have her and CPR is in progress.  On scene, the deceased and QRU medical were down a steep embankment, approximately 70 feet or more.  Fore on scene used a fire hose to tie off on the basket used to pull her and the rescue units up the hill.  Also on scene were several employees of the Paws Up Ranch who helped pull all up the embankment.
Once on the road, medical continued CPR on the female until transported by careflight to St. Pat''s ER.  Showing up on-scene was 3 of the friends who were in the raft with the female.  They were Occupant 1,2 and 3.  I had my digital audio recorder activated when I spoke first with Occupant 1.  She stated that they all were in the raft.  Occupant 4, the deceased''s daughter was in the rear of the raft and the deceased was in front of her.  Occupant 1 said they went through a deep rough rapid and the deceased and Occupant 4 were rolled out the rear of the raft.  She  saw the deceased floating facing down stream with her feet in front of her and the life jacket supporting her.  subject was able to swim to shore and they took the raft to shore to pick up Occupant 4.  After retrieving Occupant 4, the continued back down the river to find the deceased.  As they rounded a bend, they did not see her anymore so they went to shore.  Occupant 4 and her daughter, witness 1, then took off on foot down the shore to find the deceased.  The others went back to the car to drive down farther which is where they encountered myself and medical.  When I spoke with Occupant 2 and 3, they told me the same story as Occupant 1.  Careflight transported the deceased and as I was traveling back to Highway 200, Deputy encountered Occupant 4 and Witness 1 walking on the road.  He transported them to their vehicle at Johnsrud Park where they then left for St. Pat''s Hospital.  I was soon advised by dispatch that the coroner was needed at the E/R for the deceased. Nothing further at this time.  I collected the life jacket and put it into evidence as well as all my audio and digital recordings.

Victim was fishing with the boat Operator. the boat operator did not see what happened but heard a splash as they were fishing. When he turned to look at the source of the splash, he saw the victim surface in the water and gasping, taking in a large amount of water. The victim then went face down. On September 4, 2011, at approximately 1400 hours, Occcupant 1, Operator, Occupant 2, and victim left Country Club Shore Marina, sailing in occupant 1''s 29 foot sailboat.  They were going for an afternoon sail from the Marina in Polson north to Finley Point State Park, where they were going to have a picnic.

The wind was very calm.  The boat was traveling very slowly, and had only made it out to the middle of Polson Bay, approximately one mile from shore.  While on board, occupant 1 and the victim each drank one glass of wine.  Occupant 2 drank one beer, and the operator did not drink any alcohol.   At approximately 1640 hours, the victim decided to go for a swim, to cool off.    The sail of the boat was up, but the boat appeared not to be moving.  The victim jumped off the back of the boat without a PFD.  After a short time in the water the group realized that the boat was moving slowly.  The boat was drifting away from the victim.  The victim stated "The water is so cold, get me out of here!"  He began swimming back towards the boat.  When he realized that he was not getting any closer he began to yell for help and panic.  The other occupants began to throw a rescue throw-rope and a Type IV Throwable to the victim, but were unable to reach him.  He continued to panic and started going under water.  At approximately 1652 hours occupant 2 called 911 to request some help. The operator then started up the sailboats engine to turn the boat around to get back to the victims location.  By the time the boat was turned around and the victim was next to the boats port side, the victim was beginning to sink.  The operator jumped in and brought him back to the surface, but he was not breathing.  Occupant 1 and 2, who were still on board, attempted to pull the victim out of the water, but they did not have the strength to pull him over the high gunnel of the boat.  After a few attempts occupant 1 jumped into the water and the operator climbed back on board.  The operator attempted to pull the victim out, but also failed.  At approximately 1701 hours Polson EMS arrived by boat.  They pulled the victim out of the water, into the rescue boat and began CPR and transported him to St Joseph Medical Center in Polson.  The victim was pronounced dead at the hospital.

Officer responded to a boating accident/possible drowning on the North Fork of the Flathead River.  The reporting party who lives at that address.  The victim was in a ruddered, 17.5 foot, 2 person, FOLBot, with her husband the boats operator.  They had put in to the river at Polebridge at about 1115 hrs on Sept 21, 2011.  They were planning on taking their boat down the river to Big Creek.  Earlier they had positioned their vehicle at Big Creek with the assistance from an employee of the Polebridge store.

The  operator related that he and the victim were paddling downstream.  the victim was in the front of the boat and he was in the back.  Everything was going well until they got to the S bend in the river where the accident occurred.  the operator said they were talking their way around the corners, ("paddle left - Paddle right") and as they were into the second portion of the S bend the current took the bow of the boat into a root ball on the East side of the river.  As the bow make contact with the root ball the boat bent in the middle and both occupants went down into the water.  the operator stated he was pushed under and came out the other side.  He stated he made several attempts to get back to the root ball but could not due to the current.  At that time he did not see the victim or the boat.  the operator said he knew about where the road was on the west side of the river, so he swam across, bushwhacked to the North Fork road and flagged down a passing car.  Unknown who the driver of the passing car was,  however they took the information to the residence where they called dispatch.  The Operator remained on the road to mark the location until responders arrived.

The Victim's body and the boat were recovered about 2 hrs later by Under Sheriff  and other members of the swift water rescue team.  The body was taken to the Johnson Mortuary.  The operator was checked by EMS and found to be chilled but ok.  He stated he was familiar with the river and had floated it in previous years.  4 times in September conditions and 2 times in July conditions.
location: North Fork of the Flathead RIv, MT

description: On Thursday, July 28, 2011, three individuals were floating and fishing the Boulder River in a rubber raft.  The raft ended up coming down a channel of the Boulder that brought them directly into the path of several downed trees across the channel.  All three occupants were ejected as the raft flipped.  The two male occupants were not wearing their PFD''s and and were last seen by the female occupant somedistance downstream alongside the raft just downstream from the railroad trestle.  The female occupant was able to get to shore and contact two male individuals to ask for help.  The Sweet Grass County Sheriff''s office was notified and SAR members arrived on scene approximately 1 hour after the raft had capsized.  With the assistance of and airplane the body of the operator was located sverel miles downstream from the accident site in the Yellowstone River.  The body of victim 2 was not located that day.  On Friday, July 28, 2011, SAR members resumed searching both Yellowstone and Boulder Rivers with the assistance of aircraft again.  The body of victim 2 was recovered that afternoon hung up in a log jam near the mouth of the Boulder River as it enters the Yellowstone River.

On September 9, 2011 at approximately 11:35 p.m. three people departed the Lakeside Bar / Marina in a 19 foot, 1988 Ashariti motorboat.  Operator was operating the boat and headed in an easterly direction away from the Bar / Marina at ¾ to full throttle. Operator and occupants had all been consuming alcohol at the Lakeside Bar prior to leaving.  Operator operated the boat with navigation lights on and the bow spotlight on and pointed up in the air.  After a few minutes of traveling in the easterly direction, Operator moved the spotlight down and immediately illuminated the rocky cliff directly in front of him.  Operator made an evasive left hand turn but due to how close the boat was to the cliff along with the speed and forward momentum the boat collided with the cliff.  However, since Operator did make the evasive maneuver, the boat did not hit head-on with the cliff, rather it hit just off to the right side of the bow and since the boat was in a hard left turn, it was also canted hard to the left.  This caused the boat to ride up on the cliff, continuing its left turn direction.  The boat became airborne and continued with its momentum and left cant and plunged back into the water with a severe impact on the left front bow.  This caused all three occupants to be ejected out over the left bow area directly in the path of the boat.  When the occupants were ejected, the boat''s throttle was still in the ¾ to full operational position.  Since the occupants were ejected out in front of the boat as it plunged back into the water, and the boat was still moving, they were directly in line with the boat''s path.  The boat continued in its direction and ran over Operator.  Operator was impacted with the boat and the boat''s propeller which caused significant trauma and eventual death.  The boat continued on its path and then went into a right hand turn and began turning in tight concentric circles with no one on board.  The boat eventually re-impacted the cliff further to the north where it remained wedged and at ¾ to full throttle. Investigators were able to approach the boat via the FWP patrol boat, reach in and turn off the key.  The throttle was not touched and it was photographed in the same position. The three occupants were rescued by a nearby homeowner who took them to his residence and waited  for medical and law enforcement personnel to arrive.  The boat was recovered and impounded at the FWP Helena Area Resource Office where it was thoroughly photographed. There was a small perscription pill bottle recovered in the boat that contained what appeared to marijuana. The pill bottle was labeled as Prednisone for Operator.

On July 7, 2012, a boating accident occurred on the Clark Fork River in the Alberton Gorge whitewater section that resulted in the death of a man.  The following report was compiled by Warden from eye witnesses and people involved to include the passenger who was in the boat with the victim when the incident took place. The victim and passenger were floating the Alberton River Gorge on July 7th.  In addition to the raft the victim was floating in, the passenger also brought, and intermittently used a whitewater river kayak.  Witness 2, claimed that he had encountered the passenger and the victim at Sandy Beach Fishing Access Site earlier in the day.  Witness 2 said that the victim was switching his rower''s seat frame from a middle row position on the raft to a stern position.  The victim told witness 2 that he thought the new position might be better for the whitewater section, specifically Tumble Weed rapid, which is a class III/IV rapid.  Witness 2 said he thought that was an unusual position for a rower in whitewater without having at least two paddlers in the raft to help maneuver the boat.  Witness 2, having experience in white water situations, says that you lose much of your control over the raft in a stern rower''s seat, especially if you have not rowed from that position before.The victim and passenger continued downstream and began to enter Tumble Weed rapid.  At that point, the victim was rowing from the stern position and passenger was sitting in the bow of the boat.  They entered into Tumble Weed rapid river right.  This portion of the rapid is known to be the most difficult to maneuver.  At the time of entry into the rapid, photographs show that the passenger was wearing an approved Personal Floatation Device (PFD) and the victim was not wearing a PFD.  The victims raft entered the rapid bow first but then capsized on the starboard side.  Both the victim and passenger fell overboard along with dry boxes, The victims PFD and the passengers Kayak that was on the raft.  The raft corrected itself and came back down right side up. 

During an interview with the passenger, he claimed that he saw the victim moments after they were in the water.  He said that the victim looked very distraught and asked the passenger to throw him the bow line.  The passenger said that he tried to get the bow line to the victim but it was tied to the inside of the boat.  At that time he lost sight of the victim and did not see him again until later when he was brought to shore.  During the interview with the passenger, I asked if alcohol was involved and the passenger claimed that he and the victim may have had one 12 oz. beer a piece.

Photographs were taken of the incident by witness 1 owner and photographer of Montana River Photography.  Witness 1 photographs people going through Tumble Weed rapid and then offers them on his website.  Witness 1 photographs show the raft entering the rapid and the events that took place afterward.  The photograph of when the subjects fell over board was taken at 14:08, according to camera. Two of the photographs show victim just downstream from where he went overboard.  He was facing downstream and alert.  His PFD was in the water behind him approximately 20 yards.  Those were the last photographs taken of the incident in the water.  The victims position showed that he still had more white water to go through downstream before reaching calmer water.

Another witness that was actively involved in the rescue was Witness 3.  During an interview with Witness 3, he claimed that he was kayaking Surfer Joe rapid just below Tumble Weed rapid on river right.  He said that he saw an unmanned raft on river left and yelled out, “unmanned boat!”  Witness 3 said he then ferried across into the large eddy in the middle of the river where the water was flat.  He said he then saw a man, the victim, with his head just above water. ...

Victim stopped to assist other boaters.  Boaters unrelated to victim''s party.  Boaters raft was broached on private bridge pylon.  Victim manuvered kayak to raft and grabbed rope attached to raft.  Victim flipped kayak and was entangled in rope.  Boaters and observers pulled victim from water.  CPR initiated.  Ambulance transported victim to hospital.  Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful.

On january 16, 2010 at 4:30pm three vessels idled east out of the no wake zone at seine beach, located on the tar river near grimesland, nc.  After vessels cleared no wake zone, vessel number 2 throttled up and took off.  Vessel #1 throttled up and took off.  Vessel #3 throttled up and too off.  Vessel #1 overtook vessel #2.  As vessle #2 passed vessel #1, vessel #1 lost control and veered hard to the port (left) into the path of vessel #2.  Vessel #2 attempted a port maneuver to avoid collision.

Vessel #2 struck vessel #1 on the port(left) side at the windshield, vessel #2 ramped as both vessels rotated, vessel #2 entered vessel #1 app. 12 inches from the stern on the port causing severe hull damage from vessel #2 lower unit, travelled across the passenger area, craced the hull on the starboard side (right), bent the ignition key and choke throttle lever and exited vessel #1 on the starboard side (right).  Vessel #1 operator was killed on impact as the bottom of vessel #2's hull slide across the passenger area of vessel #1. Vessel #1 is a single seat mid performace vessel with a top speed of 78 mph.  Vessel #2 is an outboard recreational vessel with a top speed of 55 mph.  Vessel #3 is a high performace vessel with top speed over 100 mph.  Vessel #3 is included in this report as a witness of the above events and stated he had reached about 55 mph when he saw the incident happen.  The above statement is from operator of vessel #2.

I determined the damage on vessel #1 & #2 is consistent with witness statement.  As the rules of the road imply any vessel  under power overtake another vessel under power, the vessel overtaking must be the give way vessel and give ample room for the vessel being overtaken.  Therefore, i determine vessel #1 as being at fault.  The district attorney of pitt county agrees and no criminal charges will be filed.

ON SATURDAY FEBRUARY 6, 2010 AT ABOUT 12:30PM two subjects WERE KAYAKING DOWN THE SOUTH FORK RIVER IN GASTON COUNTY.  one operator STATED THAT THE WATER HAD A VERY SWIFT CURRENT WHICH CAUSED BOTH OF THE KAYAKS TO CAPSIZE.  the two operators WERE SEPARATED BY ABOUT 40 FEET.  one operator WAS ABLE TO PULL HIMSELF FROM THE WATER AND CALL FOR HELP.  surviving operator STATED THAT deceased WAS HOLDING ON TO A TREE AND MADE IT OUT OF THE WATER UNTIL THE LIMB HE WAS STANDING ON BROKE.  deceased HELD ON TO THE TREE UNTIL HE SUCCUMED TO THE ELEMENTS AND SLIPPED BACK INTO THE WATER AND DROWNED.  THE KAYAKS WERE NOT RECOVERED DURING THE RESCUE.

ON APRIL 10, 2010 AT 5:30PM FOUR MEN WENT FISHING ON THE ROANOKE RIVER.  THE BOAT WAS IN GOOD WORKING CONDITION WHEN THEY STARTED OUT GOING DOWN RIVER FROM THE WILLIAMSTON ACCESS AREA.  BEFORE STARTED OUT OCCUPANT2 HAD MADE A COMMENT TO OCCUPANT1 SAYING "HEAR MAN...HERE'S A LIFE JACKET" AND TOSSED HIM A LIFE JACKET.  OCCUPANT1 IN RETURN BRUSHED OFF THE COMMENT AND DID NOT PUT THE LIFE JACKET ON INSTEAD PUT IT ASIDE.  OPERATOR HAD OPERATED THE BOAT A MILE DOWN RIVER BEFORE THEY DECIDED TO START FISHING.  THE BOAT WAS TIED TO A LOW HANGING BRANCH BECAUSE THE CURRENT WAS TOO STRONG FOR THE ANCHOR THEY HAD BROUGHT WITH THEM.  OCCUPANT2 AND OCCUPANT3 HAD BROUGHT SOME BEER ALONG WITH THEM IN A SMALL BLUE COOLER WITH NO MORE THAN A SIX PACK IN IT.  WHEN FISHING THE MEN HAD CAUGHT TWO WHITE PERCH AND A CATFISH.  WHEN IT STARTED TO GET DARK THEY MADE THE DECISION TO RETURN TO THE ACCESS AREA BECAUSE THEY DIDN'T HAVE NAVIGATION LIGHTS ON THE BOAT.  FIRST THE BOAT WAS UNTIED FROM THE TREE.  THEN THE BOAT WAS STARTED, BUT THEY HAD ENGINE PROBLEMS AND THE MOTOR WOULD NOT GO FORWARD.  OPERATOR THEN TRIED TO PUT THE BOAT INTO REVERSE AND IT DID WORK, BUT THE STEERING CABLE HAD A MALFUNCTION AND THE BOAT WOULD NOT STEER.  THAT IS WHEN OCCUPANT2 WENT TO THE BACK OF THE BOAT AND TRIED TURNING THE BOAT MOTOR BY HAND.  THE BOAT DID TURN AND STARTED MOVING UP RiVER WITH THE STERN GOING UP RIVER AGAINST THE CURRENT.   WHEN THIS WAS DONE THE STRONG CURRENT AGAINST THE STERN FORCED WATER OVER THE TOP AND SANK THE BOAT WITHIN TEN TO TWENTY SECONDS.  THE FOUR MEN IN THE BOAT WERE NO WEARING LIFE JACKETS AND DIDN'T HAVE TIME TO PUT THEM ON BEFORE THE BOAT SANK.  ALL FOUR MEN JUMPED FROM THE BOAT INTO THE WATER AND STARTED SWIMMING FOR SHORE.  operator, OCCUPANT2, AND OCCUPANT3S ALL MADE IT TO SHORE ABOUT TWENTY FEET APART FROM EACH OTHER.  OCCUPANT1 DID NOT KNOW HOW TO SWIM AND WITH THE STRONG CURRENT ON THE ROANOKE RIVER THAT DAY DID NOT MAKE IT TO SHORE.  THE THREE MEN ON SHORE TRIED CALLING FOR OCCUPANT1, BUT DID NOT GET A RESPONSE.  IT WAS COMPLETELY DARK AT THIS TIME WHEN THE THREE SURVIVORS STARTED WALKING UP RIVER ON THE BERTIE COUNTY SIDE TO GET HELP.  THEY WALKED FOR AN HOUR TO AN HOUR AND A HALF BEFORE THEY WERE PICKED UP BY ANOTHER BOAT GOING UP RIVER.  THIS BOAT ALSO BROKE DOWN ON ITS WAY TO THE ACCESS AREA, BUT THEY WERE ABLE TO CALL MARTIN COUNTY FOR HELP AT 10:15PM. ANOTHER HOUR WENT BY BEFORE A WILDLIFE ENFORCEMENT OFFICER PICKED UP THE SURVIVORS AND BROUGHT THEM TO THE ACCESS AREA FOR MEDICAL TREATMENT.  WHEN I WAS TALKING WITH THEM I COULD SMELL AN ODOR OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE ABOUT THEIR PERSON.  I THEN RETURNED TO SEARCH THE ROANOKE RIVER FOR ANY SIGN OF OCCUPANT1.  WHEN THE SEARCH WAS OVER FOR THE NIGHT I RETURNED TO THE BOAT OPERATORS HOUSe.  I WAS ABLE TO INTERVIEW HIM BETTER AND DETERMINED THAT HE HAD NOT BEEN DRINKING THAT NIGHT WHEN HE WAS OPERATING THE BOAT.  THE ONLY TWO THAT HAD BEEN DRINKING THAT NIGHT WAS OCCUPANT2 AND OCCUPANT3.

On saturday april 3, 2010 at around 6:10 am, a morrow mtn state park employee approached the access area and heard someone calling for help out in the lake while holding a flash light.  The victim stated that he had fallen from his boat.  Employee went to the park office where ne notified another person.  Both individuals returned to the access area.  Other person was unable to get a signal on his cell phone and returned to the park office to call 911 while employee stayed and talked to the victim.  At around 6:30am, morrow mtn state park ranger was notified and patrolled to the access area where the state park boat was launched.  All three individuals searched in the dark for the victim in which they located face down in the water.  The victim was accidentally struck by the state park boat propeller while searching for the victim in the dark.  The victim was brought back to the access area where ems was standing by.  The 16 foot motoboat was discovered at around 9:00am on the montgomery county shoreline.  The boat appeared to have had enough momentum to get approximately eight feet up on the shore.  The navigational lights were still on, but weak due to battery loss.  No alcohol was found.  A type ii life jacket and a type iv throw cushion were found in the bow of the boat in a closed compartment.  The victim was not wearing a life saving device.  The kill switch was in place, but wrapped around the handle and a portion of the motor mount.  The throttle was found to have an approximate quarter turn.  It was later confirmed by the stanly county medical examiners office that the victim's cause of death was "immediate drowning".

OFFICER RECEIVED A REPORT OF A BOAT ACCIDENT THAT OCCURRED NEAR HATTERAS INLET ON MAY 1, 2010 AROUND 12:30PM.  OFFICER MADE CONTACT WITH THE USCG AND WAS TOLD THERE WERE 6 PEOPLE IN THE WATER AND ONE WAS DECEASED.  A PASSING BY CHARTER BOAT AND THE USCG ASSISTED WITH THE RECOVERY OF ALL PASSENGERS. officer INTERVIEWED THE OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1.  OPERATOR STATED THAT THEY WERE FISHING JUST OFF OF A SHOAL NEAR HATTERAS INLET WHEN THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED.  HE SAID THAT HE AND HIS 14 YEAR OLD SON WERE ON THE TOWER OF THE VESSEL WATCHING THE OTHER PASSENGERS REEL IN SEVERAL FISH.  HE NOTICED A WHITE WATER WAVE HEADING FOR THE SIDE OF HIS VESSEL, HE STATED HE KNEW THE BOAT COULD HANDLE IT, and WASN'T ALARMED.  THE WAVE HIT THE VESSEL AND THREW OPERATOR AND HIS SON OFF OF THE TOWER AND INTO THE WATER.  HE THEN STATED THE BOAT CAPSIZED AND THREW ALL PASSENGERS OUT EXCEPT FOR THE YOUNGEST CHILD.  OPERATOR RECOVERED LIFE VEST OUT OF THE BOAT AND SECURED THE ADULTS WITH VESTS.  occupant STATED THAT HE AND THE OTHER 3 ADULTS WERE IN THE WATER HOLDING ONTO THE BOAT AND THEY HAD PLACED THE CHILDREN ON THE BOW.  OCCUPANT STATED AFTER ABOUT AN HOUR WENT BY A WAVE HIT THE VESSEL AND THREW THE CHILDREN INTO THE WATER.  HE STATED THAT THE TWO UNDER 13 YEAR OLD CHILDREN WERE WEARING A LIVE VEST BEFORE THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED.  AT THIS POINT, OPERATOR STATED THAT HIS FATHER, WAS STARTING To PANIC.  HE MANAGED TO TAKE HIS LIFE VEST OFF AND PUT IT UNDER HIS FATHER'S LEGS TO GIVE HIM MORE FLOTATION.  HE ALSO STATED THAT one occupant HAD STARTED TO DRIFT AWAY WITH HIS SON.  OPERATOR THEN STARTED TO SWIM TO HIS SON and another occupant WHO WERE ALSO DRIFTING AWAY. HE STATED HE SWAM THEM BACK TO THE VESSEL AND NOTICED HIS FATHER LAYING FACE DOWN IN THE WATER.  HE SWAM TO HIM AND NOTICED THAT HE WAS ALMOST OUT OF HIS LIFE VEST.  HE TRIED TO HELP HIS FATHER, BUT THE CHILDREN HAD STARTED DRIFTING AWAY AGAIN.  OPERATOR TIED HIS FATHER TO THE BOW LINE SO HIS BODY WOULD NOT DRIFT AWAY.  HE STATED THAT HE THEN SWAM UNDER THE VESSEL AND RETRIEVED FLARES AND IGNITED THAM TO SIGNAL FOR HELP.  OPERATOR SAID THEY WERE IN THE WATER ABOUT 4 HOURS WHILE ALL THESE EVENTS OCCURRED.  SOON AFTER LIGHTING THE FLARES HE NOTICED A VESSEL HEADING BACK INTO THE INLET AND WERE SOON RESCUED.  occupant AND HIS SON WERE RESCUED ABOUT A MILE FROM WHERE THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED.  Three people WERE ALL TRANSPORTED TO THE OUTER BANKS HOSPITAL AND WERE TREATED FOR HYPOTHERMIA AND WERE SOON RELEASED. CURRITUCK COUNTY COMMUNICATIONS RECEIVED A CALL AT 1849 HOURS ON SUNDAY EVENING, JUNE 6TH, FROM a subject NEAR MOYOCK, REPORTING A VESSEL ADRIFT IN TULS BAY, NEAR THE MOUTH OF NORTHWEST RIVER.  THE CALLER ADVISED THAT HE COULD SEE THAT THE MOTOR WAS RUNNING, BUT HAD NOT SEEN ANYONE ON OR AROUND THE VESSEL.  SUBJECT THEN TOOK HIS VESSEL TO INVESTIGATE.  BY THE TIME HE ARRIVED AT THE VESSEL, IT HAD DRIFTED, BOW FIRST INTO THE MARSH NEAR THE MOUTH OF BACK LANDING CREEK IN TULLS BAY.  HE STATED THAT HE FOUND THE VESSEL UNOCCUPIED, WITH THE MOTOR IDLING IN NEUTRAL, AND TRIMMED DOWN.  HE ALSO REPORTED FINDING A DOG WATER BOWL IN THE STERN OF THE VESSEL.  SUBJECT REPORTED THAT HE TURNED THE ENGINE OFF AND TRIMMED THE MOTOR UP OUT OF THE WATER.  HE STATED THAT HE FOLLOWED THE APPARENT TRACK THAT THE VESSEL HAD DRIFTED ALONG AND FOUND A SMALL BLCK DOG BARKING ON THE SOUTH SHORE OF THE NORTHWEST RIVER, JUST UP FROM THE MOUTH OF THE RIVER.  SUBJECT THEN MET ME AND CURRITUCK COUNTY DEPUTY AT THE TULLS BAY MARINA AT APPROXIMATELY 1940 HOURS AND TOOK US TO WHERE THE VICTIM'S VESSEL WAS LOCATED.  

I FOUND THE VESSEL WITH THE ENGINE OFF AND TRIMMED UP.  THE INTERIOR WAS RELATIVELY CLEAN AND THERE WERE NO APPARENT INDICATIONS OF AN ONBOARD MISHAP.  THERE WAS AN OPEN BUDWEISER BEER BOTTLE IN A "COOZIE" ON THE DASH, APPROXIMATELY 1/4 FULL.  THERE WAS A LARGE (48-56 QT) COOLER LOCATED IN THE PORT STERN OF THE VESSEL WHICH HAD APPROXIMATELY 24 BEERS ICED DOWN INSIDE.  THERE WERE ALSO 3 EMPTY BEER BOTTLES IN THE PORT STERN COMPARTMENT JUST BEHIND THE COOLER.  THERE WAS A SILVER DIGITAL CAMERA ON THE CONSOLE, HOWEVER NONE OF THE PICTURES ON BOARD WERE FROM THAT DAY.  THERE WAS A WHITE TYPE IV PFD BETWEEN THE COOLER AND THE PORT GUNWALE OF THE VESSEL AND SEVERAL OTHER TYPE III PFD'S IN THE CENTER CONSOLE.  THERE WAS A DOG BOWL WHICH CONTAINED WATER IN THE STARBOARD AFT SECTION OF THE VESSEL. THERE WAS A GPS ON THE DASH OF THE CONSOLE WHICH SHOWED THE LAST TRACK OF THE VESSSEL COMING OUT OF THE NORTHWEST RIVER AND ENDING AT ITS CURRENT LOCATION.  

WE THEN LEFT THE VESSEL AND PROCEEDED ALONG THE ROUTE THAT THE GPS SHOWED THE VESSEL HAD TAKEN, TO WHERE SUBJECT FOUND THE DOG.  WE WERE ABLE TO CAPTURE THE SMALL BLACK PUG.  DEPUTY OF THE CURRITUCK COUNTY SHERIFFS OFFICE THEN OPERATED THE VICTIM'S VESSEL, UNDER ITS OWN POWER, TO TULLS BAY MARINA, WHERE IT WAS MOORED.  AFTER QUICKLY LOOKING THE VICTIMS VESSEL OVER ONCE MORE, AND INDING NO FURTHER CLUES AS TO WHAT MIGHT HAVE HAPPEDNED, I PROCEEDED BACK TO THE AREA WHERE THE DOG WAS LOCATED AND BEGAN TO SEARCH THE WATER AND SHORE LINE FOR THE VESSELS REGISTERED OWNER.  ASSISTED BY OFFICERS OF THE NC MARINE PATROL, A USCG HELICOPTER AND BOAT CREW, AND SEVERAL (APPROXIMATELY 5-7) PRIVATE CITIZENS VESSELS, I SEARCHED THE AREA AROUND THE MOUTH OF THE NORTHWEST RIVER.  SHORTLY AFTER BEGINNING THE SEARCH, A VESSEL APPROACHED WITH THE DAUGHTER OF THE MISSING BOATER, AND SHE VERIFIED THAT THE DOG WE LOCATED WAS HER FATHER'S.  SHE STATED THAT HER FATHER HAD CALLED HER BETWEEN 1730 AND 1800 HOURS AND TOLD HER HE WAS GOING OUT ON THE BOAT ALONE WITH THE DOG.  SHE ALSO  STATED THAT ALTHOUGH THE DOG DID NOT SWIM WELL, it NEVER JUMPED OUT OF THE BOAT but operator  WOULD OCCASIONALLY STOP THE BOAT AND DIP THE DOG IN THE WATER TO COOL IT OFF.  SHE STATED THAT HIS WIFE HAD SUFFERED A SEIZURE WHILE THEY WERE BOATING THE PREVIOUS DAY AND WAS TRAnSPORTED BY EMS TO THE HOSPITAL, WHERE SHE REMAINED AND WAS BEING TREATED FOR A POSSIBLE STROKE. Six subjects were on shearon harris res wakeboarding in no name creek.  All arrived at the lake around 12:15pm.  The subjects were taking turns wakeboarding throughout the afternoon.  This was the victim's last trip to the lake for the summer and she was trying to complete a jump from one wake and cross the other wake in the air.  She had no problems jumping one wake, but crossing the other had not been completed yet.  This was also her first summer wakeboarding and this jump was a goal she wanted to complete.

Through the afternoon all subjects had taken several turns wake boarding.  It was now victim's turn to go.  She had made several passes back and forth aacross the wake without incident.  On the last jump she crossed from left to right looking out the back of the boat.  Victim did not complete the jump and fell.  The boat slowed and pulled back around to pick up victim.  As the boat approached victim, subject asked if she was okay?  subject victim responded, "yeah, but that one hurt".  Subject reached for victim's hand to pull her to the boat.  Victim went unresponsive and subject asked what hurt?  Victim was unable to respond.  All subjects assisted getting victim into the boat.  911 was called on the way to the ramp.  Victim remained unresponsive during the wait for ems.  Upon arrival of ems, victim was rushed to duke.  On the trip, victim stopped breathing, so ems went to wake med hospital. There, surgery was performed and a hole was drilled in the skull to allow bleeding and swelling to escape.  The doctor spoke with the victim's mother while i was there.  The doctor stated this was very serious but if anyone could survive, someone her age could.  There was a great possibility of brain damage, also stated by the doctor.   Subject victim never recovered.  Two days later victim was placed on life support to allow for organ removal.  

While speaking with the witnesses, none said this fall was any harder than other falls.  It was stated the front edge of the wakeboard entered the water first and faceplanted her into the water.  Victim never tried to brace for the fall by placing her hands in front of her.  The left side of the head struck the water first causing the damage.

The operator had the vessel on cruise control and at a speed of 20 mph.  He was watching the jumps in the rear view mirror.  He stated, "this fall was no different than others taken during the day by all the wakeboarders."

Between 17:30 and 17:45 hrs on the 2nd of july 2010, witnesses reported they saw the deceased riding a pwc in the cobbs creek area of hyco lake without a pfd.  Around 18:00 hrs, one witness reported seeing the subject lying on his back on the pwc while drifting.  Later the pwc was found floating and a short time later the subject was located floating face down in the water, still in the cobbs creek area.  Witnesses transported the body and pwc to shore and called for help.  When i arrived, the deceased was lying on the edge of the shoreline.  His face very blue in color.  Ems arrived a short time later and confirmed the death.  Arrangements were made and the medical examiner arrived and transported the body to chapel hill for autopsy.

After reviewing the autopsy report, it was found that the subject revealed significant ischemic cardiovascular disease with coronary atherosclerosis and cardiomegaly, as well as steathohepatitis.  Toxicology studies revealed ethenol in aorta blood (150 mg/dl;0.15%).  Based on the findings the medical examiler stated acute ethanol intoxication and ischemic heart disease contributed to the death.

He was seen at carolina seafood washing his crab fishing boat on shore by owner of carolina seafood at around 10:00am.  He was later seen by another subject around 11:00am.  He was still on shore cleaning his crab boat.  The uscg received a call of a vessel going round and round in circles in muddy creek at around 12:45pm.  Once the coast guard was on scene, they were able to get one of their officers in the vessel and stop the vessel.  The vessel was nc 0817wn, a 21' southern skimmer that was registered to Operator.  There was an unidentified vessel that recovered a green tote with several type 1 pfds, 1 type 4pfd, and a fire extinguisher.  Operator's truck and trailer were unattended backed in the water at the boat ramp with the truck still running.  I was notified of possible boating accident at 2:42pm by raleigh communications.  Once i was at carolina seafood, i spoke with the son.  He informed me that his father had come there to wash his crab boat.  After washing it, he takes it out in muddy creek and circles around while pouring water in the boat to wash off any cleaner that might remain. Search for Operator was conducted by several agencies until 1:40am on 8/29/2010, at this time the search was called off and would resume at 7:00am. 

Operator was located at around 12:55pm by the owners of carolina seafood.  Operatorr's body was recovered when he surfaced.  Operator's body was recovered within yards of the location that the coast guard had stopped his vessel.  Operator's body was transported to beaufort county hospital by aurora rescue squad.

At approximately 17:45 on september 24, 2010, an 18' bombardier jet boat was on mountain island lake in gaston county near mount holly north carolina.  This vessel will be known as vessel 1.  Vessel 1 was occupied by three people.  Operator had invited two of his friends to come with him to mtn island lake to test drive his vessel that he had just retrieved from a boat maintenance facility where it was being worked on due to some mechanical problems.  Operator advised that he and his occupants had decided to stop the vessel to drift for a while and swim.  Operator and his occupants began to jump from the gunnel of vessel 1.  

The other surviving occupant advised that the deceased had jumped from the gunnel three times.  On the third jump, victim struggled slightly and then said, "help me".  Occupant advised he swam to victim and grabbed his arm in an attempt to keep his head above water.  According to Occupant, victim closed his eyes and went under.  Occupant attempted to pull him up again and was unsuccessful.  None of the three swimmers were wearing pfds.  The operator of vessel 1, operator swam to the vessel and threw two type iii pfds to Occupant.  Occupant retrieved the pfd and secured it properly to himself and swam back to vessel 1.  

Occupant then got the vessel's whistle and began blowing it trying to gain attention of a passing vessel.  The passing vessel stopped and began assisting vessel 1 in the search for victim.  The female passenger of the assisting vessel called 911.  The male operator of the assisting vessel and his five children secured type iii pfds and all jumped into the water and began swimming to search for the now missing victim.  At approximately 18:30 i was called to the now accident scene and began my interview of the occupant and operator of vessel 1.

On 3/11/11, at approximately 1:00pm, Operator and his two companions were operating the vessel heading back from a day of fishing on the cape fear river to the boat ramp located at the end of reigel course rd in columbus county.  According to the two companions, they had struck a log just a few minutes before arriving at the boat ramp.  They stated that the boat was operating as it should and showed no sign of any damage.  According to the two men, all three occupants had gotten off at the ramp and Operator retrieved his vehicle and backed his trailer into the water to load the vessel.  Operator then entered into the vessel alone and proceeded to maneuver it around in order to drive it onto the trailer.  The men stated that the first attempt to load the vessel was unsuccessful, so Operator backed the boat up off the trailer to try again.  It was at this time that the vessel lost power and began to rapidly take on water over the stern.  According to the two witnesses, Operator appeared to panic and proceeded to jump off the boat because he thought it was going to sink.  There were three pfds laid out in the vessel, but Operator jumped out before retrieving one.  

The witnesses stated that instead of trying to swim back to the boat, which was still semi afloat, Operator tried to swim to the shore against the slow moving current.  They stated that he quickly went down under the water, then surfaced, and went down a second time.  After the second submersion he was never seen again.  They called 911 and waited for assistance.  Upon arrival at the scene, emergency personnel quickly mobilized and began a search and rescue effort to recover the victim.  When the rescue divers located the victims body it was in 13 feet of water directly below where he had last been seen.  The vessel was retrieved and was towed to the shore.  It was overturned but still afloat.  Because of the weight and position of the vessel, it was necessary to have a wrecker come down and bring the boat out of the water.  

Because the wrecker did substantial damage to the hull of the vessel while loading it, it became very difficult to determine what damage had been done to the hull, if any, prior to the retrieval of it after the accident.  Based upon witness statements and the overall view of the vessel, it appears that the vessel had prior hull damage that had been allowing water to enter into the hull.  The vessel was also rated for a motor with a maximum horsepower of 75, but was in fact fitted with a 115 horsepower outboard.  The hull showed signs that it had been compromised prior to the sinking as well.  Inspection showed two locations where the hull had cracked severely and someone had used steel brackets which were bolted to the hull in an attempt to stop any further separation.  These two places were located at the stern near the gunwale.  It appears to this investigator that the hull probably was allowing water to enter, and that the motor was too large for the vessel, adding to the overall weight.  

The fact that witnesses claim to have struck a log minutes before the accident leads one to assume that they already compromised hull may have sustained further damage and thereby allowed more water to enter in than usual.  With the added water weight, the oversized motor, and the fact that the vessel would be sitting with the stern lower in the water anyway because of the angle of the boat ramp, it's  possible that when the victim backed up off the trailer, it may have caused water to rush over the stern, flood the boat and therefore cause it to begin sinking in the rapid manner in which witnesses described.  As stated before, because of the damage done to the hull while retrieving it, it is difficult to say for certain, but it is the opinion of this investigator that the facts mentioned earlier show that this is the most probable scenario.  No alcohol or drugs contributed to this accident.

Victim arrived at the lake wheeler boat house at 7:20am and was dropped off by a friend.  The boat was unloaded and launched by 7:40am.  The vessel was powered by a small electric trolling motor mounted to the stern of the 10 foot jon boat.  Another fisherman had seen victim on the south side of the lake heading toward the penny road bridge.  Due to windy conditions, i believe victim trolled to the south side of the lake to avoid some wind as he made his way to the penny road bridge.

Approximately one hour had passed and victim was seen on the boat close to the bridge by two passing motorists heading north on penny rd.  The same two motorists, approximately 15 minutes later,  were headed back south on penny road.  As they crossed the bridge, victim was not onboard the overturned boat.  They searched for victim for a few moments and then drove to the lake wheeler boat house to notify park officials.  Park officials called 911 for assistance and sent a boat to investigate.  Victim was not located at this time.

Search and rescue teams arrived and began their search.  I arrived and gave assistance until 2:30pm.  Victim's body was located approximately 45 yards from the bridge to the east at 3:00pm.  The body was sent to the medical examiner for determination of cause of death.

Preliminary investigation reveals vessel 1 was drifting at the time of the incident.  Two people occupied vessel 1, the victim and the witness.  Both the victim and witness were fishing at the time of the incident.

Witness claimed that the victim was complaining of stomach cramps earlier in the day.  Witness said that he heard the victim say "woo woo" just before falling into the water around 13:15 hours.  While the boat started to fill up with water, the witness jumped out of the boat and swam to the shore.  He then looked back and saw the victim swimming to the shore , but then went under the water.  The witness then tried to get help.  Three young boys attempted to locate the victim but were unsuccessful.  Search and rescue were dispatched to the scene but were also unsuccessful in locating the victim.  Divers found the victim around 1615 hours.

Further investigation reveals victim's feet were tangled in fishing line, weighed approximately 250 pounds, and had no pfd on.  Vessel 1 was very small in length and width.  Vessel 1 was very unstable on the water and would have been more unstable with the amount of weight that was on board at the time of the incident.  Vessel 1 had no maximum capacity plate.

In conclusion, vessel 1 should have been equipped with some type of pfd for each occupant, even though it is not required by law.  Having pfds on board would have given the victim an opportunity to rest with a pfd while trying to untangle the fishing line from his feet.

It is our opinion that while Operator and fiancee were fishing the boat was taking on water from the livewell pump. When they started to leave, Operator explained that they were traveling slow which would raise the bow of the boat and possibly allow some water to collect in the trough t the stern of the boat.  When Operator felt the engine hit the bottom, he trimmed the engine up which allowed the bow to raise more and the stern to lower closer to the water line.  When they noticed water at their feet, Operator made a left turn maneuver to get closer to shore and shut the engine off.  When the boat stopped, water rushed in from the stern and swamped the rear of the boat.  Operator explained that the water level had risen to the bottom of the steering wheel.  When Operator stood up to get the pfds from the front compartment, his movement to the port side of the boat where fiancee was sitting allowed water to shift to the port side.  His weight along with the shift of the water caused the boat  to roll and capsize.  Operator explained that his weight is 320 poun ds and fiancee’s weight is over 250 pounds.  The capacity plate attached to the boat is 5 persons or 635 pounds and a maximum of 1135 pounds people, engine, and gear. On 3/18/12 at approximately 11:00am, a fatal boating accident was discovered on lake norman near lake campus drive in mooresville by a mother and her son while kayaking in the area.  The vessel was a 21 foot 2008 chaparral cabin cruiser with an inboard-outdrive motor.  The boat had a starboard side console, and was owned and being operated by victim.  There were no other passengers aboard the vessel.  It appears that operator fell from his boat while fishing and struck his forehead rendering him unconscious which resulted in drowning.

Subject and her son were kayaking in the area when they saw something floating in the water approximately 20 yards from the shoreline.  They approached the unknown object and discovered the victim's body floating face down.  They did not have a cell phone and paddled into deeper water to wave down a passing boater for help.  Some unidentified recreational boaters on a pontoon boat called 911 at 11:47am.  The iredell county sheriff's office responded and with the assistance of a mount mourne first responder.  They were able to recover the body from the shoreline.  The victim had a small cut on the bridge of his nose between the eyes and his lips and cheeks were blue.  The medical examiner of piedmont pathology pronounced the victim's death on-site.

The motor was not running and the boat was drifting as the victim was apparently fishing from the stern.  Two fishing rods were located within the main passenger area of the boat along with minnow bait buckets and a small closed tackle box.  A lighter and electronic smoking device (used in smoking marijuana) was also found lying in the open floorboard of the boat.  The stern of the boat was a flat platform with no railing or gunwales.  A larger tackle box was standing closed on a rear seat on the starboard side that faced the platform area.  A large cooler was tied to the starboard side of the platform and contained one striped bass.  A beach towel was lying on the port side of the platform in front of a step that led into the passenger area of the boat, which could have caused his fall.  Another fishing rod was found floating in the water approximately 30 yards from where the victim's body was located.  The fishing line was stuck on the bottom of the lake.

During the autopsy at wake forest baptist medical center in winston salem, the medical examiner pointed out that the victim had a very distinct bruise on the skull plate.  The bruise appeared to be about 1 inch wide and approximately 4 inches long.  We are awaiting the official results of the autopsy along with a toxicology report from the chief medical examiner's office in chapel hill which would take 3 to 6 months.  (note:  an addendum will follow in the event that any new or pertinent information becomes available as a result of the chief medical examiner's report or the toxicology report.)

It appears as though the victim was fishing and possibly struggled to get his line unstuck from the bottom of the lake.  He apparently fell from the back of his boat and struck his forehead' rendering him unconscious which resulted in a drowning.  It could not be determined what caused him to fall or what his head struck.

At the time of the collision, all four subjects were wearing pfds.  According to witnesses, the daughter of Operator1 who was sitting behind her dad flew approximately 6 feet into the air.  The operator of vessel 1, Operator1 and daughter were not injured.  V2 son, who was sitting in front of his dad, Operator2 was not injured.  The operator of vessel 2 was severely injured by the collision.  Operator2 was pulled from the water. According to ems personnel, the victim sustained blunt force trauma to the back, a severe laceration across his back and internal bleeding.  Occupant on V1 was pulled from the water by her dad, Operator1 and transported to the west shore line.

Vessel 2 sustained fiberglass damage to the starboard side of the stern and broke the hand rail behind the seat on the stern.  The rear of the seat of vessel 2 sustained small tears.  The impact point on vessel 1 appeared to be approximately 8-10 inches below the bow eye on the keel.  Vessel 1 sustained cracked and broken fiberglass, scratches, and paint transfer along the keel extending approximately 35-40 inches back towards the stern from the point of impact.

Halifax dispatch received the boating accident call at 11:57am.  Ems arrived on the scene at 12:16pm.  I received the call from sgt at 12:35pm notifying me of the boating accident.  Operator2 was treated on the scene by ems personnel at 70 w drumgould st.  He was transported to halifax regional medical center where he died from his injuries at approximately 2:15pm.  V2 son was transported to halifax regional medical center where he was evaluated and released with no injuries.

The operator of vessel 1 was charged with reckless and negligent operation of a vessel.  The incident was not alcohol related.

At the time of this report, the medical examiner's report has not been reviewed.

Preliminary investigation revealed that the evening on june 26, 2012, victim's family called for help in locating the victim who had not returned home from fishing.  Victim had left home to go fishing at jordan farm pond around 1800 hrs.  The victim's vehicle was found at the dam of the pont and victim's vessel was found in the pond with water inside and a small anchor out in the water.  Vessel was located approximately 40 or 50 yards from the shore line.  Rescue and investigators search the surrounding area and the mud on the shoreline for victim and any foot prints or evidence that victim may have made it out of the water.  No evidence of foot prints on the shore were found and there was no sign of victim in the area surrounding the pond.

Rescue and recovery attempted to search the pond for victim during the night, but had to terminate the search due to extreme fog and uncontrollable conditions.  Search for victim resumed the following morning and lasted all day by a series of efforts which included numerous diving teams and multiple rescue personnel.

Further investigation showed that victim was a hard worker who worked third shift the night before and also worked on the farm after.  After working his two jobs back to back, he proceeded to jordan farm pond to go fishing in vessel 1 a red kayak.  He proceeded on the pond without a pfd.  Interviews from family member stated that the victim had not had the vessel very long, but he could swim.  Further investigation revealed that victim did not use any alcohol or drugs.  It was also noted that victim had a prescription for blood pressure medication but may have not taken it the day of the incident.

On june 28, 2012, at first light, victim was located floating in the pond approximately 30 feet from the vessel which was still anchored at the location in which it was found.  Victim was recovered from the pond and determined that there was nothing suspicious regarding the incident.

It is concluded that victim fell from the vessel.  The victim was not wearing any type of flotation device when located.  Medical examiner on the scene determined that the victim passed from either drowning or natural causes and one may have assisted the other.  The victim had little experience with the vessel and could have had a major factor in the cause of the incident due to the frequent tipping of a kayak type vessel.  If victim was wearing a pfd, then he may have been able to make it to land and may have survived this incident.  If natural causes were the primary cause of this incident, then the overall result of this incident may have had no change.

At 6:39pm on 8/19/2012, a call came into columbus county 911 in reference to a boat at lake waccamaw that was going around and around in circles with no one on board.  Emergency response teams located the vessel and began a search for the operator.  It was later determined that the owner of the boat had told his cousin and a friend that he was going fishing that evening.  A search of the owner's residence and his vehicle was in the yard.  Out on the lake, the search continued but was soon called off due to darkness.  It continued the next day at dawn.  The owner's body was located the next afternoon at approximately 6:50pm near the location the boat was first seen.  There were no apparent marks on the body of any trauma. Operator and victim put their canoe on the yadkin river at the hwy 77 bridge and proceeded to float down river to the confluence of the yadkin and mitchell rivers.  This stretch of river that they planned to float and fish is approximately 4.45 miles.  After floating the river and fishing for the first part of the day, Operator and victim stopped to have lunch on the riverside.   After lunch they proceeded to float downstream where they came to an island in the yadkin river that is approximately 0.48 miles from the confluence of the yadkin and mitchell rivers where they planned to end their float.  Operator said that they usually take the channel to the left of the island, but that victim made the decision to go to the right this time.  Operator sitting in the front seat of the canoe and victim sitting in the back seat of the canoe, they proceeded around the island.  As they went around the right side of the island, Operator saw a branch that struck out from a tree on the bank.  As they passed the branch, Operator said that he avoided it, however, victim grabbed the limb as he passed by it.  When victim grabbed the branch, the canoe came to an abrupt stop, which startled Operator.  Operator turned around to see what had happened and as he did this, the canoe started turning and flipped over.  Operator and victim both fell out into the water.  Operator was immediately able to grab the canoe, but he could see victim struggling to stay above the water out past the canoe.  Operator then managed to get the canoe flipped back over.  He then pushed the canoe out to victim.  Victim was then able to grab the canoe and hold on.  Operator then swam to shore and followed victim downstream along the shore.  Operator said that victim and he exchanged a few words and that victim just laid his head down on the canoe as it floated downstream.as Operator made his way down the riverbank, he lost sight of the canoe and victim for about 30 yards.  When the canoe and victim came back into view, victim was not holding on to the canoe.  Victim was then lying face down in the water.  Operator then ran through adjoining fields and woods to the closest road where he called out for help.  A female individual on a golf cart saw him and came to help.  She took him to a telephone to call 911.
 
Operator and victim did have pfds in the canoe.  However, they were using them to sit on and not wearing them.  Operator said that victim did not know how to swim.  There were also two coolers in the canoe (48 qt cooler and small soft cooler).  Operator and victim were life long friends and went to a local church together.

On november 16, 2012 at approximately 3:00pm, operator put his boat on at davis creek boat ramp in navassa and headed out to go fishing.  According to a witness who was operating another vessel on the creek that day, operator had been having motor trouble and the witness began towing him back to the boat ramp.  Operator was able to get his motor cranked and so he advised the witness that he was ok and he untied from the towing vessel and went back up the creek to go fishing.  The witness also headed out to go fishing and passed by operator who was tying his boat to a tree limb in preparation to begin fishing that spot.  The witness had been gone about 2 hours, and upon heading bck up davis creek to the ramp, he found operator slumped over the gunwale with his head and upper body underwater. operator was deceased.  The vessel was tied to an overhanging limb from the bow and the cover was off the motor as if operator had been working on it.  The witness called 911.  It is unclear what caused this accident.  It is my opinion that only an autopsy will be able to determine the exact cause of death.  It did not appear that the death was caused by any fault of the hull or the machinery of the vessel.  The brunswick county sheriffs office notified the next of kin.  Myself and sgt secured the vessel and stored it at the dot lot in belville for safe keeping.  The next of kin was made aware of the location of the vessel.  It is unclear based upon the investigation as to the exact cause of the accident that lead to operator's death.  Based upon information from the deceased father, operator had recently gotten out of a treatment facility for drug addiction but had been clean and doing well.  Perhaps there was an underlying and unknown medical condition or an adverse reaction to detox that could have lead to the death.  Based upon my investigation, the cause of death is something beyond the expertise of this investigator.  It is unclear until autopsy results are submitted as to whether or not alcohol or drugs played any part in this accident.

Preliminary investigation revealed that on the afternoon of august 22, 2012, a friend of operator/victim 1 called for assistance when she and operator/victim 1 was thrown off the vessel/pwc and went under water where operator/victim 1 never recovered to safety.
 
Through further investigation, two witnesses who had been on the lake fishing saw operator/victim 1 and his passenger speeding through a no wake zone proceeding from the main water of lake tillery to the lilly's bridge access area.  Witnesses stated that operator/victim 1 and his passenger were not wearing pfds.  The witnesses stated that operator/victim 1 started doing 360s in a rapid manner and jumping his own wake.  It was at this time that operator/victim 1 and his passenger were thrown from the pwc.  Another boater who was in the area saw the incident and went over to the passenger first and pulled her from the water.  Once the passenger was on board, both the boater and the passenger looked to the location where operator/victim 1 had been and saw that operator/victim 1 had gone under.  The boater and the passenger of the vessel/pwc looked for victim 1, but was unable to locate him.
 
At approximately 8:45pm, rescue and recovery attempts began for operator/victim 1.  After several hours of searching, rescue and recovery found the body at approximately 1:15am on august 23, 2012.
 
In conclusion, operator/victim 1 was not wearing a pfd which is required to ride/operate a pwc.  Operator/victim 1 and his passenger were thrown from the vessel/pwc while maneuvering the vessel/pwc in tight rapid circles.  In my opinion, if operator/victim 1 had been wearing his pfd, operator/victim 1 would have been kept above water long enough to be rescued or could have swam to shore.

The following is a description of a boating accident that occurred on February 26, 2010, at approximately 1540 hours.

The operator of Vessel I and two passengers entered the Exeter River in Vessel I, a canoe.  At the time, the river was flooded with a swift current and large sheets of ice were floating down the river.  Vessel I either struck or was struck by a sheet of ice, causing all three occupants to be ejected from the vessel into the water.  None of them were wearing PFDs, but all made it on to an ice flow. However, the ice flow then sank, putting all three people back into the water.  Two of them were able to make it back to shore, but the victim sank below the water and did not resurface.  Her body was found approximately 75 yards from her entry point to the river on March 1, 2010.

The following accident occurred on March 25, 2010 at approximately 1810 hours.  The Hanover Police Department received a call reporting an overturned kayak (Vessel 1) approximately 1.5 miles north of the Wilder Dam on the Connecticut River.  Officers recovered the vessel which contained a backpack with the victim's identification inside. A few witnesses reported having seen an overturned kayak at different locations throughout the day.  The current was strong due to recent heavy rains.  NH Marine Patrol was notified at approximately 2115 hours on the evening of the 25th.  The search for the body continued unsuccessfully on the 26th.  The body was found approximately two weeks later by NH Fish and Game.

The following accident occurred on May 7, 2010 at approximately 1400 hours.

The operator of vessel I was fishing in a canoe approximately 100 feet from shore, during windy weather and choppy water conditions.  The canoe capsized and the operator, who could not swim and was not wearing a PFD, struggled for a few minutes before disappearing beneath the water's surface.   The body was recovered by the NH Fish & Game Dive Team at approximately 1730 hours.

The following accident occurred on April 9, 2011, at approximately 1600 hours. 

The operator of Vessel I had apparently loaded up the vessel, a Hovercraft, with large amounts of food, clothing, supplies, and many pieces of US Mail, and was preparing to transport these items to his residence on an island.  Witnesses on shore saw the operator preparing to launch, heard the engine stop, and heard the operator cursing.  One witness stated that his tone of voice then became distressed, and when the witness looked up, the operator was in the water.  The witness called 911, and her husband waded into the water to help the operator. By the time the witness reached the victim, he was floating face-up in the water.  Emergency responders transported the victim to the local hospital; he was pronounced dead with the cause of death determined to be drowning.  Upon investigation, it was determined that the vessel was overloaded by at least 37 pounds according the the capacity plate.  The pull cord to the vessel's engine was broken, and the separated half of the cord was in the victim's hand when he was recovered.  When investigators replaced the recovered vessel into the water to check the stability, it began to take on water quickly and was removed for fear of sinking.

The following accident occurred on August 20, 2011 sometime after 2:00 AM. Around 2:00 AM, the operator decided to take his kayak onto Moose Brook in Hancock.  At approximately 9:45 AM, his wife reported him missing.  He was located in his capsized kayak shortly thereafter.  He was pronounced deceased by the Medical Examiner with the cause of death being accidental drowning.

On September 8, 2011 at approximately 1700 hours I received a phone call from my dispatch regarding a missing boater at South Fork Reservoir.  I responded to South Fork Reservoir and met up with deputies from the Elko County Sheriffs Office on Jet Ski Beach.  The information given to me at that time was that a male subject later identified as Victim had been fishing on his vessel bearing NV registration numbers (NV 1601 KM) with three juveniles, when one of the juveniles caught a fish and the fishing pole was pulled out of one of the juveniles hands and went into the water.  At this point it is unknown if Victim reached for the pole and fell overboard or went into the water voluntarily to retrieve the pole.  From secondhand information, it was relayed to me that Victim attempted to swim back to the vessel but due to significant winds, he was unable to reach the vessel and told the juveniles to call for help and he would swim to shore on the west side of the reservoir.   At approximately 1645 hours, a group that was fishing on shore heard yells of distress coming from the drifting vessel.  The group got the attention of another boater and responded to the drifting vessel to find three young juveniles onboard.  At approximately 1845 hours, I initiated a search of the water with my patrol vessel and an underwater camera, we did not locate anything of significance.  We searched until about 2100 hours that evening.
     On September 9, at approximately 0900 hours, I again entered the reservoir via patrol vessel and continued to search for the drowning victim utilizing a drag system with large gauge treble hooks and a triangle known as the Chisago County victim recovery drag system.  We were unable to locate the victim on this day as well and searched until approximately 2030 hours.  
     On September 10, 2011 at approximately 0723 hours, I was notified via cell phone that the drowning victim had been located floating in the reservoir.  The body was found by an Elko County Sheriff''s Deputy at approximately 0715 hours.  I arrived at approximately 0800 hours at South Fork Reservoir and assisted the Elko County Sheriff''s office with the recovery of the body.  The victim was not wearing any type of Personal Flotation Device, however it was noted during an inspection of the vessel that a type IV PFD was found under the driver''s seat.  Information was also relayed to me that all three juveniles were wearing PFDs when they were contacted by the other boater.
     On September 17, at approximately 1330 hours, I interviewed the three juveniles that were on board the vessel when the accident occurred.  All three juveniles stated that one juvenile had caught a fish and was reeling it in when the fish pulled the fishing pole out of his hand.  This juvenile was standing near the driver''s seat on the starboards side of the vessel.  As the pole went into the water, it was floating near the rear starboard side of the vessel and that is where the victim of the drowning attempted to reach into the water and retrieve the pole.  As the victim attempted to grab the pole he accidently fell overboard and attempted to swim back to the vessel.  The juveniles described the waves to me as being about 14 to 18 inches tall at the time the victim fell overboard and whitecapping.  The victim could not swim fast enough and yelled at the juveniles to call for help and he would swim to shore towards the west side of the reservoir.  The boat was not under power and drifting in a south southeasterly direction.  The juveniles stated they could still see the victim for about ten minutes in the water until the vessel drifted around some tules.  From cell phone pictures sent by the victim earlier in the day, I noticed all three juveniles were wearing their PFDs at the time the pictures were taken and they said they were all wearing them at the time of the accident.  No citations were issued in this case.

EMS personnel came in contact with the victim a 64 year old male who was unresponsive.  

Victim who sustained extensive injuries to his left side was transported via medical helicopter to Renown Hospital in Reno where he eventually succumbed to his injuries on December 2nd, 2011.  He had remained in a coma up to that point.
  
According to the victim''s wife and local property owner  (neither of which personally witnessed the accident) victim was slalom waterskiing behind a Mastercraft ski boat, NV0536KT, owned and operated  by the same person when he collided with a piling protruding from the surface of the water approximately 6 feet.  The piling is present to restrict boats from the U.S.F.S. public beach.

Despite the response of the Douglas County Sheriff''s Office, no report of the incident was filed at the time by the Sheriff''s Office, U.S. Coast Guard or the Nevada Department of Wildlife as none of these agencies were notified.
  
To this date I am awaiting statements from the operator of the boat and the observer present in the vessel that day.
