While falling, his foot became wedged into the vessels railing, leaving him hanging upside down, with his head in the water.  Unable to lift himself upright, he drowned while being dragged thorugh the water.  There were no witnesses to this incident.  Alcohol was not a factor in this accident.  The victim was not wearing a lifejacket.

The deceased took a paddleboard into the heavy surf of the Atlantic Ocean, and began paddling east.  A witness saw him fall off the board, but attempts to reach him were not successful.  Rescuers were unable to locate the deceased until several days later, about 7.5 miles east of where he entered the water.  He was not wearing a lifejacket, and alcohol was not a factor.

Operator of vessel 1 was running his vessel's small inboard gas engine while tied off to his mooring.  The vessel was sealed tightly against the cold.  Carbon monoxide gas began to leak into the cabin from the engine space, with nowhere to vent out of the vessel.  The deceased was overcome by the fumes, dying of accute carbon monoxide intoxication.  Alcohol was not a factor.

The deceased was a highly expereinced windsurfer, who decided to try sailing during the immediate aftermath of Tropical Storm Irene.  Winds were estimated at around 45 mph, with waves as high as 6-feet.  The victim entered the water, travelled approximately 300 yards, and disappeared from view.  He was later found detached from his sailboard about 1/4 mile north of his entry point.  He was not wearing a lifejacket, and alcohol was not a factor.
subject departed rowboat to attempt to swim 30 feet to shore.  He had been boating with companions and was not wearing a life jacket.  The body was recovered roughly one hour later.

At TOP vessel was anchored in Raritan Bay N/W of Ward Pt. Bend at day marker #52.  Victim B (Owner/operator) states while attempting to lift the anchor, waves came over his stern and swamped his boat, then capsized it.  Victim A was trapped under hull.  Victim B swam under hull and recovered victim A.  A passing boat pulled all victims from the water and brought them to Perth Amboy Marina.  Victom A was pronounced DOA at 2138 hours.  Port and starboard scuppers closed.

Patrols responded to a report of a capsized vessel in the area of Stony Point on Lake Ontario in the town of Henderson.  Operator reports that while trolling, a wave broke over the stern.  He attempted to bail it with a cooler but a second wave swamped the boat and engines.  Operator stayed with the boat and made it ashore, occupant went missing.  Search began for occupant on 4/21/12 and continued until his body was located on lake bed in approx. 40 ft of water in the vicinity of area in which the boat capsized approx. 150 ft from shoreline adjacent to wehle State Park.  Body was recovered on 4/28/12 at 1345 hours by divers in search.  Water temp: 47 degress.  Body taken for autopsy for cause of death.

While vessel #2 was at anchor, vessel #1 was driven into anchor line, hitting operator of vessel #1 along chest and shoulder area, throwing subject from the vessel.  Subjects from vessel #2 brought victim aboard and brought hin to the marina was resuce was waiting.  Mattituck FD rescure transported victim to Peconic Bay Medical center where he was pronounced dead on arrival.
Vessel #1 operator flipped over the kayak and the vessel sank.  Vessel #1 operator couldn't swim and drowned.  No life jacket used.

A call was received from the vessel Sacre Bleu over channel 16 reporting a person in the water in the vicinity of Valcour Island.  Passenger on boat stated that her husband went snorkeling and went to unfoul the anchor and hadn't returned.  A good samaritan diver retrieved the body and the coast guard began CPR.  Victim was transferred to EMS at the Peru Boat Launch and was then transported to the Champlain Valley Physicians Hospital.

Vessel was traveling in an easterly direction on Oneida Lake.  Operator did not see buoy marker 113 and struck the concrete support.  Vessel became airborne, rolled over, and hit the water in its top.  Vessel sunk with engine resting down.  All passengers were ejected, three drowned and one was rescued.  Vessel was traveling too fast for conditions; being darkness.  Alcohol was also a factor.  No one had on a life jacket.  Vessel is unregistered, had illegal mufflers and a modified air intake as well as "no backflame arrester".

State police reported troopers were called to the northern Oswego County town of Sandy Creek around 7:30pm following the report of a missing kayaker.  The local volunteer fire department launched its rescue boat and spotted people on shore who had located an empty kayak along the lakeshore 40 miles north of Syracuse.  Soon afterward, firefighters found a man floating in the water nearby.  He was taken by ambulance to Oswego Hospital where he was pronounced dead on arrival.  The medical examiner's report indicates that the victim suffered a heart attack prior to drowning.  The victim was morbidly obese and had a history of heart trouble.

Owner of vessel asked a friend to help him move his vessel from one slip to another.  At approximately 8:27am subject fell off the back of the boat and into the water.  He said he was not feeling well and asked to go home.  At 10:55am he stated he was not feeling well and for his wife to call 911.  subject was transported to Lawrence Hospital in Bronxville and died at 12:05pm.  Suspected death due to "secondary drowning".

Surviving passenger states deceased operator made a sharp turn on PWC which caused both riders to fall off.  Surviving passenger states she swam approximately 50 yards back to PWC and climbed on.  It was at that time she noticed the operator missing.

Vessel was traveling south near the east shore of Canandaigua Lake when the operator began heading easterly towards shore to visit with friends.  As operator began turning, her 3 year old son/passenger, seated in front of her, reached up and hit the accelerator.  Vessel accelerated abruptly until striking a concrete break wall and ejecting both riders.  The son died of trauma
Operator states that while out fishing a wave hit the vessel sending owner over the side.  Operator then lost sight of him.  Operator returned to marina and arrested for BUI.

Vessel #1 was traveling south east on Fishers Island Sound and failed to navigate properly through navigational aid subsequently striking a submerged rock.  Vessel #1 continued south east taking on water from stern.  Subsequently sinking and coming to a final rest in approximately 40 ft of water. Nine people on board were recovered by other vessels in the area and one person was reported missing.  The body of the missing passenger was found with the wreckage and cause of death was determined to be accidental drowning.

Operator of vessel experienced CO poisoning and fell into the water while returning from fishing.  Son did jump into water with extra PFD but was unable to get it to victim.  Victim recovered from water on 8/28/12 by search team.

The operator and two passengers had gone out of vessel#1. The operator had just picked up the boat a day or two prior from a marina that had been working on the boat repairing the motor.  They started out at 3pm and passed through lock 24 at about 3:30 pm.  The motor died at the lock but the operator was able to get it started again.  The operator decided to head to the marina that had done the repair work on the motor.  While on the way to the marina the motor died again.  While disabled and drifting a dog on board decided to jump out of the boat around 4:30 pm.  The dog was having trouble swimming getting caught the weeds.  A passenger jumped into the water to try and assist the dog.  She was not wearing a PFD and began to struggle in the weeds also.  The operator jumped into the water with a PFD in his hands to try and assist her back to the boat.  The operator gave the passenger the PFD and she was able to swim to a channel marker with the dog.  The operator succumbed to the weeds and drowned.  A significant number of empty beer cans were found in the vessel.  Autopsy report showed the operator had a significant amount of alcohol and cocaine in his system

Vessel 1, occupied by three were traveling south on the Hudson River east of the channel when the passenger in the vessel moved improperly causing the canoe to capsize.  Operator was able to swim to shore.  the two others were last seen holding onto the canoe drifting south with the current.
Operator was found floating near his boat.  Cause and contributing factors are not known.

MISLE report 599095 indicated that the victim jumped off the boat while it was enroute from City Island to Hart Island.  Alcohol use by occupants was noted. The victim reportedly did not swim.  The boat was recently purchased.

The Victim was found floating in the water near Vessel 1 and preliminary indications are that he fell from Vessel 1 into the water.  The Victim was not wearing a lifejacket and no lifejackets were found aboard Vessel 1.  There were no witnesses to the incident.  Autopsy results are being awaited from the coroner.

Both of the Victims were observed by Coast Guard Station Ashtabula personnel at approximately 8:00 a.m. on April 3, 2010 purchasing beer at a local Gas Mart (following the discovery of the Victims a receipt was found on one of the bodies indicating three "beers" - probably 12 packs - purchased for $31.00).  The Victims then apparently found a sailboat hull on the beach and used it without the permission of the owner.  Empty beer bottles and drag marks in the sand were found near where the hull was taken.  Vessel 1 was not outfitted with sails, a rudder, a tiller, or any safety equipment.  The Victims may have launched Vessel 1 while the weather was still warm and the water was still very calm; the Victims were wearing only T-shirts, shorts, and tennis shoes.  Winds began picking up strength at approximately 1400 hours from the south-southwest direction, pushing Vessel 1 out and around Ashtabula Harbor.  Later that night winds continued to rise and waves reached six feet in height offshore.  Temperaratures dropped down into the 50-degree range overnight and wind and waves continued; winds then shifted to the northwest pushing Vessel 1 to the east and to shore just west of Conneaut Harbor.  Vessel 1 was discovered at approximately 8:30 a.m. on April 4 by someone walking the beach.  The Victims were found braced against the inside of the hull in a back to back position.  Alcohol is suspected in the incident and a toxicology report is being awaited from the Cuyahoga County Coroner.

Vessel 1, with two persons on board, was being used to run trot lines when Vessel 1 capsized in high winds, putting both occupants into the water.  Both Occupants were able to swim to shore, but upon retrieval of Vessel 1 (which washed up to the shore following the incident), one of the Occupants collapsed.  Both Occupants were transported to the hospital where one Victim was treated and released and the second Victim was pronounced dead from what is presumed to have been a heart attack.

Officers and Investigators responded to a two boat accident at Alum Creek that occurred around 5:10 pm on Saturday. The collision occurred between the Cheshire ramp and the campground ramp in the open zone of the lake. Two people were on board each vessel at the time of the collision.  Vessel 1 was operating on plane heading east along the Cheshire Causeway.  Vessel 2 was also operating on plane heading west along the Cheshire Causeway.  Both vessels were in a head-on collision situation and failed to take evasive action in substantial time to avoid the collision, resulting in Vessel 1 impacting the port stern area of Vessel 2.  The Occupant of Vessel 1 was flown from the scene of the accident to OSU, the Operator of Vessel 1 was transported by Delaware EMS to Riverside; the Operator and Occupant of Vessel 2 refused treatment at the scene but later went to a local hospital where they were treated and released. The Occupant on Vessel 1 expired later in the evening on the day of the incident.

Vessel 1, with two persons on board, was travelling east across the lake at the time of the incident.  The estimated weight capacity for Vessel 1 (there was no capacity plate) was 275-320 pounds; the actual weight aboard Vessel 1 at the time of the incident was approximately 495 pounds.  This excess weight caused Vessel 1 to ride very low in the water with very little freeboard.  The Operator, riding in the stern of the vessel near the outboard motor, shifted his weight and/or stood in Vessel 1 causing the stern of Vessel 1 to drop down even further, allowing water to enter Vessel 1 over the transom.  As water entered in the stern area, the front of Vessel 1 raised up, rolling Vessel 1 over, and putting both Occupants in the water approximately 70 yards from shore.  The Operator was able to swim to shore, while the other Occupant/Victim disappeared below the water.  The Victim's body was later recovered 30 yards from shore.  Test results on the Operator indicate that he was under the influence of alcohol approximately 5 hours after the accident.

Vessel 1 was adrift with 9 persons on board.  The persons on board had been jet skiing, tubing, and swimming for approximately 5 hours when Occupant 2 and Occupant 4 jumped into the water (without lifejackets) for one last "cooling off".  Shortly thereafter, Occupant 4 began yelling for assistance; he was approximately 100-150 feet away from Vessel 1 and an approaching storm front had started generating 2-foot waves.  At this point Occupant 2 was nowhere in sight.  Occupant 3 then jumped into the water and swam to Occupant 4 (without a lifejacket); Occupant 3 then began pulling Occupant 4 back toward Vessel 1.  Occupant 8 and Occupant 9 put on lifejackets, grabbed two additional lifejackets, then jumped into the water to assist as well.  When Occupant 8 and Occupant 9 reached Occupant 3 and Occupant 4, they were able to get lifejackets on all parties.  Occupant 3 and Occupant 9 were then able to get back on board Vessel 1, while Occupant 4 and Occupant 8 drifted farther from Vessel 1.  Meanwhile, the Operator of Vessel 1 had contacted the United States Coast Guard who responded to the scene (along with another Multi-Agency Police Vessel).  The USCG pulled Occupant 4 and Occupant 8 from the water and a search was started for Occupant 2 within minutes of their arrival on scene.

The United States Coast Guard crew and the Police Boat crew both believed that all parties on Vessel 1 were under the influence of alchol.  The Operator of Vessel 1 was interviewed immediately after the incident at the United States Coast Guard Station; he refused to perform a sobriety test or submit to any chemical test.

The Victim (Occupant 2) was recovered in Euclid, Ohio on July 19, 2010.

Two Occupants launched Vessel 1 from shore Saturday evening (time unknown).  Occupant 1 entered the water from Vessel 1 to swim; shortly thereafter, the Operator entered the water from Vessel 1 to swim as well .  The distance both the Operator and the Occupant swam away from Vessel 1 is unknown.  The father of the Operator approached the area sometime later after hearing voices near the pond.  At this time, both the father of the Operator and Occupant 2 were unable to locate the Operator 1.  The father of the Operator then had the mother of the Operator contact 911.  

The Victim (Operator) was recovered by fire department personnel one hour after submersion; resuscitation was started and the Victim began breathing on his own at approximately 1:00 a.m.  The Victim was then transported to Metro Hospital via Life Flight; the Victim expired at 5:00 a.m. that same morning.

Occupant 2 was heavily under the effects of alcohol following the incident and had to be restrained by local PD.

Alcohol containers (both empty and full) were found aboard Vessel 1; no lifejackets or registration were found aboard Vessel 1.

Based on witness statements and evidence acquired at the scene of the incident, it appears that the Operator/Victim was preparing to go fishing at the time of the accident.  Witnesses came upon Vessel 1 at approximately 7:00 a.m. with its engine running; Vessel 1 was not tied to the dock at that time.  Assuming that the Operator was simply out of sight and preparing his fishing tackle, the Witness went about his business.  When the Witness observed Vessel 1 still running and untied from the dock, with no Operator around, at approximately 9:00 a.m. they contacted 911.  Emergency crews responded and divers recovered the body of the Operator/Victim at approximately 11:20 a.m. under the dock where Vessel 1 would have been tied.

Alcohol involvement is still being investigated.

The Operator (not wearing a lifejacket) and one additional Occupant (wearing a lifejacket) were in Vessel 1 when it capsized, putting both persons into the water.  The mother of Occupant 1 retrieved him from the water; the Operator had trouble swimming and did not make it to shore.

Alcohol involvement is being investigated in this accident.

Note that Operator Inexperience is listed as Primary Contributing Factor based on the fact that, despite a total boating experience of 100-500 hours, the Operator had very limited experience with this particular vessel (0 to 10 hours).

Vessel 1, with five persons on board, was stopped (but not anchored) to allow the Occupants to swim.  The Victim and one other Occupant entered the water from Vessel 1; the Victim never resurfaced.  The Victim was not wearing a lifejacket and alcohol is believed to be a contributing factor.

The Victim's body was recovered at 2:55 p.m. on July 21, 2010.

Awaiting full WICR from Investigator for additional details.

Vessel 1 was drifting approximately 1500 yards north of the Cleveland Breakwater near the Main Harbor entrance.  The Operator remained on board Vessel 1 while Occupant 1 left the vessel near the transom voluntarily to swim.  When Occupant 1 expressed difficulty to the Operator, the Operator started Vessel 1 and approached Occupant 1 to assist.  The Operator threw a rope several times to Occupant 1 with no success.  Wind and wave conditions continued to cause Vessel 1 to drift away from Occupant 1 and the Operator then saw Occupant 1's head go under the surface and not reappear.  Weather reports indicated 24-34 mph winds in the area during this time period and USCG personnel reported 2-3 foot waves in the area upon arrival.

The Victim (Occupant 1) was not wearing a lifejacket and the Victim had been consuming alcohol prior to the incident.

The body of the Victim was recovered on July 27, 2010 (pending positive identification) off of Edgewater State Park Marina.

The Operator of Vessel 1, with two additional persons on board, was forced to use its auxiliary engine due to choppy waters near Port Clinton.  The line from the jib sail then accidentally wrapped around the prop.  The Operator entered the water to attempt to cut the line, however Vessel 1 drifted away from him in the rough water.  The Occupants still aboard Vessel 1 did not know how to operate Vessel 1 and were unable to assist the Operator.  The Operator/Victim went under shortly thereafter and did not resurface.  A search for the Victim was unsuccessful.

The Victim's body was recovered on July 26, 2010.  Awaiting WICR report from Investigator (Ottawa County Sheriff's Office) for complete details.

The Victim and his family had been camping on a small island when a storm developed.  As the storm approached, everyone in the family travelled from the island to shore (by boat) where everyone except for the Victim left the area to return to their residence.  The Victim remained behind, indicating by cell phone to his wife (who was returning to their residence) that he would return to the island (via boat) to secure the remaining camping equipment and would expect the remainder of the family to come back to the island after the storm passed to have dinner.  Shortly thereafter (about five minutes later) the Victim's wife tried to contact the Victim again by cell phone but received no answer.  The Victim's wife then contacted emergency services who responded to the scene where Vessel 1 was found in the middle of the Portage River.  A search commenced for the Victim, who was recovered at approximately 10:30 a.m. on August 16, 2010.  During the search, an aluminum boarding ladder from Vessel 1 was found embedded in a muddy area near the area where the family had gained access to the island previously.  The Victim was not wearing any shoes, and had keys, a cell phone, and his wallet in his pocket at the time of recovery; with no witnesses to the incident this evidence leads to speculation that perhaps he was intending to wade into the water to launch or retrieve Vessel 1 (hence no shoes), but did not anticipate falling into the water (with his cell phone, wallet, and keys in his pocket).  The Victim was not wearing a life jacket.  The investigation of this incident is ongoing.

The Operator of Vessel 1 opened the hatch on Vessel 1 and ran the blowers at his personal dock for 15 minutes before driving to the fuel dock.  After arriving at the fuel dock, the Operator loaded approximately 22 gallons of gasoline and added 16 ounces of high octane STP additive.  Although the Operator did not open the engine hatch at the fuel dock, the Operator indicates that he did run the blower; witnesses reported that they never heard the blower running.  Following fueling, Vessel 1 left the dock.  Vessel 1 travelled approximately 20 feet and then stalled; as the Operator re-started the engine, an explosion occurred and a fire started at the front end of the engine.  Witnesses reported that the engine hatch was thrown approximately 50 feet up over Vessel 1 as a result of the explosion.  Dockhands and witnesses then entered the water and pulled Vessel 1 back to the dock; the Operator extinguished the flames using an on-board fire extinguisher and a larger extinguisher when Vessel 1 reached the dock.  The Operator received no injuries; the one additional Occupant on Vessel 1 suffered severe head injury to the top of his head (inspection of the cabin aft roof edge revealed an indentation approximately 3/4 inch deep into the fiberglass and metal band around the edge of the roof where the Victim's head struck the roof).  The Victim was transported to Magruder Hospital where he expired as a result of his injuries on September 5, 2010.  Investigation revealed indicators that prove that considerable fuel vapor accumulated under the deck of Vessel 1 as far forward as the Operator Station.  The explosion was caused when these fuel vapors were ignited by one of several possible sources including unshielded batteries, the blower motor, or the bilge pump (definitive source could  not be determined due to fire and explosion damage).

The Victim operated Vessel 1 out onto his private pond in order to retrieve a fishing lure.  The Victim leaned over the side of Vessel 1 to retrieve the lure, capsizing Vessel 1 and placing the Victim into the 50-degree water.  The Victim was recovered from the water and transported to the hospital where he remained in serious condition for several days.  The Victim then expired on November 13, 2010 as a result of the incident.  The Victim was not wearing a lifejacket at the time of the incident and no lifejackets were found aboard Vessel 1.

Vessel 1 left the west boat ramp and proceeded eastbound down the lake with the wind.  The Operator then turned Vessel 1 back into the wind to return to the ramp and subsequently began to take on water from the bow and the stern as a result of the wind and wave conditions.  At the time of the incident winds were reported from the west at 26+ mph and whitecaps were reported.  Occupant 3, who had been seated in the stern of Vessel 1, moved toward the bow of Vessel 1 to try to offset the waves coming over the bow, however the result was additional water coming over the bow.  Vessel 1 then swamped and capsized, placing all three Occupants (none of whom were wearing lifejackets) into the 48-degree water.  Two PFDs were onboard Vessel 1 at the time of the incident; per one of the Occupants, one PFD was blown away and the second was unable to be successfully donned by another Occupant.  The three Occupants then tried to swim Vessel 1 to shore (approximately 100 feet away).  Two of the Occupants made it successfully to shore while the third Occupant lost their grip on the vessel and went missing.  One of the Occupants who made it to shore was able to run approximately 1/2 mile to where their vehicle was parked and flag down a passersby for assistance.  The remaining Occupant who made it to shore later expired at the hospital at 12:38 a.m. on Monday April 18, 2011.  The missing Occupant was recovered on Monday April 18, 2011 at 1:38 p.m. and pronounced deceased.

Per Preliminary Incident Report dated June 22, 2011:

Victim was kayaking along shore, fell out and put lifejacket on. Was asked if he needed help from people onshore, and stated yes. Rescuer paddled out to help, and tried to assist. During this time, Victim became unconscious. Second rescuer swam out ~50-100 yards and helped pull victim into shore. Rescuer stated not breathing, and rescuers began CPR. Stated no pulse able to be found.  Neighbor ran to call 911 from house, and reported victim had drowned. EMS on scene shortly thereafter. EMS report stated possible Cardiac Arrest, no lung sounds, no pulse, Asystole and Pulseless Electrical Activity on heart monitor. Last update from Mentor Fire Dispatch was that Hospital ER had gotten a pulse back, and was inducing a hypothermic state for patient transfer to Cleveland Hospital.


Follow up from responding officer (June 23, 2011):

As of right now, I spoke with Mentor Fire Chief Harvey, and got an update on Victim's condition. Family consisting of two sisters, were notified already as of last night by Mentor PD. Both were spoken with at the hospital in Concord by Mentor FD. No names have been released, but a quick article detailing what took place was written for the News-Herald. (Attached article below) Victim is currently still alive but in an induced hypothermic coma. He is on a ventilator as he is still not breathing on his own but does have a pulse. He is currently under the care of doctors at Cleveland Clinic. Chief is planning on going up there today to check on his condition and prognosis. He will update me as he finds more out later today. Chief advised it may be 3-7 days before they try to take him off the ventilator. Will be sure to keep everyone advised of developments. Chief asked that he be notified if media or news contacts us before releasing any information, names, etc. He does not have a problem if we do, just wants to know if we do beforehand. I am still obtaining information from the witnesses/rescuers. Please call if you have any other questions or concerns.


Follow up from responding officer (June 24):

Victim expired.  Autopsy to be completed and preliminary results to be availble afternoon of June 24, 2011.

Vessel 1 was towing three passengers on a tube; one of the tubers subsequently fell from the tube and was having difficulty swimming back to Vessel 1 because of wave action on the lake (the tuber was wearing a personal flotation device).  The remaining passengers aboard Vessel 1 tried to assist the tuber back to Vessel 1, with two of the passengers entering the water to provide assistance.  The Operator of Vessel 1, who was a poor swimmer and was not wearing a personal flotation device, and who was still aboard Vessel 1 at this time, lost his balance (possibly due to a boat wake) and fell overboard.  One of the passengers already in the water tried to assist the Operator (Victim), but became too exhausted to assist.  The Operator (Victim) was unable to keep his face out of the water.  Another boat in the area assisted the Victim and one of the passengers in the water to board their vessel and transported them to shore where CPR was started on the Victim.  Both the Victim and the passenger were then life flighted to a nearby hospital for care.

The Operator (Victim) was pronounced deceased at 12:45 a.m. on July 3, 2011 as a result of the incident.  

The assisting passenger was initially treated and released, but was later re-admitted to the hospital for kidney failure as a result of the near drowning he sustained.  He has since recovered.

Vessel 1 was found unoccupied and drifted onto shore in the north bay of Kelleys Island.  Shortly thereafter the Victim (the Operator) was found deceased and floating on the east side of Kelleys Island.  There were no witnesses to the events leading up to the demise of the Victim.  Follow-up on phone calls from the Victim's cell phone in the period preceding the discovery of the vessel and the deceased indicated that the last call the deceased made was to a friend to say that the Victim was on his way to a marina on the south side of Kelleys Island when his rudder broke and he had lost steering.  The Victim reported his location at that time as the east side of Kelleys Island.  The friend had asked if the Victim needed assistance, but the deceased had indicated that he had a ship to shore radio to call for assistance.  When the friend called back approximately one hour after their last conversation, the Victim did not answer.

Investigation revealed that the rudder on Vessel 1 was gone at the time of discovery; the Victim was found in swim trunks.  Preliminary results of an autopsy revealed no head trauma to the Victim and his death was ruled as an accidental drowning. 

Investigation continues on this incident, but foul play is not suspected at this time.

Vessel 1, with three persons associated with the vessel (two on board and one in the water), was anchored in the "Party Cove" area of Chippewa Lake.  The two Occupants on board Vessel 1 noticed another person (the Victim) in the water nearby and having trouble standing.  The Victim was invited onto Vessel 1 for his own safety and in order to provide him with a ride to shore.  The Victim successfully climbed the ladder into Vessel 1, however, once on board Vessel 1 he swayed, loosing his balance.  The Victim grabbed onto the roof support, slipped, then grabbed the rails for the slide on the port bow; the port rail on the slide failed and the Victim subsequently fell, striking his head on the deck.  One of the Occupants on board Vessel 1 then called for the third Occupant (in the water) who in turn reboarded Vessel 1, pulled anchor, and drove Vessel 1 to the dock.  The Occupants called 911 while en route to the dock and were met by an ambulance which transported the Victim to the community hospital for care.  The Victim was subsequently flown to Akron General Hospital for treatment of a subdural hematoma.  The Victim's BAC level upon arrival at Akron General was .369.  The Victim was treated and released and charges were filed for disorderly conduct on the Victim. 

On July 20, 2011 Watercraft was notified that the Victim had been flown again for treatment and later passed away.  The Medical Examiner ruled the Victim's death as complications of subdermal hematoma as a result of the fall on Vessel 1.

On July 6 at approximately 2100 hours, the Operator of Vessel 1 contacted his wife to notify her that he was going night fishing on the Ohio River.  At 0300 hours on July 7, workers from the Meldahl Dam on the Ohio River reported Vessel 1 floating in the area with no one on board.  Authorities were contacted and responded to the scene; subsequent investigation revealed that the truck and trailer associated with Vessel 1 were upriver approximately 2.5 miles at the Chilo Lock 34 Boat Ramp.  The truck was found to still be running, with the headlights on, and the trailer was in the water at the ramp.  A search commenced for the Operator who was found at 1:42 p.m. on July 7 approximately 20 feet from the launch ramp in 15 feet of water.  There were no witnesses to the incident, but it is supected that the Victim was in the process of launching and/or tying off the vessel at the courtesy dock when the accident occured.  The events leading up to the Victim falling into the water are unknown; open beer containers were found in the truck.  The Victim was not wearing a personal flotation device (PFD) at the time his body was recovered, however, personal flotation devices were found on board Vessel 1.

The Operator/Victim of Vessel 1 was reported to have been consuming alcohol with friends prior to arriving at Moose Island on the Tuscarawas River for a concert later in the evening.  The Victim had left his vehicle at a boat ramp downriver from the island earlier in the day and had received transport for himself and Vessel 1 to Moose Island.  The Victim reportedly continued to consume alcohol throughout the evening.  At approximately 12:45 a.m. the Victim decided to paddle dow river to the launch ramp where his vehicle was located to head home.  The Victim was last seen walking Vessel 1 in the shallow part of the river as it was too shallow to paddle where he had put in.  The Victim was reported missing the following morning at 11:41 a.m. and Vessel 1 was found 100 yards downstream from the last seen location of the Victim.  The Victim was recovered at 3:28 p.m. approximately 200 feet upstream of where Vessel 1 was located in 6 feet of water.  An autopsy is pending.

The Victim was sitting on the top of the transom of Vessel 1 while the operator was making several turns.  The male passenger subsequently fell off the back of Vessel 1.  At the same time, another passenger aboard Vessel 1 fell inside the vessel, suffering a cut on her head.  The Operator of Vessel 1 stopped Vessel 1, and another passenger reported seeing the male in the water swimming.  This passenger turned away, put on a PFD and untied a fender to throw to the Victim; when she turned back, the Victim was no longer in sight.  The United States Coast Guard arrived on scene shortly thereafter, transported the injured passenger to shore, and started a search for the missing male.  On July 19 at approximately 12 noon, the body of the Victim was pulled from the Maumee River near Cullen Park in Point Place.  Positive identification of the Victim was made by the Lucas County Coroner's Office; cause of death was ruled as drowning and toxicology reports are pending.

Vessel 1 with three persons on board was headed toward Ballast Island at approximately 30 knots.  The Operator of Vessel 1 was looking at the wrong green navigation aid and subsequently struck a steel wall, ejecting one passenger and the Operator.  The ejected passenger struck her head and was pronounced dead at the scene from major head trauma.  The Operator suffered a compound fracture on his left leg and a broken arm.  The third party aboard Vessel 1 was not ejected, but did suffer a broken arm and a head laceration.

The Victim took Vessel 1 out onto Lake Erie, leaving a note for his parents that he was doing so and taking the family dog with him.  The Victim took a PFD for the dog, but none for himself.  Approximately one half hour later, the Victim was last seen on Vessel 1 slightly offshore.  Approximately 2 hours after the Victim was last seen, the dog returned to the Victim's residence, still wearing its PFD.  The father of the Victim was not surprised that the dog returned without the Victim as the Victim had a pattern of stopping off to attend parties in the area after boating.  The mother of the Victim reported that the last time the Victim had taken Vessel 1 out with the dog they had capsized.  Approximately two hours after the dog returned home, a local resident found a kayak, paddle, and one sandal washed up along the shoreline.  Vessel 1 was also found  floating close to shore and pulled it up onto the beach (it was found right side up).

The following day the Victim's mother (who did not know the dog had retrned home alone until the next day) went looking for Vessel 1 and met the local residents who had found Vessel 1 and the associated items.  Later that day the Victim's mother contacted the police department to report the Victim missing.  She reported that she waited on making the report to make sure he had just not come home as she didn't want to trouble anyone for no reason.

The Victim was found along the shoreline on August 29, 2011 by a local resident.  The medical examiner reported his cause of death as drowning, accidental, and his BAC was found to be 0.292 with a positive test for amphetamine.  It is unknown how the Victim entered the water as there were no witnesses to the incident.

Vessel 1 ran into the Cedar Point breakwall.  There were no witnesses to the incident and no survivors on board Vessel 1 following the incident.  Onc Victim was found inside of Vessel 1 and the second Victim (assumed to have been ejected as a result of the collision) remains missing.

This incident remains under investigation.

The Operator of Vessel 1 was last seen leaving the yacht club with no one else on board Vesel 1.  The weather at the time was poor.  The Operator was reported missing by his wife later that evening, with the Coast Guard locating Vessel 1 the following morning.  Upon boarding Vessel 1, no one was found on board; waves that morning were at 6-10 feet.  Vessel 1 was seemingly intact upon discovery and was started and operated back to its dock at the yacht club.

Indications were that the Victim had left Vessel 1 voluntarily (back flap open and no signs of struggle), however there were no witnesses. 

The Victim was located in Rondeau, Ontario, Canada on November 13, 2011.  Preliminary autopsy results showed the cause of death as drowning, with no signs of trauma.

Autopsy results are pending and may not be received for 6-9 months due to backlog.

The Victim fell overboard from Vessel 1 while trying to place a lifejacket on a duck hunter's dog.  The Victim was not wearing a PFD at the time of the incident.  No one was in the immediate area at the time of the accident.  The Victim struggled for 1-2 minutes in the water before submerging.

The Victim was later recovered with the use of side-scan sonar.

This incident remains under investigation.

Vessel 1, with two persons on board, was being operated near Cranetown Island when waves began to crash into Vessel 1, eventually swamping and then capsizing Vessel 1.  Both Occupants aboard Vessel 1 ended up in the water and subsequently tried to stay with Vessel 1; Vessel 1 then submerged until only the bow was visible above the surface of the water.  Both Occupants then attempted to swim approximately 70 yards to shore; one Occupant was successful in reaching the shore and the other Occupant swam approximately 25-30 yards before disappearing below the surface of the water.  Vessel 1 did not suffer any damage as a result of the incident.

Neither Occupant twas wearing a personal flotation device at the time of the incident and no personal flotation devices were found aboard Vessel 1 at the time of the incident.

The Victim was recovered and pronounced deceased at Mary Rutan Hospital.

A witness to the incident observed the Victim standing on the front of Vessel 1 fishing.  The witness looked away and a short time later the same witness heard a "splash" and looked over to see the Victim struggling in the water.  The Victim was not wearing a lifejacket at the time, and by the time the witness got to the Victim the Victim was face-down on the surface of the water and unresponsive.  The witness tried unsuccessfully to pull the Victim onto his vessel at which time the witness entered the water and swam the Victim to the nearest shore and began performing CPR.  The witness called to another person on shore to call 911.  Emergency services arrived on scene shortly thereafter; they were unable to resuscitate the Victim and he was pronounced deceased.  

Investigation revealed that the Victim did not know how to swim and suffered from a history of "dizzy spells".

Preliminary coroner report ruled the official cause of death as drowning; additional coroner details are expected in the future regarding other possible factors (medical conditions, BAC, etc.).  Investigation continues at this time.

The Operator/Victim and a second Occupant were travelling downriver in Vessel 1 when the Victim jumped/dove out of Vessel 1 to swim, in the process striking his head on the bottom of the river.  The Victim lost consciousness as a result of the incident and was pulled to shore by the other Occupant aboard Vessel 1.  The Victim awoke with no feeling from the waist down and was life-flighted for additional care.  The Victim suffered a broken neck with a good prognosis following anticipated surgery.  Investigation revealed no indication of drug or alcohol involvement in the incident.  The Victim was not wearing a lifejacket at the time of the incident.

On June 5, 2012, the Victim was reported as deceased based on complications of the spinal injury (development of rhabdomyeltis and tissue loss) as a result of the incident.

Based on witness statements and evidence, the Victim launched Vessel 1 to go fishing.  Witness said Victim had difficulty rowing.  Victim rowed out of sight of the witness.  A short time later, another witness saw the Victim in the water trying to get back into Vessel 1.  Victim 1 indicated that he needed help; the witness called 911. Shortly thereafter the witness lost sight of the Victim.  When the police arrived, they located the Victim floating on his back.  A police Officer swam to the Victim and brought him back to shore.  Emergency Services transported the Victim to the hospital where he was pronounced deceased.
 
Investigation revealed that the capacity plate on Vessel 1 indicated a maximum capacity of 2 persons at 150 pounds; the Victim weighed 319 pounds.

Vessel 1 was approximately 20 yards out from the Riverside Launch Ramp approaching the dock and waiting for another vessel at that location to launch.  Vessel 2 was running on plane approximately 20 yards out parallel to the shoreline and starboard to Vessel 1 when Vessel 2 impacted Vessel 1.  The bow of Vessel 2 went over the top of Vessel 1, striking the Operator of Vessel 1 in the head.  Vessel 2 continued to travel over the top of Vessel 1, exiting the stern area of Vessel 1 at an approximately 45-degree angle.  Two of the Occupants aboard Vessel 1 suffered injuries, with the Operator of Vessel 1 later succumbing to his injuries resulting in his death two days after the incident.  The Operator of Vessel 2 left the scene following the incident.  None of the parties aboard Vessel 2 suffered injury.  Both vessels involved suffered damage.
 
Determination of charges will not be available until after a Grand Jury trial in 2013; damages on vessels are estimates as well until the case has been heard/settled.

Based on witness statements and evidence, on 06/19/2012 at approximately 1430, victim #1 went out on vessel #1 to cool off. Late afternoon a witness reported vessel #1 was drifting close to shore by their residence and no one was on board. Officers checked the owners residence and found that victim#1 was to be out on Vessel #1. A search was conducted without results. On 06/20/2012 the search resumed and at approximately 1426, victim #1 was located. Victim #1 was tranported to Coldwater Hospital by Celina EMS and pronounced dead.

Victim (Occupant 2) left an unanchored vessel (Vessel 1) to swim without wearing a personal flotation device. Rescue attempts by owner/ operator failed. Victim went missing presumed drown. Victim was recovered approx. 2 hrs. 50 min. later by fire dept. personell. County Coroner ruled accidental death by drowning.

Vessel 1 was anchored in the boat overnight camp area approximately 20 yards from shore with two persons on board.  The Operator went below deck to sleep at approximately 9:30 p.m.; the Occupant remained above deck drinking alcohol and listening to music.  At approximately 7:30 a.m. the following morning the Operator came back above deck to find the Occupant missing; the Operator yelled for the Victim, looked in the water, and called the Victim's cell phone with no success.  The Operator then observed that Vessel 1 had drifted approximately 100 yards from where it had been anchored on the previous evening.  The Operator pulled anchor and returned to the orignal anchor site and upon arrival observed the Victim floating facedown in the water at the surface.  The Operator turned off the motor on Vessel 1 and jumped in the water, retrieving the Victim back to Vessel 1.  Another boater in the area assisted with bringing the Victim's body back aboard Vessel 1 where the Operator tried performing CPR for approximately 40 seconds while the other boater contacted 911.  Authorities arrived on scene at which time the Victim was pronounced dead and transported.  Investigation into the incident revealed no indication of foul play; it is suspected that the Victim fell overboard on the night of the incident, possibly due to being under the influence of alcohol

Occupants capsized vessel #1 late at night dressed in winter coats. One occupant made it to shore to summon help. One occupant was rescued by a local resident in a personal boat. The third occupant was found approximately three hours later by fire dept. divers deceased by drowning. No personal flotation devices were present. Alcohol was located at the scene.

Operator and method of operation unclear at this time. Investigation pending. 
Coroner findings and toxicology pending.

Vessel 1 was launched with three persons on board.  It was reported that the plug had been pulled on Vessel 1 prior to launching and the Owner had replaced the plug after Vessel 1 had drained.  At the time of launch there were three persons on board (combined weight of approximately 705-715 pounds) along with 7-8 dozen duck decoys, two dozen goose decoys, three shotguns, 6 gallons of gasoline, three hunting bags, food, and a blind for the vessel.  Vessel 1 headed north after launch and the Operator reported that there was no water entering Vessel 1 at that time.  Upon arriving at the area where they wanted to hunt they turned Vessel 1 west to approach the shore; at this time they saw the lights on shore from other hunters in the area and turned south, at this point stopping to determine where they wanted to go.  At this time, one of the Occupants (sitting in the bottom of the vessel) stated that he felt water in Vessel 1.  A second Occupant then observed water coming over the bow of Vessel 1.  Within ten seconds Vessel 1 went vertical and submerged, putting all three Occupants into the water.  The Operator was able to grab two goose decoys and a paddle; one Occupant was able to grab a bag of duck decoys; and the third Occupant held onto a type 2 PFD.  The three could reportedly hear each other in the darkness but could not see each other.  They began to yell to each other and for help.  Approximately 10-15 minutes later one of the Occupants reported hearing a  strange "gurgling noise" and thereafter heard nothing else from the Victim.  Approximately 50 minutes later a fire department vessel arrived on scene and rescued the two surviving Occupants; the Victim's body was found later that day along the eastern shoreline of the lake.  
 
Investigation revealed that the boat plug was in place and working effectively to keep water from the interior of Vessel 1.  There was no capacity plate located on Vessel 1.  The bow and stern seats had been modified and the flotation under them had been removed.  The red and green bow light and white all-around light were found still in their storage mounts behind the stern seat.,

Operator and passenger were fishing on a private pond.  Operator stood up and lost balance, then fell in the water.  Operator was not wearing a life jacket.  He resurfaced once, he could not swim.  He went under before he could be rescued.  No life jackets on board vessel.

Victim and passengers were floating in the lake fishing, when the victim fell head-first off the back of Vessel 1 into the water and did not resurface.  The other subjects on the vessel then jumped into the lake and began to search for the victim.  After approximately 3-5 minutes, the subjects located the victim at the bottom of the lake, pulled him to shore and began CPR.  The victim was pronounced dead after being transported to the hospital.

Vessel #1 was at Pelican Island fishing in high winds at which time operator became unconcious due to pre-existing medical condition. Vessel #1 drifted North to Northside causing port side of the vessel to come ashore in tree line, starboard side of vessel took on water due to rough high waves causing vessel to swamp. Operator was lying on starboard side of vessel covered with water causing operator to drown.

Upon arrival in the area of 3100 S. Riverside Dr., officers were informed that a male had floated down the river towards the I-44 Bridge.  TFD personnel were able to locate the victim floating in the 4800 block on the west side of the river.  They pulled the victim onto their boat and then to shore and started CPR.  EMSA transported the victim to St. Francis hospital where the victim was pronounced dead at 11:51 a.m.  It was estimated that the victim had been in the water approximately 25 minutes before being pulled from the river.  I then contacted the original caller who had seen the victim in the river.  witness stated that she did not see the victim before he entered the low water dam under the pedestrian bridge struggling to hang on to his kayak.  She stated he was already out of the kayak and had struggled for 3-4 minutes, went under water for a few seconds and then came back up struggling.  She further stated that he was wearing his pfd and lost hold of the kayak.  She then lost sight of him as he floated down river.

Operator was cruising when dog jumped off of vessel 1. Operator entered water to get dog and waves moved vessel away as dog swam away leaving operator alone in rough water.   Operator began to call for help and went under never resurfacing. Recovery made at scene at 1630 hrs 06-09-2010 in 12 ' of water.

On 06-22-2010 at approximately 1200 hrs, Victim and Witness came to lake with kayak and an inflatable air matress. The Victim was in kayak and the witness was on air mattress. The witness stated that the kayak capsized for an unknown reason and the Victim began ended up in the water. The witness jumped off her air mattress to help retrieve the kayak and the Victim began to struggle in the water. He went under water several times and then did not resurface. The Witness swam to shore, went to nearest residence and called 911. Victim was located by side scan sonar and recovered by drag at 1725 hrs. Next of kin notified same date. According to property owner, lake level is approximately 10' higher than normal.

Victim was canoeing with a group of friends on the Mt. Fork River. He was last seen alone, paddling his rented canoe near the end of the trip. All friends had completed the trip except victim. They began a search and later notified law enforcement. The unoccupied canoe was found by W#2 about 75 ft. N. of US70 bridge. It was partially submerged with two lifejackets in it. McCurtain Co. S.O. and Broken Bow Fire/Rescue responded, throughly searching the area. A drag operation by OHP later involved recovery of the victim. M.E. was notified and the body transported to Norwood-Nation Funeral Home in Idabel. Full autopsy was done in Tulsa. Investigation is uncertain if victim fell overboard/capsizing or was already out of the canoe prior to drowning.

Victim was in his father's paddle boat fishing about 25 yards North of Dad's dock.  Victim's Mom was on dock.  Victim had PFD on but not fastened.  Victim fell out of the paddle boat and began to swim toward a dock located about 25 yards to the Northeast of where he entered the water.  As he swam, his pfd came off.   Victim had a broken arm and was having trouble reaching dock.  Mother jumped in to try to rescue him but before she reached him, he went under the surface and did not come back up.  Divers located his remains some 3 hours later in about 20' of water and about 20' from neighbor's dock.  Victim had been drinking and had a history of seizures.

Vessel 1 was engaged in recreational fishing in remote area approx, 2 mi NE of Rocky Point and 1.5 South of Big Hollow.  Operator was on cell phone with wife when passenger announced he was hot and going to cool off.  Passenger entered water approx 10' - 12'  deep.  Operator noticed passenger was nowhere to be seen.  Operator put on pfd and entered water in attempt to locate passenger.  All attempts failed.  Operator then acquired phone service after several attempts because of remote location and called 911, while markiing location of last sighting.  After responding unit arrived on scene, he was assisted by local rural fire department.  Toppers Volunteer Fire Department started a dragging operation in the marked area.  At 20:36 hrs., recovery was made in marked location.  Troop C headquarters was notified of recovery time.  Notification to ME was given and victim transported by funeral home.  Also notification of next of kin was performed by this Trooper.

AOI was approximatey one mile North of Standing Rock and .5 mile East of the West shoreline.  AOR is unknown due to both vessels leaving the scene prior to law enforcement arrival.  Vessels 1 and 2 were Southbound on Lake Eufaula having just left the cut.  Vessel 1 then stopped to allow passengers to use the restroom.  Vessel 2 struck Vessel 1 from behind.  Vessel 2 then went up onto Vessel 1 and slid off the left side of Vessel 1.  Both Vessels then came to rest.  Vessel 2 left the scene while Vessel 1 proceeded to the shoreline to get help for the injured onboard.  Vessel 2 was located the following day.

Vessel 1 was sailing in the Northwest Part of Lake Hefner.  A strong gust of wind blew the Catamaran on it's side.  The two adults attempted to upright the vessel, but were having problems.  The two children started drifting away, so the adults left the Vessel to swim to the children.  All four were wearing life jackets prior to the accident (although it is believed the pfd's the children were wearing were too large). The adults removed their PFD's because they thought it would help them in flipping the Vessel back over.  The two children and the passenger were rescued but the owner passed away.

Vessel 1 was attempting to cross the lake to go deer hunting when approximately 30 yards from the North Shore, it started taking on water due to being overloaded.  Occupants entered the water to swim back to shore.  The Operator and Passenger 3 made it successfully to shore.  Victim 1 began to panic and Victim 2 returned to assist him.  Neither Victim 1 or 2 returned to shore.  No PFD's were in use at the time they entered the water.  Victims 1 and 2 were recovered by the City of Tulsa Lake Patrol and Eucha Fire Department by drag method.  Both Victims were wearing heavy hunting coverall's and boots.  Vessel 1 was powered by a Minn Kota trolling motor rated at 30 lbs thrust.

Vessel 1 was northbound at approx 3/4 throttle speed enroute to alberta creek marina.  Vessel 1 struck the railroad bridge rip-rap launching the vessel onto the rip-rap.  Vessel 1 came to rest approx 10 ft north of the shoreline with the bow facing an easterly direction and the vessel tipped toward the starboard side.  Passengers stated they were in the cuddy cabin of the vessel when suddenly they were thrown around inside the cabin. Passengers crawled out through a hatch on the bow and found the operator lying face up on the rip-rap approx 30 ft northwest of the vessel.  Passengers stated the operator was unresponsive.  Operator and passengers were transported to alberta creek by pontoon boat operated by witness and  were then transferred to ems for transport to hospital.
Area of impact was approx 1/4 mile west of the west end of the railroad bridge, approx 1/2 mile north of the north point entrance to alberta creek and approx 75 yds south of the railroad tracks.  Photos taken by trp

OPERATOR OF VESSEL 1 STATED HE WAS EASTBOUND FROM THE SKI POINT AREA HEADED TOWARD THE SPILLWAY.  VESSEL 1 OPERATOR STATED HE NOTICED A BOAT PULLING A TUBE HEADING SOUTH. POINT OF IMPACT AND AREA OF RECOVERY FOR VICTIM 1 WAS APPROX 1/2 MILE EAST OF SOONER HAVEN BEACH AND APPROX 1 MILE SOUTH OF STATE HIGHWAY 9.

On 7-21-11 DEM Officer responded to East Matunuk State Beach for a report of a kit surfer in distress. When he arrived he observed a USCG boat on scene.  The weather was foggy and there was a strong wind (20-25 knots).  Dispatch informed Off. that lifeguards had pulled a male subject from the water and were treating him. Off. of So. Kingstown Police stated that he performed CPR until EMS arrived and that the victim was in the rescue unconscious and being worked on. 

Lifeguard Supervisor reported at 3:30 pm that there was something suspicious in the water.  He observed an unknown dark object approximately ½ - 3/4 of a mile from shore. He looked through binoculars and determined that it appeared to be a kite surfer but did not see movement.  Supervisor immediately contacted Fisherman’s Memorial Campground by radio and requested USCG be notified to respond.  He then contacted Lifeguard Littlefield to assist him in a rescue.  Supervisor rowed out to the kite surfer and observed a male, unconscious, with his body approximately 2’ under the surface of the water. The victim was not wearing a PFD.  Sea conditions were estimated to be around 3’-5’ with slightly larger swells.  Supervisor then notified Fisherman’s Campground to dispatch EMS.  

Supervisor said Victim’s right arm appeared to be hooked over the handle of the rope of the kite sail and that he was being dragged along by the wind.  Supervisor then tried to pull Victim into the boat but was too heavy.  He then had Lifeguard Littlefield radio to launch the rescue kayak to assist.  Supervisor said that the wind blowing into the sail assisted in bringing them closer to shore where Littlefield assisted in bringing Victim to the surf line. Supervisor said that lifeguards assisted in bringing Victim onto the beach.  Victim was still unconscious as CPR was started by Off. and EMT personnel.  South Kingstown Rescue and Fire arrived shortly after and transported him to South County Hospital. Based on medical reports and witness statements Off. concluded that Victim was kit surfing when the wind slowed causing him to enter the water.  He was unable to re-launch from the water due to lack of wind and sea conditions and his unfamiliarity with his new kite.  Victim became fatigued due to his advanced atherosclerotic artery disease.  He was unable to recover and drowned (salt water)as a result.

On May 26, 2012 DEM officers were dispatched to respond to an incident where someone fell overboard from a vessel in Pt. Judith Harbor of Refuge.  The victim was pulled from the water and CPR was performed.  He was then transported to the Pt. Judith Coast Guard boat house where a pulse and blood pressure was obtained.  Victim was then transported to So. County Hospital.  DEM officers then responded to So. County Hospital where Nursing Superintendent advised that Victim had died from his injuries. According to Off. report, all 3 occupants on the boat left Old Colony Yacht Club in Boston to ride boat, Know Lost Time, to North Carolina. At approximately 2030hs they entered the Pt. Judith Harbor of Refuge and anchored the boat.  They made sandwiches went to the stern of the boat, sat down, ate, and had an alcoholic beverage. Then around 2200 hours, Subject1 went below to bed. Subject2 and Victim continued to talk for a while and around 2330hrs Subject2 went to bed. Victim said that he wanted to stay up longer.  Subject2 left Victim sitting on the stern. A few hours later 0100-0130hrs, on May 26, Subject2 was just falling asleep when Subject1 heard a thud and Subject2 heard a splash. Both went to investigate and saw Victim treading water 15-20 feet off the stern.  Subject2 threw him a line and pulled him to the stern while Subject1 radioed “Mayday man overboard” and their position. Subject2 was holding onto Victim and struggling to get him on the swim platform when Victim lost consciousness.  Subject1 helped Subject2 get Victim from the waist up onto the swim platform, Subject2 began CPR. Pilot Boat, Pilot Conn. came alongside and a subject came on board and both he and Subject2 got Victim on the platform and continued CPR. Subject1 started the engine, pulled anchor, and was headed to the USCG station when he became disoriented in the fog and ran aground.  The USCG boat arrived shortly on scene, two personnel came on board and took over CPR. Subject1 put the boat in reverse and followed the USCG boat to the USCG dock where EMS were waiting and transported Victim to the hospital. Subject1 stated to Off. that Victim had been in the hospital a few months ago for a heart problem and was taking medication for the condition.

On 8-9-12 a boating accident involving a subject that fell overboard took place on Narrow River in Narragansett. As they made way on a westerly course towards Sprague Bridge, subject took a phone call from his cell phone.  He then had his grandson takeover at the wheel. Operator operated the boat into the “No Wake” zone southeast of the bridge. He maintained a 5mph or less speed under the bridge and through the No Wake Zone to the western No Wake buoy.  subject ended his call but allowed operator to continue to operate the boat despite operator not possessing a RI boating license. When the boat cleared the western end of the No Wake zone, operator  increased the throttle and brought the boat up on plane to a speed estimated to be over 20mph. He continued to operate on a westerly course with the throttle somewhere between ½ to ¾ power. subject was standing in between the operator’s seat and passenger’s seat. The vessel subsequently struck the sandbar and came to an abrupt stop. subject was ejected from the boat and landed head-first in around 1ft of water on the sandbar.  Neither of the two passengers were injured when the vessel ran aground. operator jumped out of the boat to assist his grandfather who was unresponsive and kept his face out of the water while the other grandson called 9-1-1.  The NPD and fire/rescue responded to Sprague Bridge.  Two good Samaritans assisted subject and loaded him and his grandchildren on their boat.  They then transported subject to a waiting NFD unit at Sprague Bridge and was treated for life threatening critical injuries. subject was then transported to So. County Hospital.  The attending physician advised Narr. Police Off. that subject sustained severe head and neck injuries and was later transferred to RI Hospital in critical condition. On 8-17-12 subject had passed away overnight.

Approximately 10 minutes after receiving the call I arrived at the mouth of Warm Creek and began approaching a houseboat that matched the description of the reporting party vessel which was drifting in the area with multiple other power boats driving around that area, apparently searching for a person.  I contacted the persons on the houseboat and was told that they had lost one of their group.  They stated that approximately 15 minutes before my arrival that the missing person had jumped off the houseboat to go swimming when they had lost sight of him in the water and could not find him. INVESTIGATION:

After having the reporting party vessel return to the Wahweap Marina, the individuals from that vessel were interviewed by NPS Ranger and other investigating NPS Personnel.  Each of the four vessel occupants filled out witness statements.  Apparently the group had just picked up their houseboat from the boat rentals and started heading up the lake to find a campsite.  After passing through the Castle Rock Cut and entering the mouth of Warm Creek, they decided to stop and swim.  

Multiple people were jumping off the top deck of the houseboat or going down the slide and swimming.  The winds were strong at the time and they stated that the swimmers would have to grab tow lines in the water from the houseboat after entering the water, as the houseboat was drifting away from them quickly in the wind.  At one point a subject jumped in the water and had the boat drift over him.  He realized that the boat was drifting away from him fast as the wind was increasing and began to panic.  He then saw VICTIM had jumped into the water and was holding on to a rope near the ski boat they were towing behind the houseboat.  PERSON stated that he then called for help and saw VICTIM let go of the rope he was holding and begin to swim towards him.  PERSON stated that VICTIM told him to calm down, then appeared to see how fast the boats were drifting away and then VICTIM began to call for help from the others on the boat.

The others on the boat heard the calls for help and another subject swam from the houseboat to the ski boat.  He untied the ski boat and was going to use it to go pick up VICTIM and PERSON, but the keys were not in the vessel.  He relayed that information to those still on the houseboat and a third person began to attempt to start the houseboat to go and pick up VICTIM and PERSON.  The third person stated he was having trouble getting the engines to start and then called for help from the NPS.  He was able to get one motor started and began heading toward where he had last seen VICTIM and PERSON.

At this same time PERSON stated that VICTIM was approximately 15 feet away from him and as PERSON was watching the houseboat and ski boat to see if they were coming to get them, he looked back toward VICTIM and saw him start to sink under the water. INVESTIGATION:

Upon arriving at the Dangling Rope Marina I contacted Operator1, who told me that she had been involved in the accident. Ranger stated that the doctor had determined that the injured female was deceased at the scene and had begun treatment on the injured male as they began transporting him toward Dangling Rope.  While in route toward Dangling Rope, doctor stated that Operator2 had also become deceased due to his injuries.

On june 27, 2010 at 1:30 pm, wco was called to a canoe accident that had occurred on the belle fourche river in butte county, south dakota. The initial call was from a passing motorist that spotted a little girl (p1) wearing only a life jacket on the side of the road, next to the bridge on sd highway 212 that goes over the belle fourche river. The motorist stopped to ask the girl what was wrong and she told the motorist she was in a canoe that had tipped over by the dam. The motorist called 911 and reported the following to butte county dispatch. The caller relayed the information from the little girl that her dad (o/o1), his dad's friend (p2) and her sister (p3) were all still in the water and she did not know where they were. P1 also said the o/o1 and p2 were not wearing life jackets.
  
Wco responded to the scene with other law enforcement and emergency personnel to begin the search and rescue / recovery of the other people. Information at this point was that p3 was wearing a life jacket while o/o1 and p2 were not. The information was also uncertain as to the time frame of how long the people had been in the water. P1 said she walked a long time as well as waited by the water's edge waiting for her dad to come back for a while.
 
Law enforcement had the diversion dam's metal water gates closed to allow the water in that portion of the river to flow out. The water dropped about 8 to 10 feet in a matter of a couple hours. Two life jackets were recovered from the churning water at the base of the chutes. Two oars were also recovered in the same location. It was determined through the bureau of reclamation data that the water was flowing at a rate of 600 cubic feet per minute on that sunday afternoon. 
  
Wco located two halves of the canoe about 1/4 to 1/2 of a mile from the diversion dam to the east. The break was in the middle of the canoe with both halves being about equal length. There was one pfd tangled in a mess of rope that was attached to the bow of the canoe. The report from p1 was that p3 was wearing a jacket while they were in the canoe. While wco was pulling the canoe halves out of the river, the airplane spotted the body of o/o1 about 1/4 mile from where the canoe halves were at. 

Wco began to walk that direction in the water when he located the body of p2. After these two bodies were recovered from the river, the airplane located the body of p3 a little further down the river. P3 was found without a pfd on her. P3's body was recovered and all were taken the funeral home of the black hills in belle fourche, sd. 

On june 29, 2010 wco spoke with p1. P1 walked wco through the events of what may have happened. P1 began by saying they had just gone under the bridge that went over the road and came around the bend when she remembers the dam. P1 can remember going over the "waterfall" which would be the three chutes of the diversion dam. P1 then talks about the canoe getting hung up against the concrete walls of the chutes and that is when she remembers it breaking in half. P1 also talks about p3 spinning in circles after going through the chutes. This might explain how p3 may have come out of the pfd she was wearing before the canoe tipped. P1 talks about how she never saw p2 after he went into the water. P1 also talks about how o/o1 came out of the water and told her to stay there until he came back. P1 said she only saw o/o1 and p3 for a short time and then they were gone. P1 then talks about walking along the water's edge back to where she saw the last bridge.

On 03/23/2010 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Operator and two others began a fishing trip at the West Fork Boat Ramp of J. Percy Priest Lake in Rutherford County , Tennessee.  They were fishing in Operator's 16ft Rebel Bass Boat.  At approximately 14:30 hours,  they noticed water ponding in the floorboard of the deck.  Operator started and lowered the outboard engine in order to drive towards the West Fork Boat Ramp.  Water began to fill the boat when Operator put the boat into forward gear.  Consequently, the stern began sinking and Operator moved to the bow with the other passengers.  The boat then rolled and all three passengers entered the water.  They held on as best they could, but eventually tried to swim to shore.  Two people made it to shored uninjured, but Operator did not.  Operator drowned before reaching shore.  The two where rescued by a good samaritan who took them to the West Fork Boat Ramp.

Autopsy examination revealed edematous lungs with abundant frothy fluid which was also present in the upper airway.  An enlarged liver, thickening of the right ventricle, and 95% atherosclerotic narrowing of the right coronary artery were also noted at autopsy.

The boat hull ,specifically the transom, was breaking down or decaying.  Additionally, the transom showed signs of repair using silicone and commerical liquid welding products.   

The boat motor exceded the capacity requirements of the capacity plate.  The additional weight of the motor combined with the occupants and their equipment overloaded the boat.  

Postmortem toxicology revealed acetaminophen, butalbital, diazepam, and its metabolite, nordiazepam.  Diazepam and butalbital have additive effects and were likely intoxicants in this case.

Hull failure, Overloading, and drug use contributed to this accident.

Based on information to date:  On July 16, 2010 at approximately 22:03 hrs a two vessel collision occurred on Kentucky Lake near Tennessee river mile(TRM) 90.0, and just south of Richland Creek.  

V1 is a 17' 1993 Astro bass boat owned and operated by the same person and also occupied by one other person.  V2 is a 168' Dravo twin screw motor vessel pushing 25 barges and operated by captain and occupied by 8 crew members  V2 is owned by Ingram Barge Co.  operator and passenger were involved in a bass fishing tournament that had launched out of boat dock in Humphreys county, TN at approx. 19:00.  

According to information given by operator1's brother, he found V1 floating in the middle of the river channel near the Shirley light and daymark at TRM 90.9 at approx. 00:15 to 00:30 on July 17, 2010.  Vessel1 operator and occupant were not in the boat and the vessel was damaged.  Operator1's brother notified authorities and Officer went to Mason's boat dock to meet him and they proceeded out to V1 to tow it in and secure it as evidence.  

TWRA, Humphreys county sheriff's department, rescue squad, and fire dept. personnel searched for the two missing men, but they were not found.  Officers were called to work the investigation also.  Upon looking at the boat, the damage seemed to indicate that V1 had impacted something and then had been passed over, or it passed under something.  Based on the coloration of the damage, and that it only appeared damaged on the upper surfaces, and the fact that a rusty substance was found in the floor of V1, then it was suspected that a barge may have been involved.  A shoe, and a life jacket were found against the old railroad levee near Eva, TN approx. 6.0 miles upstream from where the boat was recovered.  Another life jacket was found on the east facing bank of an island approx. 8.0 miles upstream from the spot where the boat was recovered.  One of the life jackets was identified by Operator1's brother as being his brother's.  

This expanded the potential search area to include a few miles upstream of where the jackets and shoe were recovered downstream to where the boat had been found.  By checking with Pickwick, Kentucky, and Barkley Dam lock operators, and also the railroad bridge operator at Hwy 70 near New Johnsonville, 4 motor vessels were identified that would fit the time window of the accident.  TWRA and USCG personnel began stopping and talking with each of the captain's of the motor vessels.  One of the vessels to be investigated was the Robert C. Loedding.  

Officers first contacted the Loedding at 10:07 on July 17, 2010 at TRM 167.  The Loedding was upbound toward Pickwick Dam.  Officers could see transfer marks on the front of barge # ING 2103 that indicated the barge had come into contact with something.  The decision was made to stop the Loedding at Pickwick Dam to further investigate.  Photographs of the transfer marks were taken by officers and they retrieved 4 items from the water that was floating between the barges.  A broken fishing rod, two packs of lures, and a piece of plywood were collected as evidence.  Upon describing the evidence to the families of V1 occupants, the families confirmed that three of the items were consistant with the equipment and bait that both men used.  The piece of plywood could not be confirmed to belong to V1.  The captain and crew were interviewed by USCG and officers.  The captain and the crew stated that they had no knowledge of anything that had come into contact with the front of barge # ING 2103.  Officers collected samples of the transfer marks as evidence from barge ING 2103.  Upon a closer examination, they also found hairs and a piece of tissue on the front of the barge.  The hairs and tissue...

On August 29, 2010 at or around 1746, I arrived at the Lick Creek Boat Ramp on Barkley Lake on a report of a boat circling with no operator.  Based upon evidence and witness statements, a synposis of the events are as follows:

Victim was alone and launched his vessel at the Lick Creek Boat Ramp sometime between 1540 and 1550 hours on August 29, 2010 and headed towards Long Creek.  At or around 1550 hours, his vessel was observed going in circles without an operator.  After witnesses searched the area for survivors, a 911 call was placed at 1554 hours.  At or around 1629 hours, Deputy notified the victim''s wife in person of the accident.

Witnesses state the vessel continued in circles until it ran aground north of the boat ramp.  A bystander stopped the motor and the vessel was later towed by Stewart County Fire Rescue to the Lick Creek Boat Ramp.  A bystander observed a hat and one flip flop floating on the surface.  He collected the items and marked the area with a yellow marker.  Shortly thereafter, a flip flop and a dipping tobacco can floated near the marker.  He also collected the items and they were later identified by subject as belonging to the victim.

Stewart County Fire Rescue performed an extensive rescue and recovery operation and body surfaced at or around 1607 hours on August 30, 2010 near the yellow marker in 8 feet of water.   The body was positively identified as Victim by his brother in presence of the Stewart County Coroner.  

The autopsy report list the cause of death as accidental drowning.

The vessel is a 1975 model 14 foot aluminum Polarcraft with a 20 hp Mercury tiller motor.  The boat is well used with multiple scratches and dents.   The olive green paint is dull and faded.  It was common for the victim to drag the boat over obstacles to get to his favorite fishing holes.  There is no evidence on the  boat or motor of a collision.  The contents inside the vessel indicate a hard roll to port.

The vessel was water tested on September 28, 2010.  There were no mechanical defects found in the motor.  Maximum speed of the vessel was around 22 mph.  When the steering handle was let go at 8 mph, the motor would immediately torque into a sharp starboard turn and decrease speed slightly.  I was unable get the items inside the boat to shift to the position where they were observed the day of the accident.

There are numerous navigational hazards in the area of the accident including submerged stumps and shallow bars.  However, based upon the evidence and the local knowledge of the victim, this does not appear to be a contributing factor. 

Evidence does suggest that for some unknown reason, the victim let go of the tiller handle causing the boat to turn sharply to the starboard throwing the victim off the port side of the vessel.

On the other hand, both occupants of Vessel 2 were wearing PFDs, but they weren''t securely fastened.  deceased's PFD came off when he was ejected.  Everyone but deceased victim (Vessel 2) made it to shore safely.  deceased victim couldn''t swim and drowned.
