On 11, May 2012 at approximately 20:34, subject called Pickett County Emergency 911 and stated that she and her husband had found an unresponsive female floating in the water near the shore at Cove Creek Recreational Area. Pickett County Sheriffs Deputy arrived on the scene at 20:48 and found subject2 standing near the shoreline. Deputy waded out 30 to 40 ft and pulled the female body which was face down in the water to shore. She had no ID on her at the time and after talking with several individuals at the campground found that she was with a male who was driving a Dodge Pickup which was parked next to the campsite. After searching the vehicle, Deputy found a wallet belonging to Victim that had her driver''s license in it. He identified the female in the water to be Victim. At that time Pickup owner had not been located. The body of Victim was sent to Nashville for an autopsy to determine cause of death. Pickup Owner''s vessel was found on the opposite shoreline floating against the bank. The vessel is a 1972 Surfrider 15ft in length. Registration on the vessel is TN 8253 X. The motor was trimmed all the way up, the throttle was in nuetral, and the key was turned to the off position. There was a rope tied to the bow eye with a loop tied on the end. The rope was floating in the water. The boat was pulled back to Cove Creek Recreational Area. Deputies and TWRA Officers packed up the campsite and took the truck and boat to JK Boat Storage on Cove Creek Rd. The search for the Pickup Owner was suspended until the following day due to darkness.
Witness from Jamestown was at Cove Creek Recreational Area and was interviewed by Officer. He stated that he had seen a female blowing up an air mattress at the campsite earlier that evening and that he did not hear any noise or fussing coming from the camp. There were no other witnesses identified who positively could say they saw anything.   
    On 12 May 2012 TWRA Officers inventoried items in the boat and truck. Two open Bud Light beer cans were found in the cab of the truck. One was in the floorboard empty and the other was in a drink holder and was half empty. Also found was a empty Bud Light case (18 beers). In a cooler in the back of the truck officers found 16 full Bud Light beers. Officers also inspected the vessel for any damage. No apparent damage was found. The search continued throughout the day for Pickup owner and was once again suspended due to darkness.
    On 13 May 2012 the search was suspended due to heavy rains throughout the day.
    On 14 May 2012, Pickett County Rescue Squad found the body of the pickup owner in 8ft of water near the area Victim was found. No apparent signs of trauma could be seen. At this time he will be sent to Nashville for an autopsy to determine cause of death.
    This incident happened in Pickett County.

Investigator assumes the following, "The truck and trailer were at the campsite...so they already launched it.  There is a boat ramp/courtesy dock there as indicated by the inserted photo but it is hard to see.  The rope was out in the water when we found the boat...so it appears that it may have came untied or ungrounded at their site...and either one or both started to swim for it....only an assumption."

Operator, his wife, and their five children had been staying on a houseboat at Lone Mountain Boat Dock since May 31, 2012.  On June 11, 2012, the family was packing their belongings preparing to go home.  Operator left the houseboat around 7:30 pm to take the four youngest children and some of the belongings from the houseboat to Lone Mountain Dock.  Operator’s wife stated Operator was gone for about two hours and she was beginning to get worried.  When Operator returned to the houseboat Operator’s wife stated he had been drinking and they began to argue about his drinking.  

Operator’s wife stated the entire family boarded the pontoon and Operator began driving extremely fast towards Lone Mountain Dock.  Operator’s wife stated she kept telling him to slow down but Operator refused and acted as if he was going to jump out of the vessel.  As the pontoon got close to Lone Mountain Dock Operator turned the vessel around and started heading away from the dock.  Operator’s wife stated she and Operator continued to argue and Operator hit her in the face knocking her unconscious.  When she came to, Operator’s wife stated Operator was on top of his step-daughter and she pulled him off of her at which time Operator struck her in the face again.  

Stepdaughter stated they were all screaming for Operator to go back to the dock.  Operator’s wife stated Operator said, " I''ll show all of them" and got out from behind the steering wheel and jumped out of the vessel.  Operator’s wife stated she threw Operator''s lifejacket out because she knew he was not a good swimmer, but the boat was going too fast and they had already gone too far past him.  Operator’s wife stated they were all too scared to jump in for fear of him trying to drown one of them.  During the panic of Operator jumping over board, the kill switch on the pontoon was pulled out and Operator’s wife did not know how to restart the vessel.  

Subject and family were on a houseboat nearby and heard the kids screaming for help.  When Subject got to the scene, stepdaughter told him what had happened and showed Subject where Operator had jumped in.  Subject found Operator floating face down close to the area stepdaughter had pointed out.  Subject is CPR certified through his work and began CPR on operator as soon as he was pulled from the water.  Operator was transported to Lone Mountain Dock where Claiborne EMS was waiting.  He passed away.

On 07/04/2012 at approximately 14:24 I received a call from Grainger County 911 stating that 4 children had been electrocuted while swimming from a houseboat at German Creek Marina Bean Station, TN.  I wasn''t on duty so I notified Region IV dispatch to relay the message to someone in-service on the water.  I arrived on scene at approximately 15:10 where four officers along with other part time officers, Grainger County Sheriff''s Deputies, Rutledge Police Department, and THP had secured the scene and evacuated the docks.  All of those injured had either been transported, or were being driven by personal vehicles to area hospitals.  

Agency personnel secured evidence:  pedestal power outlet with meter, and entire vessel TN 8734 AJ.  According to witness statements, three people were jumping from the top of TN vessel 8734 AJ into the water between their vessel and TN 5283 BP.  Those witnesses heard screams from the children and discovered two people floating face down in the water, and one other floating face up.  Several family members and bystanders jumped into the water to rescue the children, all of which encountered electrical current/shock during this process.  One person was pronounced dead on arrival to Morristown Hamblen, while another was revived en-route to Morristown Hamblen, and then flown by Lifestar to East Tennessee Childrens Hospital where he stayed on full life support until his family ceased care and attending physician pronounced him dead at 19:35 on 07/05/2012.  All of the other injuries were admitted for overnight observation, treated and released, or refused care. The final meeting with the D.A.G. took place on October 4, 2012, where it was determined that no criminal charges would be filed. This incident occurred on Cherokee Lake in Grainger County, Tennessee.

Operator2 was operating a 21ft 2207 Supra wakeboard boat, hereafter known as V2, in a northerly direction.  Statements from occupants onboard V2 stated they were heading out of Sugar Creek towards Hwy 58 bridge, so they could get under the bridge and wait out a severe thunderstorm.  They saw V1 coming south in Sugar Creek near the bank of the Hwy 58 causeway.  At approximately 100 yards, they state that V1 veered in front of them causing them to strike V1 in the front right section of the boat.  The angle of impact is approximately 27 degrees. After inspection of both vessels, it was determined that neither boat had their navigational lights on at the time of the collision.

Operator 1 passed away.

A passenger in the fatal boating accident, was interviewed and is the only witness to this incident.  Operator, driver of the 15 ft Reelfoot Lake Boat and the only vessel involved in this incident, lost his life during this incident as described by Occupant, At the onset of the accident, Occupant was sitting directly in front of Operator, as the only passenger while the two were headed in from a fishing trip. They were cruising at the boat''s absolute lowest speed and ran up on a stump that was barely submerged beneath the water. According to Occupant, the ultra slow  careful speed caused the boat to "stick" (stop) on the stump instead of "jump over" and continue forward movement. Occupant said this slow careful speed was the main reason for the boat sinking. When the boat stopped it was tilted to the port side and when Occupant looked back Operator was slumped over the side of the boat.  With all of the weight of Operator on the port side of the boat, the boat began to take on water. At that point, Operator rolled over the boat side into the water and Occupant jumped into the water in an attempt to keep the boat from getting any more water inside the hull.  During the commotion, Operator managed to grab a cooler lid and Occupant was holding on to a type II PFD. Neither Operator or Occupant were wearing a PFD when the incident occurred. 

A Type !! PFD was used by Occupant to help support him while in the water.  With both passengers in the water, Occupant recalled that Operator was spinning around in a circle with the cooler lid and would not respond when his name was yelled by Occupant.  Occupant then noticed that Operator took a big breath and passed out. Occupant grabbed Operator and held him up using a stump for support. As far as Occupant knows, head never went underwater and Operator did not drown. Occupant supported Operator''s body on the closest stump with the suspenders worn by Operator. Occupant noticed at this point that Operator''s lips and face were a deep purple in color. The boat ultimately sank with only the bow showing while the two were in the waters of Half Moon Basin and being supported by only a stump.  Approximately 30 minutes after the incident described occurred,  someone headed in from a day of fishing in the area,  heard Occupant yelling for help. 

Good samaritan helped Occupant get into the boat and the both of them pulled Operator''s unconscious body into the boat.  Upon arrival at the nearest boat ramp near the TWRA Reelfoot Office,  EMT of the Lake Co. EMS met the parties involved.  EMT made the comment that, in his opinion,  the victim had a massive heartattack. Occupant noted that during the incident while in the water or during the boat ride to the boat ramp he never felt cold. When the incident was over and he was in his truck he started to feel cold and started to shiver. Occupant indicated that he refused to go to the hospital and Brent EMT insisted that he go. Occupant ultimately was admitted to the Union City Baptist Hospital and treated for hypothermia. Occupant had undergone 2 heart surgeries in the previous years and began to have "enzyme complications" when his heart started to slow down from the commotion of the incident. Occupant was in the hospital for two days before being released.  No blood EMT or autopsy was done on Operator. The Lake Co. Coronor indicated that on his report the cause of death was noted to be "pending".  The Medical Examiner for Lake Co indicated that the cause of death was Acute MI.

On March 19, 2010 at approximately 2:00 PM the drowning victim  and passenger were at Lake Aquilla fishing in the Aquilla Creek area of Lake Aquilla.  The two men decided to move.  Upon leaving the area and getting on "plane" the boat capsized somewhere north of "Rattle Snake Island".  The surviving witness denied hitting anything. He could only describe riding and the next thing he remembered was being in the water and the boat being capsized.   The driver and passenger clung to the capsized boat for several hours.  In the beginning the boat drifted with the wind back in a southward direction toward the shore at the mouth of the Aquilla creek area of the lake.  The boat eventually stopped drifting as it became lodged on a tree stump.  The drowning victim tried sevaral times to swim beneath the boat and free PFD's from a compartment in the boat. Fearing the worst and being extremely cold the drowning victim attempted to get to shore for help.   The surviving witness advised he swam on his back and turned over to begin dog paddling.  He submerged and did not re-surface just south of the capsized vessel at approximately 50 feet.  The surviving witness was rescued by a passing boater within 20 minutes of the victim's submersion.  The witness was taken to Lake Whitney Medical Center where he was treated for symptoms of hypothermia.  
Rescue Divers and Texas Game Warden and I searched the area for any evidence that the drowning victim made to shore.  Within an hour we began to utilize sonar equipment near the capsized vessel in order to locate a body.  Rescue divers cleared the vessel to insure that the victim was not trapped under the vessel.  
Warden and I secured the vessel by rope to a nearby tree in case the vessel dislodged from the stump.
At approximately 9:30 PM using side imaging sonar we viewed an anomalie near the vessel within the search area described by the witness,. We belived the anomalie to be the drowning victim.  Due to darkness we were unable to have divers investigate the anomalie.
For the next two days a strong north wind and extreme drop in temperature hampered attempts to further search for the victim.
On Monday March 22, with the assistance of the US Army Corp of Engineers' winch boat the capsized vessel was dislodged from the stump and towed to a nearby boat ramp where it was recovered and placed on it's trailer.  Photographs were taken.  There were no clear impact spots or clear damage cause during the capsizing.  There were several scratches on the moter and corners of the vessel that appeared to be caused during towing and loading.  The throttle lever was observed to be at half throttle position.  
Region II District 3 Wardens attempted to use body dragging hooks to catch the victim in the area where the anomalie was located and the witness described the victim to be.  Several large tree limbs were removed from the area and the anomalie remained in the area.  
Divers attempted to dive where the anomalie was located.  They were forced to re-surface quickly due to cold water temperatures at the bottom of the lake.  Recovery efforts were again called off, due to darkness.
On Tuesday March 23rd in the Am Region 2 District 3 Wardens were preparing and marking the are where the anomalie was located, in preperation for cold water divers from Texas DPS to arrive and investigate the anomalie.  While marking the area Warden began to pitch a small drag hook where the anomalie was located.  On his second pitch he pulled the victim to the surface.  The victim was transported to the Culp boat ramp and turned over to Hill County SO investigators.

Based on the lack of physical evidence and the lack of memory from the surviving party to the event no determination could be made as to the cause of the accident.

On the 24th day of April, operator was launching his boat a Little Cypress Creek when he began to push away from the bank and fell overboard.  operator struck his head in the shallow water and was rendered unconscious. operator was removed from the water by emergency personal where he was found face down, and transported to the local hospital.  operator was pronounced dead at the hospital.

According to witness statements, at apporximately 12:15 a.m. Vessel 1 (2005 21'6" malibu ski boat) occupied by four adults was traveling east on the Colorado arm of Lake LBJ. State Game Warden interviewed Driver at the hospital on Sunday in which he stated he and the other occupants of the vessel left their rental cabin located in Kingsland by boat about 10:30 p.m. the night before, traveled east on the Colarado arm, also traveled to several inlets off the Colorado arm.  They decided to go back to their cabin in Kingsland, in reality, continued traveling east toward Inks Lake dam.  operator stated to Warden while on plane, he saw what he thought was a boat without navigational lights on, yelled for them to turn their lights on, swerved and collided with the granite outcropping. On or about August 9, 2010 at approximately 10:00 AM I State Game Warden was notified by TPWD communications to contact Capt. with the City of Freeport PD, in reference to a boating accident which had occurred the   previous day. I made contact with Capt and he informed me about the accident, which involved a fatality that had occurred on the Old Brazos River and gave me the contact information for a Detective who was assigned to the case. 
 On or about August 12, 2010 at approximately 1:00 PM, I met Detective with the City of Freeport PD, and he informed me about the details of the boating accident. Detective gave me copies of the information and statements they had obtained on all the individuals involved in the accident. 
  According to statements and information obtained from the individuals involved in the accident, the Knights of Columbus were having a picnic at the River Place Community House located at the Freeport Municipal Park on August 8, 2010. The park is located next to the Old Brazos River. A couple of members had brought their boats to the event and were conducting boat rides for those who wanted to go. That afternoon, an individual identified as operator was operating one of the boats. The boat he was operating was a 2010 BoatRight Custom Flat Motorboat (TX 4370 BD). operator states that he was at the dock talking with an individual. Three more individuals came to the dock, and Operator asked if they wanted to go for a ride.  The three individuals boarded the boat along with friend. Friend stood beside Operator behind the center console. Occupant1 sat on the seat on the right side of the boat, and the two females attempted to sit on the seat on the left, however Operator told one of them to sit on the seat in front of the console to balance out the boat friend stated that Operator told the three individuals that the life jackets were beside them if they wanted to wear one. Friend also stated that no one put on a life jacket as they left the dock. 
  Operator states they headed up the river towards the bridge and that he only drove the boat at about 5 mph, because he was concerned about how low the boat was sitting in the water and that some water was splashing over the sides.  Operator said another boat came by before they got to the bridge, and he turned the bow of the boat to go over the wake, and some water came over the bow. Operator was still concerned about how low the boat was sitting in the water, and he checked to make sure the drain holes were open, and had Friend turn on the bilge pump. They continued to travel up the river and went under the bridge. At this point Operator decided to turn the boat around because he was still concerned about the way the boat was riding in the water.  Operator starts to make a wide turn to the right and states that as he starts to turn back to the left, about 3 inches of water began coming over the right front side. Friend states that water started coming over the left side. At this time, operator states that one of the female occupants moved towards the right. Friend did not recall if one of the female occupants moved to the right, but stated that there was a weight shift to the right. At this point, Operator said he gave the boat some gas to try and level out the bow, however, the boat took on more water and flipped over. All the occupants returned to the surface next to the boat, except for Occupant1. occupant had become trapped beneath the boat and the railing that went around the sides of the boat. Operator, Friend, and witness who had witnessed the accident and jumped in the water to assist, worked to get occupant from underneath the boat. Once occupant was removed from beneath the boat, operator states that he began trying to perform CPR. At this point, emergency personnel arrived on scene and began assisting with the accident, victim was transported by ambulance to Brazosport Regional Hospital. The other occupants sustained only minor bruises and scrapes. to perform CPR. At this point, emergency personnel arrived on scene and began assisting with the accident, victim was transported by ambulance to Brazosport Regional Hospital.  The other occupants sustained only minor bruises and scrapes. victim was pronounced deceased by Justice of the Peace Sharon Fox at 1515 hrs. Judge  ordered a complete autopsy be performed. Resulsts are still pending at this time. Detective  had a blood sample drawn from operator. The results are sitll pending at this time. 
Note: The manufacture capacity rating for the boat: 4 person or 532lbs. 1252 lbs including persons, motor, and gear.  Detective  obtained weight information from all 5 individuals on board the vessel and it was determined the manufacture's weight capacity was exceeded by nearly 900 lbs.

On January 14, 2011 at 5:33pm while on patrol in Amistad National Recreation Area, National Park Service (NPS) agent received a report from Val Verde Sheriff's Office dispatch about a dead body at Rough Canyon boat dock. Agent responded to the area and arrived on scene at 5:49pm. As Agent pulled down to the dock he witnessed a body laying on the ramp half submerged in water and a bass boat tied to the dock. There were three witnesses on scene. NPS Agent approached the body and asked how long it had been since they found the body. One witness told me it had been 20 minutes since he and his brother found the body floating face down in the water.

Agent checked the body for a pulse and found none, the body was cold to the touch, and showed signs of lividity. The eyes were hazed over and all skin color had been lost. Based upon the amount of time the body had been in the water and its appearance, Agent did not perform CPR.

Agent asked the brothers to explain exactly what they had seen. They told Agent as they passed Big Canyon, heading up the Devils River, they witnessed the individual fishing from his bass boat at approximately 2pm. When they returned to the dock that evening, approximately 520pm, they observed the same bass boat in an adjacent cove approximately 200 yards from the Rough Canyon boat ramp. The boat didn’t have any occupants. They motored over to the abandoned boat and noticed that the engine was running, not in gear, and there was in fact no one in the boat. They then motored over to the dock to see if they could find the owner of the boat and found a male body floating face down in the water. They asked someone near the dock to call for help and they pulled the body to the edge of the water. While at the dock the brothers said the red ball cap was on the dock with a wet spot on the dock. A wallet was found on board the boat and the body was identified. Val Verde Sheriff’s Office arrived on the scene at 601pm and took over the investigation. Deputy from CID were leading the investigation for Val Verde Sheriff’s Office. The boat was not inventoried by NPS for Fire extinguishers and other water safety equipment. On board the boat was a bottle of Crown Royal in plain view.

According to Game Warden, through information from Val Verde County CID, the victim had a laceration on his head. Cause of death will be determined when autopsy is complete. 
The third witness only called 911 and was not identified.
 Warden  believes victim while docking boat hit his head on dock and fell in the water. Autopsy was incomplete and Warden was unable to determine actual cause of death by incomplete autopsy.

Three people were in a Pelican canoe (zgp45152d404) 15.5 feet in length on Lake Ray Hubbard 03/12/2011 in rough and windy conditions.  The three left the shore paddling into open water.  The wind was at an estimated 25 mph with estimated waves of almost 2 feet.  The boat was pushed by the wind and waves down the lake as they tried to turn the canoe to return to their starting point the canoe was caught by the waves, swamped and then capsized.  There were no personal floatation devices on board the boat the three individuals then tried to swim to the shore.  during the swim to shore two people lost sight of the operator as he tired out from the effort of swimming and the cold temperature of the water (53 df).  After reaching the shore the survivors were able to contact 911 and the Dallas Police then contacted TPWD Game Wardens.  A search for the victim was immediately started and was called off at approximately 9:00pm due to darkness.  The search then continued at 7:30 am the next morning until 8:30pm this daily schedule was continued until recovery of the victim on 03/16/2011 at approximately 11:00am.

On April 14, 2011 at 5: 44 pm Benbrook Fire Department, Cresson Fire Department and Tarrant County Sheriff where dispatched to Mustang Park Peninsula Point to a call of a capsized boat.  Deputy, of the Tarrant County Sheriff Department, noticed a small overturned boat drifting about 500 yards of the end of Peninsula Point and the high winds were carrying the vessel out into the center of Lake Benbrook.  

Deputy, spoke with witnesses who saw the overturned boat and made the 911 call.  The witnesses stated that they had seen 4 to 5 people on the boat and they all appeared to be wearing lifejackets.  They stated that the boat was in the middle of the lake and was headed southeast into the wind.  The waves appeared to be cresting over the bow of the boat.  The boat then appeared to turn right and head toward the peninsula at which time the winds and waves flipped the boat over.  The occupants of the boat began to yell for help.

Cresson Fire Department arrived at 1809 hours and Benbrook Fire Department at 1819 hours.  Benbrook Fire Department located and made contact with the boat at around 1835 hours, two adults and three children were pulled from the water but one child was missing.  Benbrook Firefighter dove into the water and recovered the 5 year old victim.  Victim was wearing his lifejacket and had gotten trapped under the capsized boat when it flipped.  Firefighter stated that when the boat capsized no air pocket had formed and Victim was unable to get out from under the hull.  Victim had been underwater for approximately 50 minutes.  Firefighters transferred Victim to the resuce boat and cut off his lifejacket and began cpr.  Victim was not responsive and did not have a pulse.  The rescue boat made shore at approximately 1855 hours.  Victim was transferred to an ambulance where EMT's continued cpr until he was transported by PHI Helicopter to Cook Children's Hospital at approximately 1924 hours.  

Cresson and Benbrook EMT's checked all other passengers in the boat.  No injuries were found and they were released at the scene.  EMT's and firefighters so no evidence of drug or alcohol use.

Operator’s wife later stated that the family had received the boat as a gift.  They had arrived at Mustang Park at Benbrook Lake around 1700 hours to test the boat.  All of the children were wearing their lifejackets but the parents were not.  At around 1735 hours the wind really began to pick up and they headed back to the boat ramp.  The waves were crashing over the bow of the boat and the boat was taking on water and began to sink.  Operator slowed down due to poor visibility and when he did the outboard motor stalled.  Then the winds and waves capsized the boat.  Two people where on one side of the capsized boat and three others were on the other side of the boat.  They placed the children on top of the capsized boat and then Operator began diving looking for Victim but was unable to locate him.  

At approximately 2129 hours, Tarrant County Medical Examiner's Office notified Tarrant County Sheriff Office dispatch that Victim had died.

The boat was finally recovered on 04/26/2011 by the Army Corp of Engineers.  Upon locating the vessel it had suffered severe damage.  Both sides of the vessel are gone and the only part of the transom to survive was protected by the motor mounting bracket.  The boat was finally identified by the outboard motor mounting bracket seriel number plate.  The boat was a total loss.  Any other contents that may have been in the boat are unknown.

On 4-22-2011 at aproximatley 10:38 AM, I State Game Warden received a call From State Game Warden SGT. that the US Coast Guard needed some assistance with a boating accident that occurred on the Lower Laguna Madre.  I travelled to the US Coast Guard station on South Padre Island to learn that a vessel being TX 6207 BF a 21' 7" Gulf Coast make had capsized and four persons had been thrown into the water.  One of the people involved in the capsizing was transported to Valley regional medical center in Brownsville Tx, in Cameron County. After speaking to the US Coast Guard and to the witnesses whom were present, I found out that the group of boaters were drifting along the Intercoastal Waterway when they were trying to retrieve a drift sock that had been blown out of the vessel.  The boat then capsized while they were trying to retrieve it.  The vessel was not being operated at the time of the capsizing.  US Coast Guard Lieutenant stated to me that overloading and weather conditions may have played a key factor to the vessel capsizing. 

04-22-2011 later on during the day I had called Valley Regional Medical Center to check the status of Victim and I had learned of him passing away.
      
On 04-23-2011 at approximately 9:00AM I received statements from the witnesses.  Asking the witnesses what the approximate weights for everyone on board they stated 172lbs for Occupant1, 230lbs for Occupant2, 330lbs for Victim, and 350lbs for Occupant3. 

On 4-23-2011 after receiving statements I then made contact with a representative from Tow Boat US who informed me that the vessel had been towed to his residence in Laguna Vista Tx, in Cameron County.  I then travelled to the residence and took pictures of the vessel in and out of the water. (See Photo Attachments)  All safety equipment was on board the vessel including life jackets, fire extinguisher, and type IV throwable.  The only Damage to the hull of the vessel was the right side of the transom had been smashed in by the power pole when the vessel capsized.  

05/11/2011 I received the death certificate that showed victim had died of an accidental drowning.   

05/11/2011 After taking witness statements, photos I learned that on 04-22-2011 victim accompanied by three others went out fishing on the Lower Laguna Madre on a rough and windy day.  During the trip a drift sock blew out the vessel and Victim circled back to retrieve it and raised his motor.  While retrieving the drift sock at the stern of the vessel the vessel took on water and the boat capsized throwing everyone on board into the water.  PFD's were accessible but were not used.  The US Coast Guard transported everyone back to the Coast Guard Station where Victim was the transported to Valley Regional Medical center where he later passed away.  After receiving the death certificate I learned that Victim passed away by accidental drowning.

Around 9 a.m. on Sunday, April 17th, 2011, two recreational fishermen in a boat noticed a boat grounded on the south side of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway.  They went to look and found a body floating face down nearby in the water.  They held onto the body and summoned help.  A US Coast Guard boat arrived on scene, lifted the body into their boat, with no pulse found and foam at nose and mouth, and commenced CPR.  They took the body to the Coast Guard Station Port O'Connor, where EMS arrived and continued CPR.  CPR was discontinued; on call Justice of the Peace declared the boater deceased at 10:10 a.m.  The grounded boat was a 22 foot flat-bottom Mowdy with a 200 hp Evinrude outboard.  

When the MSEO arrived, the key was turned on, the kill switch lanyard was still hooked to the light switch, the throttle was in about 2/3rds forward position.  The boat was 49' onshore in sand.  The steering was operable and the jack plate only about one half inch raised.  The propeller appears as though it had spun for some time while in the sand.  It appears the boater had been separated from the boat and it had then grounded.  The boater had a deep laceration in his left foot and had a history of high blood pressure.  

Autopsy conclusion was death due to drowning with multiple injuries as contributing factors.  The autopsy discovered six broken ribs and hypertension-type heart disease.  The toxicology report discovered no drugs or alcohol.  This event is being named as an unattended death; why the decedent originally became separated from the boat is unknown.

At 10:53 PM Goliad County Sheriff's Office received a 911 call of a possible drowning at Coleto Creek Lake.  I was notified there shortly after and responded to the lake.  I notified Wardens of the possible drowning and they both responded to the lake.  At approximately 11:15 PM officers arrived at the lake.  Officers received information from the victim’s family about the incident.  After a short search of the area at approximately 11:45 PM Warden went to the campground area of the park to find the operator of the vessel involved in the incident.  The operator was identified.

Warden interviewed Operator and was told that Victim had jumped off the boat.  Operator stated that at approximately 10:30 PM, he operated the vessel away from the shore, placed the vessel on plane, and headed toward the dam, with Victim and one other as passengers. Operator stated that as they approached an area known as the island, Victim jumped from the back of the moving vessel.  Operator stated he saw Victim enter the water and immediately came to an idle to return and pick up Victim. Operator stated he could not locate Victim in the water and searched for approximately 20 minutes before returning to the campground to call for help. Warden asked Operator if he had consumed alcohol. Operator stated he drank a few beers earlier that evening. Operator did not show signs of impairment at the time of the interview.  
	
	While Warden was interviewing Operator, I made contact with other occupant who stated that shortly after they had left the shore, and the vessel was on plane, Victim stated that he was going to jump out of the boat. Other occupant told me that Victim had jumped from a moving vessel before, and had injured himself. Because of this past incident, Other occupant did not think that Victim would actually jump from the boat. Other occupant stated that as they were near the island, he saw Victim jump from the rear of the vessel and enter the water. Other occupant stated that he briefly saw Victim splashing in the water, but when they turned to pick him up, they were unable to locate him. Other occupant said that they searched the area for about 20 minutes before they returned to shore to get help.

	Wardens and I began searching the area using spotlights and side scan sonar to try and recover Victim. Supervisors were notified of the search efforts being made.  We continued search efforts throughout the night and following morning.  We contacted DPS dive team to request assistance in the search efforts.On 05/15/11, at approximately 10:15 AM, I located a target in 17 ft. of water on side scan sonar and alerted DPS dive team. At approximately 11:10 AM, DPS divers located the victim and made the recovery. The victim was transported by boat to shore where he was pronounced deceased. The victim was released to Colonial Funeral Home at the request of the victim’s family.

Because of the windy conditions they could not catch up to the jet ski. They started to tire and tried to swim to nearby Rock Island but the waves and wind caused them to become exhausted. Occupant said that they were wearing life jackets but due to the very old age and poor condition of the life jackets, they were torn off of their bodies as they struggled in the water. No life jackets were ever found in the area. Operator went down and Occupant was beginning to go down but another jet skier rescued Occupant and took him to the bank. This jet skier could not be located later. Occupant gave conflicting stories such as the life jackets had been purchased recently at a Wal-Mart and hence were not old. Then he said he was thinking about some other life jackets nor was he sure of the colors of the life jackets. His story about the life jackets and due to many people looking and not being able to find any life jackets leads me to believe that they had not been wearing any.

At approximately 1500 hours on May 28, 2011, I, State Game Warden, was dispatched to the scene of a single vessel boat accident on Lake Livingston near Kalita Point by the Polk County Sheriff's Department.  I arrived on scene and interviewed the operator of the boat whom I identified.  Operator explained that he was pulling his friend on an intertube behind the boat making circles in a narrow cove to avoid the high wind and waves on the open water.  He stated that neither he nor Victim was wearing a PFD.  He also stated that he did not have an observer and his boat was not equipped with a rearview mirror.  Operator stated that he observed his friend Victim fall off of the tube and then submerge after making a weak attempt to swim.  He stated that he yelled out for someone to call 911 and he began diving into the water trying to find his friend.  He was unsuccessful.  He admitted to drinking a few alcoholic drinks prior to the accident and he appeared to be intoxicated.  He submitted a preliminary breath specimen which registered .12 g/210L and was transported to the Livingston Memorial Hospital for a mandatory blood draw and Standardized Field Sobriety Testing.  Game Wardens recovered the body of Victim at approximately 1645 hours that afternoon and Operator was arrested and booked into the Polk County Jail on charges of Intoxication Manslaughter after he performed poorly on the field sobriety tests.
Autopsy results later confirmed the cause and manner of death to be accidental drowning.  The victim's blood alcohol level showed to be .19 g/100ml and there was evidence he was also under the influence of marijuana.

On July 18, 2011, at approximately 15:35 hours, Travis County Deputies were dispatched to Devils Cove on Lake Travis in reference to a missing person.  Upon arrival, at approximately 15:38 hours, they were advised that a male jumped from the top deck of the boat, identified as Margaritaville.  Margaritaville is a 66' Stardust houseboat bearing TX 7123 EW.  Victim jumped off the vessel while it was transitioning at headway speed in the middle of Devils Cove, approximately 200 yards from the no wake buoys going towards the back of the cove.  Victim was not wearing a PFD when he jumped off the vessel.  The boat was still adrift when the deputies arrived, which was 10 minutes after the original call and according to the call notes, the occupants of the vessel waited a minimum of 5 minutes before calling 911.  The deputies set a buoy marker at a water depth of 35 feet where the Victim was last seen.  

The deputies gathered all the individuals looking for Victim and had them get back onto the vessel.  The deputies then anchored the vessel to a mooring buoy towards the rear of Devils Cove.  At approximately 16:04 hours, Starflight and Lake Travis Fire and Rescue checked the area.  The fire boat checked the area of where the Deputies set their marker with sidescan sonar and found no points of interest.  The Deputies and LCRA boarded the "Margaritaville" and obtained statements from the witnesses.  According to the statements, Victim was on the top deck, starboard (right) side of the boat, near the aft (rear) of the vessel.  The vessel was cruising at headway speed when Victim said he was ready to go swimming.  Victim then did a back flip off the vessel, using the railing from the awning.  Victim came back up and began swimming.  The witnesses went back to what they were doing or looked away and they could not see Victim any longer.  No one on the vessel observed Victim go under water, but there were witnesses that guessed that the time they looked away from Victim was very short.  

Deputy spoke to Witness, who stated that the entire group were servers at a local restaurant, which was being remodeled.  They took this opportunity to make a trip out to the lake, compliments of their owners.  Witness said that Victim had fallen onto hard times lately.  Victim has been sleeping on friend’s couches and the night before this trip his vehicle was broken into and all of his personal items and identification were stolen.  It is unclear whether this incident was reported or where it may have occurred.  Witness also relayed to Deputy that Victim has been drinking alcohol heavily lately and had been drinking before coming onto the vessel for their trip.  Witness knew little about Victim, other than the fact that his parents live in the Dallas/Ft Worth area.  

Victims assistance was offered to the group and was waiting on the dock of Emerald Point Marina, but once the boat began going towards the Marina they all refused.  

The only property that Victim left on the vessel was his cell phone, which Deputy seized and processed into evidence at the Travis County Sheriffs West Sub-Station.  

Case information was given to the boat Captain, and the part owners of the restaurant.

At approximately 17:37 hours, Deputy released Captain and released the vessel to its mooring at Emerald Point Marina.  The vessel is side slipped on the end of "L" dock.

Once the houseboat cleared the area Deputy went back to the scene to conduct a shoreline search and to place crime scene tape streamers off the marker buoy.

A page was sent out to the Travis County Dive Team and a plan was made to dive the scene the next morning.

On 07/19/2011 at approximately 21:42 hours, Victim's body was found floating on the surface water in Devils Cove.

The boat was launched from a ramp on the south side of the Dike with a trolling motor attached. Witnesses informed Officer that the boat the men were on appeared to be too small for four adults and the men seemed unsteady in it. Also, the men were not wearing any life jackets. A short time after the boat was launched a large wake capsized the vessel. Texas City P.D. Captain was first to arrive on the scene and found victims in the water on the south side of the Dike.  The fourth victim was nowhere in sight but was found alive. The three men were much further west of the boat and appeared to be moving slowly with the current. Minutes later additional Texas City P.D. and firefighter personnel began the task of helping to rescue the victims from the water. Three of the victims were able to come back to shore with little or no injury. However, after being pulled out of the water one person was immediately transported to Mainland Center Hospital in Texas City and later life flighted to UTMB Hospital in Galveston, TX. He passed away on Saturday morning approximately 6:20 A.M.

The boat was apparently full of Mexican immigrants who were unable to give accurate data in regards to their addresses, thier date of births, and were also unable to reveal to the reporting officer who the primary operator was, if any. On Saturday September 24, 2011 at approximately 3:30pm I Game Warden received a phone call from a local landowner about a truck that had been parked overnight at Coon Bridge Crossing on the Cibolo Creek and located a small flat bottom boat drifting in the creek downstream from the bridge.  Myself and Game Warden made the location and located the truck and checked registration.  The registration came back.  We soon after met with landowner and his wife and entered the property and located the boat that they informed us about.  The boat was indeed abandoned with the minnow bucket and aerator still running.  We examined the boat to see if there were any items left in the boat of importance and found bait and no life jackets and a bucket with misc items and no food or water of any kind.  I was able to ascertain a cell phone number for Victim and attempted to call it and only got voice mail.  I also was able to get ahold of a family member which happened to be his sister and asked if they had heard from or seen Victim and was informed that they hadn't heard from him since Friday Sept 23, 2011 a little after 5pm and had tried calling him numerous times and were unable to reach him.

I requested assistance from the local sheriff's office and had other officers make the scene as well as the local sheriff.  Captain my supervisor was also on scene for assistance and helped in the search.  After further investigation of the creek we located an oar floating in the creek just up stream from the boat as well as a baseball cap floating in the creek.  We made a couple more attempts at calling Victim's cell phone and finally located it in the boat inside of a coffee can with his wallet.  Several family members started to make the location to assist in searching for Victim by land.  We continued the search until we ran out of light to continue the next day.  Before we cleared the scene for the day we asked the family if Victim had any medical issues and they informed us that he was taking medication and had been in a couple of severe accidents in years past that caused him at times to have seizures as well as wake up some mornings and not remember who he was and had difficulty remembering things.

The next day Sunday September 25, 2011 we made the location again and started the search.  We were unable to recover a body that day but was able to find a fishing pole that was positively identified by his family as Victim's.  

On Monday September 26, 2011 at approximately 7:45am I located the body in very poor condition floating face down in the creek between the sandbar island in the middle of the creek and east bank where I stood.  The body was recovered from the creek by Karnes City Fire Department and positively identified.

On February 8, 2012 at 11:30 am, I State Game Warden received a call from the Limestone County Sheriff's Office that a boat was going in circles in the middle of Lake Mexia with no one in it.  I arrived at Lake Mexia to find the boat had been recovered by some fisherman.  The fisherman said that they saw a guy getting ready to launch the boat just after they had launched about an hour ago.  The fisherman did not see the man fall over board.  I found a type 2 personal flotation device, type 4 flotation device, and a set of keys in the boat.  I took the keys and looked in the truck and found identification.  The Limestone County Sheriff's Office sent an officer to the address on the drivers license to notify family that victim was missing.  

I launched my boat and started a bank search for him or any clues.  Game Warden arrived with a boat equipped with side scan sonar, and we started to search.  Around 12:30 pm we got an image that we believed to be a person.  Game Warden arrived to assist and got on board the boat.  We marked the location of the image with a bouy and started to drag.  We recovered the body at 5:10 pm.  Because of media and familly we met the Justice of the Peace at a different location on the lake.  The body was released to Blair-Stubbs Funeral Home, whom transported the body to Dallas Medical Examiner's Office for autopsy.

On March 17, 2012 at approximately 7:00 pm a rented tandem kayak was being paddled by individuals on Lake Buchanan near the Cedar Lodge Resort. On board were two adult males and two small boys. The boys, ages 4 and 6, were sitting in their father's laps. It is unkown what the cause was but the kayak capsized placing all ocupants in the water. The two small boys were wearing PFDs, which the rental company had supplied. The two adult males were not wearing a PFD. The adult passenger and his son were able to stay near the overturned kayak and hold on. The victim swam to his son and held him. The adult then swam to shore with his little boy. The witnesses, with a pontoon boat, headed from the shoreline out toward the other small boy but did not see any other adult. The adult had boarded the pontoon boat but could no longer see the victim. During this time a call had already been placed to the Llano County S.O. for assistance. The individuals in the pontoon picked up the other small boy, placed a weighted buoy to mark where the victim was last seen and secured the kayak. Llano County deputies arrived on scene and took statements. The Buchanan Dam Volunteer Fire Dept. arrived with a rescue boat and the Kingsland Dive Team entered the water at around 8:00pm. Texas Parks and Wildlife game wardens and LCRA rangers also arrived on scene. At approximately 9:15 pm the body was recovered. The deceased was pronounced dead and transported to Putnam Funeral Home in Kingsland, Texas.

According to wife, Operator left to go fishing on April 8, 2012 at about 3 or 4 pm with his kayak.  On April 9, 2012 at about 1:30 pm, a witness saw a kayak floating on the lake.  He noticed that it did not have anyone onboard.  He launched his boat and at about 2 pm he arrived at the kayak and found Operator’s wallet and keys on the kayak.  Game Wardens found Operator’s body floating in the lake at 6:41 pm.  He was already deceased and was still wearing his life jacket. Buckles on the PFD were improperly attached. A tox screen is pending.   

Autopsy was done on April 10, 2012. Cause of death noted was drowning.

Accident Conclusion: After reviewing the corroborating witness statements and assessing the scene and circumstances Officer believes that, other than the fact that unbeknownst to the driver the 3 passengers were sitting in an area that is unsafe to sit in under power, that the driver did nothing to directly cause or contribute to this accident. The Victim appears to have been attempting to shift her position and partially stand up at the same moment the boat struck a wave or wake causing her to fall forward off of the vessel, go underneath between the pontoons and strike the propeller causing large lacerations, massive blood loss and ultimately death from the sustained injuries.

Vessel one was travelling southwest across the Lower Laguna Madre. The operator and passengers stated that they could see several personal watercraft operating in the distance. As they travelled south west across the bay it appeared that they were in a colliding path with one of the PWC's. The operator changed his course of travel so as to avoid the collision. 

The operator of vessel 2, the PWC, crossed the boat's path and performed a circular spin and then reversed its direction of travel. 

The operator of vessel 1 stated that they were again on an intersection path and he again changed his course of travel. 

The operator of vessel 2 then performed a second circular maneuver and accelerated out of the circle in a straight line. Vessel 2 impacted vessel one on the port side of vessel 1 and the starboard side of vessel 2. Vessel 1 ramped over the top of vessel 2. The operator of vessel 2 was able to jump clear of the collision. The passenger of vessel 2 was forced under vessel 1. The propeller from vessel 1 cut across the stern of vessel 2 and through the passenger's head. 

The passenger of vessel 2 suffered severe head trauma from the propeller strike and died almost instantly. 

Witnesses from a nearby vessel livery heard the collision and responded immediately to get the victims out of the water. 

Vessel 1 was operating within the Parks and Wildlife Code with all applicable water safety equipment. Not At Fault 

Vessel 2 was a PWC operated by an individual born after 10/1/1993 who should have completed a basic boater education course PWC 31.109 
Vessel 2 was the give way vessel in the collision PWC 31.093 
Vessel 2 was a PWC operating greater than headway speed within 50' of another vessel PWC 31.106(4) 

Vessel 2 was rented from a vessel livery who failed to give proper instruction as to the applicable personal watercraft laws for safe operation PWC 31.111(b)(1)m

On 5/12/2012, at approximately 7:00 PM, I, Texas State Game Warden, was on patrol with Warden Calvin Christian in George West, Texas. I received a call about an individual who capsized his kayak at Tips Park, located Northwest of Three Rivers, TX. Warden and I arrived on scene and met Sgt. with the Three Rivers Police Department.  

Sgt. informed us that an individual, later identified, was kayaking over the low head dam when his boat capsized and he drowned. Sgt. stated there was a witness that was with Operator during the accident. 

The witness was identified. Witness stated that he and Operator had known each other for approximately two years and had been kayaking together several times before. Witness stated he was going to videotape Operator going over the dam. Operator was wearing his personal flotation device with a .357 Taurus hand gun attached to the front. Also, Operator had a dry bag inside a compartment which contained his ID, wallet, personal effects, and a model 32 Glock hand gun.

Operator went over the dam and immediately the kayak capsized. Both Operator and the Kayak went under water. Periodically, both the kayak and Operator would come up resurface and then go back down again. This action was caused by the hydraulics of the dam producing an undertow.  Witness got in his kayak to try and help Operator, but Witness felt his kayak being pulled into the current so he bailed out only three feet from shore. Witness’s kayak was pulled by the current to the dam and was then caught in the undertow of the current. 

Operator and his kayak eventually resurfaced and Operator was seen drifting down river from the dam floating face down with his PFD still on.  Operator was pulled out of the river approximately one quarter mile down river from the dam by two firefighters from the Three Rivers Fire Department. Judge Chapa, the Justice of the Peace, stated he believed it was a bad accident and pronounced deceased at 7:45 PM.  Operator’s .357 Taurus was not attached to his PFD when he was recovered.  Operator’s kayak and paddle was found the next day approximately two miles downriver from the dam; however, the dry bag with his wallet, ID, Glock handgun and personal effects were never recovered.

Vessel 1 was heading South/Southwest around Queen's Point of Oakland Park on Lake Lewisville. Operator said the victim had not been paddling for the last twenty miles.  Operator felt that victim had drunk too much water.  Operator stopped next to shore to rest and victim fell overboard when operator shoved off.  Victim went to the bottom of the river (about 4 feet) and operator swam down and recovered him. The following information was compiled from statements taken from three people:  On the afternoon of July 4th, victim and Subject left Subject’s and proceeded to the  Top Water Grill, where they were joined by Operator and his wife at approximately 2:00 pm.  This was the first time operator and wife had met Victim.  According to Subject and Operator, the group had lunch and a few alcoholic beverages.     
From the Top Water Grill restaurant all four preceded to Subject’s residence where they spent a short period socializing and according to Operator, having another alcoholic beverage.  Operator stated that Victim brought up the issue that he (Victim) owned a boat and that Victim asked Operator if he would like to go for a boat ride.  Victim and Operator proceeded to Victim’s residence.  From there, they departed from Victim’s residence in Victim’s boat, a 1998 22ft Glacier Bay, Texas registration number, TX 1602 BR.  According to Operator, the two travelled by boat from Victim’s residence,  to a second restaurant, Latitudes.  Operator stated that they had another alcoholic beverage at the restaurant, Latitudes.  
From there, the two were on their way back to Victim’s residence (traveling south from Kemah) when,  Victim slowed the vessel to an idle speed to urinate.   Victim stepped to the rear of the vessel, at which time Operator (standing at the controls of the vessel) looked away or towards the bow of the vessel.  When Operator turned around and looked back towards the stern of the vessel, Victim was gone.  Operator stated that he did not hear a splash nor did he see Victim in the water.  In an effort to determine whether Victim was committing a prank or some form of a joke, Operator contacted Subject by cell phone.  Subject advised Operator that this was no joke, at which time Operator called 911.  

The Galveston County Sheriff’s office received a 911 call from the cell phone of Operator  at 6:18 p.m. and the Coast Guard was notified by the Sheriff’s office at 6:22 p.m.  Operator  continued to look for Victim until Subject (with the assistance from a neighbor) arrived at the location of the incident in Neighbor’s vessel.  According to Neighbor, the location where they searched for Victim was the bay waters north of Eagle Point, adjacent to 12th-14th St, ¼ mile off the shoreline.  The Galveston County Sheriff’s marine division, U.S. Coast Guard and TPWD Game Wardens responded to the location and initiated a search for Victim.  Victim’s vessel, Operator and Subject were escorted to Eagle Point Marine, San Leon where they were both questioned about the incident.  According to Petty Officer Williams USCG, Victim’s body was located at approximately 7:39 p.m., at GPS coordinates N 29 30.302 / W 094 54.379, Galveston Bay Chambers County.  From that location, the USCG transported Victim’s body to the Eagle Point Marina, San Leon, where medical personnel continued administering CPR.  At approximately 7:59 p.m., Victim was pronounced deceased.  
The standard field sobriety tests were administered to Operator, at which time Operator displayed signs of intoxication.  Operator was transported to Mainland Center Hospital where a sample of his blood was secured for toxicology testing.  
An inventory of the vessel, TX 1602 BR was secured and detailed photographs taken.  No alcoholic containers were discovered nor were there any signs of blood found.  According to Operator, Subject and Neighbor, no items were removed from the vessel prior to the inspection conducted by the Game Wardens.

On July 14th, 2012 at approximately 6:30 pm. Game Warden received a call from Capt. about a boat accident that had occurred in Cedar Bayou, near Roseland Park boat ramp in Chambers County TX.  Warden arrived on scene at approximately 7:00 pm and spoke with the Baytown Fire Dept. to get updated on the situation.  Fire Depart told Warden that at approximately 4:30 pm a Jon boat with two occupants collided with another boat just south of the boat ramp.  The occupants of the Jon boat were ejected into the water and the other vessel fled the scene.  One of the occupants of the Jon boat had been picked up by another passing vessel, but the driver of the Jon boat was still missing.  
  The passenger had sustained injuries from the collision.  He had scrapes to his right cheek and on his upper right back.  He also complained of pain in his right arm.  Warden spoke with V1 occupant to ask him what had happened.  He stated that he and his friend arrived at the boat ramp at approximately 1:30 pm.  They launched V1 occupant’s Jon boat and headed north from the boat ramp with V1 occupant driving the vessel.  They drove north for some time then turned around and headed back towards the boat ramp.  When they neared the boat ramp, they switched drivers and Operator1 began operating the jon boat.  They continued to head south towards the railroad trestles.  Approximately ½ mile past the trestles there was a curve in the bayou.  As they went around this curve V1 occupant saw another vessel heading  towards them.  V1 occupant described this boat as a white, v- bottom boat with a blue pinstripe.  It had chrome railing up front that extended out.  V1 occupant stated that there were 2 individuals in the vessels- possibly a white man and a Hispanic man.   Operator1  veered to the left and  the other boat moved in the same direction as Operator1.  V1 occupant felt that Operator1 tried to move back to the right but by this time the distance between the two vessels had closed and the two vessels collided.  V1 occupant states that the next thing he knew he was under water.  When he came up he looked around and saw the boat they had collided with slow down and look back.  Once they saw V1 occupant they got back up on plane and fled the scene.  V1 occupant then looked around for Operator1, but was unable to find him.  V1 occupant then flagged down a passing vessel and told them what had happened.  This vessel picked V1 occupant up and returned him to the boat ramp.  After Warden spoke with V1 occupant he was taken to the hospital for medical treatment.

I, Denton County Game Warden was notified by another officer that there had been boat accident on Lake Ray Roberts at approximately 10:25p.m. on 8-7-12.  As I arrived two subjects were being transported to Medical Center of Plano by Care flight.  Both subjects were passengers on the vessel at the time the accident happened.  Both subjects were ejected from the vessel at the time of impact.  One passenger had a serious laceration to his mid section (Injured victim) while the other sustained a tramatic head injury (Deceased victim). Deceased victim was located on the bow of the vessel just in front of the driver’s seat window and Injured victim was located on the bow as well.  At the time of the accident, the boat was on plane and ramped into the air after hitting the rock dam.  The vessel was located approximately 30-40 yards up onto the rock dam from the water line on its keel.  Deceased victim was laying on the rocks approximately 50 feet from the vessel up the dam closer to FM 455.  I was informed that there was a third subject wearing a green shirt and blue jeans in the back seat of a patrol deputy’s vehicle.  I identified him.  Operator had a very strong odor of an alcoholic beverage on his breath, blood shot eyes, and slurred speech and was extremely uncooperative.  Operator had a very confused demeanor.  He was not sure of how many occupants were on his boat at the time of the accident.  He kept saying that there were four passengers and there was only three onboard.  Operator admitted to drinking alcoholic beverages and that he was the owner of the vessel (TX 1541 RB).  Operator stated that he was not operating the vessel at the time of the accident.  Operator had blood all over him but was not injured.  Operator refused all medical attention.   A statement was acquired from one of the passengers of the vessel that Operator was operating the vessel at the time of the accident.  The other subject, Deceased victim, was not capable of giving a statement.       
Operator refused to do any SFST’s but indicated intoxication.  Operator was asked for a sample of his blood and refused to give a specimen. A specimen was taken at 1:23 a.m. on 8-8-12 at Denton Regional Hospital for a mandatory blood draw due to serious bodily injury caused during the accident.  Operator was transported to Denton County Pre- Trial and booked in for Intoxication Assault with a vehicle (Serious Bodily Injury).

On 07/20/2012 at approximately 11:15 am, I, Game Warden, received a call from the Aransas Pass Police Dept. (APPD) informing me that there had been a boating accident in Redfish bay and that a sixteen year old female had been severely injured.  At that time I was in Corpus Christi and informed the dispatcher that I would be in route shortly to assist in the accident investigation.  
     The operator was identified.  Game Warden and I identified ourselves as Texas Game Wardens and informed him that we were working together with the Aransas Pass Police Department on this accident. I asked Operator if he could take me to the location of the accident and give me a description of events that led up to the incident.  Operator stated that as he was making a wide turn the vessel swapped ends violently and without warning. Operator added that he was unsure as to the location of the accident due to the fact that it was his first time in Redfish Bay alone. Operator’s words “swapped ends” are taken to mean that the vessel spun on its axis, as a vehicle spins on a slippery surface.   Operator also stated that when the boat swapped ends on him, Victim was ejected from the vessel and struck by the propeller. I then asked Operator if he hit a sandbar or was in shallow water at the time of the accident.  Operator’s response was that he did not hit a sandbar and also that he was not in shallow water due to the fact that when he saw Victim face down in the water, He dove in to get her.
     By this time we were exiting Hampton's Landing Marina entering the Intra Coastal Waterway that runs North and South just east of Hampton’s Landing.  I asked Operator if anything looked familiar and if he could direct me to the location of the accident.  He struggled a little bit due to the fact of not knowing the area but after looking at landmarks such as the Dale Miller Bridge and can buoys along the ICW, he began to recollect the location.  He stated that he remembered a marker on the East side of the ICW and could take us to the site of the accident.
     We proceeded in an easterly direction in a channel that runs perpendicular to the ICW with Steadmans Reef on the North side and Ransom Island on the South side.  Operator began recalling landmarks on Ransom Island which led us a location that he believed was where the accident occurred.  The GPS coordinates for the scene of the accident were recorded as N 27 52’44.4”   W097 08’13.6”, which is due east from Hampton's Landing.

On Friday, 09/28/12, at approximately 1100 a.m., League City P.D. received a 911 call of about a jet ski accident on the public waterway of Clear Creek, Galveston County.  The portion of Clear Creek were the accident took place was on the east side of Highway 3 and the railroad bridge, coordinates of Lat. 29’31.093 and Long. 095’05.092. At approximately 1230 p.m. I arrived at the public boat ramp on FM 270 located in League City, Galveston County.   
While on scene I made contact with Det.  was informed by him that the body of the operator had been found.  The body/ operator/owner of the jet was identified.  Operator was operating a yellow and white jet ski(TX-4060-JA).  At approximately 1:00 p.m. the League City Marine Division brought the jet ski back to the public ramp. Upon inspection of the watercraft  I notice heavy damage to the bow.  This accident involved a single jet ski which struck a concrete pillar.  Det. informed me that the brother of the deceased was operating the other jet ski owned by Operator.  I made contact with the brother of the decedent who was identified.  I escorted Brother to my patrol unit with the assistance of Warden and I initiated the investigation.  The following are my findings; 

Brother said that he was visiting from Amarillo to attend his niece’s wedding scheduled for that day.  On 09/28/12 Operator asked Brother to come and ride his jet skies before the wedding.  Operator was very excited that his daughter was getting married.  At approximately 10:00 a.m. on 09/28/12 Operator and Brother arrived to the public boat ramp on Clear Creek/ FM 270 in League City, Galveston County.    After Operator (deceased) backed the two jet skis in the water, Brother got on board the blue jet ski and attempted to start it. At the same time Operator was on the yellow jet ski trying to start it.  After several attempts trying to start the yellow jet ski, Brother asked his brother if there was a problem.  Operator told Brother that he had to enter a code to override the starting mechanism.  When the jet ski was started Brother stated that Operator took off east under the bridge and then went back west up Clear Creek.   Operator was not wearing a life jacket.  Brother was still at the boat ramp.  Operator left Brother with the truck still running and trailer still in the water  Brother waited a minute to see if his brother was going to come back. When Operator did not come back, Brother, still at the dock, took the trailer out of the water and parked the truck.  Brother then got back onto the jet ski and begin to head west on Clear Creek looking for his brother Operator.  Approximately 1 minute later Brother found the jet ski Operator had been riding, floating in the water.  The jet ski was located on the east side of the Hwy 3 railroad bridge with severe damage to the bow of the watercraft.  Brother circled the area of the bridge in an attempt to locate Operator but could not find him.  Brother then went to a house on the south shoreline of the creek next to the railroad bridge to call 911. 
Several pictures were taken of the pillars and the area of the crash site.  Sgt. and I then visited the home owner of the house on the south shore line.  I asked the home owner if he had seen the accident and the informed me that he had not. He allowed Brother to use the phone to call 911 and for a short time assisted with looking for his missing brother.  After the interview Sgt. and I left the homeowner. 
According to Det., the deceased was found in the general area of the crash site. The deceased was observed face down with no signs of life. The Medical Examiner's Office cause of death was by blunt force.

While on duty on 6/18/2010 at approximately 0954, I received a call from dispatch about a boat that had capsized and there was still one victim in the water.  While responding from center street in Provo and I-15 dispatch said that a grandfather and grandson had been fishing in a small metal boat about 300 yds from shore off of the knolls area.  The boat had capsized and the grandson was able to make it to shore to call 911 but the grandfather was still in the water when the grandson left to get help.  Utah County Deputy said he was close by the marina and did I want him to help.  I said yes, and by the time I got my boat started he was at the north east dock and I picked him up.  We headed towards the knolls in the 27ft rescue boat.  In the marina I turned on my lights and sirens and went full speed out of my marina.  The weather was warm and calm, the water was like glass.  Before we arrived on scene the search and rescue plane was circling over the area where the boat capsized.  LT from Utah County from the airplane, said that he could see a person in the water that looked like they were collecting debris from the boat and that they had a life jacket on. 

 I continued responding full speed until I got closer to the area.  It is known to be a rocky and shallow area.  DEPUTY spotted a person in the water with a life jacket on, as we approached we noticed he was holding on to person who was face down in the water.   I yelled to turn the guy over, he was able to do so.  We pulled along side and myself and DEPUTY pulled the face down victim out of the water, who we later found out was DECEASED. His eyes were open but with a blank stare, his skin was cold to the touch, and he appeared life-less.  We laid him across the back deck of the boat and DEPUTY turned the victim to his side and pounded on his back to get water out of his lungs.  He then checked for breath and pulse, I  was looking for a CPR mask during that time, also the other man in the water pulled himself into the boat. DEPUTY had begun CPR when I found the mask and I went to the head to help. The first two breaths I did, didn't go in so I retilted the head and did two more breaths.  Those two went in but there sounded like there was a lot of water inside Deceased.  Several times we had to turn the head because vomit and water kept coming out and filling the mask. During this time I did get a little of the victims vomit in my mouth.  After a few sets of CPR, during which we were hearing talk over the radio on where to send Life Flight to get access to the victim, DEPUTY and I decided we needed to get to a marina to meet Life Flight because I did not think I could safely get my boat close enough to shore to get the victim of the boat at our current location.  I stopped CPR and had good samaritan help DEPUTY with CPR. 

 I notified dispatch that I would be taking the victim to the Saratoga Springs Public Marina.  About half way to the marina, Saratoga Springs Fire department met us on their boat.  I stopped and had one of their paramedics come aboard and help DEPUTY with patient care.  I was driving the boat so I did not see a lot but I believe the paramedic intubated the victim and they continued CPR.  The ambulance was waiting for us at the dock in the marina.  We got the victim on the stretcher and they took him to the ambulance until Life Flight arrived.  

While the paramedics had the victim in the ambulance I had a chance to talk with the other guy in the water that had been holding on to the victim.  He had been nearby when the grandson ran on shore to find a cell phone to call 911.  The good samaritan ran around the small point at the knolls and could see the capsized boat.  He swam out to the boat and was able to flip it over.  He found a PFD and put it on and continued to search for the deceased.  By the time he found him deceased was already face down in the water.

At approximately 1830 hrs on 9/24/12 the houseboat "NO FEAR" (Vessel 2) was anchored to shore in Padre Canyon, when the wind was becoming stronger.  A wind gust blew Vessel 2 off it's anchors and the vessel started to drift away in the wind.  Multiple people tried to start the motors on Vessel 2 to try and get control of the boat and park it back on shore.  Nobody was able to get the vessel started.  The people on board became panicked as the vessel continued to drift in the wind without means to control the boat.

At this time Victim boarded a PWC (Vessel 1), without putting on a PFD, to go to a nearby houseboat (Bravada One) to seek help.  Upon arriving at Bravada One, Subject agreed to assist VICTIM.  SUBJECT briefed another person on his vessel how to keep control of Bravada One in the wind storm and then boarded Vessel 1, without PFD, as the passenger behind VICTIM.  SUBJECT stated that when they were within approximately 20 yards of Vessel 2, the PWC died and VICTIM stated that the key/lanyard had fallen off into the water.  At this time VICTIM got off Vessel 1 and began swimming/searching in the water for the key.

SUBJECT then pulled on the kill switch of Vessel 1 and was able to start it and drive it the remaining distance to Vessel 2.  I presume that SUBJECT assumed that VICTIM would be able to swim over to Vessel 2.  Once SUBJECT boarded Vessel 2, he was able to get the engines started.  At this time Subject2 had boarded Vessel 1 and was trying to get it started and drive it out to look for/pick up VICTIM.  Vessel 2 was blowing/drifting into Vessel 1 at this time and SUBJECT2 had Vessel 1 capsize and go underneath Vessel 2.  SUBJECT2 was able to grab on the bow area of Vessel 2 when this happened and SUBJECT assisted him in re-boarding Vessel 2.  During this time Subject3 was on the top deck of Vessel 2 trying to call a captain to come assist them with driving the houseboat.  

Subject3 stated she saw VICTIM out in the water and he appeared to be yelling for help.  At this time she stated that VICTIM was in between Vessel 2's current location and the location where it had been anchored on the beach.  Subject4 had discovered that victim never got back on Vessel 2 around this time and boarded another PWC and began to search the water for VICTIM.  SUBJECT3 stated she tried to direct subject4 to the area where she had last seen him, but communications were difficult.

At this approximate time SUBJECT had gotten control of Vessel 2 and after checking for people in the water near the houseboat, he began driving it back to its original anchor location on the shore and he had informed the others on the houseboat of how VICTIM had jumped off Vessel 1 to look for the key.  I believe this is the first time when everybody realized that VICTIM was missing and out in the water somewhere.  As SUBJECT drove Vessel @ back toward shore, SUBJECT2 and SUBJECT3 continued to try and spot VICTIM from the top deck of the houseboat.  By this time it was getting dark and visibility was becoming poor.  When Vessel 2 was again on the shore, subjec5 also boarded a PWC and started searching the area for VICTIM.  When it became dark subject4 returned to Vessel 2 and called NPS for help.

Multiple NPS units responded and continued the search but were unable to locate VICTIM.  VICTIM was then presumed drowned.  The search for VICTIM was continued by NPS and UHP dive teams until 10/10/12 when VICTIM was located and recovered from approximately 100 ft deep water. 

CONCLUSIONS:  The ultimate cause of Victims death was his failure to wear a PFD when he boarded the PWC to go and seek help from the Bravada One  houseboat.

HARBOR MASTER saw the boat and noticed that the bow of the boat was up and it was moving west towards the marina.  At approximately 1715 hours HARBOR MASTER noticed that he couldn't see the boat any longer.  At that time he notified me, Assistant Park Manager of the Great Salt Lake Marina State Park, about the situation at hand.  HARBOR MASTER and Park manager went to the rescue boat, Rescue 1, and left the Marina mouth at approximately 1721 hours to perform a, "hasty search," for the boat. 

Rescue one headed east  towards the Lee Creek area to search for the boat.  At the time there were 1 to 2 foot waves, wind was 0 to 18 knots and the water temperature was 47 degrees.  There was a mix of rain and snow which caused the FORWARD LOOKING INFRA RED (FLIR) to be obscure.  During the search at approximately 1810 hours we noticed a heat source on the FLIR and went towards what we thought was the boat with the subjects aboard.
