THE VICTIMS FISHED IN THE BUCKHORN AREA BEFORE TRAVELING TO AN AREA NEAR THE BOY SCOUT CAMP. STEADY WINDS FROM THE SOUTH WEST CAUSED THE WATER TO BE FAIRLY ROUGH. AT SOME POINT THE TWO VICTIMS FELL OVERBOARD AND DROWNED. victim1 WAS RECOVERED 15 DAYS AFTER THE INCIDENT (APRIL 30). victim2 WAS RECOVERED 17 DAYS AFTER THE INCIDENT (MAY 2). BASED ON THE CLOTHING THE VICTIMS WERE WEARING WHEN THEIR BODY WAS RECOVERED --IT IS PRESUMED THAT victim1 MAY HAVE SWAM FOR SOME DISTANCE BEFORE DROWNING SINCE HE WAS NOT WEARING FOOTWEAR NOR A JACKET OR SWEATSHIRT. IT IS UNKNOWN IF victim2 HAD ATTEMPTED TO SWIM TO SHORE.
location: CASTLE ROCK LAKE - WIS RIVER, WI

description: BOAT WAS OPERATING IN SOUTHEAST DIRECTION WHEN INFLATABLE TUBE ON BACK OF BOAT CAME LOOSE & FELL OFF. DAUGHTER WAS SITTING ON COIL OF TUBE ROPE IN BOAT WHEN TUBE FELL OFF THE  BOAT. DAUGHTER BECAME ENTANGLED IN THE ROPE AS IT BEGAN TO FEED OUT OF THE BOAT. DAUGHTER WAS DRAGGED OVER BOARD. MOTHER THEN JUMPED OFF BOAT TO RESCUE DAUGHTER. DAUGHTER WAS SUCCESSFULLY PULLED INTO BOAT BY FATHER (BOAT OPERATOR) WITH MOTHER'S ASSISTANCE. AFTER DAUGHTER WAS RESCUED, FATHER-OPERATOR TURNED AROUND TO ASSIST WIFE-VICTIM TO GET INTO THE BOAT. MOTHER SANK BENEATH THE SURFACE BEFORE SHE COULD BE REACHED. BODY WAS RECOVERED NEXT DAY.

VICTIM-OPERATOR WAS OBSERVED KAYAKING NEAR SHORE. KAYAK WAS LATER OBSERVED FARTHER FROM SHORE UNOCCUPIED. NO WITNESS TO WHETHER OPERATOR VOLUNTARILY LEFT KAYAK OR FELL OVERBOARD. RESCUE BOATS ON SCENE OBSERVED STRONG 'UNDER CURRENT' & WIND WAS PREVAILING TO THE NORTHEAST AWAY FROM SHORE. TWO DAYS OF RESCUE SEARCH EVOLVED INTO SEARCH AND RECOVERY OPERATION. VICTIM BODY STILL NOT RECOVERED AS OF 11-1-2010.

BOAT#2 GOING SLOW WAS HEADING UP RIVER TURNED THE CORNER TO HEAD ACROSS TO FOGGES BLUFF. PWC#1 WAS HEADING DOWNSTREAM INTO SETTING SUN & STRUCK BOAT#2 NEARLY HEAD ON INJURING TWO PASSENGERS AND CAUSING A FATAL INJURY TO PASSENGER ON BOAT#2. PWC#1 OPERATOR CLAIMED HE WAS OBSTRUCTED BY THE SETTING SUN. WITNESS ACCOUNTS IDENTIFIED PWC#1 OPERATOR WAS GOING VERY FAST.

FISHING BOAT WITH THREE MEN ABOARD WERE TROLLING APROX 3 MILES EAST OF SHEBOYGAN HARBOR WHEN TWO OF THE BOAT 3 DOWNRIGGERS GOT CAUGHT ON  A COMMERCIAL FISHING NET ROPE TIED TO THE BUOY MARKING THE NET'S LOCATION. WHILE THE BOAT WAS CAUGHT-- HELD IN PLACE, TWO OF THE MEN WERE IN THE REAR OF THE BOAT ATTEMPTING TO UNTANGLE THE NET ROPE. THIS ACTION PLUS THREE FOOT WAVES OVER THE STARBOARD STERN CAUSED THE BOAT TO FILL RAPIDLY WITH WATER, CAPSIZING THE BOAT. TWO PASSENGERS FELL OVERBOARD WHILE THE OPERATOR-VICTIM WAS TRAPPED BENEATH THE OVERTURNED BOAT FOR A SHORT TIME .THE PASSENGERS CLIMBED & CLUNG TO THE BOTTOM OF THE CAPSIZED BOAT. NEITHER MAN COULD REACH THE OPERATOR-VICTIM WHEN HE SURFACED. ALL THREE MEN WERE RESCUED BY USCG VESSELS, BUT DURING THE RESCUE THE VICTIM SUFFERED A STRESS INDUCED HEART ATTACK AND WAS LATER PRONOUNCED DECEASED AT THE SHEBOYGAN HOSPITAL.

VICTIM WAS ONE OF THREE ABOARD A DRIFTING BOAT. VICTIM DECIDED TO ENTER THE WATER FOR A 'NATURE CALL'. VICTIM REMOVED HER CLOTHES AND TOOK A PFD WITH HER AS SHE ENTERED THE WATER. VICTIM LET GO OF THE PFD & WENT BELOW THE SURFACE. VICTIM DID NOT RESURFACE.

VICTIM WAS FOUND FLOATING FACE UP IN THE WATER NEAR HIS GROUNDED FISHING BOAT. VICTIM HAD AN INFLATABLE PDF ON -- BUT IT WAS NOT FASTENED ON THE VICTIM CORRECTLY. THE COLLAR WAS IN FRONT OF HIS FACE, NOT BEHIND THE HEAD TO KEEP THE HEAD ABOVE WATER.

ON JULY 4th, VICTIM WAS RIDING ON A TUBE TOWED BY BOAT OPERATED BY HER SISTER'S BOY FRIEND. THE 13 YR OLD SISTER OF THE BOAT OPERATOR WAS ALSO RIDING ON THE TUBE. ABOUT 4 PM BOTH RIDERS FELL OFF THE TUBE WITH THE VICTIM'S KNEE STRIKING THE OTHER TUBE RIDER IN THE HEAD. WHEN THE BOAT CAME AROUND TO PICK UP THE TUBE RIDERS, THE INJURED RIDER NEEDED ASSISTANCE TO GET ABOARD THE BOAT AND MENTIONED HER KNEE REALLY HURT. THE OTHER TUBE RIDER CONTINED RIDING FOR AWHILE. THE INJURED TUBE RIDER HAD THE BOAT-OPERATOR DROP HER OFF AT THE BOAT OWNER'S DOCK. THEN THE INJURED TUBE RIDER THEN DROVE TO HER HOME. A WEEK LATER, HER PARENTS TOOK HER FOR MEDICAL TREATMENT AT AN EMERGENCY FACILITY FOR THE SEVERELY SWOLLEN LEG. SHE WAS TREATED AND WAS RELEASED. ON 7-24-10 VICTIM COLLAPSED AT HER PARENT'S HOME. 911 WAS CALLED FOR MEDICAL ASSISTANCE/TRANSPORT. THE VICTIM DIED AT THE MEDICAL FACILITY DUE TO A PULMINARY EMBOLISM CAUSED BY THE BOATING-TUBING INCIDENT INJURY.

BOAT WITH SIX PASSENGERS & OPERATOR ABOARD WAS TOWING TWO PEOPLE ON ONE TUBE. ONE TUBE RIDER FELL OFF & SWALLOWED SOME WATER & WAS ASKING FOR ASSISTANCE.  BOAT OPERATOR BROUGHT THE  BOAT NEAR THE FALLEN RIDER. BOAT OPERATOR (NOT WEARING PFD) LEFT THE BOAT TO ASSIST THE  FALLEN RIDER FIRST ONTO THE BOAT. THIS EFFORT WAS NOT SUCCESSFUL, SO THEY ATTEMPTED TO GET THE FALLEN RIDER BACK ONTO THE TUBE. THE DRIFTING BOAT WAS MOVING FARTHER AWAY FROM THE FALLEN TUBE RIDER & BOAT OPERATOR. THE FALLEN RIDER WAS UNABLE TO REBOARD THE TUBE SO THE BOAT OPERATOR BEGAN SWIMMING TOWARD HIS DRIFTING BOAT. NO ONE ON BOARD THE BOAT KNEW HOW TO OPERATE THE BOAT. BOAT WAS DRIFTING AWAY DUE TO STRONG WINDS & CHOPPY WAVES. BOAT OPERATOR ATTEMPTED TO REACH THE DRIFTING BOAT. WHEN THE OPERATOR GOT ABOUT 25 FEET FROM THE FALLEN RIDER, HE BEGAN STRUGGLING IN THE WATER. HE YELLED FOR HELP, WENT BELOW THE SURFACE. HE RESURFACED ONCE & YELLED FOR HELP THEN WENT UNDER WATER AND DID NOT RESURFACE. NEARBY BOATS WERE ALERTED TO THE SITUATION. ONE BOAT REACHED AND TOOK THE FALLEN TUBE RIDER BOARD THEIR BOAT. ANOTHER BOAT RESPONDED AND SEARCH FOR THE MISSING BOAT OPERATOR WITH NO SUCESS. THE DRIFTING BOAT HAD DRIFTED & WAS STRIKING A PIER. SOMEONE CAME DOWN TO THE PIER, BOARDED THE BOAT, AND OPERATED THE BOAT TOWARD THE AREA THAT THE VICTIM WAS LAST SEEN. THE OTHER TUBE RIDER WAS ABLE TO SWIM TOWARD & REBOARD THE BOAT.

ONE OF SEVEN PEOPLE ABOARD A CABIN MOTOR BOAT WERE DRINKING & DRIFTING ABOUT 2 MILES EAST OF MILWAUKEE HARBOR. ONE INDIVIDUAL DECIDED TO LEAVE THE BOAT & SWIM. THIS OCCUPANT DID NOT RESURFACE & WAS REPORTED MISSING. USCG CONDUCTED SEARCH PATTERNS WITH NO SUCCESS.  VICTIM'S BODY WAS FOUND NEARLY A MONTH LATER NEAR SHORE OF ST FRANCIS.

SOMETIME BETWEEN 1:30 & 2AM, BOAT OPERATOR & COMPANION BOARDED A PONTOON DOCKED AT PIER LOCATED AT W1626 CTH J, MUKWONAGO. THEY WENT FOR A SHORT RIDE AND RETURNED TO THE SAME LOCATION. OPERATOR-VICTIM HAD DIFFICULTY OPERATING THE PONTOON ONTO THE BOAT LIFT. THIS ACTION CAUSED THE COMPANION TO FALL INTO THE WATER. AFTER THE COMPANION GOT BACK ABOARD, OPERATOR-VICTIM TOLD COMPANION TO GO INTO THE RESIDENCE AND HE WOULD COMPLETE OPERATING THE BOAT ONTO THE LIFT. AROUND 6:30AM, THE SAME MORNING, THE OPERATOR'S GIRLFRIEND WAS LOOKING FOR HIM. SHE NOTICED THE PONTOON WAS ADRIFT NEXT TO A PIER AT W1622 CTH J WITH NAVIGATION LIGHTS ON & MOTOR ENGAGED IN REVERSE BUT NOT RUNNING. AUTHORITIES WERE CALLED. VICTIM'S BODY WAS LOCATED BY DIVE TEAM AT ABOUT 3:30PM SAME DAY IN 9 FT DEEP WATER. VICTIM WAS NOT WEARING PFD.

BOAT OPERATOR-VICTIM STOOD UP TO START ENGINE. ENGINE WAS IN GEAR. WHEN ENGINE STARTED IT MOVED THE BOAT QUICKLY FORWARD TOSSING THE BOAT OPERATOR OVERBOARD. OPERATOR-VICTIM WAS A NON SWIMMER AND WAS NOT WEARING A PFD. THE OTHER BOAT OCCUPANT WAS A NON SWIMMER, SO HE DID HAVE THE MEANS TO REACH & SAVE THE VICTIM. ONLY ONE PFD WAS ABOARD THE BOAT.

OPERATOR & PASSENGER (MOTHER) WERE TRAVELING BETWEEN FISHING LOCATIONS AT APROXIMATELY 30 MPH. BOAT WAS TRAVELING EASTERLY THEN NORTHWESTERLY NEAR THE WEST SHORE OF THE LONG LAKE NARROWS.  THE NEXT THING THE OPERATOR REMEMBERS WAS BEING IN A MEDICAL HELICOPTER AND TOLD TO NOT MOVE. MEDICAL INVESTIGATION SURMISED THAT BOAT OPERATOR HAD A SEIZURE FROM A VASCULAR MALFORMATION ON HIS BRAIN. THE BOAT WAS FOUND GROUNDED ON THE WEST SHORE OF LONG LAKE NARROWS WITH PASSENGER (MOTHER) DECEASED. OPERATOR SUFFERED SEVERE INJURIES TO HEAD & BACK.

VICTIM & COMPANION WERE OPERATING IN SEPARATE KAYAKS ON LAKE SUPERIOR, ON A TRIP FROM LITTLE SAND BAY/TOWN OF RUSSELL BOAT LANDING NORTH TO SAND ISLAND. DUE TO WIND & HIGH WAVES KAYAKERS GOT SEPARATED. COMPANION HEADED NORTH & THEN WEST TO EAST BAY ON SAND ISLAND WHERE OTHER KAYAKERS WERE CAMPED. COMPANION CALLED NATIONAL PARK SERVICE & USCG FOR HELP. OVERTURNED KAYAK WAS RETRIEVED ABOUT .25 MILE OFF EAST SIDE OF SAND ISLAND BY NATIONAL PARK SERVICE. VICTIM WAS FOUND NEXT MORNING.

BOAT OPERATOR-VICTIM WAS DRIVING GRANDFATHER'S PONTOON BOAT FROM OWNER'S DOCK TO BOAT LANDING FOR REMOVAL FOR THE SEASON. GRANDFATHER OBSERVED PONTOON BOAT NOT MOVING ON THE LAKE & GRANDSON NOT SEEN ON THE BOAT. LAW ENFORCEMENT SERVICES WERE CONTACTED. VICTIM'S BODY WAS DISCOVERED AND REMOVED BY FIRE DEPT DIVERS.

BOAT OPERATOR-VICTIM LAUNCHED HIS BOAT AT GREEN BAY MUNICIPAL BOAT LANDING WITH INTENTION TO TRAVEL TO EAGLE'S NEST MARINA TO MEET A FELLOW DUCK HUNTER. AFTER HE DID NOT ARRIVE AT THE MARINA, THE OTHER DUCK HUNTER KEPT GOING BACK TO INITIAL BOAT LAUNCH SITE TO DETERMINE IF OPERATOR VICTIM HAD RETURNED TO THE BOAT LAUNCH. AFTER HOURS HAD PASSED,THE USCG & LAW ENFORCEMENT SERVICES WERE CONTACTED. USCG HELICOPTER LOCATED VICTIM'S BODY AT 12:30PM APROXIMATELY .5 MILE FROM SHORE. USCG VESSEL RETREIVED THE BODY.

CALLER TO EMERGENCY LINE REPORTED HEARING CALL FOR HELP ALONG THE WOLF RIVER. DNR WARDEN & TWO COUNTY DEPUTIES RESPONDED. SEARCH  FOUND UNOCCUPIED BOAT. SUBSEQUENT SEARCH FOUND VICTIM SUBMERGED IN WATER AND CAUGHT ON TREE SNAG IN RIVER. VICTIM WAS NOT WEARING PFD. INVESTIGATION SURMISED VICTIM WAS IN PROCESS OF UNTYING BOAT STERN LINE FROM A TREE WHEN HE LOST BALANCE AND FELL OVERBOARD STRIKING HIS HEAD ON THE TREE. VICTIM WAS FOUND 50 YARDS DOWNSTREAM OF BOAT.

VICTIM & COMPANION RENTED A ROWBOAT TO GO FISHING. AT ONE POINT THE WIND WAS BLOWING THE BOAT TOWARD SHORE. THE OCCUPANTS TRIED TO ROW THE BOAT OUT TO DEEPER WATER. WIND & WAVE ACTION TIPPED THE BOAT CAUSING THE OCCUPANTS TO FALL OVERBOARD. THE COMPANION FELL ONLY HALF WAY OUT OF THE BOAT & WAS ABLE TO REMAIN ABOARD THE ROW BOAT. THE VICTIM FELL OVERBOARD WITH UNSECURE PFD AND PFD FELL OFF. COMPANION ATTEMPTED TO THROW HIS PFD TO PERSON IN WATER. IT WAS NOT SUCCESSFUL. VICTIM ATTEMPTED TO FLOAT-SWIM BACK TO THE BOAT. VICTIM WENT UNDER WATER & DID NOT RESURFACE. COUNTY DIVE TEAM FOUND VICTIM A SHORT TIME LATER.

VICTIM & COMPANION WERE KAYAKING IN SEPARATE KAYAKS WHEN VICTIM'S KAYAK CAPSIZED DUE TO WAVES ON THE LAKE. VICTIM RESURFACED & STAYED WITH KAYAK AND TRIED SWIMMING KAYAK TOWARD A NEARBY WATER TRAMPOLINE. WHEN VICTIM APPROACHED THE TRAMPOLINE, HE WAS UNABLE TO GRAB & HOLD ONTO TRAMPOLINE & WENT UNDER THE SURFACE. VICTIM WAS RECOVERED & QUICKLY MOVED TO SHORE BY ANOTHER KAYAKER. VICTIM WAS GIVEN EMERGENCY MEDICAL ASSISTANCE (CPR) BUT HE FAILED TO RESPOND.

VICTIM WAS OPERATOR OF A SMALL SAILBOAT REPORTED MISSING ON 6-3-11 BY HIS SISTER WHO HAD STOPPED BY THE VACATION COTTAGE OF THE VICTIM. USCG SEARCH FOUND THE SAILBOAT ON SAT JUNE 4, FOUR MILES OFFSHORE OF PENSAUKEE RIVER--OCONTO COUNTY ON THE BAY OF GREEN BAY WITH NO OCCUPANT. VICTIM'S BODY WAS LATER RECOVERED ON SUNDAY JUNE 5, SOUTH OF WHERE SAILBOAT WAS LOCATED.

KAYAK #1 OPERATOR & 3 OTHER KAYAKERS LEFT LITTLE SAND BAY BOAT LAUNCH TOWARD SAND ISLAND TO CAMP OVERNIGHT. ALL FOUR MADE IT HALFWAY TO SAND ISLAND WHEN THE LAST KAYAK TOOK ON WATER. KAYAK #1 OPERATOR TURNED BACK TO HELP. WHEN HE DID HIS KAYAK WAS STRUCK BY 3 TO 4 FOOT WAVES FORCING HIS KAYAK TO ROLL HALF WAY OVER & BECOME PARTIALLY SUBMERGED. ONE OF THE OTHER KAYAKERS GRABBED ONTO THE FIRST KAYAKER IN TROUBLE AND TRANSPORTED HIM INTO SHORE AT SAND ISLAND. KAYAK#1 OPERATOR TOLD THE OTHERS THAT HE WAS OKAY & WOULD FOLLOW THE OTHER THREE TO SAND ISLAND. KAYAKER#1 WAS LAST SEEN ASTRIDE HIS PARIALLY SUBMERGED KAYAK (BOW DOWN IN WATER) FALLING BEHIND THE OTHER THREE. KAYAKER#1 WAS LATER FOUND FLOATING FACE UP ABOUT 200-300 YARDS AWAY FROM HIS OVERTURNED KAYAK. KAYAKER#1 WAS FOUND WEARING TYPE 3 PFD VEST, T-SHIRT, SHORTS & KAYAK SKIRT AND WITH HIS LEGS INSIDE A WET SUIT.

VICTIM & COMPANIONS WERE HAVING A CONTEST TO SEE WHO COULD STAY IN THE TUBE THE LONGEST. AS THE BOAT WAS PASSING UNDER THE BRIDGE, THE TUBE & RIDER STRUCK A CONCRETE PILLAR. THE BOAT & TUBE WERE TRAVELING IN A RELATIVELY STRAIGHT LINE WHEN APPROACHING THE BRIDGE. BUT INSTEAD OF PASSING AT A 90 DEGREE ANGLE UNDER THE BRIDGE & BETWEEN THE BRIDGE SUPPORTS, THE BOAT WAS DRIVEN AT AN ANGLE THAT BROUGHT THE TUBE & RIDER CLOSE TO ONE PILLAR AND STRIKING THE OTHER PILLAR MORTALLY INJURING THE TUBE RIDER. INVESTIGATION ENCOUNTERED RESISTANCE & MISINFORMATION IN DETERMING WHO WAS THE BOAT OPERATOR. THE CASE HAS BEEN REFERRED TO THE COUNTY DISTRICT ATTORNEY.

PWC#1 OPERATOR WITH ONE PASSENGER & DECK BOAT#2 WITH OPERATOR & 4 PASSENGERS WERE HEADING IN SAME DIRECTION WHEN DECK BOAT# 2 MADE A SHARP U-TURN TO THE LEFT. DECK BOAT OPERATOR ASSUMED PWC WAS BEHIND HIM ON THE RIGHT AFTER THE TURN, BUT SUDDENLY NOTICED THE PWC WAS COMING AT BOAT#2 FROM THE PORT SIDE. BOAT#2 OPERATOR ATTEMPTED TO TURN TO STARBOARD (RIGHT) TO AVOID CONTACT, BUT PWC STRUCK THE PORT STERN SIDE OF DECK BOAT#2. THE IMPACT THREW 2 PASSENGERS ON BOAT#2 INTO THE WATER & THE PWC OPERATOR & PASSENGER INTO THE WATER. PWC OPERATOR FELL INTO WATER AT BOAT#2 STERN & BECAME ENTANGLED IN BOAT#2 PROPELLER. PWC OPERATOR WAS PULLED ONTO DECK BOAT#2 BY HER STEP-FATHER/OPERATOR OF BOAT#2. PWC OPERATOR SUFFERED MASSIVE INJURIES & DIED ON WAY TO THE MEDICAL FACILITY.

AROUND MIDNIGHT SIX PEOPLE RODE A SMALL BOAT OUT TO AN ISLAND TO RECREATE. AROUND 3AM ON THEIR RETURN TO THE BOAT OWNER'S CABIN, THE BOAT TOOK ON WATER OVER THE BOW SINCE THE BOAT WAS OVERLOADED. WITH WATER RUSHING OVER THE BOW, THE PASSENGERS PANICKED & THE BOAT ROLLED OVER--CAPSIZED. OPERATOR & PASSENGERS (EXCEPT ONE) STAYED NEAR THE CAPSIZED BOAT. ONE PERSON (VICTIM) SWAM FOR THE SHORE TO GET HELP OR A CANOE TO RETURN TO THE OVERTURNED BOAT. THIS SWIMMER GOT HALF WAY TO THE SHORE & YELLED FOR HELP. TWO PASSENGERS THEN LEFT THE BOAT & SWAM TOWARD THE VICTIM. TWO WITNESSES IN A CANOE REACHED THE VICTIM FIRST & TRANSPORTED HIM TO SHORE WHERE CPR WAS PERFORMED. CPR WAS CONTINUED BY MILLTOWN EMS WHO TRANSPORTED THE VICTIM TO A MEDICAL FACILITY WHERE HE WAS PRONOUNCED DEAD.

OPERATOR-VICTIM WAS ON A BOAT WITH FRIEND WHO WAS FISHING. VICTIM WOULD LEAVE THE BOAT TO GO SWIMMING AND RETURN. THE LAST TIME ACCORDING TO THE FRIEND ON THE BOAT, THE VICTIM WENT SWIMMING & CALLED FOR HELP AS THE BOAT WAS DRIFTING AWAY FROM HIM. THE PASSENGER WAS UNABLE TO START THE BOAT MOTOR OR THE TROLLING MOTOR TO MOVE THE BOAT CLOSER TO THE VICTIM-SWIMMER. THE VICTIM-SWIMMER DISAPPEARED BENEATH THE WATER SURFACE & DID NOT REAPPEAR. VICTIM'S BODY WAS FOUND BY MARKESAN WATER RESCUE TEAM ABOUT THREE HOURS AFTER HIS DISAPPEARANCE.

OPERATOR WITH THREE PASSENGERS LEFT MILWAUKEE HARBOR THROUGH THE BREAK WALL MAIN GAP. BOAT CRUISED AROUND LAKE MICHIGAN FOR AWHILE. UPON RETURN TO MILWAUKEE THE BOAT STRUCK THE BREAK WALL HALF MILE SOUTH OF THE MAIN GAP. AFTER IMPACT THE BOAT DROPPED DOWN INTO THE WATER WITH STERN ON LAKE BOTTOM & BOW ABOVE WATER SURFACE RESTING ON BREAKWALL. OPERATOR & PASSENGERS WERE EJECTED FROM THE IMPACT INTO THE WATER. THREE PASSENGERS WERE RESCUED FROM THE BREAK WALL. THE BOAT OPERATOR-VICTIM WAS FOUND LATER AROUND NOON THE SAME DAY FLOATING NEARBY.

3 PERSONS WERE ABOARD A DRIFTING BOAT. ONE PASSENGER LEFT BOAT TO SWIM WITHOUT A PFD. SOON AFTER THE OTHER PASSENGERS NOTICED THE SWIMMER STRUGGLING IN THE WATER. THEN BOTH REMAINING PASSENGERS LEFT THE BOAT WITHOUT PFD, AND SWAM TO THE STRUGGLING SWIMMER. BOTH ARRIVED AT THE STRUGGLING SWIMMER & KEPT HIS HEAD ABOVE WATER. ONE STAYED WITH THE STRUGGLING SWIMMER WHILE THE OTHER (VICTIM) SWAM FOR THE DRIFTING BOAT. A SHORT TIME LATER STRUGGLING SWIMMER & COMPANION WERE RESCUED BY A PASSING BOAT WHICH TOOK THEM BACK TO THEIR BOAT. THAT IS WHEN THE PERSON (VICTIM) SWIMMING TO THE DRIFTING BOAT WAS NOT FOUND ABOARD & MISSING. RESCUED BOAT OPERATOR & PASSENGER DROVE THE BOAT TO THE LAKE GENEVA COUNTRY CLUB TO CALL EMERGENCY. WITHIN AN HOUR A DIVE RESCUE TEAM RECOVERED THE VICTIM FROM THE BOTTOM OF LAKE. VICTIM WAS TRANSPORTED BY FLIGHT FOR LIFE TO MILWAUKEE HOSPIAL WHERE HE WAS PRONOUNCED DECEASED.

THREE WOMEN ABOARD PONTOON RETURNING FROM  WENDT'S LAKESIDE SUPPER CLUB. WHEN THE PASSENGER- VICTIM WALKED TOWARD FRONT OF BOAT & FELL OVERBOARD. BOAT OPERATOR TURNED MOTOR OFF& PLACED BOAT MOTOR INTO NEUTRAL. OPERATOR THEN REMOVED HER PANTS & DOVE UNDER BOAT TO LOCATE VICTIM. VICTIM'S SWEATSHIRT WAS ENTANGLED IN THE PONTOON MOTOR PROPELLER. BOAT OPERATOR TRIED TO KEEP VICTIM'S HEAD ABOVE WATER. PASSENGER CALL TO 911 FAILED. PASSENGER CALLED PREVIOUS PASSENGER LOCATED AT THE SUPPER CLUB. PREVIOUS PASSENGER & FRIEND WENT LOOKING FOR PONTOON & FRIENDS ON LAKE. (ASSISTING PONTOON OPERATOR ASSISTED IN REMOVING VICTIM & TRANSPORTING VICTIM TO LANDING WHERE COUNTY OFFICER & EMT WERE LOCATED. VICTIM WITHOUT PULSE OR BREATHING WAS TRANSPORTED TO HOSPITAL. COUNTY CORONER DETERMINED VICTIM'S DEATH WAS DUE TO SEVERE TRAUMA-INJURY & DROWNING.

VICTIM WAS OPERATOR DRIVING A PONTOON BOAT WITH THREE FAMILY MEMBERS ABOARD, FROM MAIN LAKE TO SPRING LAKE OF THE LEGEND LAKE CHAIN. AFTER ARRIVING AT TOMOW'S BAY ON LEGEND LAKE, OPERATOR STOPPED THE MOTOR. BOAT WAS DRIFTING SLOWLY. THE OPERATOR, HIS BROTHER-IN-LAW, AND HIS NIECE WENT SWIMMING--DIVING FROM THE FRONT OF THE PONTOON BOAT. BROTHER IN-LAW, AND NIECE SWAM BACK TO THE SWIM PLATFORM AT THE BACK OF PONTOON BOAT. BOAT OPERATOR'S SON HAD REMAINED ABOARD. WHEN THE TWO SWIMMERS RETURNED TO DECK OF THE PONTOON, THEY NOTICED OPERATOR-VICTIM WAS NOT SEEN ON BOAT OR IN THE WATER. BROTHER-IN LAW MADE NUMEROUS ATTEMPTS TO LOCATE THE VICTIM WHILE HIS DAUGHTER CALLED 911. TWO DIVE TEAMS & OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENT ARRIVED & CONDUCTED SEARCH EFFORTS UNTIL DUSK. VICTIM'S BODY WAS FOUND EARLY THE NEXT MORNING FLOATING ON SURFACE OF THE LAKE. CORONER PRONOUNCED DEATH DUE TO ACCIDENTAL DROWNING.
location: SPRING LAKE - LEGEND LAKE CHAI, WI

description: PRELIMINARY FINDING: BOTH BOATS WERE OPERATING AT PLANING SPEED (BOTH THROTTLES WERE FOUND ALL THE WAY FORWARD. THE DIRECTION OF MOVEMENT IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME. IT IS PRESUMED BOAT#1 PORT SIDE WAS STRUCK BY THE FORWARD PORTION OF BOAT#2 DUE TO THE DAMAGED FORWARD 1/3 PORTION OF BOAT#2 AND WITH THE FRONT RIGHT CORNER OF BOAT#2 CURLED UP & BACKWARD. BOAT#1 PASSENGER WAS INJURED & THE OPERATOR WAS KILLED. BOAT#2 OPERATOR WAS SLIGHTLY INJURED AS WAS ONE PASSENGER. THREE PASSENGERS ON BOAT#2 WERE KILLED BY THE IMPACT. WAITING FOR SUBMITTAL OF THE ACCIDENT RE-CONSTRUCTION REPORT

VICTIM WAS OBSERVED FISHING ALONE. WITNESSES LATER HEARD VICTIM YELLING FOR HELP & VICTIM WAS OBSERVED IN THE WATER NEXT TO THE ANCHORED ROWBOAT. WHEN ASSISTANCE ARRIVED, VICTIM WAS FOUND FLOATING FACE DOWN, NOT BREATHING & NON RESPONSIVE. VICTIM WAS LOADED ONTO BOAT & TAKEN TO THE PIER LOCATED AT N739 PARK DRIVE. CORONER ARRIVED AT SCENE & DECLARED VICTIM DECEASED. THE AUTOPSY DETERMINED THE VICTIM DIED FROM CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE -- NOT DROWNING. EVALUATION OF WITNESS REPORTS, SCENE DESCRIPTION & EVALUATION, & CORONER REPORT (DETERMINED VICTIM DIED FROM CARDIAC ARREST). CAUSE OF DEATH WAS ATTRIBUTED TO CARDIAC ARREST DUE FROM CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE BROUGHT ON FROM FALLING OVERBOARD, AND PANIC??.

VICTIM & GIRLFRIEND WERE FISHING. VICTIM STOOD UP IN BACK OF BOAT TO URINATE. VICTIM LOST BALANCE & FELL OVERBOARD CAUSING BOAT TO TIP & PASSENGER-GIRL FRIEND TO FALL OVERBOARD. BOAT FILLED WITH WATER & WAS 3/4 FILLED WITH WATER. VICTIM & PASSENGER ATTEMPTED TO SWIM TO SHORE. WHILE SWIMMING, VICTIM BECAME DISTRESSED & WENT UNDER THE SURFACE. PASSENGER-GIRL FRIEND SWAM TO VICTIM & ATTEMPTED TO HOLD VICTIM'S HEAD ABOVE THE WATER. A PONTOON BOAT CAME BY TO ASSIST IN RESCUE EFFORT. THE PASSENGER-GIRL FRIEND & TWO PERSONS ON THE PONTOON WERE ABLE TO GET THE VICTIM ONTO THE PONTOON BOAT. CPR WAS INITIATED & CONTINUED UNTIL PONTOON BOAT REACHED DILLY LAKE BOAT LANDING. GROUP CONTINUED CPR UNTIL AMBULANCE ARRIVED. VICTIM WAS TRANSPORTED TO SPOONER HOSPITAL WHERE VICTIM WAS PRONOUNCED DECEASED.

People  on washington island reported seeing an individual clinging to a capsized canoe about 500 yards or further out from shore. When rescue boats arrived to the scene, no one was observed in or around the canoe.  Another person who was in the canoe before it capsized was found to have swam about 500 yards from the capsized canoe to shore to get help. Investigation determined per interview of the survivor of this incident, the two men had walked down to the beach. They decided to take the canoe out into the lake. The one pfd in the canoe was very wet so it was left behind. They paddled south for about .25 mile when they decided to turn around. During the turning manuever, the canoe became unbalanced and the survivor fell overboard. In subsequent attempts by the man in the water, to reboard the canoe, the canoe capsized throwing the 'victim' into the water. Both men made several attempts to upright the canoe with no success. The survivor decided to swim for shore while the other man stayed with the canoe. The survivor swam an estimated 5oo yards to shore. Once on shore the survivor went to many residences along the north shore & discovered they were empty and closed for the season. The survivor eventually made it back to the residence they originally left, and someone in the residence called 911. Uscg, dnr, door county sheriff & washington island police dept. Le personnel conducted a search of the area until darkness. The following two days of continued search did not find the victim's body. It remains missing.

VICTIM HAD BEEN DRINKING WITH FAMILY MEMBERS THE NIGHT OF 11-5-11. LATER THAT NIGHT THE VICTIM LEFT HIS CABIN & KAYAKED TO TWIN OAKS RESORT. VICTIM CONSUMED SEVERAL MORE DRINKS. On 5-25-12 at 2:11pm, the fond du lac county sheriff's dept was notified of a body floating in the middle of lake winnebago. At approximately 2:52pm, the body was recovered by the fond du lac sheriff dept dive team and transported to the brothertown harbor. Body was recovered in calumet county waters. Victim was not wearing a pfd, and had been in the water for days. Winnebago county sheriff dept determined the victim's vehicle and boat trailer had been parked at the black wolf boat landing for about five days. At the time of the officer's investigation report, the victims boat had not been found. Autopsy performed on 5-26-2012by the fond du lac county me office determined cause of death was drowning. the boat registered to the victim was a 1973 14 ft aluminum mirror boat with either a 25 or 50 hp motor. The boat sat very low in the water due to the installation of a false floor (added weight). The friend who did not accompany the victim this time, surmised the victim likely went out early sunday morning when the lake was calm and a clear sky. Then when the weather later changed and the water became rougher, he  presumed the victim began to return to shore and likely encountered higher waves that broke over the side of the boat since it sat so low in the water, and likely filled with water and sunk or capsized. The victim was found wearing a rain suit but not a pfd. Victim had told his friend that he needed to get a new larger pfd to fit over his rain suit.

Victim was sailboat operator racing in a sailboat regatta. The sailboat overturned when rounding the first pin. The self inflating pfd worked when operator-victim fell into the water. The victim-operator attempted to upright his sailboat with assistance by some race officials. He then began to struggle in the water during this attempt. Race officials attempted to get the victim out of the water onto their ski boat, but were unable to do this do to the victim's extreme obesity. A nearby pontoon boat was called to help the victim. Prior to the pontoon boat's arrival. The victim continued to struggle in the water and became unconscious. Pontoon arrived and people aboard were successful in getting the victim aboard. By this time the victim had no pulse and was not breathing. Pontoon transported victim to shore where county sheriff office ems were waiting to transport victim to a hospital. Victim was pronounced deceased at the hospital. County medical examiner autopsy determined victim died from myocardial infarction (heart attack) while struggling in the water. Autopsy found severe coronary atherosclerosis and aoritic stenosis in the victim likely do to his morbid obesity (5'6", 266 pounds).

On september 5, 2010, it was reported that the operator had taken an inflatable pontoon type raft out to try to retrieve a boat which had blown away from shore.  The reporting party had last seen the operator about 100-150 yards e-se from solider rock at 11:00-11:30 pm.  A game warden and a ranger went out in a boat to try and find the operator, while other rangers searched the shoreline.  The pontoon raft was located washed ashore about 1/4 miles from the boat that had blown away and a paddle was found floating a few yards from the pontoon raft.  The search continued until 02:30 am on september 6th.  Due to rough conditions and limited visibility, it was decided to forgo any searching by boat until dawn.  It was also decided that additional assistance and equipment was needed, as it was felt that the operator had probably succumbed to hypothermia and or drowning.  Rangers continued searching the shore throughout the night.  At around 6:30 am, game wardens began searching the reservoir with side scan sonar equipment.  Dive teams and cadaver dog specialists arrived around 8:00 am.  A game warden and the dog teams marked a location where three different dogs indicated a body may be.  The reservoir was searched with side scan sonar throughout the day until about 7:45 pm, when efforts were turned over to platte county search and rescue.  On september 12th at around 10:00 am, the body of the operator was found floating ne of hall's marina.  Much decomposition had occurred and the body was identified by wallet containing identification in the victims pocket.  The body had decomposed to the point where blood and/or urine could not be tested for drug or alcohol.

THE BOAT WAS ANCHORED AND THE THREE OCCUPANTS WERE FISHING.  SOMEONE SHIFTED POSITIONS.  THE STERN WENT UNDER AND THE BOAT BEGAN TAKING ON WATER.  THE BOW FLIPPED UP, THE BOAT ROLLED TO STARBOARD.  THE OPERATOR FLIPPED BACKWARDS OFF THE STERN AND FELL INTO THE WATER.  ONE OF THE PASSENGERS DOVE OUT FROM THE PORT SIDE.  THE OTHER PASSENGER REMAINED ON THE BOAT.  WHEN THE OPERATOR AND PASSENGER SURFACED, THEY SWAM TO THE BOAT WHICH WAS ANCHORED AT THE BOW AND NEARLY FULL OF WATER.  THE PASSENGER IN THE WATER DECIDED TO SWIM TO SHORE.  THEY WERE ABOUT 20 YARDS FROM SHORE.  THE BOAT SEEMED TO BE HELD DOWN BY THE ANCHOR.  THE OPERATOR WENT AROUND TO THE BOW AND CUT THE ANCHOR LINE.  THE OPERATOR LOOKED OVER FOR THE PASSENGER IN THE WATER AND SAW ONLY HIS JACKET FLOATING IN THE WATER.  SO, THE OPERATOR AND THE PASSENGER (IN THE BOAT) PULLED AND ROWED THE BOAT TO LOOK FOR THE PASSENGER.  THEY FOUND HIM FACE DOWN IN THE WATER.  THE OPERATOR PERFORMED CPR.  HE PULLED HIM A SHORT DISTANCE AND THEN WAS ABLE TO STAND UP WITH HIM IN CHEST DEEP WATER THEN GOT HIM TO SHORE.  THE OPERATOR PERFORMED CPR FOR ABOUT 15 MINUTES WHILE THE OTHER PASSENGER WENT FOR HELP.  FREMONT COUNTY SHERIFFI'S OFFICE AND EMT'S ARRIVED.  THEY WERE NOT ABLE TO REVIVE HIM AND HE WAS PRONOUNCED DEAD.

AT 1:45 P.M., THE OPERATOR LAUNCHED HIS CANOE ON THE GREEN RIVER WITH FOUR OCCUPANTS.  THE GREEN RIVER WAS EXTREMELY HIGH, FLOODING OUT OF ITS BANKS.  AFTER 45 MINUTES TO 1 HOUR, THE MOTOR QUIT WORKING AND THE OPERATOR (GRANDFATHER) AND ONE OF THE OCCUPANTS (FATHER) USED PADDLES TO STEER.  THEY APPROACHED AN ISLAND AND IMPACTED THE POINT OF THE ISLAND WITH THE STARBOARD SIDE OF THE CANOE, CAUSING THE CANOE TO ROLL COUNTER CLOCKWISE, EJECTING ALL FIVE OCCUPANTS.  THE GRANDFATHER AND FATHER WERE ABLE TO GET TWO OF THE CHILDREN TO SHORE.  THE CANOE AND THE OTHER CHILD WERE RECOVERED APPROXIMATELY 5 MILES FURTHER DOWNSTREAM.  THE CHILD DROWNED.  HE WAS WEARING A PFD THAT WAS AN ADULT SMALL/MEDIUM.  THE STRAPS WERE TIGHTENED AS FAR AS POSSIBLE, RESULTING IN THE LEFT SIDE OVERLAPPING THE RIGHT SIDE.

ON AUGUST 20, 2011, AT APPROXIMATELY 4:30 P.M., A THUNDERSTORM WITH STRONG WEST WINDS CAME UP NEAR THE CAMP OF two folks.  AN INFLATABLE INNER TUBE BLEW INTO THE WATER AND OPERATOR2 WENT TO RETRIEVE IT USING A PWC.  OPERATOR2 BOARDED THE PWC AND WAS OPERATING WITHOUT A PFD.  THE PWC WAS INOPERABLE, BUT BEGAN FLOATING INTO THE BAY WITH OPERATOR2 STILL ABOARD.  OPERATOR1 GOT ONTO THE OTHER PWC TO RETRIEVE THE INNER TUBE AND ASSIST OPERATOR2.  HE WAS ALSO OPERATING WITHOUT A PFD. 

IN APPROXIMATELY FIVE MINUTES, OPERATOR1 WAS ABLE TO RETRIEVE THE INNER TUBE AND RETURN IT TO SHORE AND THEN WENT TO ASSIST OPERATOR2.  THE PWC OPERATOR2 WAS UTILIZING HAD A TOW ROPE TIED AROUND THE HANDLEBARS AND OPERATOR1 MANAGED TO TIE THE OTHER END TO THE REAR HANDLE OF HIS PWC.  OPERATOR1 THEN TRIED TO TOW OPERATOR2'S PWC IN WITH OPERATOR2 ON THE PWC WHEN A WAVE, APPROXIMATELY 18 TO 24 INCHES TALL, HIT OPERATOR2'S PWC AND THREW HIM OVERBOARD INTO THE WATER.  THE TOW ROPE TIED TO OPERATOR1'S PWC POSSIBLY CAUSED THE NOSE OF THE PWC TO DIP IN A DOWNWARD ANGLE WHICH MAY HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE PWC TOSSING OPERATOR2 IN THE WATER.  

OPERATOR1 QUICKLY UNTIED OPERATOR2'S PWC FROM HIS AND NOTICED HIS KEY WAS MISSING.  OPERATOR1 JUMPED INTO THE WATER TO RETRIEVE THE KEY FROM OPERATOR2'S PWC.  DURING THIS TIME, OPERATOR1 WAS YELLING AT OPERATOR2 TO REMOVE HIS HOODED SWEATSHIRT (NO HOODED SWEATSHIRT WAS FOUND ON OPERATOR2'S BODY WHEN RETRIEVED).  AFTER RETRIEVING THE KEY, HE MADE IT BACK TO HIS PWC AND WAS GOING TO ASSIST OPERATOR2, BUT OPERATOR2 NEVER RESURFACED.  AT THE TIME HE WAS SUBMERGED, OPERATOR2 WAS BELIEVED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 500 FEET FROM THE SHORELINE IN THE MIDDLE OF THE COVE.  THE DROWnING OCCURRED IN APPROXIMATLEY 10-15 MINUTES FROM THE TIME THE INDIVIDUALS LEFT THE SHORELINE TO THE TIME OPERATOR2 BECAME SUBMERGED.  THE SWEETWATER COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT WAS NOTIFIED AND ARRIVED ON SCENE AT 5:16 P.M. AND AN IMMEDIATE SEARCH BEGAN.  ASSISTANCE WAS REQUESTED FROM THE SUBLETTE COUNTY SEARCH AND RESCUE TEAM AND SWEETWATER COUNTY DIVE TEAM.  THE SEARCH WAS SUSPENDED AT 8:00 P.M. AND RESUMED THE NEXT MORNING.  OPERATOR2'S BODY WAS RECOVERED AT 2:00 P.M. ON AUGUST 21, 2011.

OPERATOR AND TWO PASSENGERS WERE DRIFTING DOWN THE NORTH FORK RIVER WHEN THEIR DRIFT BOAT HIT A ROCK AND WERE LODGED AGAINST IT.  THE OPERATOR TURNED AROUND TO CHECK ON PASSENGERS.  ONE OF THE PASSENGERS HAD FALLEN OUT OF THE BOAT.  THE OPERATOR WATCHED THE PASSENGER SWIM DOWN STREAM THROUGH RAPIDS AND ARRIVE IN WATER THAT LOOKED SLOW AND SHALLOW.  THE OPERATOR GOT THE BOAT OFF THE ROCK, BUT THE BOAT STARTED TO FILL WITH WATER.  THEY WERE ONLY A SHORT DISTANCE FROM SHORE, SO THE OPERATOR AND OTHER PASSENGER ROLLED AND PULLED THE BOAT TO SHORE.  AS THEY WERE DOING THIS, OPERATOR LOOKED FOR THE PASSENGER IN THE WATER AND NOTICED HE WAS NOT MOVING, DRIFTING SLOW IN SHALLOW WATER.  THE OPERATOR LEFT THE BOAT AND WENT FOR HELP.  THE PASSENGER'S BODY WAS LATER FOUND IN A RAPID, LODGED ON A ROCK, FACE UP.

ON AUGUST 29, 2011, AT APPROXIMATELY 7:30 P.M., A FAMILY (FATHER, MOTHER AND SIX CHILDREN) WENT KAYAKING ON BIG HORN LAKE EAST OF LOVELL, WY.  THEY PADDLED TO A NEARBY ISLAND, AND AS THEY HEADED BACK, A STORM BLEW UP CAUSING HEAVY WAVES AND SCATTERING THE KAYAKS.  THE FATHER ASSISTED TWO OF THE CHILDREN BACK TO SHORE, BUT WAS UNABLE TO GO BACK OUT TO HELP THE OTHERS, DUE TO THE STRONG WINDS AND WAVES.  THE FATHER WENT FOR HELP AND AT 7:52 P.M., A CALL TO THE BIG HORN COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT WAS RECEIVED REQUESTING SEARCH AND RESCUE ON THE LAKE.  MANY EMPLOYEES OF THE PLANT, WHERE THE FATHER DROVE TO, ALSO ATTEMPTED TO HELP.  THE LARGE WAVES PREVENTED MANY LIGHTER BOATS FROM LAUNCHING.  ONE OF THE CHILDREN (VICTIM) WAS LOCATED AT 11:00 P.M., THE MOTHER AND TWO OF THE CHILDREN WERE ALL LOCATED TOGETHER AT 11:17 P.M., ONE OF THE CHILDREN (VICTIM) WAS LOCATED AT 12:02 A.M.  ALL WERE TRANSPORTED TO BIG HORN COUNTY HOSPITAL IN LOVELL, WY.

On 6-20-12 at approximately 1200 hrs, a canoe with three individuals left the beach in the Indian Point area on Glendo Reservoir.  They paddled to the south with one of the individual's father chasing them in a kayak, with three PFDs to give to the individuals.  The father could not catch the canoe and went back to the rest of the scout group to prepare them for the day on the water.  The camping neighbor ran to the scout camp and advised them the three individuals in the canoe were in trouble.  The father and other scouts and scout leaders ran to the point on the beach and observed one individual from the canoe was in shallow water, one was swimming circles about twenty yards off shore and the other individual could not be seen.  Subject swam out and saved the one individual from the canoe and then went back out to find the canoe and his son.  Subject found the canoe but could not see his son.  He dove several times and then he looked with a jet ski accompanying him but could not find victim.  State Parks Officers and Platte County Search and Rescue were notified.  Game Warden was notified and then Game Wardens were told and everybody responded to the area.   A search area was established and divers from Casper were called.  The divers could not find anything on 6-21-12.  The side sonar unit from Sublette County Search and Rescue was called and they arrived on 6-22-12.  At approximately 1230 hrs, divers from Carbon County pulled up the body with the help of the side sonar unit from Sublette County.

After the recovery of the one subject, an investigation revealed that the canoe overturned from waves and the three subjects were ejected from the canoe.  Two of the three subjects showed signs of hypothermia.  One swam to shore, one was rescued and the third drowned.  There were no citations issued and the father was given a Boat Accident Investigation Report to fill out and return to our department.

Victims capsized and were ejected due to heavy weather.
